events.title: Inspire America To Vote
events.description:
Voter engagement in America is at a critical crossroads. Today, nearly 100 million citizens who are eligible to vote are not participating in our democracy. That is nearly half of all eligible voters sitting on the sidelines, their voices unheard in shaping the future of our country. This represents not just lost opportunities, but a deep challenge for the health of our democracy. Many of these citizens feel disconnected, frustrated, or overwhelmed by the voting process, while others may simply not realize the power their participation holds. Whatever the reason, the result is the same: millions of Americans are not contributing to decisions that affect their communities, their families, and the nation as a whole.

The goal of Inspire America To Vote is to address this challenge head-on. We believe that voter engagement is not just about encouraging people to cast a ballot—it is about fostering meaningful conversations that can inspire, educate, and empower those who have not yet taken that step. To do this effectively, we must equip ourselves with the tools, strategies, and confidence to engage in productive dialogue with non-voting citizens. It requires understanding their concerns, breaking down barriers, and showing them that their participation matters.

This event is designed to help you become a more effective advocate for civic engagement. We will explore how to connect with people in ways that are respectful, motivating, and action-oriented. By learning to communicate the importance of voting and inspiring those around us, we can transform apathy into action and ensure that more voices are represented in our democracy. Every conversation counts, and together we can help close the gap between eligible citizens and active voters, strengthening the foundation of our democratic process for generations to come.

This is our moment to step up, engage, and inspire. The work we do here will ripple across communities, turning potential into participation, and apathy into action.

Inspire America To Vote will feature a diverse lineup of guest speakers and motivational leaders provided by [Keynote Speaker](https://keynotespeakers.info/) and [Motivational Speaker](https://motivationalspeakerz.com/) who bring years of experience in civic engagement, community organizing, and voter advocacy. These speakers have worked directly with communities across the country, helping non-voters understand the power of their voice and how they can make a meaningful impact through participation. Their insights will provide attendees with real-world strategies for engaging citizens who have historically been disengaged from the voting process. Each speaker brings a unique perspective, from grassroots organizers who have successfully mobilized local neighborhoods, to national experts who have shaped voter outreach campaigns on a larger scale.

Motivational speakers will also play a central role in the event, inspiring attendees to take action in their own communities. These speakers understand the psychological barriers that prevent people from voting—apathy, distrust, confusion—and they will share practical techniques for addressing these challenges with empathy and effectiveness. Through stories of personal experience, case studies, and actionable advice, attendees will leave with a renewed sense of purpose and the confidence to motivate others to participate in democracy.

The sessions will focus not only on theory but on applied best practices. Speakers will break down successful outreach methods, from leveraging social networks and community relationships to using persuasive communication techniques that resonate with individuals across diverse demographics. Attendees will gain hands-on knowledge in facilitating conversations about civic responsibility, addressing objections, and encouraging first-time voters to engage with the process.

In addition to formal presentations, the event will include interactive workshops and Q&A sessions, allowing attendees to directly learn from experts and explore how to tailor strategies to their own communities. These opportunities for dialogue will ensure that participants leave equipped with both the knowledge and practical tools needed to implement voter engagement initiatives effectively.

By combining motivational inspiration with concrete expertise, Inspire America To Vote will provide a comprehensive learning experience. Attendees will not only be energized by the speakers’ passion but will also walk away with clear, actionable steps they can take immediately to reach non-voting citizens. This event is designed to create a ripple effect—arming committed individuals with the skills, strategies, and motivation necessary to strengthen voter participation and ensure that every eligible citizen understands the power and importance of their voice in shaping the future of our country.

events.description:
In the 1940s, Norwegians quietly defied Nazi occupation by knitting and wearing red, pointed hats with tassels. A simple garment became an act of protest.

More recently, knitters in Minnesota revived this tradition during a surge of ICE activity—using red hats as a visible sign of solidarity and resistance.

We carry that work forward here. Proceeds from the sale of our patterns and finished hats and bandanas are donated to CASA de Maryland, supporting immigrant communities through advocacy and assistance.

Join us as we knit, crochet, sew and craft in solidarity. We will keep gathering—as long as there is a need to resist.

🧶 **Resistance Knit-In (Ongoing)**  
📅 **When:** Sundays (ongoing)  
⏰ **Time:** 2–4 pm  
📍 **Where:** The Shops at Kenilworth – Common Area  

**How:** Supplies if you have them for the Melt the Ice Hat, Pin or Baltimore Bandana and/or the Blue Wave Hat . Knit and crochet patterns can be found on Ravelry. Beginners welcome, and supplies may be available to share.

events.description:
Please join Engaged Defenders for Democracy in south Cary every Tuesday from 7:30-9am as we gather to demonstrate at the intersection of Kildaire Farm Road and 1010. This peaceful visibility event is intended to motivate people to take an active role in defending our democracy. Inaction supports the regime, so our goal is to connect with drivers on their morning commutes and inspire them to make the shift from idle bystander to engaged participant. We also want to give people who are currently uncertain or afraid the courage they need to TAKE A STAND and get involved to protect our democracy.

This is a positive and nonviolent demonstration. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement.

Please bring positive signs only. Some examples: “Stand up, you are not alone!” “Courage is contagious!” “Dissenting is patriotic!” If you've never done this before, we're happy to help you. We will have extra signs for anyone who needs one. Feel free to bring a friend.

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy

events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has public restrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

Join your neighbors each week at the intersection of Baltimore Pike & Route 320 (southeast corner of Springfield Mall property) as we stand up for constitutional government and the rule of law.

Many in our community are concerned about actions by the Trump administration that they believe undermine congressional authority, democratic norms, and long-standing constitutional principles. We gather to peacefully affirm that the United States is a republic governed by laws - not by any one individual.

**When & where**
We meet weekly at the intersection of Baltimore Pike & Route 320. We remain on public sidewalks and do not block traffic.  Please bring signs or flags if you’d like.

**Our values**
This is a peaceful, nonviolent event. We ask all participants to engage respectfully, avoid confrontation, help de-escalate any tensions, and follow all local laws and safety guidance.
	
Everyone who supports constitutional democracy and peaceful civic engagement is welcome.

**Transportation**
We encourage public transportation to the intersection via bus or trolley.  If you drive, please do not use the Mall's parking lot. There is plentiful free parking on nearby residential streets such as Sheffield Drive (one block northeast) or Cedar, Walnut, and Ogden Avenues (two blocks south).

events.description:
The Mission: It all comes down to the home stretch. We are making the final calls of the year to ensure every single voter in our community reaches the finish line for the General Election.

Non-Partisan Outreach: Our focus is 100% on voter turnout and ensuring everyone has the resources to participate.

Full Training: We provide a streamlined training to ensure you are ready to handle last-minute voter questions.

events.description:
Across the country, immigrant communities are under attack — targeted by raids, detention, and dehumanizing policies that tear families apart. These tactics are being weaponized as part of a broader authoritarian crackdown that threatens the rights and freedoms of everyone.

Now is the time to come together, to stand shoulder to shoulder, and to say clearly:

events.description:
QPP is an action-oriented community for queers and allies joined together in solidarity, providing mutual aid-based survival work — rooted in principles of racial justice, gender justice, disability justice, economic justice and class justice — and creating a place of true belonging and community.

🌈

Here are our group norms:

Respect Worth/Dignity: We respect the worth and dignity of others and that guides our interactions with everyone in the group.

Intent: We assume others are acting with good intent. If someone says or does something insensitive or hurtful, we help them learn.

Accountability: We know that we can all make mistakes, and we endeavor to act with grace to acknowledge them and repair any damage done.

Embrace Growth Mindset: We strive to see mistakes or conflicts as opportunities to learn and grow.

Intergenerational Respect: We acknowledge that, while the lived experiences of group members of various ages will differ, we will give everyone's thoughts and actions due consideration. No one is too young or too old to contribute or to have great ideas.

Confidentiality: We agree that stories stay and learning leaves. We can apply what we learn from others in the group, we cannot share their stories.

Step Forward/Step Back: We strive to promote equitable participation in the group using the "step forward/step back" framework. If you frequently speak up in conversations, consider stepping back to make room for other voices. If you typically remain quiet in conversations, consider stepping forward to make your voice heard.

Leadership Rotates: We do not have a hierarchical structure. Working groups (including leadership!) are all made up of volunteers, and involvement in them is not set in stone. If you want to be involved in a working group, please let someone in that group know. (Planning consists of volunteers.) Choose how you best think you can contribute, and let someone know.

## The Power of Talking with Voters
With 8 years of experience on the frontline of innovation, Swing Blue Alliance is your go-to for taking effective action in the upcoming midterm elections.  

### Don't miss our featured presentations! 

- Join us on the ground with Lisa Pedulla, SBA, NH Lead, in purple NH for an update on how conversations at the door are moving the needle - with both Democrats AND Republicans!
- With Election Day just around the corner, see how special attention is being paid to critical competitive races.  Hear about calling opportunities from the SBA phone bank team that are available across Maine, Pennsylvania, and North Carolina – to ensure every voter turns out to flip Congress, defeat Susan Collins, and flip the Pennsylvania State Senate.

- Swing Blue Alliance co-lead Susan Labandibar will share findings from the AI Visibility Project, and what the project has learned about improving the accuracy and completeness of candidate information online.

We’ll also share concrete ways to put your time and energy to work before Election Day. The Frontline Update runs from 10:00–10:30 AM ET.

This is a focused, 30-minute meeting designed to deliver high-impact updates quickly and clearly, followed by optional time for Q&A.

---


## Frontline Update 
**Where grassroots volunteers get informed, inspired, and mobilized**

The Frontline Update is Swing Blue Alliance’s monthly virtual gathering for volunteers across the country who are ready to turn urgency into action.

Each month, we bring you inside the work that’s shaping the next elections — and the future beyond them.

### What You’ll Get

**The Latest on Key Races**  
Hear directly from campaign leaders, partner organizations, and Swing Blue Alliance team leads about the most critical state and local races on the horizon. From state Supreme Courts to House of Delegate races to emerging battlegrounds, you’ll learn what’s at stake — and why it matters now.

**Campaign Spotlights**  
We regularly highlight election campaigns where early volunteer engagement can make a decisive difference. You’ll meet candidates, organizers, and grassroots partners building power in places that are too often overlooked.

**Clear, Immediate Actions**  
We don’t just talk about strategy — we plug you in. Whether it’s canvassing, phone banking, postcarding, fundraising, protest organizing, or message testing, you’ll leave every meeting with concrete ways to take action.

**The Bigger Strategy**  
The Frontline Update connects the dots between today’s volunteer opportunities and our long-term strategy to defend democracy, protect voting rights, and build durable Democratic power.

### Who It’s For

- New volunteers looking for a place to start  
- Experienced organizers ready for their next assignment  
- Grassroots leaders who want to stay aligned and informed  
- Anyone who believes democracy is worth fighting for  

Whether you can give an hour a week or lead a team, this is where you find your place in the fight.

---

**Join the next Frontline Update and be part of what comes next.**

events.title: HOUSE MAJORITY RUNS THROUGH CALIFORNIA | Phone Banks!
events.description:
**In 2025, California made history by passing Prop 50. Now it’s time to turn that victory into lasting change by Taking Back the House!**

We're going to reach out to voters in our targeted districts early to hear their issues, concerns and ideas. And we'll be using some of the best practices from **Deep Canvassing** to have more engaged and meaningful conversations. 

**Join our virtual phone banks with the Bay Area Coalition and other California Democratic Party partners and help stop the Trump / MAGA authoritarian takeover.**  

We need your help! Virtual phone banks using the Scale to Win dialer have become an essential part of campaigns. Whether you’re new to phone banking or an expert, you have a place with our people-powered campaigns. The good news is, phone banking is easy to learn and can be done from the comfort of your own home. We'll provide training on both the deep canvassing script and how to use Scale to Win.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: L-S Dems Community Meeting
events.description:
Join us for our monthly Lampeter-Strasburg Democratic community gatherings! We meet each month to connect, build community, and drive local change. Our gatherings rotate between traditional meetings, casual happy hours, and social events. This specific event page is for one of our traditional meetings.

During standard meetings, we discuss upcoming elections, hear directly from local candidates, plan volunteer activities, and organize get-out-the-vote efforts that make a real impact right here at home. We also break down current political developments at the local, state, and national levels to stay informed and ready for action.

Whether you are a longtime volunteer or taking your very first step, you are welcome here. There is no pressure or obligation—come listen, ask questions, bring a friend, and discover how you can help strengthen our local Democratic community.

Decisions that impact our community get made in public meetings, often with little public input in the room. The Spartanburg County Democratic Party is building a **“Civic Watch”** team to attend key local meetings, take notes for the party and the public, and sign up to speak during public comment when timely issues come up.

The **Spartanburg School District Seven (D7) Board of Trustees** makes decisions that affect students, educators, families, and taxpayers across our community. Board actions shape **school budgets**, **academic priorities**, **student support services**, **facility planning**, **safety policies**, and the overall direction of public education in our area.

By attending these meetings as a volunteer observer, you’ll help ensure our community stays informed about what’s happening in our schools. Whether you choose to **speak during public comment**, **take notes**, or simply **be a presence in the room**, your participation matters.

No prior experience is necessary—just a willingness to show up and pay attention to what’s happening in your community.

events.title: ICE Out of Home Depot/ICE Out for Good!
events.description:
Home Depot depends on the labor of immigrant workers, from construction to disaster recovery, profiting from global markets while turning its back on vulnerable communities here at home. This injustice cannot continue. Together, we have the power to demand accountability and justice.

Join us as we make it impossible for Home Depot to ignore the voices of the people. We stand united, sending a clear message that our communities deserve protection, respect, and solidarity—not neglect.

Here in Lancaster we have been hosting a series of sustained events to continue the pressure on the Home Depot corporation and the wider Lancaster County community. We gather along Fruitville Pike with our signs and our presence demonstrating our support for our immigrant neighbors. We encourage the Home Depot to publicly condemn the ICE raids taking place on or near their properties. We urge our community to condemn the cruel and illegal actions of ICE throughout this country. We come together to be an example for corporations and our local community to ACT, to SPEAK UP, and to take a STAND!

events.title: Together We Sing
events.description:
Join us each Thursday evening 6:00-7:00

With all that is going on in our world, human beings are challenged to the core, and our nervous systems are in overdrive. There is so much fear, anger, and ranting about what people are against and what others are doing that is ruining our lives. Against-energy is exhausting! I'm weary from the pounding of toxic negativity. I am for Peace on Earth and Goodwill to ALL! I want to know what you are for. From the deepest place of integrity, human dignity, and decency, what are you for? We cannot think, feel, or act from our deepest selves when our nervous systems are ragged with hyper-stimulation. I want to create a place for people to gather as a community with the common desire to feel welcome, safe, and to nourish our nervous systems.

I am a singer, singing coach, and rhythm circle facilitator. I envision gathering in a circle as friends, with the common ground of being human, and singing in a way that soothes our nervous systems and lifts our spirits.

You don't need to have a "great" voice or read music. I will teach you simple and beautiful songs. When we sing together, our breathing regulates, and the vibration created in our singing works together to shift the nervous system out of fight-flight-freeze into rest, digest, and coherence (the quality of forming a unified whole)... community!

I weave a spirit of play, rhythm, and movement into my teaching.

Interesting fact: Play is as vital to survival as food and water. The Science of Play, by Stuart Brown

 

Cullie Treichler

events.title: States Win CA Peninsula Virtual Phonebank!
events.description:
Join States Win CA Peninsula every Saturday at 10am PT to elect Democrats in majority making State Legislature districts! Read about our candidates and races below. 

[**Meet Hadley Haas:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/hadley-haas/) Hadley is a Pittsburgh native, parent, and advocate who turns personal challenges into action. Democrats hold the PA House by just one seat. HD 44 is a top flip opportunity in suburban Allegheny County—a district shifting toward pragmatic leadership. Electing Hadley strengthens the Democratic majority and protects progress on gun safety, reproductive freedom, and economic relief.

[**Meet Chris Thomas:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/chris-thomas/) Chris comes from a working-class family of veterans, coal miners, and educators. He worked construction before becoming a middle school math and science teacher, where he saw how underfunded schools hurt students. Now a community organizer across Montgomery and Berks counties and a volunteer firefighter, Chris knows what it means to show up for neighbors. Republicans control the PA State Senate. SD 24 is increasingly competitive as suburban and small-town voters reject gridlock and rising costs. 

[**Meet Robyn Vining:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/robyn-vining/) Robyn's race is the most flippable Senate district in Wisconsin this cycle under the fair maps that took effect in 2024. Robyn has already proven she can win tough races, flipping her Assembly district and defending it in multiple close contests, and now she’s bringing that same strength to the fight for the Senate. Winning this seat is essential to building a Democratic majority.

[**Meet Jenna Jacobson:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/jenna-jacobson/) Representative Jenna Jacobson’s commitment to public service was shaped by her mother, a single parent and pastor who balanced raising two children while relying on food stamps and pursuing her education. Breaking the GOP’s legislative grip and building a governing majority capable of delivering real progress for working families across Wisconsin is not possible without electing Jenna and flipping this seat.

[**Meet Kristie O'Brien:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/kristie-obrien/) Kristie is a lawyer, mediator, and mom who is running for the Arizona State Senate in Legislative District 13. This race is a critical opportunity for Democrats to flip a key Arizona State Senate seat and move closer to winning a majority in the chamber. Legislative District 13 is one of the most competitive districts in the state, with recent statewide Democratic candidates carrying the district even as Republicans narrowly held legislative seats. 

[**Meet Sarah Pounds:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/sarah-pounds/) The path to reclaiming a Democratic House majority, and a full trifecta, runs through Michigan House District 54. In 2024, Democrats lost with a razor thin margin here. This year, both Republicans and Democrats have named HD-54 a top target. Sarah Pounds is exactly the candidate this moment calls for: a public school educator with firsthand experience of the kitchen-table issues this district cares about—fully funded schools, lower costs, and protected reproductive freedom. Investing in Sarah now is how Democrats turn the narrowest of losses into the majority they need.

[**Meet Trevor Jung**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/trevor-jung/) Wisconsin State Senate District 21 presents a critical pickup opportunity on the path to flipping the chamber and building a Democratic majority that can move the state forward. Electing Trevor Jung would all but guarantee Democratic control while adding a proven local leader focused on lowering costs, investing in public education and workforce development, and ensuring economic growth benefits Wisconsin families, not special interests. 

**Why phonebank:** The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. Every call helps us clean our lists, which makes for a faster, more efficient phonebank!

**Come one, come all:** No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

events.title: Feeding Agency Bulk Pick Up for Pepper Place Farmers Market in Birmingham (Jefferson County)

location.venue: The Farmers Market at Pepper Place | Outdoors

events.description:
{Please know this is for registered feeding agencies to sign up, not for individuals} 

Each Saturday during the market season, we will have an opportunity for a local feeding agency to pick up and receive that days produce donations by our gracious farmers. Are you a feeding agency that would like to have some fresh produce to add in with your food distribution? We would love to have you as one of our agencies that pick up fresh produce donated by our amazing farmers throughout the market season. 

🛑THIS CAN BE A SUBSTANTIAL AMOUNT OF PRODUCE (USUALLY A PICKUP TRUCK WORTH), IT WILL HAVE TO ALL BE PICKED UP BY ONE AGENCY. IF IT NEEDS TO BE SPLIT BETWEEN MULTIPLE AGENCIES, IT WILL NEED TO BE DONE BY THE AGENCY AFTER PICK UP.  There is no set amount donated each week, the amount and what is donated can vary greatly depending on what the growers have. There will be certain times where there might be a surplus of a particular item(s). 

🛍️Produce will be bagged in plastic bags by volunteers and ready for pick up at 12:45pm each Saturday on site of the market. If you have not picked up from us before at this market please connect with Adrienne first before signing up. 

 ⭐If for some reason you need to cancel your scheduled pick up please make sure to connect with me ASAP so I can get somebody else scheduled in your place. Our volunteers do not usually have the ability to take the produce to a drop off site so communication is very important.

‼️Please do not just show up to receive produce without talking with Adrienne prior and signing up! 

Instructions will be sent out to the receiving agency on Friday, it will go to the email/phone registered.

events.title: 📢✊ After We March, We Organize! 🔥 Solidarity Warriors Indivisible Action Group 🗽

The real power comes from what we do after the march. Research shows that no movement with 3.5% of the population in continuous mobilization has ever failed 📊 — but only when they go beyond demonstrations into mass noncooperation, noncompliance, and strategic action that dismantles the pillars holding up authoritarianism. 🛡️ How to Protest Safely
🌎 Immigrant Rights
🪶 Indigenous History
🔐 Cybersecurity
✊ Community Organizing Tactics
and much more!

events.title: Weekly 6th Ave Bridge Bannering Over I-5 | Mondays
events.description:
There is street parking, but a lot of it is metered; Linda will have quarters with her on the bridge in case you need some.  There aren't meters on the bridge itself so try to nab a spot there first. 

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

Join Swing Left and Indivisible Oregon for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We’ve launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Indivisible Elk Grove - Laguna -- Members Meetings
events.description:
The onslaught of news, the chaos coming out of the White House – it’s all meant to overwhelm us. It’s a deliberate strategy to sow confusion and make us believe we are powerless to fight back. The antidote: Coming together in community to process what’s happening, to sift through what’s important and what’s just noise, and coalesce around strategies for fighting back. Join Indivisible Elk Grove – Laguna’s co-founders Joann and Jim every first and third Saturday of the month, as we carve out an hour to discuss what’s happening and – more importantly – what actions can be taken at our local level to fight for our democracy!

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

Nonviolence

events.title: States Win Sacramento & Friends Phonebank!
events.description:
Join States Win Sacramento on Wednesdays at 2:30pm PT to make calls for our candidates,  **Jacob Martinez**, **Kevin Volk**, **Edgar Soto**, and **Jan Maino!**

**Jacob Martinez** is a lifelong Mesa resident, a dedicated community advocate dedicated community advocate, and first-time candidate running to represent LD-9 in the Arizona House. He is a proud graduate of Mesa public schools and ASU Law. In addition to his local roots, Jacob serves in the US Navy Reserve, where he has strengthened his commitment to service, leadership, and accountability.

**Kevin Volk** is running for reelection in Arizona's State House LD 17, and this race is a must-win if Democrats want an opportunity at governing in a majority. Kevin won his previous election with the support of States Win Sacramento. Since then, he has championed affordable
housing, boosted early childhood education funding, and advanced water conservation technologies to protect Arizona's long-term future.

**Edgar Soto** is running for Arizona's State Senate LD 17, which is one of Democrat's clearest pickup opportunities in the Senate *and* the state! Edgar is a Marine Corps veteran, educator, and community leader running as a first-time candidate to flip the Arizona State Senate seat in District 17. His deep roots in the community and lifelong commitment to service drive his work to strengthen public schools, keep communities safe, and build an Arizona that families can afford.

**Jan Maino** is running to flip Michigan State House District 46! She is bringing decades of experience as a licensed social worker, school board president, nonprofit leader, and community advocate to her campaign. Jan’s work has always been rooted in showing up, listening, and helping people navigate real challenges with dignity and respect. Jan is running to bring the same community-first leadership to Lansing. 


**Why phonebank:** The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. We also help improve our candidate’s data! 

**Come one, come all:** No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

events.description:
### Let's flip Wisconsin blue!

Join States Win Chicago on Wednesdays at 5pm CT to make calls for our candidates, Robyn Vining and Brandy Tollefson.

**Meet Robyn Vining:** Robyn has built a reputation as a tireless advocate for public education, healthcare access, common-sense gun reform, and economic fairness. States Win has proudly partnered with Robyn across multiple cycles, and she has a proven record of flipping
and holding competitive seats. Now, she is taking that to the next level in her race for State Senate. Robyn’s race is the most flippable Senate district in Wisconsin this cycle! Winning this seat is *essential* to building a Democratic majority in Wisconsin. 

**Meet Brandy Tollefson:** Brandy is running to flip AD-88 to help lower costs for families, expand access to affordable health care, and fight for all kids to get the education they deserve. -Budget allocations and funding priorities 
-Curriculum and instructional policies 
-Community engagement and transparency 

We need advocates who are willing to show up, pay attention, and help ensure decisions are made in the best interest of students and families.

By participating, you can: 
-Speak up for students and families 
-Monitor whether funding and curriculum decisions meet the needs of all students Support transparency, equity, and strong public education 

Your voice matters.

ChalkWalk | Saugatuck @ 4:30pm | Hosted by: Good Trouble Indivisible

Create Public Awareness With Us!

Good Trouble Indivisible’s ChalkWalk is a creative public-awareness action using sidewalk chalk to encourage people to pause, read, think, and talk about what is happening in our country.

GTI ChalkWalks transform ordinary sidewalks into a continuing public message. As people walk through downtown Saugatuck, they stop to read, take photographs and videos, ask questions, share their thoughts, and have meaningful conversations with us. 

These peaceful public-awareness actions help bring important issues out into the open—where they can be seen, considered, and discussed.

There are many ways to participate, and you do not need to be an artist or get down on the sidewalk to help.

👉 Help chalk or outline the prepared words. 

👉 Hold a sign of your choosing about democracy, freedom, justice, or another current issue.

👉 Hand out Good Trouble Indivisible cards and information.

👉 Talk with passersby about current events and our work.

👉 Take photographs or video that we can share on social media and our website.

👉 Simply stand with us and help create a visible community presence.

Participants who would like to speak with the public will be given information and talking points. 

Come help for the entire event or stop by for however long you can. 

ChalkWalk is peaceful, lawful, protected FREE SPEECH…welcoming, and open to everyone who believes that public awareness matters—and that silence and inaction are not our only choices.

Bring a democracy sign to hold if you like.  Chalk and handout materials will be provided by Good Trouble Indivisible. 

We hope you will join us—and help turn our sidewalks into important conversations.

Good Trouble Indivisible is a Michigan nonprofit corporation and a chapter of the National Indivisible.

events.title: Messaging Storm - Weekly Calls to Congress
events.description:
## Messaging Storm
 
### Wednesday October 21, 2026

**A coordinated call to our Elected Officials**

U.S. Capitol Switchboard

(202) 224-3121

### **Call Congress and Demand they stop Trumps Russian diesel deal and support Ukraine.**

**Background** 
In both 2022 and 2026, Congress passed legislation to make purchasing Russian gas and oil more difficult, banning Russian energy imports (2022) and placing tariffs on Russian oil and gas (2026). These bills were passed with bipartisan support to prevent the US funding Russia’s attacks on Ukraine. However, on October 9, 2026, the president lifted the Congressional sanctions and said he struck a deal with Russia and that the US could purchase from Russia; Russia also lifted their own ban on exports as a result. This “deal” has caused a bipartisan rebuke  from Senators, and on October 16, 2026 Congressman Meeks of NY introduced legislation to block Trump’s deal with Russia. Tell Congress we should oppose any deal with Russia, that you support Ukraine and that we should be buying our needed energy for the winter from allies like Canada, not imperialistic authoritarians. 


### Call Script

 **adapted from 5calls.org**

Hi, my name is [NAME] and I’m a constituent from [CITY, ZIP].
I'm calling in opposition to the Trump administration's deal to import Russian diesel. There are three concerns I have regarding this. First, I want [REP/SEN Name] to demand the Trump administration follow the law banning Russian energy imports. The U.S. should not be funding Putin's war while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. Second, Representative Meeks on October 16th, proposed legislation to block Trumps deal, I want [REP/SEN NAME] to support this. Finally, Americans need fuel for their homes this winter, we should return to purchasing from our ally, Canada, as we have in the past. Congress needs to lift the tariffs on Canada so Americans can afford heating their homes this the winter. 
Thank you for your time and consideration.

**Leave full address if leaving a voicemail so your opinion is tallied.**

**Other reading**

Acharya, P. (16 October 2026). House Democrat introduces bipartisan bill to block Trump’s Russian diesel deal. [Politico.](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/16/house-democrat-bill-blocks-trump-russian-diesel-deal-01123646)

Bikales, J., Ahn, A., and Ewing, G.R. (9 October 2026). Trump lifts sanctions on Russian diesel, suggests US may buy amid surging fuel prices. [Politico.](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/09/trump-diesel-sanctions-lifted-russia-01114977)

Freking, K. (11 October 2026). Bipartisan group of senators calls on Trump to 'reverse course' on Russian diesel plan. [PBS.](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/bipartisan-group-of-senators-calls-on-trump-to-reverse-course-on-russian-diesel-plan)

House Foreign Affairs Committee. (16 October 2026). Meeks Introduces Legislation to Block Trump’s Russia Diesel Deal [Press Release.](https://democrats-foreignaffairs.house.gov/2026/10/meeks-introduces-legislation-to-block-trump-s-russia-diesel-deal)

Join us to remind people that democracy is on the line. Meet up on local Lancaster, PA, overpasses. Overpass messages change each week based on current events AND the enduring themes we need to remember.

The current regime is a menace, throwing kerosene on every fire. Cruel detention and deportation continues, the MAGA budget cuts critical supports for medical care and nutrition just to give huge tax breaks to those who have enough. Extremists in government are trying to avoid accountability by gutting voting rights and rigging voting districts. And the corruption and cronyism threatens all of us. It can seem like so much; it can seem hopeless. And yet, our neighbors need to know we RESIST this. That we are standing up, and we are the majority. We always need to encourage nonviolence in that effort.

Each week we stand up for vocal, peaceful, resistance. This message is a mantra of hope and determination that we can hold and share with each other in even our darkest moments. The message should be seen and heard EVERYWHERE–join us! 

Indivisibles and friends will gather on local Lancaster overpasses. Location details will be sent after registration. At each location there is sufficient parking. Indivisible LT will provide letters for the slogan to hold and flags. Feel free to bring your own signs as well. We recommend using LARGE letters, keeping it civil, and brief.

events.description:
Piloted in 2021, "WELLderness: An Outdoor Wellness Series" was developed to bring members of the community together (in person and online) to engage in activities that would have a positive impact on their physical and mental health and well-being. Throughout the year, people have the opportunity to participate in FREE events that center around fostering better connections to self and the environment.

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

Explore the gardens, tune into your senses and connect with nature during this guided Forest Bathing walk. Registration is free and required to attend.

Sage is a certified Forest Bathing Guide, who has been practicing Nature and Forest Therapy since 2018. His practice has been offered through the Friends of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens, Friends of the National Arboretum, and Nature Worx. He's provided walks for the general public, and personalized or private walks for summer camps, folks in recovery, veterans, and marginalized communities. Sage's professional background includes massage therapy, outdoor educator, veteran, and professional cyclist. Sage is an Outward Bound and National Outdoor Leadership School alumni.

Participants should bring a water bottle, snack, bug spray, sun protection, and/or anything else one may carry when spending time outdoors. Wear comfortable clothing and shoes for being outdoors.

events.title: Are Your Friends Registered to Vote?

sponsor.name: Building Bridges for America Action Fund

events.description:
### More than a quarter of eligible voters are not registered to vote.

#### In key states like North Carolina and Georgia, the number is even higher.

### You can help!

### Three Easy Steps:

- **STEP ONE:  Who Needs to Hear from You?**  
_Go through your contact lists, your email directories, your family connections, your personal network.  Is everyone registered to vote?  Has anyone moved recently?  Who needs reminders to do things?  Does everyone know that voting matters to you?_

- **STEP TWO:  Reach Out**  
_Reach out personally.  Let them know:  Voting is important to you.  Ask them to join you as a regular voter.  Share the [National Voter Registration Form](https://www.eac.gov/voters/national-mail-voter-registration-form).  It's usable almost everywhere, to register or update voter registration.  And it's available in nearly 20 languages.  Local election information is available at [eac.gov](https://www.eac.gov/voters/register-and-vote-in-your-state)._ 

- **STEP THREE:  Follow Up**  
_A week later, touch base again.  Ask if they've checked their registration.  Thank them!  You have built a bond around your shared values._

Research backs it up:  Personal contact WORKS.  These calls are some of the most effective tools we have to build progressive power.

events.title: Doors in the D4: Canvass with Michael Mazzocco for Phoenix City Council District 4
events.summary: Knock doors with Michael Mazzocco for Phoenix City Council, D4.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Knock doors with Michael Mazzocco in District 4

Two hours, a partner, and a short walk. That is how this race gets won, one porch at a time. You do not need a script memorized or a political background. You need comfortable shoes and a willingness to listen. We handle the rest.

### Why it matters here

District 4 is the only majority-renter district in Phoenix, and it is the first open council seat since 2013. The people most affected by what the city does next are the ones least likely to get a knock on the door. When you walk a route, you reach them. That is the whole game.

### Why Michael

Michael Mazzocco has lived and worked in D4 for nearly 20 years. He built the Greater Phoenix Equality Chamber of Commerce from a volunteer board into a fully staffed organization, seven years on the board and four as president. He has raised millions for Valley nonprofits. He would be the first Native American to serve on the Phoenix City Council.

He is running on affordable rents, homelessness solutions that actually work, an Office of Economic Empowerment to bring local businesses back into D4 storefronts, scaling the city's Community Safety Plan, which cut violent crime 40% along the I-17 and 27th Avenue corridor, to the rest of the district, and shade where the heat is worst.

### Why your door matters

You know your neighborhood better than any consultant. Walk it with us and you are not handing out flyers, you are having real conversations with people who rarely get asked what they need. Your neighbors are already out here doing it. There is room for you.

### What you'll do

Walk a short, mapped route with a partner and knock 30 to 40 doors. We train you before you step off, pair you with an experienced volunteer, and hand you the route, the script, and the literature.

Shifts are short and timed around the weather: weekday and weekend mornings, before the heat climbs. Pick the slot that fits your week below.

Bring comfortable shoes, water, and a charged phone. We bring the coffee, the training, and everything else.

### Can't walk a route?

You can still put one in the field. Chip in: secure.actblue.com/donate/mazzocco4d4. $25 covers the literature for one precinct walk.

Paid for by Mazzocco for Phoenix and authorized by Michael Mazzocco.

## Phone Bank for Michael Mazzocco — Phoenix City Council, D4

District 4 voters live on the phone. **25,525 calls for service for homelessness** inside D4 last year — about 2,100 every month. **83,410 active voters**. Picking up the phone is how we hear what's actually happening on every block in D4.

Michael Mazzocco has lived and worked in D4 for nearly 20 years. Mayor Gallego appointed him chair of Phoenix's Human Relations Commission. Throughout the year, people have the opportunity to participate in FREE events that center around fostering better connections to self and the environment.

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ 

"Listening to Nature: A Gateway to Connection"

Join Christine for this immersive sound experience. You'll start by learning about resonance, which refers to the process of attuning to and harmonizing with both body sensations and the energy of those around us. As a group you'll select one of the 8 principles of resonance as your focus for the session. Next, you'll relax and enjoy Christine's musical sound accompaniment as you engage with the natural environment. The session will end with a guided meditation. 

From Christine: "By practicing attentive listening in the gardens, participants will enhance their ability to listen actively to reduce conflict and the judgmental voice. This session highlights the importance of accompaniment, making it easier to regulate emotion. Active participation attempts to enable compassionate connection to promote trust, safety and healing. The formation of traumatic memory happens when we feel alone. Accompaniment starts to happen when one person consents to let another travel with them, emotionally or physically, for more than one resonant exchange ultimately fostering a sense of peace, well-being, and a stronger bond with nature, all essential for human health and vitality."

Christine Maila is a certified Resonant Healing Practitioner. Christine supports clients with unconscious contract/sacred vow work and time travel empathy, as well as other Resonant Healing practices. She draws on her mindfulness practices and background in education while supporting others in moving forward in their lives with more autonomy, inspiration, love and freedom. 

View her profile here: https://sarahpeyton.com/practitioner/christine-g-maila/

She especially enjoy introducing the practice of yoga to beginners and focuses on making her classes approachable and accessible for all skill levels.

events.description:
My name is Angelita Morillo and I am running for re-election for Portland City Council, District 3 (SE Portland with a tiny piece of NE).

In my first year in office I fought corporate rental price fixing by passing the Algorithmic Price Fixing Ban, I held landlords who want to profit off of detention facilities (like ICE) in our community accountable, I pushed for fossil fuel contracts to be investigated, I funded the restoration of Parks bathrooms in District 3, I secured Portland Street Response’s place in our public safety infrastructure, I’ve centered the voices of unhoused and working class people in the City’s approach to homelessness, and I’ve pushed for local transportation funding.

I moved from Paraguay to the United States as a kid, and my experiences as a queer immigrant who has experienced homelessness have shaped and developed my interest in local government and policy. After attending Lincoln High School and Portland State University, where I studied Political Science and Legal Studies, I worked in Commissioner JoAnn Hardesty's office in Constituent Services and Tribal Relations policy. From there, I went on to do anti-hunger policy with Partners For a Hunger-Free Oregon. 

I am passionate about local government and ensuring that policy makers are led by the community they serve and not the other way around. I love Portland and all that it has given me and I want to give back to it so we can work together to make it a better place to live for all of us. Join me in creating a Portland that works for everyone and re-elect Angelita Morillo for District 3!

P.S. If you are a Portland resident, your first $25 donated will be matched TEN TO ONE by the city's Small Donor Elections program that helps benefit grassroots candidates like me! Read more about the program here.

We are calling on lawmakers at every level of government to champion laws that protect voting rights, defend election officials and volunteers, stop voter suppression, strengthen election security, and fully fund fair, accessible elections.

Our vote is our voice. Our voice is our power. And democracy only works when every eligible voter can participate freely, safely, and equally.

Please take one minute to send a letter to lawmakers and urge them to protect the freedom to vote.

events.title: Health Care Is a Human Right, Not a Luxury

No one should be forced to choose between seeing a doctor, paying rent, buying groceries, or taking on medical debt just to survive. Yet every year, people in America suffer, delay care, go bankrupt, and die because our health care system puts profit before people.

Congress must act. We are calling on every member of Congress to co-sponsor and pass the Medicare for All Act so every person in the United States is guaranteed the care they need, when they need it. Health care is a human right. Send a message to Congress to build a healthcare system that puts people, dignity, and life ahead of corporate greed.

SCAMPS Schedule

Noon – 12:05 pm: Welcome In

12:05 – 12:10 pm: Intro to Group

12:10 – 12:15 pm: Clown-isthenics: Easy Primal Body Exercises, Sitting or Standing

12:15 – 12:50 pm: Open Floor Sharing – Show and tell your projects, including costume/makeup ideas, puppetry, slogans, signs, and songs. Share pics, documents, and takeaways from past demonstrations. Share action/performance ideas and inspiration for the world you want to see.

12:50 pm: Closing Words

events.description:
# Standout for Justice: Burlington ICE Detention Center

**Join us to stand in solidarity with those detained and to alert the community to the I.C.E. facility in Burlington.**

The conditions reported inside are inhumane: no due process, no mattresses, no showers, and minimal food. Your presence makes a tangible difference—immigrants have reported that seeing supporters outside transforms their spirit from fear to hope and confidence.

### **Event Details**
*   **Time:** 10:00 AM – 12:30 PM
*   **Location:** Meet on the green at **1000 District Ave, Burlington**.
*   **The Action:** We gather at 10:00 AM outside the facility to show direct support to those inside. Bring fod which will be distributed to immigrants leaving the facility.  
*   **The March:** Once we have enough participants, we will move as a group to **Burlington Mall Road** to raise public awareness of this facility. 

> **Important Note:** Please arrive at the 1000 District Ave location at the start. We move to the Mall Road as a group based on turnout; arriving early ensures you find the team and can participate in the march.

### **What to Bring**
*   **Food for the immigrants:** Shared items for those being released.
*   **Protection:** Sunscreen, a hat, and appropriate gear depending on the weather.
*   **Footwear:** Comfortable shoes for standing and walking.
*   **Signs:** We provide a small number of signs, but feel free to bring your own! **Note:** If you are bringing several signs, you can drop them off at 1000 District Ave first before parking.

### **Parking & Transportation**
**Please Read:** Parking at 1000 District Ave is strictly for customers; vehicles identified as belonging to protesters **will be towed**. 

*   **Safe parking and public transportation options will be provided via email once you register for the event.**

events.title: Call voters for a virtual phone bank to call OR-5 with Indivisible OR and Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join Indivisible Oregon and Swing Left for a virtual Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters over the phone.

At this phone bank, we’ll:

- Call all types of voters -- not just those who vote like us.

- Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. 

You can join and call from just your computer/tablet, but we recommend being prepared with a phone and earbuds as well!

––

About the program:
This isn’t traditional phone banking—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- Why we’re starting early: launching a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns are even off the ground.

- How we’ll go big: calling every voter, not just the ones we normally rely on, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

*Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.*

events.title: VOTER SUPPRESSION MARCH | Zeeland | Hosted by: Good Trouble Indivisible

address_lines: LOOK FOR JAN's YELLOW JEEP in the parking lot.

events.description:
GOOD TROUBLE INDIVISIBLE’S

— VOTER SUPPRESSION MARCH —

SATURDAY, JULY 25, 2026
ZEELAND, MICHIGAN

Good Trouble Indivisible will coordinate a silent Voter Suppression March through downtown Zeeland.

Please register in advance. We provide all signs.

Please dress in black.

Our public-awareness signs expose the laws, policies, tactics, and deliberate barriers being used to suppress the vote and silence the voices of the American people.

Voting is the foundation of representative government.

When voting rights are attacked, democracy itself is under attack.


LOCATION:

📍 Meet in front of Zeeland City Hall.

LOOK for Jan’s yellow Jeep at 11:30 AM to sign in and pick up your sign.

The march will begin promptly, so please do not be late.


SCHEDULE

⏰ 11:30 AM — Sign-in and sign pickup

Good Trouble Indivisible provides all signs. Signs are not available once the lineup begins.

⏰ 11:45 AM — Lineup and instructions

You must be present for lineup and instructions to participate in the march.

⏰ 12:00 PM — Voter Suppression March begins promptly

⏰ Event concludes at approximately 1:00 PM

Water and protein bars will be provided by Good Trouble Indivisible.

Participants will march silently in a coordinated, single-file formation through downtown Zeeland while dressed in black and carrying voter-suppression public-awareness signs.

The march is accompanied only by the steady heartbeat drum.

Participants walk slowly and silently, directly in line with the person in front of them, emulating a funeral procession representing the death of our democracy.

We do not acknowledge passersby.

We look straight ahead.

We remain expressionless.

Our Safety Team will lead and flank participants, ensure safe street crossings, and help protect the formation.

At designated points throughout the march, the procession will stop, turn toward storefronts, restaurants, and the public, and raise our signs in silent witness before continuing forward.

No chanting.

No screaming.

No chaos.

Just silent, disciplined civic resistance.

This powerful visual style of protest has drawn attention throughout Michigan and across the United States. Other organizations have contacted Good Trouble Indivisible for help replicating these marches in their own communities.

Together, we are creating a Civic Resistance Ecosystem and building public awareness through our unique model of silent, disciplined protest.


WHAT TO WEAR:

Participants dress in black clothing.

Comfortable walking shoes are strongly recommended.


HOW TO PREPARE:

WE provide the signs.

YOU dress in black.

WE provide bottled water and protein snacks.


IMPORTANT NOTES:

• This is a silent march.

• Signs will be provided.

• Participants must attend lineup and instructions.

• Please remain respectful of pedestrians, motorists, local businesses, and members of the community.

• Water and protein snacks will be provided.

• Comfortable walking shoes are recommended.

• This is a structured performance action with a limited number of signs and positions.

• Registration is required.

If the group has the time, energy, and interest following the Voter Suppression March, an additional silent march CONSTITUTIONAL VIOLATIONS, may be held. The Voter Suppression March is the only scheduled and required march. If there is group interest in a second march it will be optional, not required. 

Together, we remain visible, peaceful, disciplined, and impossible to ignore.

We the People means ALL OF US.

WATCH OUR VOTER SUPPRESSION MARCHES

See examples of our voter-suppression signs and silent-march choreography here:

👉 https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61576925081008

ABOUT GOOD TROUBLE INDIVISIBLE

Good Trouble Indivisible is a Saugatuck and Douglas–based Michigan nonprofit grassroots advocacy organization committed to nonviolent action, democratic accountability, and the defense of human rights.

GTI has organized more than 200 public actions across West Michigan.

We show up — week after week — to defend democracy, voting rights, constitutional government, human rights, and the right to peaceful protest.

VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITY

Want to help organize actions like this?

Many volunteer roles can be performed from home.

Call or text Jan Cohen at (269) 932-8806 or email:

📧 Action@GoodTroubleIndivisible.org


CONTACT US:

☎️ Good Trouble Indivisible: (616) 287-2221

☎️ Jan Cohen: (269) 932-8806

📧 Action@GoodTroubleIndivisible.org

🌐 https://goodtroubleindivisible.org

OUR COMMITMENT TO NONVIOLENCE

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action that is community-led and grounded in moral witness, public accountability, and collective care.

We expect all participants to act lawfully, seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation, and avoid engaging with individuals who disagree with our values or attempt to disrupt the event.

Weapons of any kind, including weapons legally permitted to be carried, should not be brought to this event.

⚠️ Limited positions are available.

Registration is required because this is a structured performance action with a limited number of signs.

Call or text Jan Cohen with questions at (269) 932-8806.

events.title: Civic Watch: Anderson County Commission
events.description:
The Anderson County Commission is where many of the county’s biggest public decisions are made — budgets, appointments, policy decisions, spending priorities, and issues that shape daily life across Anderson County.

These meetings are public, and Civic Watch is a simple invitation to show up, observe, and stay informed.

County Commission typically meets on the third Monday of each month, with presentations beginning at 6:00 PM and the regular meeting starting at 6:30 PM. Public comment is held at the beginning of the regular meeting.

This is not a rally or organized action event. It’s civic participation through public observation.

What to expect:
• Presentations beginning at 6:00 PM
• Regular Commission meeting at 6:30 PM
• Optional public comment at the beginning of the meeting
• Observe discussion, votes, and public business
• Take notes if you'd like
• Learn how county government works in real time

Official County Commission agendas:
https://andersoncountytn.gov/county-commission-meeting-agendas/

Can’t attend in person? Watch live:
https://www.andersoncounty.tv/live

Past meetings are archived at:
https://www.andersoncounty.tv/

If you'd like to attend with others, we’ll gather a few minutes beforehand and sit together.

Open to anyone interested in transparency, local government, and civic engagement.

events.title: Knock on doors with SouthSide Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join other SouthSide volunteers (and friends) for a canvass with Ground Truth—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. Swing Left launched this [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how Democrats connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on more doors in a targeted precinct on the Southside of Columbus, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking more doors, not just the ones campaigns usually do, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Montrose Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome. 
* Bathrooms are accessible at the Coffee Bean close by. 
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Knock doors with Iris Bender for NC House
events.description:
Join us as we head out into the neighborhood to speak with voters about the November election.

No experience necessary, and training is provided! After you've signed up to canvass, register for an online training on canvassing with MiniVAN. Click [here to sign up](https://www.mobilize.us/ncdems/event/766304/?utm_source=rsvpemail) or [here to watch a recorded training](https://youtu.be/C4mAUovRFgs).

If you have never canvassed before, we try to pair you with someone who has experience, but you can also just bring a friend if you prefer. You will need a smartphone for the MiniVAN app which incorporates GPS to help find homes, shows your script, and lets you record responses so we have them in our database. While canvassing, you will have individual doorhanger bags of candidate information to leave with voters or at their doors, a handful of voter registration forms, and contact information on our area's current representatives. 

Most of our lists will require you to drive. Some canvassing lists will be clustered fairly close together while others may require driving from house to house.

Canvassing is statistically the single best way to turn an Unaffiliated voter into a voter for Democratic candidates, so we hope you join us.

events.description:
NUESTRA VOZ CUENTA

Trae a un Amigo: Conoce tu Boleta
Viernes, 9 de octubre | 6:00–8:00 p. m.
Oficina de los Demócratas del Condado de Brown

¿Sabes exactamente qué aparecerá en tu boleta este noviembre? ¡Ven y descúbrelo con nosotros!

Nuestra reunión de octubre de Nuestra Voz Cuenta será una noche informal y práctica para aprender sobre tu boleta, hacer preguntas y prepararte para votar con confianza. Trae a un amigo, vecino o familiar.

Durante la noche podrás:

Encontrar tu boleta: Busca tu boleta específica según tu dirección.

Saber quién te representa: Mira mapas de los distritos del Congreso, Senado estatal, Asamblea, Junta del Condado, municipios y distritos escolares.

Conocer a los candidatos: Tendremos varios candidatos presentes para conocerlos y aprender sobre los cargos que aparecerán en la boleta.

Entender los referéndums y preguntas electorales: Veremos el lenguaje de las preguntas y explicaremos claramente qué significa votar SÍ o NO.

Aprender sobre el referéndum de las Escuelas Públicas de Green Bay.

Prepararte para votar: Averigua dónde votar, cómo votar temprano, cómo devolver una boleta de voto ausente y qué necesitas saber para el Día de las Elecciones.

No necesitas ser experto en política. Esta noche está diseñada para cualquier persona que simplemente quiera entender mejor su boleta antes de votar.

Ven con tus preguntas. Trae a un amigo. Sal preparado para votar.

events.title: Let our VOICES be heard -- our FREE SPEECH is being denied!
events.description:
*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

**Eastlake Village Marketplace, located on Otay Lakes Rd.**  

BACKSTORY:  After being at the corner in front of Islands on Otay Lakes Rd. for over 16 months, our group has been told by the Sudberry Management team that "they" own the sidewalk and they no longer want us there!  
 
We had double the amount of protesters at the first ones, we reminded them that we are peaceful and that we will not be leaving until 11 so they will have to call the police  The police arrived and waited in the lot until afterward to show the coordinator a map that included the sidewalks (as in:  Sudberry owns it!!).  He also advised that since that is NOT the norm, she should look into it.   (I call non-emergency before each and every protest-they all know me).  

Thank you to all our detectives for doing all the legwork and the legal work ... turns out they were wrong ... the city owns the space!

We showed up in greater numbers, and basically the cops never showed up for them ... same the following weekend - I chatted with the property manager afterward and she switched her story up a little bit ... said, that we are blocking the ADA ramp and that they could be sued!  

After our "detectives" once again did the research.  Turns out their existing ramp isn't quite up to standards, but it isn't worth it to make a fuss -- on either of our ends. 

SO, that all being said -- we are still wanting greater numbers at this corner to show them that this community doesn't take kindly to having our First Amendment Right to peaceful protest being blatantly violated!

So here is the updated plan - based on the last few weeks:

**DO NOT PARK IN THE MARKETPLACE PARKING LOT!  Unless you have a handicapped placard!** 

Do NOT buy one thing from any of their shops or restaurants.

Instead, we park by Kohl's and meet right at that corner on Eastlake Blvd.  Cross the street and just march to Island's on the "forbidden" sidewalk, march across the street to McD's and cross over to the Arby's and we can go back the same way and do it all over again.  

We do not step on the grass, we don't leave anything personal on the ground, we pick up after ourselves ... We keep it cleaner than we found it. 

**MOST IMPORTANTLY:  STAY CLEAR OF THEIR RAMP!   We refuse to let them intimidate us, so don't give them even 1 reason.  We move out of the way of ANY passersby!  Don't even wait for them to have to say "excuse me" ... just make plenty of room for them ... we smile and we are friendly (they might want to join us!) ... ESPECIALLY if a walker or a wheelchair or even just a bike needs to pass!

Signs to consider - anything First Amendment/Free Speech themed ... maybe even call out Sudberry for trying to stifle us!  

 We want the community to stay away from places that don't honor our basic first amendment right to free speech!  

**Remember that driving by and beeping counts as RESISTANCE!  I can't say it enough, it's invaluable!  I know gas prices suck, but if you are nearby, drive by a few times and make a TON of noise!**

Also, this is for those of you who can't be physically on the streets, but you still want to RESIST from the comfort of your own home:

How about calling one or more of the restaurants in the Food Court that sees and hears our protests weekly ... to remind them that we refuse to do business when our voices are being silenced!   Here is the link for the names and the phone numbers:

https://shopeastlakemarketplace.com/

I ask to speak to the lead manager .. we are polite, but right to the point ... *we used to support your business, but no longer* is your message and then tell them whatever your reason is that your money will no longer be spent ... Remember that lots of them are on OUR side (I know Luna Grill is with us, for instance ... I also know that Great Clips is NOT -the owner harassed us over a year ago and was a real live one! -- feel free to call Great Clips repeatedly .................).  You don't need to give them your name, just tell them you are a customer and you are disappointed in their stance on free speech.  

The second part of this, is that if you can actually boycott as many of these places as possible, I guarantee the message will be heard!

See you Sunday -- tell your friends!  Make this the protest you come out and support for the next few weeks until they stop harassing us.

More information to consider:

*1 sign or whatever you can carry
*plan on walking back and forth, so be comfortable
*leave valuables in your car (license and cc or a few bucks if you want)
*wear sunscreen AND your hat
*clean up after your fur babies
*don't forget your water bottles

See you on the streets!
Janine
events.accessibility_notes: just be ready to walk ... we need to keep this protest moving because we don't want to give them even one reason to harass us!  Be comfortable!  Protect from the sun!

events.title: Call voters in Arizona CD 01 with Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth Phone Bank designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters over the phone.  (https://ourgroundtruth.org)

At this phone bank, we’ll:

- Call all types of voters -- not just those who vote like us.

- Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. 

You can join and call from just your computer/tablet, but we recommend being prepared with a phone and earbuds as well!

––

About the program:
This isn’t traditional phone banking—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- Why we’re starting early: launching a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns are even off the ground.

- How we’ll go big: calling every voter, not just the ones we normally rely on, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

*Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.*
