events.title: 2nd Annual RISE UP AGAINST Domestic Violence March: Seattle
events.description:
Volunteer with RISE UP AGAINST Domestic Violence

RISE UP AGAINST Domestic Violence is a community-led movement dedicated to raising awareness, increasing access to resources, advocating for legislative change, and creating spaces for healing, connection, and hope. This march brings together survivors, victims, advocates, family members, allies, and community supporters who have been impacted—directly or indirectly—by domestic, family, intimate partner, and interpersonal violence.

We are seeking volunteers to help both before and during the event. Opportunities include:

Posting and distributing flyers
Printing or donating copy services
Community outreach and resource gathering
Collecting water, snacks, and supplies for participants
Event setup and breakdown
Safety Team volunteers
First Aid and Emergency Response volunteers
Resource and information table support
Participant check-in and wayfinding assistance
General event support

This event is more than a march—it is a gathering rooted in community, healing, education, remembrance, empowerment, and collective action. Together, we honor survivors, support those currently navigating abuse, remember those we have lost, advocate for meaningful change, and celebrate the courage, resilience, and liberation that are possible on the healing journey.

Whether you can volunteer for an hour, a day, donate supplies, share resources, or help spread the word, your support helps create a safer, stronger, and more connected community.

Join us as we RISE UP, speak out, and stand together against domestic violence. 💜

Date: October 25, 2025
Location: Seattle, Washington

Everyone is welcome. Survivors, advocates, service providers, community organizations, family members, friends, and allies are encouraged to participate.

events.title: Protect the Vote: Inside Poll Observer Training
events.description:
### This is the _Live on Zoom_ training, you can find the _On-Demand_ training here: https://mobilize.us/s/oQ3mL0

# Protect the Vote as a Poll Observer

Every voter deserves the chance to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Inside Poll observers help ensure election laws are followed, identify potential issues, and report concerns so they can be addressed quickly. Most shifts are calm and routine, and you will never be expected to handle situations on your own. We'll provide the training, resources, and support you need to be successful.

### What You'll Learn

- Poll observer basics
- What to expect at the polling place
- Updated guidance for situations observers may encounter this fall
- What to look for and how to document issues
- How to report concerns and get support
- The role poll observers play in protecting voters

### Why It Matters

With critical elections ahead, we need trained volunteers in every corner of North Carolina.

Poll observers serve as our eyes and ears inside polling places, helping ensure election laws are followed and that voters can cast their ballots without unnecessary barriers.

Whether you've done this work before or are brand new, we'll help you get ready.

#### No Prior Experience Required

We'll provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel confident serving as a poll observer.



#### Important: This session is for NCDP Inside Poll Observers. 
If you are an **attorney, law graduate, or law student** looking to serve as an **At-Large Legal Poll Observer through the NC Voter Protection Alliance (NCVPA),** please sign up here: https://tinyurl.com/NC26LegalPollObserver

events.title: VOTEFEST 3.0 - MARCH TO THE POLLS
events.description:
2:00–3:30 PM — VOTEFEST IN THE PARK
3:30 PM — MARCH TO THE POLLS

October 24 is a big day: it’s the last day to register to vote and the first day of early voting. So we’re turning MacDonald Park into a celebration of participation — with music, signs, art, food, voter information, and HeadCount on site registering voters right up to the deadline.

At 3:30, we’ll pick up our VOTEFEST signs, carry them at the front, and take the energy of the park into the streets as we head to the polls together. Marching together to vote draws on a powerful American tradition, rooted in Black churches and communities in the South, where voting became more than an individual act — it became something communities did together, visibly and joyfully.

Before the march, VOTEFEST will fill the park with the Curtis Watts Trio, Great Neck Singing Resistance, the League of Women Voters, HeadCount, hands-on art projects, voter information, civic action, empanadas, and plenty of reasons to stay awhile.

Register. Sing. Make art. Get informed. Then at 3:30, we take it to the streets — and to the polls.

events.description:
Ready to make a real impact for Senator Judy Seeberger and Senate District 41? 

We are hitting the pavement to have the critical face-to-face conversations that win close elections. Door knocking is one of the most effective tools we have to turn out voters, persuade undecided neighbors, and make sure people know what Judy Seeberger has done for our communities. Judy knows exactly how much every vote matters. In 2022, she won this seat by just 321 votes. Those 321 votes were the difference between winning and losing, and they helped secure the DFL’s narrow one-seat majority in the Minnesota Senate. 

Today, the DFL still holds the Senate by just one seat, while the Minnesota House is evenly split. That means Senate District 41 is not just another race; it could help determine the balance of power at the Capitol. That is why this shift matters. Research and campaign experience have shown that strong direct voter contact can move turnout by up to 5 points, and in a district decided by only a few hundred votes, that impact can be the difference between victory and defeat. 

Every door we knock on brings us one step closer to re-electing Judy and protecting the progress we have made on clean water, public safety, consumer protection, strong schools, veterans, broadband, and support for working families. Judy brings the experience of a firefighter, paramedic, attorney, and state senator and voters deserve to hear directly why her leadership matters for Senate District 41. 

Whether you are a seasoned canvassing pro or this is your very first time, we will make sure you are fully prepared. We will start with a comprehensive training, go over our talking points, answer questions, and set you up with a partner if you would like. Campaigns are won by people talking to people. In a race this close, every conversation matters. Join us, knock a few doors, and help us build the voter engagement we need to deliver a strong win for Judy Seeberger in November.

Event Details
What to Bring: Please wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a fully charged cell phone. We will be using a mobile app to track our progress!

What We Provide: Training, literature, snacks, and plenty of team spirit.

Your voice is the most powerful tool we have. Let's get out there, meet our neighbors, and share our vision for the future!

events.title: OCCUPY MAIN STREET
events.description:
We’re sick and tired of violence perpetrators and sexual predators not being held accountable - from Donald Trump and the Jeffrey Epstein scandal to your neighborhood pedophile down at the corner store who has custody of his child rape victim. “Occupy Main Street” gives a platform for neighborhood communities to protest against injustices that disenfranchise children and victims of sexual assault, domestic violence and child abuse in all its forms.

Five children die every day from child abuse. Family Court and Social Services remove children from innocent protective mothers. There is an irrecoverably grievous failure of our own government to protect innocent children. The United States of America is the only industrialized nation in the world not to have ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Public Officials are too busy making money off of abusing and exploiting children to consider the effects of their depraved actions on future generations.

More than 58,000 children per year are ordered to live with their abusers by family courts nationwide. It’s the most colossal and catastrophic obliteration of human rights ever perpetrated en masse to the general public. It is the biggest public corruption scheme ever devised - bigger than the holocaust - and the media won’t touch it. The revolution will not be televised, folks. It’s treason. It’s discrimination, and it’s time now for the world’s most monumental public conspiracy to come to an end for good.

Laws shouldn’t defy Mother Nature.

Women and children rarely ever make false reports of abuse. It’s estimated that 2% of reports of abuse are false. However, Family Court, Social Services and Law Enforcement mistreat victims making reports as though they’re false the vast majority of the time. There is an inherent societal bias against victims. 99% of sexual abuse crimes are committed by men. However, when abuse by a father is alleged in family court, protective mothers lose custody at extremely high rates. The police convict sexual predators only 2% of the time. It’s systemic abuse of women and children. Abuse of the mother also counts as abuse of the child. However, the "public authorities" don’t follow the authorities on the science.

Too often, public authorities fail the most vulnerable among us, and victims require support from their community to create an outcry before their voice can be heard. We must not tolerate the most vulnerable people in our communities being continually victimized any longer. We are protective mothers of victimized children and concerned citizens alike. We are empowered to support the abused, the silenced, the oppressed, the trafficked, the exploited, the kidnapped and the enslaved. We should take to the streets to stand up to the injustices being perpetrated against children and victims by individuals and by the authorities who fail to hold abusers accountable - the “authorities” who criminalize the victims rather than the perpetrators.

These vulnerable people need our support and that’s exactly what we’re here to do. Gather together outside the homes of predators where children are being unlawfully detained under color of law. Create a buzz and make waves in the name of children’s rights and justice for victims in all respects. Take to the streets and protest at strategic locations to let abusers know we are there to hold them accountable and God is watching. Create your local neighborhood watchdog chapter and give a voice to the voiceless! Support non-violent resistance to judicial orders giving child custody or unfettered contact to abusers. Empower peaceful civil disobedience to send the message to authorities to let them know that we don’t stand for discrimination against victims and we don’t support unconstitutional acts that perpetuate domestic abuse for their own personal financial gain at the expense of our children as they are the entire future generation. We aren’t afraid to stand up in the name of children’s rights and justice for victims. Join together - there is strength in numbers!

I have personally experienced firsthand discrimination against women in the system. The doctrines used to keep abusive fathers in children's lives are a double standard, as the opposite applies to protective mothers. I was accused of alienating him, while the courts, police, and CPS assisted in him alienating - and all out estranging -  me from my child. The mental illness of the perpetrating parent was ignored, while my psychiatric injury from the trauma he and the system conspired to cause was used against me. The father was determined to be unfit by a forensic mental health evaluation in 2015. I was never found unfit. The forensic mental health evaluation recommended that I have sole custody. However, in spite of his unfitness, another family court judge ordered him sole custody in 2108.

After I reported to the authorities that the paternal parent was abusing my daughter, I was told that if I violated the order granting the abuser visitation and didn’t send my daughter to unsupervised visits with her perpetrator, I would lose custody. However, when he violated custodial orders, the police refused to intervene, the judge refused to switch custody back to me and instead he discredited my proof, and I was permanently erased from my daughter’s childhood while the perpetrating parent faced no consequences. 

I initially filed in family court in December 2013. I was awarded full and sole custody throughout the first two litigations. The police never held him accountable. While I had full custody, I was told by Ulster County Crime Victims Assistance Program that, despite the ongoing evidence of continuous abuse against my daugher, if I didn't send her kicking and screaming to the court-ordered unsupervised visits with her father that they would order full custody to him. On August 20th, 2015, custody of my four-and-a-half-year-old daughter was illegally seized without due process in family court, and for two and a half years, I was denied contact with her, bookended by supervised visitation. The perpetrating parent was ordered unsupervised visitation even though the recent forensic mental health evaluation advised against it. I’ve been fighting for my right to protect my daughter ever since.

At first she was unlawfully detained away from me into custody of grandparents with no due process, in violation of laws and in violation of our rights, despite the fact that there were no extraordinary circumstances and I was never found to be an unfit mother. CPS never substantiated the abuse I reported against my daughter's father, after she disclosed to me, as well as professionals, myriad ways in which he abused her. Nevertheless, family court fraudulently orchestrated the removal of my daughter from my custody on the false premise that if she wasn't immediately illegally detained into grandparent custody, that she was going into foster care, despite the fact that, unbeknownst to us at the time, CPS didn't substantiate the abuse and, in fact, furnished an unfounded COI report to family court the same day my daughter was kidnapped under color of law. At the end of the two and a half year period where my four-and-a-half year old daughter was denied her mother, the Grandparents' attorney finally admitted for the record that there were no requisite extraordinary circumstances that warranted the placement of the child into grandparent custody, and sole custody was ordered to the abusive father, regardless the fact that I was never found unfit.

Despite the fact that I regained occasional contact with my daughter at that time, I was still unable to protect her from the ongoing abuse by her father.

Very clear bias is present as a pattern of practice against protective mothers in family court. I was told by family court professionals that I will never get custody back from the father because a parent must be found unfit in order to have custody removed. Yet, I was never found unfit when they removed custody from me.

The father violates the order with impunity to deny me all contact with my child for years. He was never arrested or held accountable for violating orders. The police told me they could not pursue criminal charges against him because they were cross-jurisdictionally instructed by the corrupt family court judge not to get involved. However, in 2016 when I attempted to protect my daughter in violation of the void order detaining her into abuse, I was arrested, jailed and fined for simply briefly coming into contact with her. I was arrested 3 times and ordered to pay $2,000, and subsequently $5,000 in bail, which is excessive considering that when the father was arrested in 2012 for his acts of violence against me in violation of a restraining order, prior to entering family court, his bail was only set at $1,000 - in the same county.

This is systemic corruption, collusion, retaliation and discrimination, and it is against the law.

The police, CPS and Family Court and affiliates all conspired to cover up the child abuse. They retaliated against me for speaking up about the abuse and and criminalized me for trying to protect my daughter, while the perp walks free, and continues to endanger the child and alienate me from her to this very day more than a decade later.

The perpetrating parent, his attorney, the corrupt Attorney For The Child and the judge have colluded to deny me all contact with my daughter, after I attempted to protect her from continued abuse. The father continuously violates the court order with impunity, frequently denying me what little contact I was entitled to under the order, and the judge refused to admit the evidence.  The authorities won’t do anything to step in. He is abusing my daughter and violating the order to deny me all contact. She is a victim of coercive control, and is being forced, under threats to her wellbeing, to say she wants no contact with me, against her will. She is being lied to about the conditions of the order. The police refuse to criminally charge him, and the family court judge refuses to acknowledge on the court record that the father is maliciously fracturing my daughter’s attachment to me and depriving my daughter of her mother. As a result, I haven't had any visitation with my daughter in over a year - since Mother's Day of 2025,

Furthermore, I am ordered to pay child support beyond my means to our abuser.

My daughter is now fifteen and I have been unable to be there to protect her and guide her into her womanhood. Both my daughter and I suffer severe devastating effects from the traumas of court-ordered separation and inescapable abuse. My daughter suffers from Dissociative Identity Disorder, and I have C-PTSD.

I'm raising awareness about the human rights violations committed against me and my case, and I am determined to find solutions to better society and future generations. I invite you to stand with me to help advocate for the protection of victims and the prioritization of children’s wellbeing, as well as for accountability for perpetrators and the systems that enable them. Your support can help bring change and hope to families like mine.

If you’re able to donate, the funds raised will help me cover legal fees, secure stable housing, meet daily living expenses, and continue my advocacy efforts to protect my children and others facing similar challenges. Because of domestic violence, public corruption and systemic failures, I have been made homeless. Every day is a crisis. events.title: Compost Hub Support: Augustus Hawkins
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This location has bathrooms available
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER 
Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT
All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Constitutional Observer Training
events.description:
## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

events.title: Book Group: "One Day Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This" by Omar El Akkad
events.description:
Join us as we discuss "One Day Everyone Will Have Always been Against This" by Omar El Akkad.

Description from the publisher's website: 
NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER • NATIONAL BOOK AWARD WINNER • From award-winning novelist and journalist Omar El Akkad comes a powerful reckoning with what it means to live in a West that betrays its fundamental values.

“[A] bracing memoir and manifesto.” —The New York Times

“I can’t think of a more important piece of writing to read right now. I found hope here, and help, to face what the world is now, all that it isn’t anymore. Please read this. I promise you won’t regret it.” —Tommy Orange, bestselling author of Wandering Stars and There There

A NEW YORK TIMES NOTABLE BOOK • PALESTINE BOOK AWARD WINNER • FINALIST FOR THE NATIONAL BOOK CRITICS CIRCLE AWARD FOR CRITICISM

On October 25, 2023, after just three weeks of the bombardment of Gaza, Omar El Akkad put out a tweet: “One day, when it’s safe, when there’s no personal downside to calling a thing what it is, when it’s too late to hold anyone accountable, everyone will have always been against this.” This tweet has been viewed more than 10 million times.

As an immigrant who came to the West, El Akkad believed that it promised freedom. A place of justice for all. But in the past twenty years, reporting on the War on Terror, Ferguson, climate change, Black Lives Matter protests, and more, and watching the unmitigated slaughter in Gaza, El Akkad has come to the conclusion that much of what the West promises is a lie. That there will always be entire groups of human beings it has never intended to treat as fully human—not just Arabs or Muslims or immigrants, but whoever falls outside the boundaries of privilege. One Day, Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This is a chronicle of that painful realization, a moral grappling with what it means, as a citizen of the U.S., as a father, to carve out some sense of possibility in a time of carnage.

This is El Akkad’s nonfiction debut, his most raw and vulnerable work to date, a heartsick breakup letter with the West. It is a brilliant articulation of the same breakup we are watching all over the United States, in family rooms, on college campuses, on city streets; the consequences of this rupture are just beginning. This book is for all the people who want something better than what the West has served up. This is the book for our time

We will be doing general garden maintenance including planting, picking up trash, mulching, composting, pruning, watering plants, weeding, and harvesting.

### 🤝 What is a Service Saturday?
Service Saturdays are an opportunity to build community amongst our members and neighborhoods while giving back to our city! Community building is a key step toward creating *lasting social change*.

### 🌱 What is AgLanta?
[AgLanta](https://aglanta.atlantaga.gov/) is a City of Atlanta initiative with a vision for 100% of Atlanta residents to live within half a mile of affordable fresh food. The Aglanta [Grows-A-Lot](https://aglanta.atlantaga.gov/aglanta-grows-a-lot) program encourages entrepreneurs, non-profits, and residents to apply for a 5-year renewable license to adopt a vacant, city-owned property to start a new urban garden or urban farm in Atlanta. The program was launched to ensure that 75% of Atlanta residents are within a half-mile of healthy food by 2020 and develop a resilient food system by 2025.

Court starts: around 9:00 AM
Court ends: between 10:30 and 11:00 AM

Why this matters:
ICE has stepped up enforcement in Robertson County. Families are being separated. Neighbors who have lived here for years are being pulled into deportation proceedings. Our presence at the courthouse, peaceful, visible, and consistent, does three things:

  * It tells the individuals walking in that they are seen and supported.
  * It tells their families that this community has their back.
  * It reminds local officials that Robertson County is watching.

You do not need to stay the whole time. Even 20 minutes of presence in the morning matters. Bring water, comfortable shoes, and a sign if you have one. If you do not have a sign, come anyway. We often have extra signs. New folks are always welcome and you will find a community of people who care.

events.title: Protest ICE Deportations & the AROCC Detention Center at Mesa Gateway Airport
events.description:
## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

When local lawmakers recently conducted a surprise visit to the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center here at Mesa Gateway, they were sickened by what they found. Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

#### 📢 Join us on Saturday, October 24th to challenge the illegal, inhumane, and unconstitutional ICE removal operations!

    
--------------------------------------

## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- We have compiled public records, congressional oversight letters, and local reporting into one place. 
- Please read our complete [Mesa Valley Indivisible AROCC and ICE Air Deportations Fact Sheet](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/ice-deportationsarocc) to understand the full scope of our key concerns and see how you can take action.

--------------------------------------
## 🚨 Important! 🚨

- To ensure you receive all necessary information for the upcoming event, please make sure you have officially registered via Mobilize.
- All vital updates—including parking instructions, logistical changes, and additional details—will be sent to the email address provided during registration. 
  - If you have not registered on the platform, we will be unable to send you these updates.
  - Keep an eye out for emails from Mesa Valley Indivisible and check your spam/junk folder if you do not see them!
  - [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) prioritizes strategic visibility to ensure our message reaches the widest possible audience. To keep our movement growing, we protest at high-traffic areas where Mesa residents are most likely to see us and join the cause.

--------------------------------------------

##  ✨Protest Information:

- MVI's goal is to always to pack all 4 corners of the intersection. Please look for the empty spots and fill them!
- Make sure to stand side by side and not behind one another so every driver & the media can see how many attendees are present!
- Please share with friends, family, neighbors, EVERYONE!

--------------------------------------------

## 🪧 Sign Ideas:

Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to ICE deportations & the AROCC! Some ideas include:

- Abolish ICE
- ICE separates families
- AROCC is a humanitarian crisis
- Prison without due process is a concentration camp
- Illegal deportations without due process is human trafficking

--------------------------------------------

## 📷 Pictures & Videos
- Make sure to always tag **Mesa Valley Indivisible** on our group [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1CFYV1DSaT/), [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/mesavalleyindivisible/), [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc), [BlueSky](https://bsky.app/profile/mesavalleyindivisi.bsky.social), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc)
- Please always include #MesaValleyIndivisible #AbolishICE #CloseAROCC #RecuseBiggs #ReleaseEpsteinFiles

events.title: Political Fundraising: Legal or a Scam?
events.description:
**Your donations could be going to a grifter, not a campaign or candidate.** 

Ever wonder why you’re getting so many political fundraising emails and texts? Have you wondered if they are legit or just a scam? 

ScamBusters is proud to offer a free (virtual) class to educate you:

- about good and bad political action committees (PACs), 

- why and how you're targeted

- how to identify potential fraudulent PACs, and 

- where you can be assured your hard earned money goes to the causes you care about, instead of grifters. 

This informative presentation ends with some instructions on how to 'throttle the noise', reduce unwanted spammy texts and emails.

These training and helpline sessions will orient new volunteers and address any questions that arise for volunteers already trained and engaged in phone banking. 

ACLU of Indiana text banks are conducted remotely. No prior experience is necessary. You only need a phone, computer, and internet access to participate from the comfort of your home. You will use provided scripts and suggested responses to help voters register, inform them of what’s on their ballot or encourage them to turn out to the polls. 

Once trained, volunteers may text on their own schedule, while the text bank link is active, (and so long as calls are made within the hours of 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time of person being called).

We the People are stronger together. 
Join us to text bank! Action is the antidote to anxiety.

## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

events.title: Defend Democracy
events.description:
Stand up and join our peaceful protest to Defend Democracy and Celebrate 250 Years of No Kings in America!

Time to get active! Join us in exercising your First Amendment rights as our Founding Fathers intended! You will feel empowered and part of a community of guardians of democracy at our weekly events.

Daily we are witnessing an unprecedented dismantling of our democratic system. This president and his posse have created a world of chaos. We are experiencing attacks on our freedom of speech, civil rights, and right to vote. We are losing access to health care and social programs, and the future of our Social Security is in jeopardy.

We are being exposed to immense corruption in which the ultra-wealthy continue to increase their wealth and power while the workers suffer the consequences with higher costs and lower wages.

We have been entered into a WAR that has no end in sight, that was not needed nor wanted by anyone except this power-hungry administration.

Our immigrant neighbors, as well as U.S. citizens, continue to be victimized by inhumane and illegal actions of ICE.

And we must not forget or be silent about the contents of the Epstein Files. Let us remind the world that we demand justice for the survivors!

If any of these issues resonate with you, then come join our protest!

Let’s stop the insanity and corruption together!

We the People Have the Power to Defend Democracy!



### What to Bring

- A BIG sign that shows how you really feel and can be read from across the street
- A water bottle
- A friend
- A lawn chair (optional)

### What to Wear

- Hat
- Sunscreen

### Type of Protest

This is a standing protest, not a march. Please feel free to bring a lawn chair if you need to.

### About the Protest

We are a family-friendly, strictly nonviolent peaceful protest. We oppose violence, vandalism and destruction of property. This protest is a lawful exercise of our First Amendment right to peaceful assembly.

*Hosted by Sunnyvale Tesla Takedown*

events.title: Deep Canvass for Democracy Phonebank
events.description:
Times are hard, and people are tuning out of politics in big numbers. But if people give up on our democracy, our communities will pay the price. That's why People's Action Institute's Deep Canvass for Democracy program is helping people rediscover their self-interest in political life. Democracy depends on ordinary people talking with one another about the issues that shape our lives. Yet many of us have never learned how to have conversations in a way that builds trust and understanding and leads to action.

At a time when so many people feel disconnection, distrust, and uncertainty, our ability to engage across differences isn’t just a skill - It's how we save our democratic norms.

Deep Canvassing is a tool that has proved we can build across differences and win the things we need in our lives. It uses curiosity and storytelling to give people a new perspective and energy to fight for change.

Whether you want to deepen connection as a community leader, neighbor, or within your own family, join us to learn how to Deep Canvass.

### National Hear America Canvass Day
On Saturday, October 10th, 11 member groups across 8 states will hold a day of action to go out, listen to voters' concerns, and contribute to our 300,000 conversation goal. So far, we are at 100,000 conversations and hope to make a huge dent in our goal today.
Launch starts at 12-1 Eastern, and the in-person canvass team returns at 4:30 pm Eastern to debrief our conversations from the day.

In this Deep Canvass training and phonebank, you'll learn about compassionate curiosity, storytelling, and dialer hours, and talk to real people to practice your skill set. No experience is needed.

events.title: How does your vote impact food insecurity in your community?
events.description:
ITAG is proud to partner with Seed Theatre to present our second Good Trouble Lives On event, centered on one powerful call to action: Vote.

Marginalized communities are disproportionately affected by food insecurity. But did you know that your vote can directly influence funding, policies, and support systems that help address these inequities?

This engaging panel will feature individuals who will share their lived experiences with food insecurity, as well as insights from their work serving impacted communities. 

Panelists will also discuss how key elected offices at the local and regional levels can shape policies and funding that affect access to food and other essential resources.

Speakers will provide an overview of food insecurity in our region, including current data, available community resources, and the most pressing needs facing local communities.

Join us for an important conversation about the connection between civic engagement and food justice—and discover how your vote can help create meaningful change.

Disclaimer: 

This event is non-partisan and does not support nor endorse any particular candidate or ballot measure.

A core principle behind all Good Trouble Lives On events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. 

Photography & Media Consent Notice: 

By attending this event, you acknowledge and agree that you may be photographed, filmed, or otherwise recorded. These images and recordings may be used by Indivisible TAG and Seed Theatre for promotional and marketing purposes, including publication on websites, social media, and other digital or print materials.

Your attendance constitutes your consent to such photography and media use, unless you notify the event organizer in writing prior to or at the time of entry.

events.title: 10/29 - Voter Mobilization @ SMU Campus with Beto

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join us and special guest **Beto O'Rourke** for the **Every Campus Counts** tour at **SMU**! We are showing up to talk to students, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with existing and potential student voters
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone

### Shift Schedule & Flow (Subject to change)

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, we ask all volunteers to arrive **60 minutes before Beto arrives** for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[12:00-1:00pm]: Setup & Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals before the crowd gathers.

- **[12:30pm-3:00pm]: Voter Engagement & Mobilization** | The main event! We hit the campus ground running and get folks set up on Reach (plus a special appearance by Beto!)

- **[3:00-4:00pm]: Beto Town Hall and Q&A

- **[4:00-5:00pm]: Walk to the Polls - some volunteers will walk with students to the polls for early voting.
Takedown & Post-Event Debrief** | We will pack up our gear, tally our total Reach adds, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: TBD

- **Volunteer Parking**: TBD

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes

_Note: Clipboards, pens, all other necessary materials will be provided at the check-in table, but feel free to bring your own backup supplies just in case!_

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single campus counts. Sign up for a shift today!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
# Knock Doors with Families Not Politics — Defend Colorado Kids and Families

This November, Colorado voters will decide two ballot measures that sound simple but aren't. Propositions 134 and 135 are being sold as measures about fairness and safety — but the fine print tells a different story, and voters deserve to know it before they vote.

Propositions 134 is so vague that it could subject *any* kid, in *any* sport, from kindergarten through college, to invasive verification just to prove they belong on the field. Propositions 135 hands medical decisions that belong to families and doctors over to politicians — and could block care for kids who aren't even transgender, including teens fighting cancer.

That's where you come in. Join Families Not Politics for a community canvass and help us have real conversations with Colorado voters about what these measures actually do. Our research is clear: when voters hear the full picture, they move — but it takes volunteers like you, at the doors, making the case.

No experience needed. We'll kick things off with training and a team briefing before heading out together, and you'll leave with everything you need to have a confident, meaningful conversation. Wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and come ready to talk with your neighbors.

Every conversation moves a voter. Every voter we move gets us closer to defeating these measures in November. We hope you'll join us.

events.title: Angie for Florida: Neighborhood Captain Orientation
events.description:
A Neighborhood Captain is a volunteer who takes ownership of a specific neighborhood or area and becomes the local point person for the campaign.

You can request an area ranging from approximately 50 to 1,000 doors.
Your turf is generally centered around your home, neighborhood, or a location you choose.You commit to making sure the doors in your area are reached.

You personally knock doors and connect with voters. You can bring along friends, family, or a few volunteers to help. You will continue to have support from the main campaign team with training, literature, voter lists, questions, and other resources.

Your mission is to take ownership of your neighborhood, connect with your neighbors, and make sure they know Angie Nixon and why this campaign matters.

events.title: Tucson Shutdown Committee, Sun., 9/13 and weekly thereafter
events.description:
Tucson Shutdown

Please join Shutdown Trump Committee meeting, by Zoom, weekly on Sundays. The Steering Committee meets from 7-730 pm each week, followed by the General Meeting, from 7:30-8:30 pm. All are welcome to observe the Steering Committee meeting, but only the Steering Committee members (active Working Committee heads and sponsoring organizational reps) participate and vote.  You will be given the zoom link after you sign up. This meeting is for anyone who wants to volunteer.

Trump has threatened to cancel the mid-term elections. This would be a crucial step in completing his authoritarian takeover. The only thing that has been shown to reliably stop such a takeover is large-scale, non-violent noncooperation. An historic coalition came together in St. Louis in late May to call for exactly such a shutdown–if he does try to cancel the election. MayDayStrong.org has 600 labor unions and community groups as members.  Seven representatives from Tucson organizations went to St. Louis, including Democracy Unites Us, Party for Socialism and Liberation, Tucson Democratic Socialists of American and the local African-heritage ministerial alliance. Nine cities representing 30% of the economy have already committed to disrupt their economies for two weeks in case he does try to cancel the elections, so called “Tier 1” cities. Some of us in Tucson seek to make us a “Tier 2” city, to support the national Shutdown by disrupting our local economy as much as possible, at or above the scale of January 30th, for as long as we can. 

Please join us as individuals or representing a group.

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
Hosted by Helping Mamas, Inc (www.helpingmamas.org)


What does it mean to be a mother in America today?

No Country for Mothers follows Reshma Saujani, activist and founder of Moms First, as she explores the realities of motherhood in the United States: from the challenges families face to the systems that shape the experience of raising a family.

Join Helping Mamas Inc. for a special screening of No Country for Mothers, followed by a community panel discussion examining the realities of motherhood today and what it takes to build stronger systems of support for mothers and families.

The evening will bring together community leaders, advocates, and voices from across Atlanta for an opportunity to watch, listen, and continue the conversation about what families need to thrive.

Panel Speakers:

Moderator - Alia Lamborghini, SVP Global Revenue, Yahoo DSP

Molly Battin, SVP & Chief Marketing Officer - The Home Depot

Shannon Womack, Head of Brand & Creative - Delta 

Jennifer McKeenan - COO, Fanatics

Jamie Lackey, CEO, Helping Mamas

Jo Kirschner, Chairwoman, Primrose Schools

Every Monday at 4:30PM we stand up to tyranny at the corner of Murray and Beacon. Bring a sign, bring your shouting with joy voice and join us for an hour as we let passer by's know we are not pleased with the current state of our democracy. We're there for an hour (provided the temperature is not over 90 or under 40) and we'd love it if you stopped by.


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Get out the Vote with Dayenu and Center for Common Ground
events.description:
### Dayenu is a U.S.-based Jewish climate organization that advocates for bold climate action while also supporting voting rights and civic engagement as essential to building a more just and sustainable future. In this phone bank, they join forces with Center for Common Ground to reduce voting barriers and get out the vote for the 2026 midterm elections.

### We are calling Black voters in Georgia, encouraging them to vote in the upcoming midterm election and providing resources that make it easier to check where they are registered and find the voting information they need.

#### Make calls with us every Tuesday from 3 pm PT/6 pm ET to 5pm PT/ 8 pm PT. 

Beginning phone banker? We start each call with a training for anyone who needs it. You can also train yourself beforehand by checking out [our training slides](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGstUCSwjE/oWn7cjYLXJDiksQn6VbPww/view?utm_content=DAGstUCSwjE&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h1f8f5f4824).

Experienced? You can start making these calls immediately and pop back into the zoom with any questions along the way.

You can also make these calls on your own time 9am-8pm within the target state's time zone - no need to wait for an event!

For more information about this phone bank, please visit the [CFCG Phonebank Page](http://centerforcommonground.org/phonebanks)

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Athens - GA Senate!
events.description:
Join Indivisible Georgia District 10 and Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. Ground Truth is a new approach to voter contact that’s changing how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors (https://ourgroundtruth.org).

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

You’ll receive additional details, including the meeting location, after you sign-up. Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference. 

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ 7th Ave & Osborn in midtown Phoenix
events.description:
**Join us for our afternoon rally on 7th Ave & Osborne in midtown Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 The rally starts at 4:00. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 5:30 PM. Some attendees meet up afterward at Mi Patio ($4.99 margaritas!), others go to Lix Uptown Ice Cream ($4 scoops!). We’re a friendly bunch.

🅿️ There’s plenty of parking in the Safeway lot on the NE corner. We haven’t had issues before, but parking enforcement is unpredictable. If concerned, check with others.

🚦🚶‍➡️ We gather on all four corners of the intersection, with the primary meeting spot on the northeast corner of 7th Ave & Osborn.

🖌️ One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

😷 RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are common on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ 7th St & McDowell in Central Phoenix
events.description:
**Join us for our Tuesday morning rally on 7th St & McDowell in Central Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 The rally starts at 7:30. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 8:30 AM.

🅿️ There’s plenty of parking in the Safeway lot on the NW corner. We haven’t had issues before, but parking enforcement is unpredictable. If concerned, check with others.

🚦We gather on all four corners of the intersection, with the primary meeting spot on the northwest corner of 7th St & McDowell.

🖌️ One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

😷 RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are common on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.title: Arkansas Society of Freethinkers - Pint Nite / Humanist Happy Hour
events.description:
A casual, come-as-you-are gathering for freethinkers, skeptics, humanists, and anyone who enjoys good conversation over a drink or a meal. No agenda, no program — just an easy evening to meet people in your community who share a commitment to reason, compassion, and living ethically without reliance on the supernatural.
What to expect
Show up, grab a seat, and talk about whatever's on your mind — current events, books, life, the big questions and the small ones. Your host will be there to welcome you, introduce you around, and answer questions about the Arkansas Society of Freethinkers and the American Humanist Association if you have them.
First time? You're especially welcome.
A lot of people find Humanist Happy Hour an easier first step than a lecture or formal meeting. You don't need to identify as a humanist (or anything in particular) to come — just bring curiosity and an open mind.
About drinks
Alcohol is optional and never expected. The venue has non-alcoholic options and food, so come however you come.
Finding us
We meet on the third Monday of each month at 7 PM at the Flying Saucer in downtown Little Rock. Street parking is free but limited after 6 PM on President Clinton Ave. Additional street parking is free and usually available off President Clinton Ave, but may require walking a block or two. Paid lots and garages are also available in the area, including the library garage located in the same building as the Flying Saucer.
Hope to see you there.

events.title: Election Protection Poll Monitor Training 2026
events.description:
Thank you for your interest in Election Protection with the Ohio Voter Rights Coalition! Please register for one of the available trainings listed to become a nonpartisan Poll Monitor for the November General election. 

***Please note - you only need to attend one of the trainings listed here, not all of them!

Ohio's Election Protection program is part of the national 866ourvote.org program to promote the 866-OUR-VOTE hotline and ensure that all voters have an equal opportunity to vote and have that vote count. Trained poll monitors are a friendly face outside of polling locations to help voters if they have questions and report any issues.

Even if you have served as a poll monitor in past years, we do ask that you sign up and retake it again so you can be refreshed with the information and updated on new information relevant this year. If you are unable to attend, please register and keep an eye out for a follow up email that will come with a recording of the training and notes. 

Please reach out if you have any questions! Thank you again for helping out with Election Protection and poll monitoring with the Ohio Voter Rights Coalition.

events.title: Danville Weekly Canvassing & Phone Bank for MC - Mary Catherine Roberson for IL HD104
events.description:
# Your Vote Counts More Than Ever‼️
If you ever thought your vote didn't matter, know that just **TWO** short years ago, IL HD104 came down to **269** certified votes. A district that spans Champaign and Vermilion counties and includes all of Danville, parts of Urbana, Savoy, Rantoul, and all the gorgeous farmland in between. A district that houses almost 60k registered voters; **two hundred sixty-nine votes.**

‼️2-6-9 ‼️

That means every single one of us is a conversation away from changing who represents this community, and a real conversation on someone's porch is proven to move *far* more voters than any ad, mailer, or cold text ever will — because it comes from someone they trust, not a stranger.

## Be Like MC: One of Us, Doing the Work
These are our neighbors, the people we wave to, whose kids go to school with ours, who deserve better than what they're getting. This isn't a phone bank in some other state, it's your own block, where your knock matters more than almost anything else we could do.

The energy is there. The votes are there. The time is now. Your neighbors just need someone they trust to ask them to show up.

That's you.

Bring your shoes and your excitement. We'll bring the map.

events.title: Garden Work Day with Root Down LA

address_lines: McKinley Ave & E 46th St, Los Angeles, CA 90011

events.description:
Join Root Down LA on the last Saturday of every month for a hands-on volunteer workday dedicated to caring for our community garden. Together, we'll tackle important seasonal projects that keep the garden healthy, productive, and thriving. Whether you're an experienced gardener or trying it for the first time, there's a meaningful task for everyone. After a rewarding day of working side by side, we'll gather to enjoy a delicious, veggie-inspired meal made with fresh, wholesome ingredients. Come lend a hand, learn something new, connect with your community, and help grow a vibrant space for everyone. We'd love to have you with us!

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! 
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities. 
* No prior gardening or composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome! 
* This location has bathrooms off-site. 
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to help be stewards of the land. 
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Ballot Count Canvass Observer Training
events.description:
Be a Ballot Count Canvass Observer on Election Day and help ensure every vote is counted! Each PA county has a central location where ballots are sorted and counted (“canvassed”). This begins at 7:00 AM on Election Day and continues throughout the week.

Canvass Observers help ensure every vote is counted by monitoring the canvassing process, providing progress updates, and reporting any irregularities to the Voter Protection Team. We will train and support you every step of the way! 

We need Canvass Observer volunteers for morning, afternoon, evening, and overnight shifts, beginning at 7AM on Election Day and continuing until the last vote is counted. Once you complete this training, you tell us your availability and where you can go, and we will assign you a shift and location. (Those who complete training earlier will have more options!) You only need to complete one session of this training.

events.title: Train to #ProtectTheVote in Texas
events.description:
This training is required for all poll monitor volunteers.

Please select ONLY ONE time and date to attend our training sessions.

Our Election Protection program makes sure eligible voters know how to cast their ballots and ensure they are counted. Join us to mobilize voter protection field programs across the country — looking out for voters’ rights while practicing safe social distancing.

Election Protection is a nonpartisan program. Please read our volunteer agreement to understand expectations on how to act in a nonpartisan manner while serving as poll monitors. You can find the nonpartisan agreement here: https://www.commoncause.org/nonpartisan-agreement/

events.title: High School Dems – Organize. Lead. Build Your Future.
events.description:
Are you ready to do more than just watch politics? At the Brown County Dems, you can help shape it!

The Brown County High School Democrats are building a team of young leaders who are stepping up, speaking out, and gaining real-world experience. We meet twice a month from 6:00–7:30 PM at the Dems Office  to organize, connect, and take action.

At these meetings, you’ll:

*Plan and canvass together*—learn how to talk with voters and make a real impact in your community
*Connect with candidates*—join the broader membership to meet gubernatorial candidates and other leaders
*Get plugged into real teams*—social media, fundraising, outreach, events, front desk, and more
*Build real skills*—communication, leadership, organizing, tech, and teamwork you can quantify and add to your resume
*Learn from experienced leaders* while helping pass knowledge, experience, and skills from one generation to the next
*Stay in the loop*—receive our full newsletter and calendar so you can jump into any opportunity that interests you

This isn’t a passive group—it’s a launchpad. Whether you want to knock doors, create content, organize events, or lead a team, you’ll gain experience that matters—now and for our future.

Join with us to be part of the nationwide political change in America.

If you can, bring a chair to sit on and a clipboard or something similar to write on.

events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Every good protest movement needs music. Music lifts us up and has always sustained us in troubled times. We will gather to weave our voices together in chants and songs; building community along the way. Our songs will encourage and inspire us, and everyone around us, as we embark on this consequential march toward the midterms in November, and beyond. All voices, all ages, are welcome. There is no charge to participate. We are all on this journey together. We meet every other Wednesday evening, from 6:30 to 8 pm.

Carmichael Resistance Choir Cantor: Christiana Quick-Cleveland



*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: NO COUNTRY FOR MOTHERS — VIRTUAL SCREENING
events.description: The system was built for mothers to fail. That's the argument of No Country for Mothers — a documentary 2,500 mothers pooled their money and their names to make, breaking a Guinness World Record for the most credited associate producers on a single film. A record that had stood since 1991. I'm one of those 2,500. That fact says something on its own. Mothers stopped waiting for someone else to tell this story and built the case themselves. What this actually is Seventy-eight minutes of film. Then we talk, and the conversation is the real event — the film is the reason we're all in the room. People tell me afterward that it was the part they didn't expect and didn't want to leave. How to come Camera off is completely normal. Most people keep them off. Come in whatever you're wearing. Feed a baby through it. Fold laundry with one ear in. Step away when someone needs you and come back. Leave early if you have to. All of that counts and none of it needs explaining. If it falls apart entirely, the recording stays open for 48 hours. Practical Free. Link goes out the morning of. Real language in the film — headphones if there are little ears nearby. Recommended 16+. Bring one friend who needs to hear she isn't the only one figuring it out. Hosted by Megan Darrell, founder of Big Mother Energy and one of the film's 2,500 associate producers. The world needs your big mother energy.

Pajamas allowed. Cameras optional. You don't have to say a word to belong. Open to moms everywhere — no zip code required. We'll email your watch link before the showing starts.

And said plainly: this circle is a way in, not a gate. Every mother is welcome at every showing — this is just the room where everyone's living your chapter.

events.description:
Join Indivisible Georgia District 10 and Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. Ground Truth is a new approach to voter contact that’s changing how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors (https://ourgroundtruth.org).

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

You’ll receive additional details, including the meeting location, after you sign-up. Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference. 

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Calls for Climate: Support Local Climate Justice Champions!
events.description:
We are getting out the vote for crucial down-ballot elections where we have an opportunity to win on climate justice this fall and summer. Join Lead Locally and Jane Fonda Climate PAC for **Calls for Climate**, a virtual phone banking series to reach voters in these key races. 
 
**Our next phone bank is on Monday, October 19 and we're making calls to voters about Fern Leard for PA State House, featuring special guest Bill McKibben!**

Calls for Climate is a virtual phone bank that you can join from anywhere — all you need is a computer and a phone. Each week, we’ll be talking to voters about a local race with important stakes for climate and democracy.

**Upcoming phone banks:**

- **October 19:** Fern Leard for PA State House with Bill McKibben!
- **October 26:** Brad Chambers for PA State House
- **November 2:** Mark Pinsley for PA State Senate

Local races like these are often determined by a small number of votes, so every voter we can talk to really does matter.

Whether you're making calls for the first time or a seasoned phone banker, we’ve got you covered! We’ll begin by learning what is at stake in the race (often from the candidates themselves), review the phone banking script, and walk through how to use the calling platform.

Learn more about the races we are prioritizing here: https://callsforclimate.org/

events.description:
Join us as we collect signatures to keep building a stronger, safer, and more equitable 26th Ward. Working families deserve a city that works for them - good jobs, safe streets, a home they can afford, and a real voice in decisions that affect their lives. I’m Alderperson Jessie Fuentes, and I’m running for Re-election to deliver for working families by focusing on three promises:

Build affordable housing now — fast-tracked, mixed-income developments with strong tenant protections, community land trusts, and funding for deeply affordable units so parents and seniors can stay in the neighborhoods they love.

Deliver real safety through investment — expand proven violence-prevention programs, fund crisis-response teams for mental-health and substance calls, fix lighting and sidewalks, and invest in youth jobs and after-school programs so our streets are safer and our kids have opportunities.

Practice co-governance — make decision-making local: participatory budgeting that directs resources to neighborhood priorities, empowered community advisory committees, transparent city contracting, and regular, multilingual neighborhood events so families shape the policies that affect them.

I will also fight for living-wage job pipelines, affordable housing, reliable transit, and support for small businesses so families can do more than survive. Join our campaign to turn these promises into results. Sign, volunteer, or donate today to keep building a stronger, safer, and fairer community for working families.

events.title: Brookline Rally for Democracy, October 2026
events.description:
Brookline Rally for Democracy

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Easton
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: [Yolo County] Self-Directed Door Knocking — Eric Jones for Congress (CA-4)
events.description:
Knock doors on your own schedule, anywhere in the Yolo County portion of CA-4.

Self-directed canvassing means you pick the day, get your turf, and go. There's no launch event to show up to and no meeting spot. We'll get you set up beforehand.

BEFORE YOUR FIRST SHIFT

Your County Captain is Mel Halem. She'll reach out after you sign up to get you literature and a turf assignment.

We also run a volunteer Slack with a channel for every county in the district. You'll get the invite when you sign up.

New to canvassing? Come to a virtual training first. Thursdays at 6:00 PM and Sundays at 3:00 PM, 45 minutes. You'll leave knowing how to talk to voters, how to use the app, and what to do at the door. Sign up here:


ericjones.us/trainingsignup


WHEN TO GO OUT

You can knock between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM. The hours that actually work:

Weekdays — 4:00 to 8:00 PM

Weekends — 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM

People are home and willing to talk then. Go earlier and you're mostly knocking on empty houses.

WHAT A SHIFT LOOKS LIKE

Aim for 50 doors. Twenty-five is the floor, and most turf lets you hit that in an hour or two. Move quickly — we have a lot of doors between now and November 3.

Sign up for whatever days you can. Come back as often as you want.
