Your County Captain is Karl VonZabern. He'll reach out after you sign up to get you literature and a turf assignment.

We also run a volunteer Slack with a channel for every county in the district. You'll get the invite when you sign up.

New to canvassing? Come to a virtual training first. Thursdays at 6:00 PM and Sundays at 3:00 PM, 45 minutes. You'll leave knowing how to talk to voters, how to use the app, and what to do at the door. Sign up here:


ericjones.us/trainingsignup


WHEN TO GO OUT

You can knock between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM. The hours that actually work:

Weekdays — 4:00 to 8:00 PM

Weekends — 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM

People are home and willing to talk then. Go earlier and you're mostly knocking on empty houses.

WHAT A SHIFT LOOKS LIKE

Aim for 50 doors. Twenty-five is the floor, and most turf lets you hit that in an hour or two. Move quickly — we have a lot of doors between now and November 3.

Sign up for whatever days you can. Come back as often as you want.

events.title: [Virtual] Phone Banking — Eric Jones for Congress (CA-4)
events.description:
Join us to phonebank for Eric Jones! Eric is running against a long term blue dog Democrat, who relies on a ton of corporate cash from PG&E, large insurance companies who refuse wildfire claims and Big Pharma. Meanwhile the cost of living keeps rising as these major companies continue to bankroll incumbent politicians. 

Eric is fighting to change that. Eric Jones wants to ban Congressional stock trading and foster economic opportunity to revitalize the American Dream. 

HOW IT WORKS

Sign up for any weekday shift, 5:00 to 7:00 PM. Join the Zoom link you'll get after you sign up. We'll spend the first few minutes on training and getting you set up, then you'll start dialing.

Stay for the full two hours or drop off when you need to. Take as many shifts as you want.

WHAT YOU NEED

A computer and a quiet spot. Headphones help. That's it — the calling happens through your browser, so you don't need to use your own phone number.

NEW TO THIS?

Come to a virtual training first if you'd rather learn before you dial. Thursdays at 6:00 PM and Sundays at 3:00 PM, 45 minutes. Sign up here: https://ericjones.us/trainingsignup

Or just show up to a shift. We train at the top of every one.

WHY IT MATTERS

The incumbent was elected nearly 30 years ago. The only way voters hear there's a choice —  and a true difference between the candidates —  in this race is if someone tells them. That's the whole job.

Sign up for whatever nights you can.

2. Marriage Equality [https://vaformarriageequality.com]

events.title: Urbana-Champaign Weekly Canvassing & Phone Bank for MC - Mary Catherine Roberson for IL HD104
events.description:
# Your Vote Counts More Than Ever‼️
If you ever thought your vote didn't matter, know that just **TWO** short years ago, IL HD104 came down to **269** certified votes. A district that spans Champaign and Vermilion counties and includes all of Danville, parts of Urbana, Savoy, Rantoul, and all the gorgeous farmland in between. A district that houses almost 60k registered voters; **two hundred sixty-nine votes.**

‼️2-6-9 ‼️

That means every single one of us is a conversation away from changing who represents this community, and a real conversation on someone's porch is proven to move *far* more voters than any ad, mailer, or cold text ever will — because it comes from someone they trust, not a stranger.

## Be Like MC: One of Us, Doing the Work
These are our neighbors, the people we wave to, whose kids go to school with ours, who deserve better than what they're getting. This isn't a phone bank in some other state, it's your own block, where your knock matters more than almost anything else we could do.

The energy is there. The votes are there. The time is now. Your neighbors just need someone they trust to ask them to show up.

That's you.

Bring your shoes and your excitement. We'll bring the map.

Don’t be lulled by headlines about Trump’s tanking popularity. We can win, but it’s going to take a strong ground game to build a progressive response to the current chaos. We need to reach voters, talk about what’s at stake and let them know how important their vote is.
 
We'll make the less than 90-minute drive from Chicago to our meetup location in Wisconsin (exact location coming soon). We’ll have a pre-canvass briefing once we get there, then split off into pairs to knock doors and talk with voters. We'll provide all the info and prep you'll need and will have carpools for anyone needing a ride.

events.title: Speak From the Heart: Storyteller Training for Families, Not Politics
events.description:
Every week, we're bringing together volunteers, family members, and community members to build one of our most powerful tools in this campaign: our own stories.

Coloradans are being asked to vote on Propositions 134 and 135 this fall; measures that would have real consequences for kids, families, and medical care across our state. The research is clear: most voters don't start out understanding what these measures actually do. What changes minds isn't a debate. It's a real conversation with someone whose life is affected.

That's where you come in.

In this 1.5 hour-long virtual workshop, you'll learn how to:

- Shape your own experience — as a parent, a trans person, a faith leader, friend, a neighbor, a medical provider, or an ally — into a story that connects
- Lead with empathy instead of argument, so conversations open people up instead of shutting them down
- Bridge from your story to the facts that matter most to undecided voters
- Feel confident having these conversations with your community, friends, family, neighbors, and canvassing contacts

No experience necessary. Whether you're planning to canvass, phone bank, talk to your own family, or just want to feel more prepared for the conversations already happening around you, this training is for you.

This session repeats weekly — come to the one that fits your schedule.

events.title: CCNM's Democracy Action Hour
events.description:
Join Common Cause New Mexico for our monthly **Democracy Action Hour**, a space for volunteers, supporters, and community members to get updates, take action, and help build a stronger democracy in New Mexico.

Each month, we’ll share what’s happening in our democracy work, highlight ways to plug in, and connect people with concrete next steps. 

We’ll discuss key democracy priorities, including:

- **Election Protection** and how to volunteer for the November election
- **Legislative Pay**, a ballot measure to help make the New Mexico Legislature more accessible to working people
- The **pocket veto amendment** and what it means for transparency and accountability
- Opportunities to join local **Community Action Teams** and help build people power beyond Election Day

Whether you are brand new to Common Cause or have been involved for years, this is a chance to learn what’s happening, meet others who care about democracy, and find a meaningful way to take action.

**This is a nonpartisan event. All are welcome.**

### What to Expect
- Updates on Common Cause New Mexico’s democracy work
- A short issue spotlight or mini-training
- Clear volunteer opportunities and next steps
- Time for questions and discussion
- Opportunities to get involved locally through Community Action Teams

RSVP today and invite a friend, neighbor, or family member who cares about protecting voters and strengthening democracy in New Mexico.

events.title: East Fishkill, NY: Congressional District 17 Community Canvassing in Westchester
events.description:
Join Food & Water Action to knock on doors in Congressional District 17 to take back the House and stop data centers by electing Cait Conley.

You'll get trained on how to canvass, have fun, and chat with your neighbors!

Why join us? Rep. Mike Lawler is voting away our rights to clean water, a safe climate, and healthy food.

- He was among the deciding votes on the disastrous Big Ugly Bill that gutted essential services while giving handouts to fossil fuel companies and billionaires.

- He voted to kick 10,000 households in his district off food assistance and to take healthcare away from thousands more.

- He co-sponsored a bill to take federal funding away from local government wastewater systems and facilitate wastewater privatization, which can lead to higher bills for households and local businesses.

- He voted to cut funding that would protect children from lead poisoning and to make it easier to fast-track the approval of dirty fossil fuel infrastructure and expansions (like the Enbridge pipeline that runs through his district) that will raise our utility bills.

These actions are despicable and will directly impact thousands of New Yorkers who call the lower Hudson Valley their home.

Join us to talk to our neighbors across Congressional District 17 about why Cait Conley is the best choice to win data center regulations in Congress, stop new nuclear from being built at Indian Point, and stop cuts to food assistance and clean water funding. 

No prior canvassing experience is necessary. We'll train you before the canvass starts - join us!

--

_Paid for by Food & Water Action, Not Authorized by any Candidate or Committee._

In the US military, deadly force briefings are issued every time time a change of guard is made. It’s clear that ICE officers too, need a reminder.
DHS policy is quite clearly spelled out in DHS Policy Statement 044-05 paragraph H - The use of excessive force is unlawful and will not be tolerated. Those who engage in such misconduct, and those who fail to report such misconduct, will be subject to all applicable administrative and criminal penalties.
Stand with us we remind the Stockton ERO of the proper use of deadly force and encourage them to obey the law.
We are watching. 
If you live in a mixed status household, think carefully about signing up - but you can attend anyway.

events.title: PORTLAND - Worker Rally for Universal Healthcare
events.description:
The purpose of this event is so that Unions stand shoulder to shoulder in solidarity and in power, to demand Universal Healthcare in Oregon. In particular, we demand that our legislature passes the bill or refers it to the voters for 2028.

Please also join our NoKings event on October 17th
https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/1020800/

Here is a link to the most recent Workers Rally flyer which changes as we add endorsements! Please print and share widely!
https://canva.link/8eobhbi7n3ibq2w

## What This Means for Union Members

- **Health Care for all** – Everyone in, no one out
- **Quality Care** – PEBB + quality coverage (the kind insurance our lawmakers get)
- **Fair, predictable costs** – Insurance costs go down dramatically for most workers
- **Premiums only** – UHPGB projected cost estimates are premiums only; they don't include copays or deductibles
- **Save our Schools** – $500–800 million/year in projected savings for K-12 education
- **Save our public services** – Hundreds of millions/year in projected savings for government programs
- **Easier Contract Negotiations** – The rising cost of healthcare no longer competes with demands for higher compensation
- **Coverage untied from employment** – A job loss or early retirement before Medicare no longer means scrambling for individual coverage (25 million workers in the US only stay in their current job for health insurance)
- **Better coverage in our rural communities** – Normalized rates will be a lifeline for rural clinics and hospitals
- **So much more** – Like lower workers' comp and auto insurance rates, since medical costs are no longer priced into those premiums

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Session 4: The Iceberg Is Right Here
Connecting history to our community today, how the past continues to shape the present right where we live.

The essence of the Good Trouble Anti-Racism Workshop Series 
(hereafter referred to as GTAR Workshop Series) is encapsulated in a quote from Congressman John Lewis: "Not the civil rights we inherited-but the civil rights we are building." 

GTAR Workshop Series is created and led by Sondra Light-Holt - a Black woman, a community health provider and advocate, a lifelong resident of Sandusky Ohio, and an active member with the NAACP. She is a board member of Serving Our Seniors and brings 25 years of experience in the field of healthcare to this Series.

THE GTAR Workshop Series is anti-racism education through the lens of healthcare, allowing us to more fully understand one another across racial lines, thus strengthening and expanding our community. Racism is America's wound. This series provides information regarding the harms of racism in housing, healthcare, education, and the justice system. Each session equips participants with factual knowledge, historical context, and civic language to recognize and respond to systemic racism in their own lives. 

The Series intentionally encourages people of all races to open up, share their experiences, ask hard questions and be heard without judgment. We'll learn, expand and strengthen our community, and take action by working together to heal our wounds, thus mitigating future damage. Medical racism runs throughout this series as a core thread, because community health is inseparable from community justice. 

Solidarity is practiced in real time, not just discussed in theory. Attendees are encouraged to share experiences of being targeted by racism, or being encouraged to behave in a racist way. Additionally, discussion is open to talking about positive experiences of friendship or power-sharing partnerships across racial lines. This model allows participants to acknowledge what has occurred in the past and make choices about how to build their future. 

Each session contains 2 parts: the Education portion of each Workshop provides relevant information to absorb; the Training portion builds solidarity across races. 

Topics: 
Session 1-How We Got Here-The Blueprint of American Racism (8/13) 
Session 2-The Iceberg-Seeing What You Were Taught Not to See (9/10) 
Session 3-It's Personal-Lived Experience, Privilege & the Stories We Tell Ourselves (10/8) 
Session 4-The Iceberg Is Right Here-Our Community Today (11/12) 
Session 5-What Do We Do Now-The Call to Action (12/10)

The essence of the Good Trouble Anti-Racism Workshop Series 
(hereafter referred to as GTAR Workshop Series) is encapsulated in a quote from Congressman John Lewis: "Not the civil rights we inherited-but the civil rights we are building." 

GTAR Workshop Series is created and led by Sondra Light-Holt - a Black woman, a community health provider and advocate, a lifelong resident of Sandusky Ohio, and an active member with the NAACP. She is a board member of Serving Our Seniors and brings 25 years of experience in the field of healthcare to this Series. 

THE GTAR Workshop Series is anti-racism education through the lens of healthcare, allowing us to more fully understand one another across racial lines, thus strengthening and expanding our community. Racism is America's wound. This series provides information regarding the harms of racism in housing, healthcare, education, and the justice system. Each session equips participants with factual knowledge, historical context, and civic language to recognize and respond to systemic racism in their own lives. 

The Series intentionally encourages people of all races to open up, share their experiences, ask hard questions and be heard without judgment. We'll learn, expand and strengthen our community, and take action by working together to heal our wounds, thus mitigating future damage. Medical racism runs throughout this series as a core thread, because community health is inseparable from community justice. 

Solidarity is practiced in real time, not just discussed in theory. Attendees are encouraged to share experiences of being targeted by racism, or being encouraged to behave in a racist way. Additionally, discussion is open to talking about positive experiences of friendship or power-sharing partnerships across racial lines. This model allows participants to acknowledge what has occurred in the past and make choices about how to build their future. 

Each session contains 2 parts: the Education portion of each Workshop provides relevant information to absorb; the Training portion builds solidarity across races. 

Topics: 
Session 1-How We Got Here-The Blueprint of American Racism (8/13) 
Session 2-The Iceberg-Seeing What You Were Taught Not to See (9/10) 
Session 3-It's Personal-Lived Experience, Privilege & the Stories We Tell Ourselves (10/8) 
Session 4-The Iceberg Is Right Here-Our Community Today (11/12) 
Session 5-What Do We Do Now-The Call to Action (12/10)

events.title: Banned Book Club - Civil Disobedience & To Kill A Mockingbird
events.description:
For the remainder of October and throughout November we will be exploring How To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee. I feel it is important to advise that this book may have triggers for some people. If you feel you might not be in an emotional space to handle the topics mentioned, or that this title just isn't for you, please feel free to skip parts or the book in full and stay tuned for December's title.

Content Trigger Warnings for To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee include the following subjects:

• Abuse
• Murder
• N-word
• Racism
• Rape (mentioned)

Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

This month we spent the first half discussing Civil Disobedience by Henry David Thoreau and will now be focused on the beginning of To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee.

October 5th & 12th, was dedicated to Civil Disobedience by Henry David Thoreau.
October 19th & 26th, will be dedicated To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

events.title: States Win Colorado & Friends Phonebank!
events.description:
### Let's turn Wisconsin blue!

Join States Win Colorado on Tuesdays from 5 to 7 PM MT to help our candidate, Jenna Jacobson, build progressive power in the Wisconsin State Senate.

**[Meet Jenna Jacobson:](https://stateswin.org/candidates/jenna-jacobson/)** Representative Jenna Jacobson's commitment to public service was shaped by her mother, a single parent and pastor who balanced raising two children while relying on food stamps and pursuing her education. Now in her second term in the Wisconsin State Assembly, Jenna is running to flip Senate District 17 in southwest Wisconsin. Breaking the GOP's legislative grip and delivering real progress for working families across Wisconsin is not possible without electing Jenna and flipping this seat.

**Why this race:** All eyes are on Wisconsin heading into the 2026 midterms. With fairer maps now in effect, there is a real path to Democratic majorities in both state legislative chambers for the first time in over a decade. So much is at stake: reproductive freedom, public education, voting rights, economic fairness. Winning in Wisconsin will not only decide the balance of power in Madison, but help shape the national landscape in 2026.

**Why Colorado is calling Wisconsin:** Colorado already has a Democratic trifecta. Wisconsin is two Senate seats away from its first Democratic Senate majority in more than 15 years, and this district was decided by about one point at the presidential level in 2024. States Win started in 2017 as Sister District on one idea: volunteers in safely blue states adopt the swing-state legislative races where a few hundred conversations actually move the outcome. That model has helped flip 10 legislative chambers since. Two hours on the phones from Colorado does more for progressive power in a district like Jenna's than almost anywhere else you could spend them.

**Why phonebank:** The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. Every call helps us clean our lists, which makes for a faster, more efficient phonebank.

**Come one, come all:** No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). Our phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

We're a brand new chapter, and this series is where States Win Colorado comes to life. Tuesdays, 5 to 7 PM MT, every week through Election Day on November 3. Grab your headphones, bring a friend, and let's win Wisconsin from the Rockies.

events.description:
**Thursdays on Zoom, from 3 PM - 5 PM PT and/or 5 PM - 7 PM PT**

Join us at **States Win Puget Sound** to help support candidates across the country win their elections! We will be calling in support of **Representative Lindsey Prather** of North Carolina and **Holly Lyon** running for Arizona State House! Training and support will be provided. Bring a friend!

**Grow Democratic Power in the North Carolina House**

Rep. Prather won her seat in 2024 by a narrow margin, reflecting the district’s competitive nature and the political crosscurrents in Buncombe County and surrounding communities. With Republicans controlling both legislative chambers and a Democrat in the governor’s office, defending HD 115 is essential to preserving the governor’s veto power and protecting public education, reproductive freedom, and fair representation in one of the South’s most closely watched battleground states.

Holly Lyon is a retired Air Force Colonel, teacher, and leader running for the Arizona State House in Legislative District 17. Holly is running for the Arizona State House to give Legislative District 17 leadership that listens, works through differences, and focuses on practical solutions. Her race is crucial to help Democrats move closer to flipping the Arizona House. 


**Why phonebank:**

The data proves it. Phonebanking is the best volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. Every call helps us clean our lists, which makes for a faster, more efficient phonebank!

**Come one, come all:**

No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). We'll share successes and address questions throughout, all while contacting voters in crucial state legislative races. Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

**Accessibility**

Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information.

events.title: KYD: County Commission Observer Corps

sponsor.name: KnoxDems - Knox County Democratic Party (KCDP) TN

events.description:
Ever wonder how local decisions actually get made? Join the Knox Young Dems Observer Corps.

Observer Corps members attend local government meetings, follow what happens in the room, and help report back to the community. Our goal is simple: increase youth presence, public transparency, and accountability in the places where local power actually moves.

The Knox County Commission makes decisions every month on land use, housing, healthcare, infrastructure, public safety, education, taxes, and more - decisions that will shape Knox County for years. Right now, the 18-35 demographic is underrepresented in these rooms. We are changing that by showing up, learning the process, and helping our community understand what happened.

As an Observer, you do not need to be an expert. KYD will help you know what to look for. Before the meeting, registered observers will receive a short guide, an observer report document to fill out, and the most current agenda available by email.

What we do:

Attend local County Commission meetings.

Observe the meeting’s conduct, major discussion points, public comments, votes, and next steps.

Take notes using KYD’s observer report guide.

Help KYD report back to the community on issues that affect young people and working families in Knox County.

We maintain a neutral, professional presence during meetings. Observers are not required to speak, lobby, or participate in public comment. We simply exercise our right to know what local government is doing and help make sure more people know too.

You'll rotate through roles as both the canvasser and the voter, so you get a feel for both sides of the conversation. What to expect:

A quick rundown of our talking points and canvassing goals Paired and small-group role-play "dry runs" at the door Real-time feedback from fellow volunteers and staff Tips for handling common responses — skeptics, slammed doors, and everything in between A relaxed, no-judgment space to mess up and try again

Event Details

Date: October 18th, 2026 
Time: 3PM 
Location: Coopers Tavern, 20W Mifflin St, Madison 
Cost: Free! Drinks available for purchase.

Following the screening, we’ll host a community discussion about maternal health, postpartum recovery, nutrition, and how we can work together to better support mothers in our community.

At JOIAAS, our mission is rooted in the belief that when mothers are nourished, families thrive. We hope you’ll join us for an evening of education, connection, and meaningful conversation.

The JOIAAS Team

events.title: Logan County IEP Circle

location.venue: Southern WV Community & Technical College- Library

events.description:
IEP Circles WV is a parent-led community where families of exceptional learners come together to find support, build knowledge, and create change. If you're navigating an IEP, 504 Plan, evaluations, school communication, or accessing services, these gatherings are designed to help you feel informed, connected, and supported.

Each meeting brings caregivers together with experienced advocates, education attorneys, and community partners who provide practical guidance, answer questions, and facilitate meaningful discussions. You'll have opportunities to share experiences, learn from other families, discover helpful resources, and build lasting relationships with people who understand the challenges you face.

Beyond individual support, IEP Circles helps families understand the larger issues affecting special education. We'll explore how school funding, staffing shortages, IDEA funding, and state and federal policy decisions impact the services available to students. By connecting personal experiences to these broader challenges, families can better understand why obstacles exist and how they can work alongside educators and other parents to improve public education.

For those interested in taking the next step, IEP Circles also offers opportunities to develop advocacy skills through workshops on legislative advocacy, storytelling, public speaking, community organizing, and civic engagement. Whether you simply want support or hope to help shape the future of special education in West Virginia, you'll find a welcoming community where your experiences are valued and your voice matters.

Together, we can strengthen support for our children, build stronger communities, and advocate for a public education system that works for every student.

events.description:
Phone banking is about making connections. It's a chance to reach voters, share important election information, identify supporters, and answer questions before Election Day.

No experience necessary!  We will give you training and a refresher for anyone who wants to brush up on the basics, learn a few new tips, or feel more comfortable making calls. Whether you're a seasoned volunteer or haven't phone banked in a while, we'll help you get ready for the 2026 election.

We will use a calling system that requires you to log in on a device. This method conceals your phone number and prevents people from calling you back. The system cycles through callers with options to update records in real time and provides a script on your screen.

What to bring:

your laptop or tablet

any headset or headphones you want to use

your smartphone

enthusiasm for the 2026 elections!

Individuals will receive guests, assist with voter registration and absentee requests, undertake routine office duties, and help with mailings and relate office campaign preparations.

events.title: Knock Doors with Team Callee!
events.description:
Join Team Callee to knock doors for our DPLC & ESDSA endorsed candidate Callee Ackland for Springfield City Council!

Callee is a Navy veteran, library volunteer, tenant advocate and a renter herself, running with a focus on affordability and sustainability. Help us reach every voter in Springfield to spread the word about her progressive campaign and unseat the Republican appointee!

We'll meet at Willamalane Park on G Street (near the back of the parking lot, closest to Mohawk Blvd) for a canvass training, then spread out and knock doors across Springfield. We're happy to set you up with an experienced canvassing buddy if this is your first time knocking doors! Reach out if you have any questions :)

events.title: Iowa Forward Poll Observer Training
events.description:
Are you interested in protecting Iowa voters this fall? Join us as a Democratic Poll Observer for the general election!  

Poll Observers are the eyes and the ears of our team on the ground during Early Voting (happening now) and on Election Day (November 3).  Their presence is critical to show our community members, and local, state, and federal officials, that we are committed to protecting each other and our democracy.  

There is no residency requirement to be a poll observer and you can observe anywhere in the state! We will answer your questions and provide full training and resource materials.  We welcome new and experienced poll observers alike. You only need to sign up for a single one-hour training to be a poll observer.

This is an online event. You will receive a link in your email to join our Zoom meeting the day before the event.

We are recruiting more than 1,000 poll observers for this election.  Please invite your friends to sign up and join us for this training!

events.title: Election Defenders Weekly Hangout
events.description:
Election Defenders is a weekly organizing call to learn, plan and promote resistance to authoritarian interference in our democratic elections.

We act in service of democracy and in line with lawful, nonviolent civil resistance against authoritarians.

The meeting will be hosted on Zoom every Saturday at 11:00 AM CT and will bring interested parties together to build the skills and community needed to amplify resistance voices across the country.

Why It Matters

Free and fair elections are a basic pillar of healthy democracies, and our elections are under attack by the Trump regime.

Trump and his enablers are trying many tactics: disenfranchising legitimate voters, blocking mail delivery of ballots, calling for armed intimidation at polling locations, making false or unsubstantiated claims about voting fraud, etc.

Election Defenders will support activists who wish to use lawful, nonviolent civil resistance to protect our democracy.

When: 

Every Saturday at 11:00 AM CT (9am PT, 12pm ET)

Format: Weekly group call via Zoom

Duration: 60 minutes

Focus areas: 

Understanding the entire election process and its vulnerabilities, utilizing training and information opportunities, supporting and growing the resistance, coordinating election protection efforts.

events.title: Phone Banking - HYBRID (Boulder or Online)
events.description:
**Phone Bank for Hands Off Colorado**

Join us for a virtual phone bank supporting Hands Off Colorado, a campaign of Rocky Mountain Equality to defeat the anti-trans and anti-immigrant ballot measures this fall. This is one of the most effective ways to make an impact from home — no experience necessary!

**What to expect:**

We'll be using an online dialer platform that connects you directly to voters and supporters — no need to dial numbers yourself. Once you're connected, you'll read from a simple, conversational script designed to help you have real conversations, not a robotic pitch. The script walks you through an introduction, a few key talking points about what's at stake, and a couple of questions to gauge where the person you're speaking with stands.

Before calls begin, a trained lead will walk everyone through:
- How to log into the phone bank platform
- How the dialer works (it does the dialing — you just talk!)
- A walkthrough of the script and how to enter responses
- Tips for handling common questions or pushback

**Why it matters:**

Every conversation helps us identify supporters, share accurate information, and build the coalition we need to protect trans and immigrant Coloradans. Phone banking is flexible, low-pressure, and a great option no matter your schedule or experience level.

**What you need:**

- A computer with internet access (calls are made through your browser or phone using the platform — no personal phone number is shared)
- Enthusiasm for the cause!

events.title: Call to Flip the Pennsylvania State Senate
events.description:
Join us to make calls to **flip the Pennsylvania State Senate** giving the Democrats a Trifecta with Democrats controlling the Pennsylvania Senate, House and Governor for the first time since 1993, allowing Democrats to: 

* Redistrict PA Congressional maps to counter Republican efforts across the country

* Pass needed legislation including raising the minimum wage beyond $7.25 an hour, funding public transit, implementing paid family and medical leave, and expanding access to affordable housing. 

* With 19 electoral votes Pennsylvania is the largest battleground state, so Democratic control is critical for upcoming 2028 elections. 

We're calling every other week to elect **Brian Wrightson** in Senate District 40 ( in congressional district PA 08, where Paige Cognetti is running to flip) and to elect **Eileen Hartnett Albillar** in Senate District 6 (in congressional district PA 01, where Bob Harvie is running to flip). 

Check each week for more details on who we are calling for.

events.title: Hands off our vote! GOTV: Weekly Rally in September and October
events.description:
As we head into election season, join Muncie Resists for weekly get out the vote rallies on the sidewalk at the corner of McGalliard and Wheeling. We will meet every Wednesday from 5:30 to 6:30 PM during September and October reminding folks to register to vote, vote early, and make a plan.  

Bring a sign, bring a friend, and stand up for what matters. This is a peaceful, family-friendly gathering, rain or shine. Whether you've been coming to MR events for months or this is your first time showing up, you're welcome here. Courage is contagious. Make your voice heard. 

**What to bring:** a sign (or borrow one from our collection), water, a chair if you would rather sit and weather-appropriate clothing.

events.title: Love as Action: Athens, GA
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Athens Quakers to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On the 1st Saturday of each month at 11:00am we will gather at Alps Road and Baxter Street.

Our purpose is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Saturday Canvass

sponsor.name: Joanna Robinson for State Representative (OR Working Families Party)

events.description:
Help us win Oregon House District 15!

Join Democratic, Independent, and Working Families Party nominee Joanna Robinson as we knock on doors to gather support and turn out voters!

📅 Saturday | 10:00 AM 

📍Location | Grand Prairie Park, 2530 Grand Prairie Rd SE, Albany

Canvass Flow:

- Check in at 10:00 AM.
- Hear from Joanna, followed by a short training for those who need it.
- Head out to talk with voters about why our district needs a representative who answers to working people, not corporate PACs and special interests.
- Return to the launch location when you're done, debrief with campaign staff, and sign up for more canvassing!

Whether you've knocked a thousand doors or never knocked one in your life, we've got a spot for you and all the training and hands-on coaching you'll need! No experience needed.

> **Community Drive:** We're collecting hygiene items, clothing, and food for [Young Roots Oregon](https://youngrootsoregon.org/)’s Family Haven Shelter Program, an emergency placement home with 24/7 staffing support for young mothers ages 18-24 years old and their children who are experiencing displacement, escaping violence, or homelessness. See the list of needed items below, and bring what you can to the Canvass!

> *All products need to be unscented and new.*

> - Laundry soap
- Dryer sheets
- Shampoo & Conditioner (children and adults)
- Bar soap & liquid body soap
- Socks for all sizes
- Underwear (women and children)
- Sports/cami style bras (M, L, XL)
- Sheet sets (King, Queen, Twin and crib)
- Tampons & pads
- Diapers and wipes
- PJ sets - infant to Women's 2XL
- Baby formula
- Baby/children's snacks

Learn more about the essential work Young Roots Oregon does for our community at [www.youngrootsoregon.org](https://youngrootsoregon.org/).

events.title: SALEM & VIRTUAL - Share Your Comments at a Universal Health Plan Governance Board Meeting
events.description:
The State of Oregon's Universal Health Plan Governance Board (UHPGB) is developing our state's transition plan to a universal healthcare system. They recently voted to delay the delivery of their plan to the Oregon Legislature until December 2026. 

Learn more about the Board here: https://www.hcao.org/uhpgb

They have set aside time in their monthly meetings to hear from YOU about what you need in a new system. Share your perspective with the Governance Board in the form of Public Comment.

TALK TO THE PEOPLE MAKING THE PLAN! 

You must register in advance to reserve your time for public comments by emailing uhpgb.info@dcbs.oregon.gov. Or, if attending a meeting in person, you may sign-up 15 minutes before the meeting begins.

The Board meets on the 3rd Thursday of the month, both remotely and in-person at 350 Winter St. NE, Salem OR 97301. Often meetings are in Basement Conference Room F: please check meeting information for room changes. 

Upcoming meeting dates:
August 20th, September 17th, October 15th, November 19th, December 17th.

Meeting times and materials are posted here:
https://www.oregon.gov/uhpgb/board-meetings/Pages/2026-meetings.aspx


The UHPGB mission: "We’re creating a strong, workable plan so everyone in Oregon can get the high-quality, equitable health care they deserve. This new system will be simpler, more affordable, and more sustainable — cutting costs for families and businesses while building a healthier, more stable future for our state."

Health Care for All Oregon has seen in real time that public comments has changed the work of the Board, and the framework of the plan. Your input can make a difference in this work.

Interested in attending and speaking virtually? To speak you must inform UHPGB Staff 24 hours in advance to reserve your spot, by emailing uhpgb.info@dcbs.oregon.gov.

Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.  

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

**These races include:**
**SENATE:**

 - **Michigan Senate** *(Build Race - Movement Champion)* - **Abdul El-Sayed**, who is born and raised in Michigan, studied to be a doctor but then realized he wanted to dedicate his career to building government systems that actually work for Michiganders. He has secured free glasses for kids who need the,, removed lead from Detroit’s elementary schools, taken on Michigan's biggest polluters and made Narcan universally accessible. He has also spearheaded a program to eventually cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders over 2 years. He is a true fighter and is ready to take that to DC on behalf of the whole state!
- **Maine Senate** *(Build Race - Movement Champion Race)* - **Troy Jackson**, who is a logger from Allagash, a lifelong fighter for workers' rights, and former Maine Senate President who is running to put power back in the hands of working people and unseat Susan Collins.  
- **Georgia Senate** *(Block MAGA Race)* - **Jon Ossoff**, who is an incumbent democratic Senator for the state of Georgia. He was born and raised in Atlanta. He is focused on exposing and stopping governmental corruption all while being one of the few US Senators whose campaign refuses corporate PAC money. 
- **Mississippi Senate** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Scott Colom**, who is a District Attorney for the 16th judicial district of Mississippi. As DA, he has pursued policies like avoiding incarceration for non-violent offenses, was the first District Attorney in Mississippi to offer restorative justice for victims, and is currently on the Advisory Board of the VERA Institute for Justice, a partner that SURJ has worked with over the years. 
 
**HOUSE:**

- **Michigan Congressional District 7** *(Build Race - Movement Champion)* - **Will Lawrence**, who is an organizer and coalition-builder with experience speaking truth to power and getting results at the local, state and federal level. Born and raised in Mid-Michigan, Will has fought tirelessly to protect people’s rights to housing (co-founder of the Rents Is Too Damn High Coalition), bring good, green jobs to the district (as a co-founder of Sunrise Movement) and to ward off data center greed. 
- **Tennessee Congressional District 9** *(Build Race - Movement Champion)* - **Justin Pearson**, who is an organizer, born and raised in Southwest Memphis, Tennessee. He grew up in a working class family and has been advocating for his community since the age of 15, fighting for better education for his classmates. He has since formed Memphis Community Against the Pipeline (MCAP) to fight billion dollar oil companies that would have polluted over a million people’s drinking water, fought alongside workers for better wages and taken on the xAI data center for their illegal pollution.
- **California Congressional District 22** *(Build Race- Movement Champion)* - **Randy Villegas**, who is a 30-year old son of immigrants and activist for immigrant rights in his area. He is an elected school board trustee in Visalia, CA and political science professor who is running to represent California’s 22nd congressional district, representing Bakersfield and portions of the central valley.
- **North Carolina Congressional District 11** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Jamie Ager**, who is a fourth generation Western NC farmer. Running on making healthcare accessible, lowering costs, stopping government waste and corruption, and getting necessary relief to Hurricane Helene survivors.

**New**
**North Carolina Statewide** *Build Race- Movement Champion*- **Anita Earls** is an associate NC Justice running for re-election. On the NC Supreme Court, Earls has championed healthcare access, education, and protecting the right to vote. Earls is a critical line of defense to protect and re-institute fair maps for NC voters.

    
Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!
      
***

## Logistics:

-   These phone banks are online on the Zoom platform. Log into the call on Zoom on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
-   We have a robust training on the call to give you all the information you need -- a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
-   Returners can start early.
-   You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.
-   ***Please note the time zone for call time.***
    
***

## Feeling Unsure?

-   **Our model works** - learn from the best! Our phonebanks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
-   Our conversations are based on **open-ended questions** and **deep listening.  You do not need to be an expert** on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
-   Want to hear what a phonebank is like? Check out [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U3w4tNKPTY8) interviewing SURJ phonebankers.
    
***
## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and **this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections** – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to **put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.**

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, **protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi** and **flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.**

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by **supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south** who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

***

## About SURJ:

[Showing Up for Racial Justice](https://surj.org/) (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: Mike Mondays: Healthcare Is A Human Right!
events.description:
Nobody should have to choose between seeing a doctor, buying groceries, paying rent, or keeping the lights on.

Join Hudson Valley residents outside Congressman Mike Lawler’s Mahopac office as we examine his healthcare record and discuss how federal decisions affecting Medicaid, Medicare, the Affordable Care Act, hospitals, and other health programs are reaching directly into our homes and communities.

Healthcare policy isn't an abstract debate in Washington. It determines whether families can afford prescriptions, whether rural and community hospitals remain accessible, whether people with disabilities receive necessary services, and whether millions of Americans can get care when they need it.

We’re coming together to make the consequences of those decisions visible and to make clear that elected officials like Mike Lawler must answer to the people whose healthcare hangs in the balance.

events.title: Mike Mondays: People Over Profits!

We’ll look back at the votes and policies that defined Lawler’s record, hear from people affected by decisions made in Washington, and connect the issues that too often get discussed separately.

The question running through this entire series has been simple: Who does our Mike Lawler work for?

The ONLY answer should be the people—not corporations, billionaires, wealthy donors, or politicians seeking to accumulate power.

This is bigger than one politician and bigger than one election. Democracy requires ordinary people to know what their representatives are doing, organize around the issues affecting their lives, and hold power accountable.

Know the record. Know your power. Organize your community. People over profits!

Our last phone bank is Sunday, November 1, from 4:00 to 5:00 PM.

events.title: 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence
events.description:
Each year since 2013, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation (NAAF), the charitable arm of the Newtown Action Alliance (NAA), and numerous partners in the gun violence prevention community have sponsored the National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on or near the anniversary of the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. These multidenominational events, held in Washington, D.C., at the National Cathedral and St. Mark’s Episcopal Church, bring together survivors of gun violence, victims’ family members, concerned citizens, faith leaders, lawmakers, leaders of gun violence prevention organizations, and activists from across the nation. 

The 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence will be held on Wednesday, December 9, 2026 from 7-9:00pm ET at St Marks Episcopal Church on Capitol Hill, Washington, D.C. 

December 14, 2026 is the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook tragedy. By this December, more than 1.4 million Americans will be killed or injured by guns since the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. We urge you to join the gun violence prevention community in our collective effort to continue to shine a light on the devastating epidemic of gun violence in our nation until these gun deaths and injuries are reduced. 

The victims, survivors and the families impacted by gun violence are often forgotten. We have lost our #FreedomToLive. Therefore, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation and the Newtown Action Alliance, in partnership with 160+ organizations  will host the annual national vigil service of mourning and loving remembrance for all who have fallen victim to the ongoing epidemic of gun violence in America. 

Our goal is simple. The gun violence prevention movement will unite to support the families and communities impacted by gun violence, educate, continue to raise awareness, and keep this critical issue front and center throughout our nation. Together, we will renew our vow to #HonorWithAction to #EndGunViolence in America by restoring our #FreedomFromGunViolence.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Belmont County, Ohio!
events.description:
Show solidarity with fellow progressive activists in rural Ohio! On July 18th, two Ground Truth canvassers in Belmont County, OH, were surrounded by 4 police cars. They were ordered to cease and desist from canvassing or face arrest for “Soliciting and Creating a Public Nuisance.” Of course, political canvassing door to door is constitutionally protected free speech. No permit or fee can be required, and it is definitely not grounds for arrest. One of the canvassers who was stopped was a Latino naturalized citizen, and racial profiling appeared to play a part.

We’re working with local candidates and activists, the ACLU, the County, the City, and the Police Department to make sure every area officer understands our rights and protect them. We remain focused on deep canvassing in Eastern Ohio and listening to our neighbors’ concerns. We are determined to strengthen voter participation through exercising our constitutional civil rights. We do not seek to escalate this situation. We are building mutual trust and respect with our neighbors.

WHAT YOU CAN DO TO HELP: The best thing you can do to help is to sign up for deep canvassing shifts with us in Belmont County, OH! We need folks now more than ever to stand in solidarity with us! 

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on every door in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

About the program

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- Why we’re starting early: We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big: knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Pierce County Postcard-Writing LAST 10 WEEKS!
events.description:
Join the mighty Pierce County Dems postcard writing team. It was a part of a three “touch” contact plan (doorknock/literature drop, phone call/voicemail message, and then the personalized postcard) all in a window of two weeks from the day we knock on their door. We identified hundreds of voters that weren’t previously ID’d and those we didn’t talk to, we are planting seeds of voting for Democrats.

Write 30-60 postcards with personalized messaging from home each week for the last 10 weeks til election day. Pick up your postcards, stamps, and list on Saturdays from Pierce Dems office in River Falls and then get the postcards done and in the mail by the end of the week. Easy, kinda fun, and powerful.

Reach out to Kelsey Davison for coordination 608-512-2820 or Terre Thomas 612-590-2954

Join Target Majority (a local Indivisible & Swing Left Group) for a Ground Truth canvass in must-FLIP PA-08.   

We are knocking every door and identifying persuadable voters who Dems normally don't contact, in order to elect Paige Cognetti in a true toss-up race in a Trump '24 district where she's recently demonstrated a 1-point lead.

To help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House, Swing Left has launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the voters campaigns usually talk to

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, identifying net new voters for the Democratic Party and candidates  

- Add these new voters' partisanship scores, likelihood to vote, and contact info directly into the Democrats' voter database so they will follow up with persuadable folks

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to people’s needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re started early and will continue every year:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground. Likewise, we'll continue this important work through 2027 ahead of 2028. (And beyond.)

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ internal conflicts around voting and around party affiliation, getting to the “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

**A core principle behind all Target Majority events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.**

events.title: Help Azalea Reach All of Maine House District 80
events.description:
Azalea needs volunteers willing to help get the word out about her candidacy - you signing up to help canvass or drive is how this gets achieved! 

For drivers: Azalea will meet you at a convenient location, and you'll help her get to the addresses included in a turf. Turfs take about 2-3 hours, but any amount of help is appreciated! This is also a great opportunity to learn how to canvass for those who haven't before. 

For canvassers: Azalea can get you a turf of your choice, both by location and political affiliation. Canvassing is not about convincing voters, but for getting information distributed in one of the most reliable ways - on people's doorsteps. She needs volunteers who can either primarily distribute material, or find strong supporters to help her reach her Maine Clean Elections goal (Buckfield, Hebron, Otisfield, and Oxford residents can donate $5 only at www.maine.gov/cleanelections). Training & tips provided if you need! 

For virtual participants: Text and Phonebankers are also incredibly helpful! By choosing the online option, you are signing up for a banking shift to reach out to strong likely supporters to make sure they've made their individual contribution and have a plan to vote. 

Azalea was born and raised here in the Western Foothills. Now, as a 28 year old, 2-term Selectman living in her hometown, she is perusing office at the State level out of frustration over poor rural representation, and to demand more legislative action beneficial to our inland economies. She will be fighting for working families, fair benefits, and prioritization of Mainers over wealth while in Augusta. See more at www.azafor.me

events.description:
Our Latham Bridge Brigade will be taking part in a special New York Thruway Project to remind NYS residents that their voices matter. Over 44 Thruway overpasses will be displaying 15-foot banners with messages encouraging voter participation. 

We will be displaying the banners from our usual spot on the Route 7 overpass at Old Loudon Road, rather than the Thruway, to take advantage of traffic heading for the Northway.

There are two banners to be used, so we need your help holding the banners in place. You can also bring your own signs or use one of ours. Bring noisemakers, bring a friend, bring family - all are welcome. 

Please sign up ASAP for one or more of the dates listed. This will be a fun and impactful protest, so we hope you can join us! As always, lots of free parking is available at St. Ambrose Church, just steps from the bridge.

Also, please note that the bridge brigade will start a bit earlier than usual on the NYS Thruway Project Saturdays.

events.title: Staff the Community Outreach Booth (2026)

location.venue: Findlay - Hancock County Public Library Grounds (weather permitting)

events.description:
Looking for an easy, social way to get involved locally?

We’re building a team of volunteers to regularly staff our pop-up Democratic booth outside the Library, typically on Saturday mornings and Sunday evenings.

People stop by to pick up candidate yard signs and literature, learn more about who’s running, ask questions, and find ways to get involved—and we need friendly volunteers there to welcome them.

You might help:

-Greet people who stop by
-Hand out yard signs and candidate literature
-Help visitors find information about our Democratic candidates
-Have friendly conversations about the people running to represent us
-Connect interested people with events and volunteer opportunities
-Keep signs and materials organized and stocked
-Help set up or pack up the booth
-Simply make our local Democratic Party feel visible, approachable, and welcoming

You do not need to be a political expert.

We’ll provide candidate information, literature, basic talking points, and experienced volunteers to help you get comfortable. You’re never expected to know every answer—or debate someone who wants an argument.

Sometimes the best response is simply:

“I’m not sure, but I can help you find out.”

And you don’t have to volunteer every weekend. Help once in a while, choose the dates that work for you, or become one of our regular volunteers who helps us keep the booth staffed consistently.

Whether you like talking with people, organizing materials, handing out signs, or just want a simple way to contribute a couple of hours, we can use your help.

Pick some shifts which work well for your schedule using the form below.

events.title: Weekday Door Knocking in Detroit!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!  Doors don't take a break during the week and neither do we - join us Tuesday through Friday to talk to voters.

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Post Election Review
events.description:
Minnesota takes election security seriously. Before the Election, we have the Public Accuracy Test. During the election, election judges ensure that the processes in the polling places follow the law. After the election, we have the Post Election Review. 

**[Minnesota Statutes 206.89](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/206.89)** states that after every state general election, Minnesota counties perform a post-election review of election results returned by the optical scan ballot counters used in the state.  The review is a hand count of the ballots for each eligible election (U.S. President, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, and Governor) in the selected precincts compared with the results from the voting system used in those precincts.

The post-election review is carried out by the County Canvassing Board, made up of the County Auditor (in St. Louis County, Nancy Nilsen), the Court Administrator of the District Court (Kim Vizena), the mayor/chair of the town board of the largest municipality in the County(Roger Reinert), and two County Commissioners (Patrick Boyle and Ken Musolf). 

Come witness this historic process. Our elections are precious. Maybe in prior years we could let this operate in the background. 2026 is different. 

Note: the starting time, 9 am is set, the ending time depends on how long it takes to review the selected precincts.

events.description:
Jump Jam is back on Saturday, on November 7th (rain date from October 10th), and we'd love to have you on the team!

Hosted at the Subaru of Spartanburg Bike Park, Jump Jam is PAL's annual bike park fundraiser featuring kids' bike races, amateur and professional dirt jump competitions, food trucks, vendors, and family activities. Every dollar raised helps support the maintenance and improvement of the bike park while introducing more children and families to cycling and outdoor recreation.

It takes an incredible team of volunteers to make the day possible! Whether you're helping set up before the event, checking in kids for the races, assisting along the course, or helping us pack everything up at the end of the day, your time makes a real difference.

Three volunteer shifts are available throughout the day, and every volunteer will receive a PAL T-shirt. No previous experience is necessary - just bring comfortable clothes, closed-toe shoes, and a willingness to jump in and help!

Shift Descriptions:

10:00 AM - 1:00 PM | Set Up

Help transform the bike park for Jump Jam! Volunteers will assist with setting up tents, tables, banners, signs, inflatables, race course signage, vendor areas, and other event equipment before participants arrive.

1:00 PM - 4:00 PM | Kids Ride & Check-In

Help make the Kids Ride a success by checking in participants, distributing race T-shirts, lining kids up by age group, holding age group signs, directing riders along the course, and handing out finisher medals.

4:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Crowd Voting & Breakdown

Walk through the crowd with QR codes so attendees can vote for the Best Style competition, then stay after the awards ceremony to help the PAL team break down the event, pack equipment, and clean up the park.

Thank you for helping PAL create another unforgettable Jump Jam. We couldn't do it without you!

We have the chutzpah to protect the people and places we love. This fall, it's all hands on deck to build people power for our climate, our democracy, and a livable future.


We'll be rallying to mobilize every single climate voter to get to the polls for the midterm elections -- and put our future before fossil fuel profits.

At each shift, we ground ourselves in Jewish wisdom, go over the scripts, then get to work calling voters. 

If you've already been trained by Dayenu or the Environmental Voter Project, you can jump right into calling. If this is your first time phone banking, no worries; we'll train you before you start calling.

All you need to participate is a phone (landline or cell) and a web-enabled computer or tablet. Closed captioning is available and Scale to Win is compatible with most screen readers.

events.title: Poll Observer Training
events.description:
Poll Observers serve as the campaign’s eyes and ears on Election Day providing critical, real-time information to the campaign about any issues arising at polling locations across the state. The campaign will assign poll observers to serve at a polling location based on the poll observer’s availability and willingness to travel. In New Hampshire, poll observers are not required to be New Hampshire voters or residents.

In this training we will go over the basics NH Election Law, Frequently Asked Questions, and an overview of the reporting system.

This training is for volunteering for the General Election on Tuesday, November 3rd!

events.title: Cook County door knock for Trina Swanson
events.description:
The November 3rd General Election is fast approaching and to unseat Pete and get Trina elected, conversations need to happen early!

Join us in Grand Marais at 530PM for a simple training at the First Congregational Church. For this Door Knock, we will need people who are able to drive. We plan on going out of Grand Marais, further South to more rural parts of the county.

Join #TeamTrina as we hit the doors to talk with voters across the district. Canvassing is the single most effective way to connect with our neighbors and build the momentum we need to win on Election Day.

This is your opportunity to help elect Trina Swanson to Congress and support DFL candidates up and down the ballot. Together, we can reach voters, share our vision for Northeast Minnesota, and build the grassroots movement it takes to win.

No experience? No problem! Every shift begins with a brief training, so whether it's your first time canvassing or you're a seasoned volunteer, we'll make sure you have everything you need before heading out. Feel free to bring a friend, or we'll pair you up with another volunteer.

Please bring a charged phone, comfortable walking shoes, and something to keep you hydrated.

Every door knocked and every conversation brings us one step closer to victory. We hope you'll join us!

events.description:
Join Kaylee Peterson for another Virtual Fireside Chat. We’ll take a closer look at recent public comments and policy decisions from Representative Russ Fulcher, discuss where I stand on the issues that matter to Idahoans, and, most importantly, answer all your questions.
Have a question about healthcare, the economy, public lands, workers’ rights, or government accountability? Want to hear my response to something Rep. Fulcher has said or done? Bring it on. I want to hear what’s on your mind, and I’ll make time to answer your questions directly.

ORIGINAL EVENT CANCELLED. EXPLANATION BELOW:
***Unfortunately, the forum will no longer take place as originally planned. In an effort to make the event as fair and balanced as possible, we transitioned organization of the forum to a nonpartisan organization. During that transition, the venue originally scheduled to host the event decided not to move forward with hosting it. These circumstances were outside our campaign’s control, and with less than a week before the event, we had to make a decision about how best to move forward.

Rather than let that opportunity to connect with voters pass us by, our team accepted an invitation to travel to North Idaho to meet with voters in person. There will also be another candidate forum in Moscow on October 23, featuring both myself and the Independent candidate, hosted by Indivisible. We’re working to make that event available online as well.

If you know how to throw great parties that people can’t wait to attend, know a fantastic fundraising auction when you see one, or want to be part of an event that truly makes a positive impact in our world, we have an opportunity to share with you.

Each year, Food & Water Watch hosts an annual benefit event, Against All Odds, with an in-person New York City reception and an online virtual program — and we want your help! Against All Odds is all about coming together, cheering on our victories, and raising critical funds needed to protect our food, water, and climate. 

**Our Benefit Host Committee, a select group of dedicated Food & Water Watch supporters, not only helps make it all possible, they also make the event fun, exciting, and movement-building.**

Host Committee Members work directly with Food & Water Watch staff to shape aspects of the event that foster a sense of community, boost our fundraising efforts, and increase the reach of our donor-activists, ultimately resulting in a highly engaging and successful benefit. 

**Does this sound like something YOU want to be part of? Sign up to chat with our team and learn more about being part of the committee that makes it all happen.**

events.title: Durham Canvass to Defeat Harmful Constitutional Amendments
events.description:
A handful of state lawmakers want to scam our community with two constitutional amendments on the ballot this fall. These amendments will let big corporations and rich people skip paying what they owe while working people pick up the tab. Neither amendment will save everyday people any money. If these amendments pass, it could mean billions of dollars in cuts to our schools, health care, and other public services. 

Durham For All and Durham Public School Strong are partnering to mobilize thousands of people to vote against these harmful amendments and demand that corporations and billionaires pay what they owe in taxes so our kids, educators, and communities have what they need to succeed.

Join us as we knock on our neighbors' doors or talk with people at community events to get the word out about these harmful amendments and make sure they are defeated at the polls! 

If you’ve never canvassed before, or if you just heard about these amendments yourself, that's okay! We will equip you with talking points and help you shape and share your story of why this matters to you. All canvassing will happen in pairs, so bring a buddy and/or come prepared to make a new friend.

There will be Spanish interpretation and childcare at the launch site for all weekend canvassing shifts.

events.title: "Flip Flops on the Ground" Literature  Drop
events.description:
Democracy is NOT a spectator sport—and Arizona can finally change!

Did you know the last time Democrats held the majority in the Arizona House was 1966? For nearly 60 years, single-party control has shaped our state, leading to issues that impact our families every single day:

Packed Classrooms: Composite state rankings consistently place Arizona public education near the bottom (48th to 51st). While state averages mask the crisis, actual core classrooms (Math, English, Science) regularly pack 30–35+ students into a single room with low teacher retention and bottom-tier funding.

Corporate Loophole: Arizona is now one of the least affordable states to live in, yet under state law (A.R.S. § 43-1111), over 80% of corporate filers pay only the $50 minimum state tax floor (JLBC data), leaving working families to carry the load.

We have the power to change this.

Tempe Rising Indivisible is organizing "Flip Flops on the Ground" Lit Drop shifts to get crucial campaign information into the hands of voters across key neighborhoods.

🎯 Our Target Districts
Protect & Hold (Keep Blue): Legislative Districts 9 & 12

Flip the House & Commission (Turn Blue): Legislative District 13 & Congressional District 5

👟 How You Can Help
Walkers: Come get your steps in! Whether you have 1 hour, 2 hours, or 3 hours, every neighborhood covered matters.

Drivers Needed: Prefer driving over walking? We urgently need drivers to transport lit drop teams and cover larger routes!

We provide all materials, turf maps, and a brief launch overview before you head out. Bring water, comfortable shoes, and a friend!

Together, we can flip Arizona. Sign up today or check out our latest videos to learn more:

Please note the address given is the meeting place.  Please be on time and or check the event chat.
