events.title: Protect the Vote: Outside Poll Observer On-Demand Training
events.description:
# Protect the Vote as an Outside Poll Observer

Every voter deserves the chance to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Outside Poll Observers help identify potential issues outside voting locations and report concerns so they can be addressed quickly. Most shifts are calm and routine, and you will never be expected to handle situations on your own. We'll provide the training, resources, and support you need to be successful.

## What You'll Learn

- Outside Poll Observer basics
- What to expect outside a voting location
- Updated guidance for situations observers may encounter this fall
- What to look for and how to document issues
- How to report concerns and get support
- The role Outside Poll Observers play in protecting voters

## Why It Matters

With critical elections ahead, we need trained volunteers in every corner of North Carolina.

Outside Poll Observers help us understand what is happening around voting locations, identify potential barriers or concerns, and make sure issues are quickly reported to the appropriate team.

Whether you've done this work before or are brand new, we'll help you get ready.

## No Prior Experience Required

We'll provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel confident serving as an Outside Poll Observer.

### Recommended Prerequisite

We encourage you to attend a Know Your Rights training in addition to this session. It provides important background on North Carolina election law and voter protections that will help you succeed as an Outside Poll Observer.

Sign up here: https://www.mobilize.us/nc-coordinated/event/953390/

### After signing up, you'll be directed to the recorded training video and next steps.

events.title: Anytime Virtual Phone Banking: Clyde for Congress
events.description:
Phone Bank for Clyde on Your Own Schedule

We know your schedule is busy, so we have made it easier than ever to make a difference on your own time. Sign up to make calls for the Clyde Jones for Congress campaign whenever it fits into your day—whether that is for 15 minutes between errands or two hours on a Sunday afternoon.

Phone banking is the fastest way to scale our grassroots outreach and talk directly with voters across Alabama's 1st Congressional District about lowering healthcare costs, fighting for working families, and bringing accountability back to Washington. With our flexible phone banking system, you can pull up a list and start dialing whenever you have free time.

How it Works:

Sign Up: Register here to receive instant access to our virtual phone bank hub. Your confirmation email will include details for how to start making calls right away from wherever you are. 

Start Dialing: Log in from any computer, tablet, or smartphone. 

Log the Data: Simply select the outcome of your call on the screen, follow the script to chat with the voter, and click to move to the next neighbor!

What You Need:

A laptop, desktop, or tablet with internet access.

A quiet, comfortable place to make calls.

Your unique login link (sent immediately upon RSVP).

Every call moves us one step closer to victory. Secure your access today and start dialing when it works best for you! For technical support or questions along the way, our organizing team is just an email or text away.

events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: De-Flock Mitchell County
events.description:
DE-FLOCK MITCHELL. Are you unhappy with your comings and goings in Mitchell being recorded by Flock and searchable nationwide?

On Sept 8 14 people went to speak at the commissioners meeting (12 against flock, 2 for) and at the end of the meeting the commissioners decided not to take up the question of cancelling flock and instead kick the can down the road to the next commission after the Nov election. events.title: Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm
events.description:
#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. 

#### Join by Zoom .. The Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday sessions: Burnout - ZOOM at 9:00 a.m. & This is the Plan @4pm CST, -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

events.title: Calling voters in Pennsylvania's 7th!

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
### The election is around the corner. Let’s turn our anxiety into action!

We the Fighters is a group of everyday people who have decided to step up. In the face of injustice, we choose to act together over despairing alone. And we’re inviting you to join us.

We’ll be calling voters in our district to talk about our representative’s vote for the “Big Beautiful Bill,” what it has meant for our lives, and our chance to hold them accountable this November.

**We use an approach called deep canvassing:** asking meaningful questions, sharing personal stories, and making space for people to talk about what matters to them. We believe those connections are how we build the power to change things.

### Never done anything like this? You’re exactly who we need.
You don’t need political experience or all the answers. Bring yourself, a willingness to listen, and the belief that everyday people deserve better.

We’ll train you before your first call and support you along the way.

events.title: Honesty Coalition 2026 LGBTQ+ Youth & Parents Listening Session
events.description:
This session is for students and their parents. We'll have two rooms in the Zoom—so parents and students can speak freely with their peers!

The Belonging for Every Student Listening Campaign is a statewide effort to better understand how recent anti-LGBTQ+ laws are shaping the experiences of students, educators, and families across Ohio.

Over the past few years, laws like House Bill 8 have required all 611 school districts in Ohio to adopt new policies. While these policies are public record, what remains unclear is how they are being put into practice and how they are impacting real people in school communities.

This autumn, we are listening. We want to know: How are districts implementing these policies? Are schools going beyond what the law requires? How are LGBTQ+ students and families being affected? What changes are educators experiencing in their classrooms, materials, and ability to support students?

By gathering stories, insights, and data from across the state, this campaign will help build a clearer picture of what’s happening on the ground. These findings will directly inform advocacy strategies for the 2026–2027 school year, ensuring that efforts to support safe, inclusive, and equitable schools are rooted in the lived experiences of Ohio communities.

Please share with young Ohioans who have something to say about the experiences of LQBTQ+ students in our schools in the 2026-2027 school year.

events.title: Poll Greeting for Early Voting at Brambleton Center (1-2 hour shifts, NOT ALL DAY)
events.description:
We need your help to cover the polls in Roanoke County for early voting! Sign up to be a smiling poll greeter where you can welcome voters to the polls and hand out sample ballots with the names of Democratic candidates and information on 3 proposed state constitution amendments.

Shifts are typically 2 hours, but you can do more or less. When you sign up for a given day, a representative of the Roanoke County Democratic Committee will call you to coordinate a specific time slot(s).

Voters who cast their votes for Democratic candidates want to see themselves represented! You can be the Democratic poll greeter that lifts our voters up and makes them feel validated and proud to be a Democrat!

Poll-greeting is a simple activity. As voters come to the polls, simply ask if they would like a sample ballot. If so, then hand them one and point out that there is also information on the sample ballot about the proposed state constitutional amendments which they will also be voting on.  It is that easy! As voter leave the polls, thank them for coming out and voting.

Feel free to bring a friend or come alone!

events.title: Hop on the Bus to Maine to flip the Senate!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Maine—a must-win Swing State—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Troy Jackson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Davis Square at 8:30am and return around 7:30pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

**Dangerous nitrates linked to cancer have been found in Iowa’s drinking water, and we need your help to fight back.** We're bringing more people into our movement by having conversations and spreading awareness among our neighbors, igniting a spark that leads to taking action.

_Join our weekly one-hour virtual training on having Conversations for Clean Water!_ You will learn how to have meaningful conversations with neighbors about the water crisis and next steps in the fight for clean water.

This year, Food & Water Action fought the Iowa legislature to restore our statewide water monitoring program and _sued the EPA_ to protect Iowa’s drinking water. Now, we’re talking to our neighbors statewide to understand how the crisis is affecting everyday Iowans and provide meaningful ways to fight back. **Help build the movement to fight for what Iowans deserve.**

Together, we'll learn about what we can do to keep our water safe and send a clear message to elected officials: **stop putting Big Ag ahead of working families.**

events.title: The People's Tea
events.description:
Join us for “The People’s Tea,” a biweekly power hour where we’ll discuss what’s going on, what it means, and what we can do. 

At the People’s Tea, we will slow down, process the news, and make sense of what’s happening. We’re building a space where we can stay informed without losing our humanity (and sanity), and move from feeling overwhelmed and isolated toward understanding, connection, and collective action. 

We will meet every other Wednesday at 8 PM Eastern / 7 PM Central / 6 PM Mountain / 5 PM Pacific. There’s only one requirement to join. This will be a judgment-free space where we will show compassion and curiosity. We simply expect you to be respectful and non-judgmental. There are no expectations to have all the answers, know the “right” things, or even know where to begin. 

Come learn, listen, and connect.

Other notes: 
- There are two garages backing onto Vaden Drive; one on the Vienna side of the highway and one on the Fairfax side.  You need a credit card or metro card to exit the garages; weekday parking is $4.95.   Neighborhood parking is very limited.
- Bring water, hat, snacks, folding chairs, and sunscreen as needed for your own comfort.  Please take any litter home with you.
- Please be cautious if you cross Vaden Drive for the other side of the bridge.
- There is a public restroom in the Metro station.
- Check your email in case there is a last minute change. The event may be altered due to rain or extreme temperatures.
- We will do one Thurs in Oct (the 22nd) because early voting at the Jim Scott Rec Center on Vaden Drive starts there Oct 22 and runs to 7 PM.
- Most drivers react positively to our messaging.  If you receive a negative reaction, please remain positive (or at least neutral) to avoid escalating the situation.
- We must not block pedestrians getting across the bridge, so please leave room on the back end of the bridge sidewalks for pedestrians.
- No weapons of any kind and no violence. 
- If you wish to bring friends or family members with you, they are welcome. Please familiarize them with our rules and safety tips.

Our mission is to bring visibility to specific issues we're facing under the Trump regime, encourage action, and foster a sense of community for those that feel disheartened by the state of our nation. Join us and help us fight fascism!

Learn more about the Visibility Brigade at www.visibilitybrigade.com

events.title: Queer Out the Vote Traverse City - Canvass for EQMI
events.description:
In 2025 and 2026 alone, more than 20 anti-transgender bills were introduced in the Michigan House of Representatives. Bathroom bans. Sports bans. A legislative package designed to strip access to transgender healthcare young people and families who need it in Michigan. We were able to ensure none of these bills passed because we showed up!

We know that previous gains can be lost and further progress can be jeopardized when we stop showing up. What happens this November will determine whether Michigan continues to be a place where LGTBQ+ people can live openly, access the healthcare they need to thrive, and be treated with dignity. 

When Equality Voters Turn Out, Equality Moves Forward!

When equality voters turnout, we move Michigan forward. And nobody is more equipped to engage the LGBTQ+ community and our allies than Equality Michigan. That’s why we need your help this summer and fall, knocking on our neighbors doors, meeting them face-to-face, making sure they have the info they need to vote and the inspiration they need to stay engaged long after November 3rd, to hold our elected officials accountable.

Sign up TODAY!

	•	Brief training and script walkthrough at the start of each shift
	•	Calls made through our online dialer, no special equipment beyond your computer and headset
	•	Campaign staff or skilled volunteers on hand the whole time to answer questions
	•	Join from anywhere: home, dorm, couch, wherever you’ve got wifi

What you need:

	•	A computer with internet access
	•	A headset (for clear calls and to keep your hands free)

Join the Capital District Area Labor Federation, AFL-CIO as we make calls to union members across the Capital District in support of our AFL-CIO endorsed candidates in the November 3 General Election.

Whether you’re a seasoned volunteer or making calls for the first time, everyone is welcome!

All you need to participate is:

A cell phone
A laptop, desktop computer, or tablet
A few hours to help us turn out union members this election!

The Zoom link and additional instructions will be emailed to registered participants prior to each phone bank.

When union members stand together, our voices are stronger. Sign up, make some calls, and help us turn out the union vote on November 3!

events.title: Virtual Phone Bank
events.description:
One Team will be hosting phone banks to connect with voters across districts all over the state, identifying and mobilizing voters who care about fairness, inclusion, and justice for all.

These phone banks are one of the most effective ways to build real momentum heading into the midterm elections. By having direct conversations, we’re not only helping people get engaged early, we’re also gathering critical information that will guide our strategy for the months ahead.

The data we collect now helps us understand which areas are energized, where we need to focus more outreach, and how to tailor our message to meet people where they are. This groundwork will be essential as we ramp up organizing and mobilization efforts for the midterm elections.

Whether you’re a seasoned volunteer or brand new to phone banking, we’ll provide all the training and tools you need. Every call makes a difference and every volunteer helps build the foundation for equality and progress!

This event is virtual but you will need:

Please have a laptop, phone, and headphones to utilize for each phone bank. We’ll provide all the training, scripts, and support you need to feel confident making calls.

Every volunteer, every call, and every conversation helps strengthen our movement for equality and progress. Join us bi-weekly and help us make a difference, one call at a time!

events.title: Signs of GOTV Visibility Event - Watsonville

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**Join Indivisible Pajaro Valley for our new Get Out The Vote roadside rally!**

This event is modeled on the Signs of Fascism protests but is all about encouraging people to register and vote. Here's what to expect:

- The protest will last about an hour 
- Please dress colorfully (perhaps in red, white, and blue!) and wear comfortable shoes.
- We will stand spaced 10-15 feet apart by the side of the road, and each person will hold one sign.
- Our signs are in English on one side and in Spanish on the other side, so we will periodically switch languages all at the same time.
- This is not a somber protest the way Signs of Fascism is! When possible, we will have music. Feel free to bring a flag to wave, and to dance!

We will need a minimum of 15 people to have the most impact. We have 20 signs, so we can have up to 20 sign holders - but we will need a few additional folks to record, keep an eye out for any hazards or disruptions, and keep the sign-holders coordinated.

events.title: Westwood Baptist Church Presents: StayAwake Bi-Weekly Check-Ins
events.description:
StayAwake Bi-Weekly Check-Ins are our virtual gathering space to stay informed, stay engaged, and stay ready for the **November 3rd General Election** and the ongoing work of protecting our communities. 

Every other Thursday, we come together to learn what’s on the ballot, understand the issues **impacting our communities**, and explore practical ways each of us can be the difference.

These sessions help us live out the three **StayAwake** Commitments:

- **Dinner Table Conversations** — learning how to talk with family and friends about what matters most.

- **Voter Registration & Education** — helping others check their registration status, apply for absentee ballots, and get fully election ready.

- **Petition Campaigns** — adding your name to efforts that hold politicians accountable and protect the rights of Black people at home and across the nation.

events.title: Weekday Door Knocking in Brighton!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!  Doors don't take a break during the week and neither do we - join us Tuesday through Friday to talk to voters.

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Butte Door Knocking
events.description:
Nothing beats talking to a voter on their doorstep about Sam! Join Sam's Crew for a day of knocking doors around Butte. We'll meet at our campaign office at the Carpenter's Union Hall, where we'll train you on how to knock doors for Sam and you'll get a chance to practice before you head out.

We'll have a list of doors for you to knock, the script for your conversations, and a handy reference sheet on Sam's background and platform that you can carry with you. After everybody has knocked doors for a couple hours, we'll reconvene to debrief how it all went with some cold refreshments!

You do not need to have knocked a single door before this event - this is for beginners and experts alike! Talking in person with voters is one of the most effective and rewarding ways to spread the word about Sam, and we'll make sure you have the skills and tools to feel confident to get out there!

events.title: Solidarity Saturdays: Midterms are HERE!
events.description:
Early Voting gets underway on October 17. It's time to show our numbers!

Stand in solidarity with friends, neighbors, and community members on **October 24, for Solidarity Saturdays (11am-1pm)**. Together we are stronger!

We will gather on the sidewalk of the Nevada Legislative Building to raise our voices, uplift one another, and show that our community refuses to be silent in the face of abuses of power.

Bring your protest signs, your passion, and your commitment to defending democracy. Whether you’re a seasoned advocate or showing up for the first time, your presence matters. Let’s stand together. Let’s speak out. Let’s make our voices impossible to ignore.

🦺 PLEASE NOTE: Our rallies are nonviolent. When there are one or more aggressive counter protesters at our events, the best way to respond is to ignore and de-escalate. De-escalation includes staying calm, maintaining your distance, using a calm voice, and having a neutral stance. If you are concerned about your or someone else's safety, please go tell a security team member in a yellow vest. Remember, counter protestors are exercising their first amendment rights just as we are-- but we also don't want a situation to escalate or to lead to any violent behaviors. 

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Georgia GOTV Phone Bank
events.description:
GA Ossoff Weekly Phone Bank — Every Thursday

Join us as we call Georgia voters to help them return their mail ballots and make a final plan to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.

Every week, we're reaching voters across Georgia to make sure they're ready to participate in one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide the outcome—we're making sure no voter is left behind.

We'll help voters who have already requested mail ballots complete and return them on time, understand key deadlines, and make a clear, confident plan to vote, whether by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send follow-up texts with early voting, polling location, and absentee ballot tracking information to those planning to vote early or on Election Day.

Volunteers will have real conversations with voters and help turn intention into action—making sure ballots are returned and votes are counted.

📞 Weekly phone bank: Thursdays at 12p.m. PT / 3p.m. ET (every week through Election Day)
🔥 No experience needed—training, scripts, and support provided.

This is how we win close races, by making sure every vote counts.
Your call could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Georgia!

events.title: Intro to Abolitionist Feminisms Series: Intro to Abolitionist Feminisms Panel
events.description:
Hear from organizers and advocates in a conversation about abolitionist feminism, transformative justice, incarceration, and what it means to build movements rooted in collective liberation. This panel will connect the ideas explored throughout the series to the work happening in our communities today.
Panelists include Florida NOW members Sana Hafeez and Amaria Smith, as well as Miss Mei with Decrim305 and Hugo with Success Stories, the program featured in the film we are screening, The Feminist on Cell Block Y.
Stay after the panel for a brief Q&A chat. The panel will be recorded and uploaded to YouTube.

events.title: Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club Discussion: Abolition. Feminism. Now.
events.description:
Join the Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club for a discussion of Abolition. Feminism. Now. by Angela Y. Davis, Gina Dent, Erica R. Meiners, and Beth E. Richie.

n this groundbreaking book, four leading abolitionist feminist thinkers and organizers explore the history and present-day practice of abolition, drawing connections between struggles against prisons, policing, racism, gender-based violence, and economic injustice. The authors examine abolition not simply as an effort to dismantle systems of punishment, but as a project of building the social, political, and economic conditions that allow communities to thrive.

The book brings together decades of feminist organizing, scholarship, and movement-building to ask what it means to imagine a world beyond punishment, and how we begin creating that world now.

Join us for a conversation about the book’s central ideas, the movements and histories it explores, and what abolitionist feminism can teach us about building a more just and liberatory future.

Monday, December 21st, at 6:30 PM on Zoom

All are welcome, whether you’ve finished the book, are still reading, or are joining the conversation to learn more.

events.description:
Join us in Birmingham for a Young People's Hearing on Sex Ed in Alabama! This year Alabama Senate Bill 209 to mandate Abstinence Only Until Marriage Curriculum in all K-12 public schools and removing ANY sex ed from being taught K-4 passed. We, our young people, and our organizational partners mounted a 3-year legislative fight against this bill and it will go into effect on October 1, 2026. 

We will commune over dinner provided by URGE and start with a quick policy training on how to hold your state legislators accountable to the way they voted on this bill AND we'll have postcards right there :)  

The goal of this event goes beyond just legislative advocacy and is to create a safe space for our young 18-30 yo BIPOC LGBTQ+ member base to come together and hold their own People's Hearing on sex education in Alabama and share how it has shaped/does shape their lives. We'll close out with a relational organizing training by our State Organizer to discuss how we take the power we built back into our communities. 

For admission to the event, we are asking folks to bring menstrual products to support Yellowhammer Fund's community care work. No one will be turned away if they don't have a donation. 
Preferred products are Honey Pot pads & wipes, Playtex, U by Kotex, Cora, L. organic tampons, Monthly period panties.

To keep our community safe, you MUST register to attend this event, and we will close registration 24 hours before the event.

This event is a collaboration between URGE Alabama, Yellowhammer Fund, & the Alabama Youth Activist Alliance in the Alabama Reproductive Health, Rights, & Justice Coalition

events.title: Beyond the Ballot #4: Storytelling for Change
events.description:
What if the story you almost decided wasn’t important enough to tell is _exactly_ the story someone needs to hear?

**Facts tell us how big a problem is. Stories show us who is living inside it.**

Behind every policy debate is a human experience: a parent struggling to find childcare, a teacher watching a student fall through the cracks, a young person wondering whether adults are listening, a family trying to stay housed.

Your experience may carry more power than you realize.

**_Storytelling for Change_** will help you turn lived experience into a story that can move hearts, illuminate an issue, and inspire action.

And you won’t just learn about storytelling. You’ll begin building a story you can actually use with an elected official, in your congregation, at a community meeting, or anywhere your voice could help move someone from understanding an issue to caring enough to act.

You don’t need to be a public speaker. You don’t need a dramatic story. And you don’t need to “perform.”

You already have a story. Come learn how to make it move.

This is Workshop 4 of Beyond the Ballot, and we are almost at the culmination. We’ve explored voting, advocacy, and relationships. Now we add story.

Then, in Workshop 5, we bring it all together.

Don’t stop one conversation short.

#### Beyond the Ballot
A non-partisan 5-part virtual workshop series equipping faith communities and everyday people to lead with purpose before, during, and long after Election Day.

events.title: Beyond the Ballot #5: Building Beloved Community

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**What if we stopped trying to change the world alone?**

One person can vote. One person can call a legislator. One person can tell a powerful story, but lasting change takes all of us.

**_Building Beloved Community_** is where the entire **_Beyond the Ballot_** journey comes together. And after four virtual workshops, we’re gathering **IN PERSON**.

We’re going to practice building community. Across generations, faith traditions, race, culture, experience, and difference.

You’ll meet people you may never otherwise encounter, explore what builds trust and collective power, discover the gifts and influence already present in the room, and ask one big question:

**What could we accomplish if we stopped working separately and started working together? ****

If you joined us for the first four workshops, do not stop now. This is where the journey has been leading.

If this is your first one, come anyway. There is room for you here.

Children and families are facing challenges too big for isolated people, congregations, and organizations to solve alone.

**We need each other.**

This isn’t just the end of a workshop series. It’s the beginning of what comes next.

**Somebody has to build the community we keep saying we want. Why not us? Why not now?**

#### Beyond the Ballot
A non-partisan 5-part virtual workshop series equipping faith communities and everyday people to lead with purpose before, during, and long after Election Day.

events.title: DCCC Rural Action Cohort Phonebanks
events.description:
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee's (DCCC) National Rural Engagement program is welcoming volunteers for our Rural Action Cohort for the 2025-2026 election cycle!

What is the Rural Action Cohort?

The DCCC Rural Action Cohort is a newly created initiative built of and by rural folks and will be doing rural-specific, virtual, direct voter contact to rural voters across our battleground districts with each session offering participants exposure and connections with leading national and statewide rural organizations across the country to help build the different toolboxes, infrastructure, and efforts of our cohort in our own communities.

It is a virtual opportunity for like-minded rural volunteers and committed leaders to build a community specifically for mobilizing our networks and taking regular action to take back the House with a coalition that reflects our communities.

We know that we must both build lasting infrastructure and do direct action and outreach to meet this moment and build lasting change for our folks on the ground. We hope this to be a starting point that can be scaled in cycles to come.

The virtual cohort will be active leading up to the Election with activation including phonebanks, text banks, and Days of Action targeting key House districts that are part of our path to victory while the emphasis is placed on being OF rural folk, BY rural folk, and FOR rural folk!

events.title: Weekly Doorknocking with No Hate in WA State in Whatcom

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
What to expect

New to canvassing? That’s completely okay! No experience is required, and we’ll start every shift with a short training so everyone feels prepared before heading to the doors.

We’ll meet together at the Community First Whatcom office, go over the basics of the conversation, show everyone how to record who they spoke with at the door, and get paired up before heading out to canvass in the community.

For your first shift, you can shadow an experienced canvasser so you can hear how they talk with folks at the door and get comfortable before jumping into conversations yourself.

Most of the shift will be spent walking through a neighborhood and having short conversations with voters. You do not need to memorize a script or be an expert. We’ll provide the information, materials, and support you need.

Please bring:

A fully charged smartphone
Comfortable walking shoes
Weather-appropriate clothing
Water and anything else you may need while walking

Additional details, resources, talking points, MiniVAN instructions, and arrival information will be sent after signup so you have everything you need to feel prepared for your shift.

Why door knocking matters

Most of us have had an election where the ballot showed up and we realized we hadn’t researched everything on it yet, or where voting almost slipped our minds altogether. One of the most effective ways to help people participate is simply reaching them before their ballot arrives, having a one-on-one conversation, and making sure they know what is on the ballot and why it matters.

Those conversations can make a real difference. Here in Whatcom County, the 2026 primary for the 42nd Legislative District Senate race came down to just four votes between two candidates.

If knocking on doors sounds intimidating, know that canvassing is typically a really positive experience. We’ll be reaching out to voters who regularly participate in elections and having short, friendly conversations with people in our community. You’ll also be out there alongside other volunteers, not doing it alone.

Rob is visiting every corner of the state to share his vision of an Iowa that isn’t Redder or Bluer, but Better and Truer with voters, and so are we! Whether you’re a long-time volunteer or stepping up to help for the first time, we’ve got you covered.

Before knocking doors, we will make sure everyone gets trained on how to talk to voters, how to record canvassing data, and canvassing best practices. Then, we’ll hit the pavement.

Election Day will be here before we know it! We have times every day through November 3rd, and we need your help!  Find more events here: https://www.mobilize.us/iowaforward/

We can't wait to see you!

Never made calls before? No problem! Whether you are a seasoned veteran or making calls for the first time, all you'll need is your computer and a phone. events.title: TTU Tabling
events.description:
Are you serious about turning the tide in Texas? Are you tired of sitting on the sidelines and ready to make a difference? If you answered yes, then you have come to the right place!

You must complete a Zoom volunteer training for Reach App and Events if this is your first time working with Powered by People. This is a recorded training you can do at your own time Pre-Recorded Field Volunteer Training (Self-Paced))*

https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/ 
Live Training: https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/884993/

To register voters at this event, you must be a current 2025/2026 certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar in at least LUBBOCK COUNTY. Click here to sign up for VDR training (https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908495/).

NON-VDR VOLUNTEERS WELCOME TO ASSIST WITH REGISTRATION CHECKS You will help us make sure all registered voters are still active or if they need an update. You will also stay in contact with the voter until election day.

events.description:

We need volunteers like YOU to help us maintain a presence outside the Senior Center, hand out sample ballots to voters who need them, and talk with voters about the three Constitutional Amendments on the ballot. Sign up for two or three shifts between now and Election Day to Keep Loudoun Blue!

Thank you for participating in your democracy.

events.description:
This a local Indivisible event! Open to All. Bring your signs and outrage over this criminal regime and its actions. We meet at The Coos Bay Boardwalk and the blocks surrounding it contain city parking lots and small businesses on Hwy 101 Northbound and Southbound. Bring a chair for your comfort or plan on walking through the rally. We have amplified sound with contemporary protest music creating a party atmosphere. We share community and fellowship, you are not alone in your outrage!

events.title: Carrollton Democrats BLUE HQ POP-UP

address_lines: North Josey Lane & East Peters Colony Road

events.description:
Carrollron Democrats are setting up on THE BLUE TRAIL in Carrollton - Josey & Peter's Colony every weekend - alternating between Saturday and Sunday until the month of October - when we will be there Saturday AND Sunday 10-noon thru November 1st.  This is next to the newly installed Pavillion and Kayak Launch. 

Offering ICE WATER to joggers, runners, bikers to get them to stop. Then offering them a candidate slate sheet, an invitation to our Carrollton Dems picnic Sept 26th, info on Carrollton Dems, then handing them an assortment of campaign literature we have for all candidates. (They really appreciate getting their hands on the candidate lit).  😊 🇺🇸

It's also a place for folks driving by to get SIGNS for James Talarico , Gina Hinojosa, Vikki Goodwin and Steven Shook. And any other candidate who wants their signs distributed.

We have voter registration forms (with instructions). And folks can take a selfie with a LIFE SIZE TALARICO. Courtesy of Joanna Cattanach of BLUE HQ in Dallas.

Of course - we will be asking for DONATIONS to defray Carrollton Democrats efforts to GOTV in Carrollton. Join us in our 20-20-20 Initiative to educate and encourage voters to come out for EVERY election. 

*****
Suggested Donations:
*****One Sign for $20*
*****Two Signs for $30*
*****Four Signs for $50*
*****
Oh - we take CASH, Zelle, Venmo, and Square
*****
 
Not only do folks give happy honks when they see "HERE Talarico" signs posted on the street - they also stop and visit!  As word of mouth grows - hope to have many more visitors stopping by. Even had one fella ask about changing from Republican to Democrat. YEAH. Our role and goal is to educate, create informed voters - who continuously turn out for elections!

Help show our neighbors we support TALARICO and all our candidates down ballot by placing a SIGN or two in your yard. Help us fund our 20-20-20 Initiative. We will be creating literature for mailings and door to door lit drops in Carrollton neighborhoods. Dallas and Denton counties. Will have weekly "parties" in various homes and coffee shops where participants are asked to bring 20 stamps, write 20 short notes about why voting in the November 3rd election is so important, (4 templates available), and stuff and hand address 20 envelopes. If unable to donate 20 stamps - there will be stamps available. 🐝

Folks are actually HUNGRY for a change. So important to keep up the momentum - we have to have HUGE numbers they can't overcome with billions in spending. We are going to need a ground swell to break loose from the crippling and insane pillaging of our country by BLOATUS and his BILLIONAIRE cronies.

Remember - VOTE EARLY - and vote DEMOCRAT all the way to the BOTTOM of the ballot. And bring your family, friends and neighbors with you out to VOTE. 🗳

*********
Your DONATION funds Carrollton Democrats efforts to GOTV (Get Out The Vote). Our mission is to educate voters and enable them to VOTE in every election. 
**********

events.title: Team Lindsey: Wilson County Canvass (Mt. Juliet) Weeknights and Evenings

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Team Lindsey every Saturday as we talk with voters across Wilson County and build the grassroots movement needed to win Tennessee Senate District 17.

Whether you're a seasoned canvasser or knocking doors for the first time, we'd love to have you on the team. We'll provide training, scripts, and everything you need to have meaningful conversations with your neighbors about Lindsey's vision for our communities.

Our canvass launch location may vary each week depending on the neighborhood we're reaching. All registered volunteers will receive an email the evening before with the meetup location, parking information, and any additional details needed for the day.

What to expect:
• Brief training and kickoff at start time
• Door knocking for duration of the event time, if possible
• Literature, maps, and scripts provided
• Support from experienced team leaders
• Opportunities for both new and returning volunteers

Every conversation matters. Join us as we connect with voters, grow our movement, and build a campaign centered on families, community, and a stronger future for Tennessee.

Sign up today and help us bring Team Lindsey to every corner of Wilson County!

events.title: Phone Calls for Caroline
events.description:
Join Team Caroline Avinger as we contact voters to let them know about her campaign and hear about the issues they care most about.

We will have a script and call list to work from. Training and support will be provided for those who are not yet familiar with the platform we use. Please bring a charged phone or other internet-capable device, headphones, and an extra charger.

There will be snacks!

events.title: People Powered Maine Canvass: CUMBERLAND
events.description:

Every voter we talk to brings us one step closer to victory. Sign up today, and let's get to work!

events.title: Canvass for Virginia Democrats in Madison County!
events.description:
We're counting down less than 60 days till Election Day — and the road to            re-electing Senator Mark Warner and Congressman Eugene Vindman, plus Democrats up and down the ballot, runs right through Madison County.

This November's stakes are too high to sit on the sidelines. We're launching weekly canvasses right here in Madison County — running every weekend all the way through the weekend before Election Day. This is how we build the grassroots power it takes to win: door by door, conversation by conversation.

Whether you've canvassed a hundred times or never knocked a door in your life, this event is for you:

🗣️ Full training provided — no experience needed
📋 Updated talking points for veteran volunteers
🤝 A chance to stand with fellow Democrats every week as we head into the final stretch

Come once, come every week — whatever you can give. Bring a friend or neighbor along, and let's keep the momentum building weekend after weekend.

Address provided after signup.

Every door counts. Every conversation counts. 
Let's make Madison County a model for what sustained grassroots power looks like — sign up for this weekend (and mark your calendar for the next)!

events.title: Our Corners: Good Trouble and Serious Fun

location.venue: Adjacent to Lloyd Center East parking lot

events.description:
We just had our 75th consecutive weekly gathering on May 23: we emphasize inclusivity for all, with extra effort made to enhance the opportunity for seniors and people with limited mobility to participate.  Our message is serious, we are proud of our positive spirit and intergenerational crowds, and we intend to enjoy being together for this hour-- or less if that meets your needs.
Our Corners hosts music from The Good Trouble Ukulele Band and The Disruptors, as well as frequent drop-in appearances by a variety of inflatable critters (but not inflated egos!). We have also presented a Signs of Fascism event and hope to do that again.

events.title: Team Lori Phone Banking (In-Person)
events.description:
## Phone Bank for Lori Childs
Join Team Lori at the Marshfield campaign office every Thursday between now and Election Day to call voters and help elect Lori Childs.

Whether you’re an experienced caller or phone banking for the first time, we’ll provide a quick training, a script, and support throughout the shift. 

Every conversation helps us share Lori’s message, identify supporters, and make sure voters have the information they need to vote.

Please bring a charged cell phone. If you have a laptop or tablet, bring that too—some people find it easier to have one device to look at and another device to make calls from. If not, no problem: we can make it work with your cellular device.

Prefer to call from home? We also host virtual phone banks on Zoom every Wednesday. You’ll receive the same training, materials, and support while making calls from the comfort of your own home.

Sign up for a shift, bring a friend, and help us build the people-powered campaign Lori needs to win.

## Ready to turn the tide in CD35?

Join Johnny and the team as we call voters in Bexar County and ensure everyone gets to the polls in November!

## What to Expect

This phonebank is for anyone who is interested in having conversations with voters. 

#### Everyone is welcome!

New volunteers will get plenty of support to get up to speed alongside experienced volunteers. 

## Event Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact phonebank, we ask all volunteers (virtual or in-person) to arrive by 6:30pm (location provided upon RSVP).

events.title: Save Our Democracy - Central Westchester Indivisible
events.description:
#### Central Westchester Indivisible (CWI) is part of a nationwide group of Indivisible chapters and many other organizations fighting to protect our rights and to stop and reverse the Trump administration’s damage to society. Thank you for being a part of that fight!

#### These protests are intended to show our sustained opposition to the many ways the Trump administration is trying to destroy our democracy and bring our country down.  People are welcome to protest about any of the heinous acts this administration is guilty of, including:
- Attacks on the Press, such as the FCC's threats to revoke ABC affiliate licenses. 

- The illegal war with Iran, which has devolved into a perpetual series of tit-for-tat strikes and counter strikes.

- Lawless ICE/CBP.  We demand that funding be stopped until they are completely reformed with the kind of accountability we expect from real law enforcement.

- Illegal tariffs that raise inflation while dragging down our economy and damaging relations with countries that have always been close allies.

- The Save Act, gerrymandering and other threats to our elections.

We are asking people to line the sidewalk in front of Richard Presser Park in Hartsdale, NY for a peaceful, nonviolent protest. Bring a sign (a folding chair if you want). Bring the kids, bring friends.

A note about parking – there is a parking lot in the park on Central Park Avenue at the south end of the park. Also, NO metal or wood poles – please.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Whitefish Door Knocking
events.description:
Nothing beats talking to a voter on their doorstep about Sam! Join Sam's Crew for a day of knocking doors around Whitefish. We'll meet at Baker Park, where we'll train you on how to knock doors for Sam and you'll get a chance to practice before you head out.

We'll have a list of doors for you to knock, the script for your conversations, and a handy reference sheet on Sam's background and platform that you can carry with you. After everybody has knocked doors for a couple hours, we'll reconvene to debrief how it all went!

You do not need to have knocked a single door before this event - this is for beginners and experts alike! Talking in person with voters is one of the most effective and rewarding ways to spread the word about Sam, and we'll make sure you have the skills and tools to feel confident to get out there!

events.title: Election Protection for Beginners, Procrastinators, and People Seeking Community (EVI)
events.description:
Do you think everyone should be able to exercise their right to vote? Are you concerned about both what might go wrong with the election but also about your personal ability to do something about it? Whether you don’t know the difference between a ballot box and a voting center, whether you know what you should do but fear you might never get around to doing it, or you just want to pair your activism with hanging out with other like-minded people, please join our Fall Online Election Protection Group (sponsored by East Valley Indivisibles, but anyone is of course welcome)!

The beginning of each meeting will feature a presentation of timely Election Protection concepts and actions that will be recorded, followed by a closed (not recorded) conversation by attendees about their questions, concerns, and strategies.

Everyone who registers will receive a link to the presentation recording as well as action items and key takeaways for the week. Whether you can join live or just want to receive the updates, please register and invite your friends!

All meetings will be held on Tuesdays at 5pm Pacific EXCEPT the week of the mid-term election, when we meet on Monday, November 2nd. We will also have one planned post-election meeting on Tuesday, November 10th to celebrate our work and discuss next steps. We will continue this group until results are certified and winners are seated.

🚨 DWCC NEEDS LEADERS FOR 2027 ~ ALL OFFICER POSITIONS ARE OPEN!  Have you ever thought about serving your community in a leadership role? This is the time to step forward.

Every DWCC officer position is open for election for 2027:

President
Vice President
President-Elect
Secretary
Treasurer

Chair positions will also be available and are appointed by the President.

DWCC has made a tremendous impact in our community. As a PAC, we raise funds to support our voter-turnout efforts and candidates. In 2026, our annual election-year fundraiser raised an incredible $25,000!

Our work extends beyond elections. We support local charities and community organizations, and we have awarded four scholarships over the past two years ~ two in 2025 and two in 2026.

But this work cannot continue without people willing to lead.

DWCC needs its members to show up, vote for our 2027 officers, and seriously consider answering the call to serve. You do not have to know everything on day one. Mentorship and support will be provided.

If you have ever thought, “Maybe I could help. Maybe I could lead.” ~ this is your moment.

Our organization’s next chapter depends on members who are willing to step forward.

Please join us for our New Officer Elections and consider putting your name forward for leadership in 2027.

Spend a Saturday morning connecting with Durham voters at the Durham Farmers Market!

Durham Democrats volunteers will talk with community members, share Democratic literature and resources, and help make sure voters know what’s happening in the upcoming election.

This is a great volunteer opportunity whether you're experienced with voter outreach or doing it for the first time. You’ll always volunteer with a partner — no one will be asked to work the market alone.

How it works

Every Saturday | 8:30 AM–12:00 PM

Choose a two-hour volunteer shift:

events.title: Day of Action for EARLY VOTING 10/15-31: Phone Bank with Team Davis
events.description:
What we're doing:
Every conversation matters, even the ones that happen one phone call at a time. We're gathering everyday of early vote to call Democratic and unaffiliated voters across NC-01 to listen to what's on their minds and earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again; What was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, and it will come down to who shows up and has the best conversations, whether at the door or on the phone.

We're not just asking for votes. We're listening first to what voters and their families care about, what's worrying them, and what they need from their next Representative. Then we're asking for their support, and making sure every single one of them knows: early voting runs October 15th–31st, and Election Day is November 3rd.

Why your help is essential:
You don't need a car, comfortable shoes, or even to leave your couch: just your voice and a little time. Phone banking lets us reach voters who might never answer the door, and every call you make is one more NC-01 neighbor who hears directly from our campaign instead of an ad.

The ask:
Join us in-person or virtually to make calls using our auto-dialer. Use the script as your guide, listen more than you talk, and invite voters to make a plan to vote early or on Election Day. 
No experience necessary, we'll train you, and our team will be with you the whole time.

What you'll receive:
Auto-dialer access
Call script
Zoom link for live training and support during your shift

*In-person Phone banking: please bring your fully charged tablet/laptop with you, along with your fully charged mobile device.

events.title: Hands Off Our Vote! Protest - Indivisible Yolo
events.description:
In America, the right of citizens to vote and to have their vote counted is fundamental! We are a nation where the law rules--not a self-proclaimed king. "Hands Off Our Vote" are Yolo County Days of Action to stand up for the rule of law and the right of the people to elect principled leaders who will represent their interests--not those of the billionaires. 

On numerous Wednesdays leading up to the election, we're showing up in Davis at the corner of 5th and B Streets (in front of City Hall) from 4:30-5:30. Bring your signs and your voices! We will remind everyone to vote early and use ballot boxes! 

The President has made it clear that he will do anything to prevent the fair midterm elections that will undoubtedly serve as a rejection of his failed policies! He has gutted federal agencies whose mission was to protect the rights of the people to vote. He has even instructed the U.S. Postal Service to interfere in the election by refusing to mail state ballots to voters and by changing the age old practice of same-day postmarking. His masked, armed forces have indicated that they might show up to polling places under the pretense of enforcing immigration laws, but with the clear intent of discouraging voter participation. We need to be clear, the people will prevail! 

As a reminder, a core principle behind "Hands Off Our Vote" events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: Educating Texas: Text Bank for Pro-Education Candidates
events.description:
Every Monday  | 6:00 - 7:30 P.M. | Virtual 

Join us Monday nights as we combine learning with action. Educators will be virtually text banking for pro-public education candidates while building our collective political power.

Each session in our Educating Texas series digs into a different public education topic affecting our students, educators, and staff; connecting what we learn directly to the work of turning out voters who will fight for our schools. 

This is political education in action. Join us in text banking for candidates who will show up for public education and higher education. 

Bring a working cell phone and your energy to change Texas!

Schedule: 
 
September 28 

•	We will learn about the SBOE and how this board of 15 elected members oversees public education policy in Texas. 

October 5  

•	We will dive into how to increase teacher pay to retain qualified teachers and protect schools from program cuts. 

October 12  

•	We will discuss the state takeover playbook. We have watched it play out in Houston, and it's well underway at the new state takeover districts, too. We can't let it spread any further. 

October 19  

•	We will discuss book bans and how the state is attempting to re-write history through curriculum changes. Students and educators are feeling the chilling effect. 

October 26 

•	The last week of early voting. Help us remind voters to go to the polls! 

November 2 

•	The night before Election Day. We need all hands on deck to do a final Get Out The Vote push.

events.title: Tech Time: MiniVAN 101 to Secure the Vote
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Monday, October 19th from 1-2 pm ET for our free virtual live training: **Tech Time: MiniVAN 101 to Secure the Vote.**

  

This session is designed to teach you the technical skills needed to create a MiniVAN campaign in VoteBuilder. Unlike our other virtual live trainings, this session focuses more on demonstrating hands-on, hard skills rather than high-level theory and strategy. If you already have access VoteBuilder, there will be opportunities to follow along and practice throughout the session.

  

We’re here to help, so join us to learn the following:

*   Describe how MiniVAN is used as a tool for direct voter contact
*   Review the three key steps for setting up a canvass in VoteBuilder
*   Demonstrate how to organize a MiniVAN campaign for your volunteers and organizers

  

**This training is right for you if you're planning or managing a voter contact program using VoteBuilder/VAN.**

  

Learn more about our trainer [**Manny Espitia**](https://traindems.org/our-team#trainers/manny-espitia)**.**

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: Tech Time: Cutting Turf for GOTV
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Wednesday, October 21st from 1-2 pm ET for our free virtual live training: **Tech Time: Cutting Turf for GOTV.**

  

This session is designed to teach you the technical skills needed to effectively use VoteBuilder to create a virtual phone bank. Unlike our other virtual live trainings, this session focuses more on demonstrating hands-on, hard skills rather than high-level theory and strategy. If you already have access VoteBuilder, there will be opportunities to follow along and practice throughout the session.

  

We’re here to help, so join us to learn the following:

*   Define turf-cutting and describe its role in door-to-door canvassing
*   Identify the key decisions involved in cutting effective turf, including canvassing method, turf size, and geographic considerations
*   Demonstrate how to cut, review, and assign turf in VoteBuilder

  

**This training is right for you if you're planning or managing a voter contact program using VoteBuilder/VAN.**

  

Learn more about our trainer [**Nikki Otake**](https://traindems.org/our-team#trainers/nicole-otake)**.**

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

Together, we'll spread the call to action about what we can do to keep our water safe and send a clear message to elected officials: _stop putting billionaires ahead of working families._ These virtual phone banks will be hosted on Zoom and kick off with a community check-in, plus training for first-time callers! We'll debrief at the end to share lessons learned and talk about what's next. 

Please note: you will need a phone AND a computer, laptop, or tablet to participate! Please contact an organizer if you don't have access to these devices, and we will do our best to accommodate. 

**No experience is required; beginners are welcome!** Calls will not be made using your phone number.

events.title: Eyewitness to the Resistance: Photojournalists on the Front Lines of Protest

location.venue: San Francisco Main Public Library, Koret Auditorium

events.description:
Join us for **Eyewitness to the Resistance: Photojournalists on the Front Lines of Protest**, an extraordinary panel discussion hosted by Indivisible SF and Pro Bono Photo.

When history unfolds in the streets, photojournalists put themselves in the center of the chaos to document the truth. From the chants of resistance to the quiet moments of raw human courage, these photographers capture the images that define a generation.

In this compelling discussion, you will hear firsthand accounts from the front lines of activism. The panel will dive deep into:

**The Stories Behind the Shots:** The danger, the emotion, and the split-second decisions that go into capturing iconic movement photography.

**The Power of Visual Journalism:** How authentic imagery shapes public perception, fuels social change, and counters misinformation.

**The Ethical Front Lines:** What it means to bear witness to history while staying safe and maintaining journalistic integrity.

This event is free and open to the public. Please RSVP to receive notifications and updates prior to the event. SFPL link with more info: https://sfpl.org/events/2026/10/22/presentation-eyewitness-resistance

**Join volunteers to knock on doors and register voters!**

Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to win in 2026 and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to Democratic voters in Stockton.

*In 2024 Adam Gray flipped the seat by only **187 votes**. Let's talk to Democrats now to hold CD13 in 2026, as we take back the House majority!*

Read more about how Adam Gray always puts the Central Valley first - https://gray.house.gov/

Read more about Jaron Brandon is the Democrat rural California needs- https://votejaron.com/

events.title: De-escalation Training
events.description:
If you've ever found yourself in a situation where someone was agitated or argumentative and you didn’t know how to defuse the situation, you may benefit from de-escalation training.

Our political divide in America has widened to a destructive degree. Conversations about politics with family, friends and neighbors have, unfortunately, become harder and harder in recent years. These types of conversations should be spirited but also respectful and productive, and too often that is lost to heated emotions.

This 60-90 minute session covers basic de-escalation techniques, including verbal and non-verbal, examples of what to do and what not to do; basic causes of escalating behavior; practice scenarios; and when (and who) to call for help.

Our trainer, Liz, is a practiced de-escalation educator and lawyer who practiced for 35 years in multiple public sector jobs. In her various roles, she also trained managers, supervisors, and employees, on how to deal with and respond to discriminating and harassing behaviors, including scenario-based training such as this de-escalation webinar.

events.description:
Now that our evenings are getting darker earlier we are returning to our Saturday mid-morning pop events at the corner of Sanborn Street and Pine Grove Avenue.  With the mid-terms around the corner, please consider lots of get-out-the-vote messages and only the occassional candidate message. 

Pease watch our Facebook page for additional sign ideas. We rather like  'Hate isn't Patriotic," and "Your Vote is Your Super Power." What's caught your eye that resonated with you?

This a local Indivisible event!

We will meet from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. every Saturday, beginning Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. Please pay close attention to the weather and dress accordingly. We will have handwarmers available for those who might need them. Parking is available across Pine Grove Avenue along the service drive, at the Sanborn tennis courts and baseball field and along Sanborn east of the baseball field. 

Please join us to help get out the vote!!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: 威善高 Scott Wiener 電話拉票活動! Chinese Phone Bank!

sponsor.name: Team Wiener: Supporting Scott Wiener for Congress

events.description:
歡迎參加我們每週之電話拉票活動,支持威善高 (Scott Wiener) 競選國會!

每逢星期三及星期四下午1:00至4:00,來自選區之義工一同致電選民、分享威善高政綱，並協助我們競選團隊。

毋須任何經驗。活動開始前我們將提供簡短培訓，過程中亦會全程提供支援。無論閣下是初次參與電話拉票，抑或經驗豐富之義工，我們誠意歡迎閣下加入。

電話拉票是我們接觸選民之重要方式之一。

閣下需要準備:
- 一部手提電話
- 一顆願意協助威善高當選之熱誠!

即刻報名，與我們一同建立這場由人民力量推動的競選團隊。

Join us for our Weekly Chinese Phone Bank for Scott Wiener for Congress!

Every Wednesday from 1:00–4:00 PM, volunteers from across the district come together to call voters and share why Scott Wiener is the right leader for Congress.

No experience is required. We’ll provide a quick training at the beginning of the phone bank and support throughout the event. Whether you're a first-time caller or a seasoned volunteer, we’d love to have you join us.

Phone banking is one of the most important ways we connect with voters!


What you need:
- A cellphone
- Enthusiasm to help elect Scott Wiener!

Sign up and help us build the people-powered campaign that will win this race.

events.title: Relational Office Hours (Tuesday)
events.description:
For returning relational volunteers! Drop in for an update on our race and to ask questions about all things relational organizing! We can help you reach out to your friends and family if you are struggling with starting the conversation!

Tell us what is working and what is not. We will be a resource to you and will try to help in any way we can!

events.title: Join Team Jake for Relational Organizing (Saturday)
events.description:
Learn how you can help us win by speaking with your friends, family, and neighbors about Jake.

Relational organizing is the idea that people talking to friends and family is more effective than strangers talking to strangers, and we believe it is the key to our victory.

In this meeting, we will equip you with the tools to become a trusted messenger for the campaign and help you start your first conversations about Jake.

events.title: Canvass for Mary Allen for Congress - Vincennes
events.description:
Talking to our neighbors is one of the most effective ways in building support and votes for a candidate. By volunteering, you're joining a movement of everyday people across Indiana's 8th district who are tired of representatives who vote for the ultra-wealthy but leave the rest of us behind. You're part of a movement of people who believe in the promise of government to be the best of us: how we support each other, build communities where we can thrive.

Don't worry if you've never canvassed or phone banked before. It can be a little nerve-wracking for some people, and that's okay. We're doing it because it matters. And the campaign team will be there to support you as you try new things.

events.title: Team Folk Tuesday Weekly Phonebank
events.description:
One of the best ways to reach voters is one on one conversations. Help us reach as many voters as possible by phone banking with our team. 

All you need is a phone, a laptop/computer/device and you!

Staff will be on the call to train you on the phones and Anders' platform. They will stay on the call for the duration, just incase you have any questions or need an answer asap!

Thank you for volunteering, we can't do this without you!

events.title: Knock Doors for Abdul, Jocelyn & Michigan Democrats in Marquette
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to Get Out The Vote & talk with voters in your community!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Canvass for Mike Croley in Cookeville
events.description:
Let’s send Mike Croley to Congress for TN’s 6th District! Join us for a morning of community canvassing where we will knock doors and talk to our neighbors about why Mike Croley is the best choice for TN-06 this November.

All levels of experience are welcome: we will provide a short training, all the materials you need, and pair new volunteers with experienced canvassers. Just bring a charged phone, comfortable walking shoes, and water.

Every door we knock builds the momentum to win this election. Whether you can join one shift or every week, your support helps move the needle.

RSVP today and let’s make history!

events.title: Spring Branch BigWalk for SBOE6
events.description:
🚪 Let’s Talk to Our Neighbors About Michelle Palmer and other Dem candidates!

Join us for a neighborhood block walk to meet voters, listen to our neighbors, and introduce them to Michelle Palmer, candidate for Texas State Board of Education District 6.

Michelle is a teacher who understands Texas classrooms firsthand. She believes our students deserve fact-based, high-quality education and that educators should have a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape our schools.

This is about more than knocking on doors—it’s about building relationships, listening to our community, and making sure voters know what’s at stake for public education.

💙 No experience necessary—training and materials will be provided!
👟 Wear comfortable shoes and bring a friend.
🏡 We’ll walk together, talk with neighbors, and share why Michelle Palmer is the right choice for District 6.

Every door matters. Every conversation matters. Every vote matters.

Let’s get Michelle Palmer elected and flip Texas BLUE up and down the ballot!

events.title: Virginia Fall Wine Festival
events.description:
Get out there with a COVA Coalition Street Team to talk to voters at community events and show people that the resistance is alive and well! We'll share educational materials and discuss why it's important to vote "yes" on the 3 amendments to the Virginia Constitution that will be on the ballot this November; show people how to register to vote or check/update their voter registration on their phones; give out stickers; and encourage others to find their voice, take action, and protect democracy.

PLEASE NOTE that this activity involves standing and walking: We will NOT have a table at this event; instead, we will walk around and talk to people as they enter and leave the venue. We will not have tickets to attend the event, so we will not enter the park. Volunteers are welcome to purchase their own tickets to attend the event before and/or after their shift.

Where: Town Point Park, 113 Waterside Drive, Norfolk, VA 23510
 When: October 17 & 18, 2026 (multiple volunteer shifts available)

We will brief team members on the content and importance of the 3 amendments, train you on how to engage people, and provide you with the materials needed (flyers, clipboard, stickers, etc.).

events.title: Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
Dear friends,  

I am one of the millions of Americans who rely on mail in voting. But now, the government is trying to rush through a dangerous, untested USPS rule that could disenfranchise millions of voters who rely on mail in voting. Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here’s what’s happening: 

•USPS built a brand new ballot screening system in just 3 months (normally takes over a year)

•It was given less than 1 week of testing

•A “zero failure” policy means: one barcode error = thousands of ballots rejected

•The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to allow this rule to take effect before the midterm elections

📢 "Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable" – That's Our Message

We are saying NO to:

❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing

❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots

❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

We need to make our voices heard – NOW.

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find your members of Congress

•	Find your U.S. Representative:  
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

•	Find your U.S. Senators:
 https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use this template (copy and paste)

Subject: UNTESTED. UNSAFE. UNACCEPTABLE. – Protect Mail-In Voting Now

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to take immediate action to protect mail in voting.

The new USPS ballot system is:

❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing

❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots

❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

Over 250 current and former members of Congress have already urged the Supreme Court to block this executive order.Please join them.  

I ask you to:  

1.Support Senator Blumenthal’s investigation

2.Co sponsor legislation to protect mail in voting rights

3.Call on USPS to pause and independently test this system

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.

Sincerely,  
[Your Full Name]  
[Your Address]  

Step 3: Send it!  

•Use your members’ official website contact forms (fastest)

•Or email/call their offices directly

events.title: March to the Polls: Souls to the Polls
events.description:
Nearly 97 percent of Americans have access to vote early. Voters are choosing it over waiting for Election Day. They know something the politicians making it harder don't: voting early is power.  

In 2026, over 40 states are pushing bills to restrict voting. Shorter windows. New ID requirements. Fewer polling places. Mail ballot restrictions. That's exactly why you vote early October 24. 

Avoid the chaos, vote on your terms.
