events.title: Phone bank for Kelly
events.description:
Kelly needs your help so that she can help everyone in Northeast Indiana and win! Sign up and you can phone bank from home to help elect Kelly!

If you want to make calls with a Google Voice:

For Android and iPhone:

Sign up for Google Voice & get your number
Important: Google Voice doesn’t offer 1–800 numbers. 
Make sure that your phone is on and can get texts. To check, we’ll text you a code.
1.	Download the Google Voice app.
2.	Open the Voice app  .
3.	Sign in to your account.
4.	Review the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy    tap Continue.
5.	To pick your Google Voice number, tap Search.
•	You can search by city or area code. If numbers aren’t available, try a nearby city or area code.
6.	Next to the number you want, tap Select. 
7.	Follow the instructions.

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

Judges make decisions that affect many parts of our lives, from evictions and divorces to lawsuits and criminal cases. But judicial races can be some of the hardest races on the ballot to research.

Join us for a ***virtual conversation with Injustice Watch*** to learn how judicial elections work, what judges do, and how to find trusted, nonpartisan information about the candidates on your ballot. _This event is part of the Know Your Power: A Civic Education Series by Indivisible Greater West Loop!_

events.description:
Join us at T-Bone's Authentic Philly-Style Cheesesteaks and Hoagies to reach voters across Alabama and help them register to vote!

Whether you're a seasoned organizer or making calls for the first time, we'll provide training, scripts, and support. Additionally, we will be distributing voter registration forms and QR codes on-site to help community members resist the voting purge.

Shift Details & Capacity

Sundays (3:00 PM – 6:00 PM)
Capacity: 20 volunteer slots per 1.5-hour shift (3:00–5:30 PM and 5:30–6:00 PM.
Note: The restaurant is closed to the general public on Sundays, giving us full, focused space for phone banking!

Tuesdays (5:00 PM – 7:00 PM)
Capacity: 10 volunteer slots 
Note: Tuesday phone banks run during normal operating hours, so come hungry and support a local business by ordering food while you make calls!

Important Event Rules
Multiple Shifts: You are welcome to RSVP for multiple back-to-back 1-hour shifts per day.
Bring a Friend: Power in numbers! Inviting a friend, neighbor, or family member to sign up with you is highly recommended.
What to Bring: A charged cell phone, a laptop/tablet (if available), and headphones with a microphone.

### 40 days. 1,215+ miles. One canoe. And one incredible mission.

## Join us at Firemen’s Park in Chaska on Saturday, October 25 at 1:00 PM to welcome Amy and Dave Freeman as they roll into town on their statewide Pedal to the Polls journey!

Amy and Dave are biking more than 1,200 miles across Minnesota with a canoe in tow to raise awareness about protecting the Boundary Waters and encourage Minnesotans to get out and vote for Boundary Waters champions this November.

We’ll celebrate their arrival with a Pedal to the Polls rally, hear a little about their journey, grab a group photo, and then put the energy into action with a GOTV canvass.

### 🚲 What to expect:
- Welcome Amy & Dave as they arrive in Chaska with their canoe!
- Rally together and celebrate their incredible journey.
- Knock doors in support of getting voters engaged and out to the polls.

events.title: Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This an at-home/online Indivisible event!

Dear friends,  
I am one of the millions of Americans who rely on mail in voting. But now, Our Votes Are in Danger! the government is trying to rush through a dangerous, untested USPS rule that could disenfranchise millions of voters who rely on mail in voting. Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here’s what’s happening: 
•	USPS built a brand new ballot screening system in just 3 months (normally takes over a year)
•	It was given less than 1 week of testing
•	A “zero failure” policy means: one barcode error = thousands of ballots rejected
•	The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to allow this rule to take effect before the midterm elections

📢 "Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable" – That's Our Message
We are saying NO to:
❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing
❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots
❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment
We need to make our voices heard – NOW.

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find your members of Congress
•	Find your U.S. Representative:  
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative
•	Find your U.S. Senators:
 https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use this template (copy and paste)

Subject: UNTESTED. UNSAFE. UNACCEPTABLE. – Protect Mail-In Voting Now

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to take immediate action to protect mail in voting.

The new USPS ballot system is:
❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing
❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots
❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

Over 250 current and former members of Congress have already urged the Supreme Court to block this executive order.Please join them.  
I ask you to:  
1.	Support Senator Blumenthal’s investigation
2.	Co sponsor legislation to protect mail in voting rights
3.	Call on USPS to pause and independently test this system

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.

Sincerely,  
[Your Full Name]  
[Your Address]  

Step 3: Send it!  
•	Use your members’ official website contact forms (fastest)
•	Or email/call their offices directly

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

Estas enmiendas permitirán que las grandes corporaciones y las personas adineradas eviten pagar lo que deben, mientras que los trabajadores tendrán que asumir la cuenta. Ninguna de las dos enmiendas le ahorrará dinero a la gente trabajadora. Si se aprueban estas enmiendas, podrían significar recortes de miles de millones de dólares en nuestras escuelas, la atención médica y otros servicios públicos.

Durham For All y Durham Public School Strong se han unido para movilizar a miles de personas a votar en contra de estas enmiendas perjudiciales y exigir que las empresas y los multimillonarios paguen lo que deben en impuestos, para que nuestros niños, educadores y comunidades tengan lo que necesitan para prosperar.

¡Únete a nuestros esfuerzos para tocar las puertas de nuestros vecinos o hablar con la gente en eventos comunitarios para dar a conocer estas enmiendas perjudiciales y asegurarnos de que sean rechazadas en las urnas!

Si nunca has hecho campaña puerta a puerta o si acabas de enterarte de estas enmiendas, ¡no te preocupes! Te daremos argumentos clave y te ayudaremos a moldear y compartir tu historia sobre por qué esto es importante para ti. Todas las actividades de alcance se realizarán en parejas, así que trae a un amigo o ven preparado para hacer nuevas amistades.

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus on October 24th will leave 96th and Broadway at 8:00am and return around 7:00pm. (Note that the bus on October 31st will have a different departure location - to be announced!)
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 9:30am-5pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus!

To defeat the harmful amendments on the ballot this November, we need to make sure NC voters understand how dangerous they are. These amendments are crafted in a confusing way, on purpose, to make voters believe they’re going to make our lives easier. We know that’s a lie, and we are going to have face-to-face conversations with thousands of voters at the polls to ensure they know it too.

Finally, we’ll commit to taking action together during Early Vote and on Election Day.

events.description:
### Help Get Out The Vote!

As we populate 5 bridges within a 1.5 mile stretch along I-75 between Eight (8) Mile & Nine ½ (9.5) Mile Roads.   All bridges are easily accessible with parking nearby (some details below).  Harry St is the tallest bridge with 5 walk-up ramps (others are all 4). 

(Browning Street Visibility Brigade/Stand Up Indivisible/50501/Fighting 9/NE Oakland Indivisible/Macomb Defenders Rising/etc.)  

Our Messages can reach anywhere from 5,000 – 6,000 cars an hour.   (50 cars/minute = 50 x 60 minutes = 3,000 x 2 sides north & south = 6,000). Come join us for an hour or a ½ hour, whatever you can.  Exercise your arm as you exercise your freedom of speech right and wave at passing cars.   Bring signs to hang or flags to wave/hang...Canadian flags, Veteran’s flags, Ukrainian flags, Pride flags, etc.   If you can’t bring/make anything, know that YOU and YOUR PRESENCE are what’s important.

 
**Bridge 1** – Bernhard Ave – North of 8 Mile Rd.  GPS - West of I-75 use *1041 Bernhard Ave 48030* , East of I-75 use 960 E. Bernhard Ave. Street Parking.  (GPS: 42.45146871068798, -83.09355233205308)

**Bridge 2** – Harry St – This is the highest bridge.  GPS – Northbound *1001 E. Harry Ave, 48030*.  United Oaks Elementary School.  Street Parking. (GPS: 42.45669838679273, -83.0946655418343}

**Bridge 3** – Highland St –  GPS – Southbound near Tabernacle Baptist Church* 22323 S. Chrysler Dr, 48030*.  Street Parking.  Might be able to park in Church lot.  (GPS:  42.4580849417477, -83.10140190321641)

**Bridge 4** – Orchard St – Street Parking both sides on I-75.  GPS - East of I-75 use Hazelcrest Place Apartments, *100 Hazelcrest Pl, 48030*.  To park near the wall at these apartments, enter by Orchard Street off of John R.  West - Parking is allowed on the street on the West side of I-75.  We are not recommending you park in the church lot. (GPS:  42.464850906623546, -83.10630231670692)

**Bridge 5** – Browning St – Near Roosevelt Invest School.  GPS - West of I-75 use *24131 S Chrysler Dr, 48030*.  Can use school lot if school is out. Street Parking also, both sides of I-75. (GPS:  42.4702020519217, -83.11081209157966)


                    COME WHEN YOU CAN, LEAVE WHEN YOU MUST

#### Messages heading Northbound: ####

    Bridge 1 – Bernhard Ave – VOTE EARLY    VOTE IN PERSON
    Bridge 2 – Harry St – THE ANTIDOTE IS YOUR VOTE
    Bridge 3 – Highland St – RIDE THE BLUE WAVE
    Bridge 4 – Orchard St – BLUE TSUNAMI COMING NOV 3
    Bridge 5 – Browning St – VOTE EARLY    VOTE IN PERSON


#### Captains on each bridge: ####
    1.     Stand Up Indivisible- Jay & ME Scott
    2.     Mary & Joe Johns
    3.     Dallas, Beth & Alex
    4.     Kathie Patton-Eriksson/Beth Chilton
    5.     Cathy King

#### Minimum Display on each bridge: ####
    + The message above example:  RIDE THE BLUE WAVE
    +  The American Flag (attached to fence or on a pole)
    +  A Blue Wave (image displays a simple, colorful illustration of ocean waves in shades of blue)

If you are able to make letters or provide any materials, please let us know.  Letters need to be at a minimum, 24” high, the taller/bigger the better.  You will also need bungees, carabiners, and possibly grommets and zip ties if you make your own letters or signs.  Big hands on noodles, bubbles, music, etc.  I have guides/lists to send to anyone separately if you are interested in making your own letters, banners, or for supplies.  Just let me know. 

NOTE: WE HAVE 5 OF THE WORD “VOTE” – 2 VINYL, 3 IN LETTERS.  WE ALSO CAN HELP WITH LETTERS FOR THE PHRASES.   WE JUST NEED TO KNOW WHAT YOU CAN MAKE AND WHAT YOU MAY NEED.  WE ARE MAKING 5 “WAVES” AND MIGHT MAKE MORE.  We also have 3 Vet flags. 
 
#### Miscellaneous: ####

We will have big signs for the bridge but feel free to bring your own. (With letters at least 2 feet tall!)  See Size Chart.  The document appears to be a table or chart displaying specifications for signage, including font size, viewing distance, and speed in MPH, with various numerical values and measurements for different distances.

+ If you want, bring a cold drink, a lawn chair or any creature comforts you may need.
+ PLEASE LEAVE THE CENTER OF THE BRIDGE OPEN so pedestrians and bicyclists can pass through.
+Please keep it civil.  No swear words or hand gestures even though you will get some from the cars.

IMPORTANT: In the unlikely event that disrupters approach you, do not engage in any way, just walk away and notify another member to pull out their phone & film. We want to keep this a safe and peaceful event for everyone.

events.title: 📞Tuesday phone banks at the WDHQ to flip the House BLUE!
events.description:
Join us at the Westside Democratic Headquarters on Tuesdays to call target voters in priority Congressional Districts CA-22 and CA-48 for, respectively, Randy Villegas and Marni von Wilpert.  These are both flippable districts and must-wins for us to take back the House!

"Flip the House" phone banks will be open at the Westside Democratic HQ on Tuesdays from 1 to 3 p.m. and from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.

To join the phone banks from home on Zoom, register here to receive the links:
  Afternoon (1-3 pm):  https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/1021227/
  Evening (5:30-7:30 pm):  https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/

In CA-22, call voters in a district that now favors Democratic candidates, and oust the Trumpy incumbent David Valadao.  Our candidate -- Randy Villegas -- is progressive, smart, and tuned into the needs of the residents of his district.

In CA-48, help us replace the Trumpy outgoing Rep. Darrell Issa with a strong Democratic candidate who will fight for California families. Marni von Wilpert is ready to fight for working families, older adults, and ALL Americans!

Gather with like-minded activists from the Los Angeles area to make a difference in the November election, reunite with old acquaintances, and make some new friends!

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way by our in-house phone bank coordinators. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient. 

You can bring your own computer, laptop or tablet -- or use one of the WDHQ's Chromebooks to make the calls.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

events.title: GLCLC Walk Labor2026: Hosted by the GLCLC
events.description:
Join the KY State AFL-CIO for the Labor2026 program as we hit the pavement to build power for working families!

Elections are won at the doorstep. This election season, we are mobilizing union members across the Commonwealth to talk to our siblings and neighbors about the issues that matter most: protecting our right to organize, securing fair wages, and ensuring safe working conditions for every Kentuckian.

Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or a first-time volunteer, we need your voice. We will provide all the training, materials, and snacks you need to have meaningful, face-to-face conversations with voters in your community. By showing up for our endorsed candidates, we ensure that labor has a seat at the table in Frankfort and beyond.

Why Join a Labor Walk?

Strength in Numbers: Show our collective power as a unified labor movement.

Direct Impact: Research shows that peer-to-peer union conversations are the most effective way to turn out the vote.

Solidarity: Connect with fellow union members from across various trades and sectors.

In Solidarity,
The KY State AFL-CIO Labor 2026 Team

events.title: 📞Thursday phone banks at the WDHQ to Flip the House BLUE!
events.description:
Join us at the Westside Democratic Headquarters on Thursdays to call target voters in priority Congressional Districts CA-13 and CA-45 to help re-elect, respectively, Adam Gray and Derek Tran.  We're also making calls for CA-22 candidate Randy Villegas to flip this district blue!  These districts are must-win in the nationwide strategy to Take Back the House!

"Flip the House" phone banks will be open at the Westside Democratic HQ on Thursdays from 2 to 4 p.m. and from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.

You can also join these phone banks from home (on Zoom) by registering here:

  Afternoon (2-4 p.m.) https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/1021227/
  Evening (5:30-7:30 p.m.)  https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/

In CA-13, Adam Grey is common-sense Blue Dog Congressman focused on lowering consumer costs, strengthening California farms and small businesses, and making life better for Valley families.  In 2024, in the closest Congressional election in the country, Gray defeated the Republican incumbent by 187 votes.

In CA-45, Congressman Derek Tran has been working to lower costs for baby food, energy, prescription drug prices, and more.  With a Democratic majority in the House, Rep. Tran can so much more. He's ready to fight to restore benefits for California's most vulnerable families and expose the horrible impact of Trump’s tariffs on consumers and small businesses.

In CA-22, call voters in a district that now favors Democratic candidates, and oust the Trumpy incumbent David Valadao. Our candidate -- Randy Villegas -- is progressive, smart, and tuned into the needs of the residents of his district.

As we work on campaigns in key Congressional districts with the goal of FLIPPING the House BLUE, we cannot afford to lose one seat.

Gather with like-minded activists from the Los Angeles area to make a difference in the November election, reunite with old acquaintances, and make some new friends!

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way by our in-house phone bank coordinators. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient. 

You can bring your own computer, laptop or tablet -- or use one of the WDHQ's Chromebooks to make the calls.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

Looking for an engaging space to read impactful books, share bold ideas, and dive into meaningful conversations about bodily autonomy? Look no further.

​Handmaids of Las Vegas, Population Connection, the #Fight4Her Campaign, and Read Freely Nevada are thrilled to introduce the Repro Roulette Readers Book Club! Together, we are creating a community dedicated to exploring reproductive rights, justice, and freedom for all through the power of literature and healthy, open communication.

​✊ Why "Repro Roulette"?
​The landscape of reproductive rights can sometimes feel like a game of chance, but our collective knowledge and activism shouldn't be. We’re shaking things up by mixing serious, vital discussions with a welcoming, high-energy environment. Come for the books, stay for the community, and let's build something powerful together.

events.title: Join the Longest-Running U.S. Economic Discussion: 13 Yrs Strong! Tues, Sept Review: Oct 20@7 Zoom
events.description:
#### Join the Longest-Running U.S. Economic Discussion: 13 Yrs Strong! Tues, Sept Review: Oct 20th @7 Zoom

_Tuesday, October 20 @ 7 PM CDT — Fiscal & Economic September Review — 13 Years Running! Jobs, Wars, Tariffs, ICE & Deportations, Health Care, Affordability, & Inflation_

#### Let us know you will be attending … RSVP Here -> https://mobilize.us/s/7BPNGh

Join us for a timely discussion of September’s employment report, the latest inflation numbers, and what they mean for working people in Illinois and across the country.

#### The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ September employment report, released October 2, shows:

•	U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs in September, compared with an average monthly gain of 45,000 over the prior 12 months. 

•	The unemployment rate was 4.2%, with approximately 7.1 million people unemployed.[bls]

•	Labor-force participation stood at 61.8%, and the employment-to-population ratio was 59.2%. 

•	Average hourly earnings for private-sector workers rose 5 cents to $37.81—an increase of 0.1% for the month and 3.0% over the past year.[bls]

•	July and August job growth was revised downward by a combined 60,000 jobs. July now shows a loss of 10,000 jobs, while August’s gain was revised from 162,000 to 133,000.[bls]

#### Where Jobs Grew—and Where Workers Face Strain
Employment changed little across all major industries. Health care continued to trend upward, adding 17,000 jobs, while construction added 11,000 and manufacturing added 9,000. Financial activities declined by 7,000 jobs.[bls]

Behind the headline numbers, many workers continue to face significant challenges:

•	Approximately 1.9 million people had been unemployed for 27 weeks or longer, accounting for 27.1% of all unemployed people.[bls]

•	Another 4.5 million people were working part time for economic reasons but wanted full-time work.[bls]

•	About 5.8 million people outside the labor force said they wanted a job. Of those, 1.5 million were marginally attached—available for work and having searched within the past year, but not during the most recent four weeks.[bls]

•	The unemployment rate for Black workers increased to 7.0% in September.[bls]

#### Affordability & Inflation: The Pressure on Household Budgets

The latest available Consumer Price Index report, covering August, showed overall prices rising 0.4% for the month and 3.4% over the year. Annual increases included:
•	Food: 2.7%
•	Shelter: 3.0%
•	Energy: 16.3%
•	Gasoline: 27.4%
Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, was 2.4% over the year.

The September CPI report is scheduled for release Wednesday, October 14, at 7:30 AM CDT. We’ll include those new September inflation numbers in our October 20 discussion.

Let’s Dig Into the Numbers—and the Policy Choices

We’ll unpack September’s jobs report, the downward revisions to earlier months, and the latest inflation data. We’ll also discuss the Trump administration’s policies on war, tariffs, immigration enforcement and deportations, health care, and federal spending—and examine how those choices intersect with jobs, household costs, affordability, and debt.

What do these developments mean for working families? What is happening here in Illinois? And what can we do together?

Join us on Zoom to dig into the numbers, cut through the spin, catch up on this year’s U.S. and Illinois economic news, and share your thoughts. Bring your questions and your perspective!

events.description:

events.title: Become a Neighborhood Vote Protector
events.description:
*Español Abajo*
## Protect the vote in your neighborhood 
### Become a neighborhood vote protector. Every vote is a decision about our healthcare, housing, wages, and who gets to make the rules – which is exactly why it needs to be protected. The Trump administration is trying rig the outcomes of the election by creating chaos, fear and new roadblocks to keep us from voting. 

We Are CA is training thousands of Neighborhood Vote Protectors across the state to watch the polls in their communities, safely safely document and report incidents to legal experts, and make sure every voter knows their rights to cast a ballot without fear or intimidation. 
Join a short training to learn how you can look out for your neighbors, your block, and your local polling place.

Wed Sep 23 6-7:30pm

Wed Oct 14 6-7:30pm

Wed Oct 21 6-7:30pm

Sat Oct 24 10-11:30am

-----

*Español*
## Protege el voto en tu vecindario
### Conviértete en un Protector del Voto en tu Vecindario. Cada voto es una decisión sobre nuestra salud, nuestra vivienda, nuestros salarios y sobre quién decide las reglas — y es precisamente por eso que necesita ser protegido. La administración Trump está tratando de manipular los resultados de las elecciones creando caos, miedo y nuevos obstáculos para impedirnos votar.

We Are CA está capacitando a miles de Protectores del Voto en todo el estado para vigilar los centros de votación en sus comunidades, documentar incidentes de forma segura a través de líneas directas legales, y asegurarse de que cada votante conozca sus derechos para emitir su voto sin miedo ni intimidación.

Únete a una capacitación breve para aprender cómo puedes cuidar a tus vecinos, tu cuadra y tu centro de votación local.

Miércoles 23 de sept | 6–7:30 pm

Miércoles 14 de oct | 6–7:30 pm

Miércoles 21 de oct | 6–7:30 pm

Sábado 24 de oct | 10–11:30 am

events.title: 🗳️ Boletas, Pozole, y Proposiciones
events.description:
¡Comparte un rico pozole y prepárate para las elecciones de medio término del 3 de Noviembre con Resilience Orange County (ROC)!

En este evento educativo conversaremos sobre las proposiciones de la boleta con lenguaje claro y sencillo. También compartiremos información sobre cómo votar y las opciones para entregar tu boleta, con espacio para hacer preguntas y aclarar dudas.

Ven a aprender y convivir con tu comunidad. ¡No necesitas conocimientos previos! Toda la comunidad es bienvenida, puedas votar o no.

events.title: 🎃 Spooktacular Souls to the Polls🎃
events.description:
Don’t let voting questions spook you! Join Resilience Orange County (ROC) for a Halloween-themed community gathering to get ready for the November 3 midterm elections.

We’ll share information about how and where to vote, options for returning your ballot, and how to make your voting plan. Come ask questions, explore resources, and connect with your neighbors.

Bring your family and friends! Everyone is welcome, whether you’re eligible to vote or not.

events.title: The Pioneer Project
events.description:
The Pioneer Project is a two-part program where participants will be trained in the fundamentals of legislative advocacy and then supported as they practice what they learned in a real-world policy campaign. The program begins with 8 remote trainings over the course of 4 weeks (skipping over the week of Thanksgiving) that will equip our trainees with the skills to design a policy, propose it to their lawmakers, and pull the right levers to get it passed into law. After completing the trainings, participants can choose to join us in our mission of jumpstarting a nationwide transition to clean energy by launching a policy campaign of their own. 

Our curriculum covers the process of legislative advocacy from start to finish, and is based on the lived experience of youth and environmental advocates over the years. Legislative advocacy is a skill that allows everyday people to weigh into and lead political decisions in their community. Right now, politicians mainly hear from corporations and paid lobbyists when making their decisions and creating policy. Legislative advocacy opens the door for anyone to enter that conversation and make political change. 

The second and most exciting phase of the program is our clean energy policy campaigns, led by past participants in the states where a clean energy transition is needed the most. After completing all the trainings, participants can choose to launch their own statewide policy campaign or join an ongoing campaign using our clean energy policy framework. Throughout these campaigns, participants will apply everything they've learned from the trainings in real life, strengthening their knowledge with experience. Policy campaign teams will be provided with continuous support from Pioneer Energy through coaching, templates, and other resources. 

Everyone and anyone is welcome to join the Pioneer Project, but we believe this program will be especially helpful to grassroots groups looking to add another tactic to their toolbox, young activists learning how to build their own power, and people interested in a future in public policy.

PROGRAM DETAILS: The training phase spans 4 weeks, skipping over the week of Thanksgiving. Trainings are Monday and Wednesday at 6 PM est, and run for an hour or less. Finally, these trainings are free, remote, and open to all!

TRAINING TOPICS
November 16th: Welcome to Pioneer Energy
November 18th: Engineering a Policy
November 30th: Preparing for the Project
December 2nd: Researching your Legislature
December 7th: Lobby Meetings
December 9th: Bill Drafting and Sponsorship
December 14th: Supporting the Bill
December 16th: Advocacy and the Home Stretch

events.description:
### Join Food & Water Action every other Saturday to talk with our neighbors about Iowa's water crisis!

Iowa has _the fastest-rising cancer rates in the country._ We know this is linked to the pollution from industrial agriculture that flows into the waterways we get our drinking water from. Now, we’re canvassing our neighborhoods, asking people how they’ve been impacted by the water crisis and listening to their stories. 

Together, we will organize, talk to our neighbors, and share information about what we can do to keep our water safe, starting with electing candidates like Chris Jones for Ag Secretary, who will hold polluters accountable and clean up Iowa's water! 

We will meet at _Lafayette Park at 11 AM_ for a brief training session on how to have effective conversations.

Then, we will pair up and head out!

After everyone finishes their list/shift, we meet back up at Lafayette Park and debrief over pizza!

**No prior experience canvassing is needed!**

We use the website OpenField to track our conversations, so please bring a fully charged phone. We'll spend some time during the training familiarizing ourselves with OpenField.

events.title: Seeberger for MN Senate Weekly Phone Bank!
events.description:
Ready to make a real impact for Senator Judy Seeberger and Senate District 41?

Join us for our Weekly Volunteer Phone Bank and help us connect with supporters across the district. We’ll be calling constituents and supporters to spread the word, build excitement, recruit volunteers, identify lawn sign supporters, and find more people who are ready to support Judy and get involved with the campaign.

Judy knows exactly how much every vote matters. In 2022, she won this seat by just 321 votes. Those 321 votes made the difference between winning and losing, and they helped secure the DFL’s narrow one-seat majority in the Minnesota Senate. Today, the Senate is still closely divided, and Senate District 41 remains one of the most important races in the state.

That is why this work matters. Our opponent is already working hard, and we need to match their energy. Every phone call helps us connect with supporters, recruit volunteers, grow Judy’s lawn sign presence, and build the kind of grassroots support that wins close elections. In a race this competitive, even small actions can make a big difference.

Judy has delivered results for our communities on clean water, public safety, consumer protection, strong schools, veterans issues, broadband, and support for working families. As a firefighter, paramedic, attorney, and state senator, she brings real experience and steady leadership to the job, and voters deserve to hear why her leadership matters.

Whether you are an experienced volunteer or this is your very first time, we will make sure you are fully prepared. We will start with a training, go over the script and talking points, answer questions, and make sure everyone feels comfortable before we begin. Campaigns are won by people talking to people, and every conversation counts.

Event Details
What We Provide: Training, script, support, and everything you need to get started.

What to Bring: A charged phone and a willingness to help grow Judy’s campaign.

Questions? Please contact Laine at 218-392-0377 for more information.
Let’s get to work, connect with supporters, recruit volunteers, and build support for Judy across SD41!

events.title: Postcards & Conversation With Our Down Ballot Candidates
events.description:
Join us for a series of special events with candidates.

**Joseph C. Damiani and Sylke Jackson, Candidates for Town Council, Clarkstown ,NY, will join us on Wednesday October 21st, at 8:00pm ET.** Clarkstown is a suburban town in Rockland County, NY on the west side of the Hudson River. Clarkstown sits in Congressional District NY-17 where Cait Conley is running to defeat incumbent Republican Mike Lawler. Clarkstown is governed by a Town Supervisor and 4 Town Council members. Clarkstown currently has a Republican Town Supervisor and 4 Republican Town Council members, despite the fact that there are more registered Democrats than Republicans. Past elections for Town Supervisor and Council were in off years with low turnout. With a shift to even-year elections and greater Democratic turnout expected this election cycle, there is a good chance to flip these seats. 

**Teresa Clifford, candidate for Town Supervisor, and Rita Romeu, candidate for Town Council, Somers, NY, will join us on Wednesday October 21st, at 8:30pm ET.** Teresa Clifford and Rita Romeu are running for local government in Somers, NY, as part of the Democratic ticket aimed at providing new leadership, increased transparency, and proactive community management.  If successful, their elections would shift the balance of power on the Somers Town Board to a 3-2 Democratic majority. Somers sits in Congressional District NY-17, a red-to-blue district NY Democrats are working hard to flip. Supporting these candidates helps them turn out voters for their local offices but also for Democrat Cait Conley who is working hard to unseat Republican Mike Lawler.


We strive to build community, educate voters, and use our Sharpies to write to save democracy together. Write postcards with us or just join the conversation. If you need help getting started with postcarding, please visit our [FAQ](https://markersfordemocracy.org/postcarding/postcarding-faq).

If you are with the media and want to attend, you must notify us at markersfordemocracy@gmail.com at least two hours before the start of the event. All discussions are off the record.

This event is co-hosted by [Markers For Democracy](https://markersfordemocracy.org), [Downtown Nasty Women Social Group](https://linktr.ee/DNWSG), and [Team Min](https://linktr.ee/teammin
).

events.title: Virtual Friendbank to Battleground States (FINAL ONE!)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The most effective election defense is to rack up lots of wins with big margins - make the results **too big to rig!**

Stockpiling the early vote means bigger margins - and  **we're going to drive the largest early vote turnout in American history!**

You probably know a lot of "supervoters" - they vote every election, rain or shine. They are often the people who love to vote on Election Day. Well they now have a superpower: move their vote up by 2-3 weeks!

YOUR superpower is to activate your friends to vote early! 

Come to this virtual friendbank (our FINAL one for this election!), and get all you need to drive up early vote numbers in your crew - and also to help *them* activate *their* friends.

We're focusing on a list of battleground states below, so please join us if you have friends or family in any of these states:

•	Alaska

•	Arizona

•	Florida

•	Georgia

•	Iowa

•	Maine

•	Michigan

•	North Carolina

•	Ohio

•	Pennsylvania

•	Texas

•	Wisconsin

When people vote *as early as possible,* they create social proof ("we're all voting!"), they can fix any ballot problems before it's too late, and will massively shrink the target for any Election Day sabotage. 

See you there!

events.description:
# Help Make Arctoberfest Happen! 🎃🍂

Arctoberfest is going to be an incredible evening of food, fun, community, and celebration — but we can’t do it without **YOU!**

It takes a lot of hands (and a lot of heart!) to make an event like Arctoberfest come together. Whether you can give us a couple of hours before the event, join us for part of the evening, or help us wrap things up at the end of the night, **we’d love to have you on the Arctoberfest team!**

No special skills required — just bring yourself, a willingness to help, and your best Arctoberfest spirit. 🍁

## 🎃 Setup Crew | 1:00–3:00 PM

Help us turn the space into **Arctoberfest!**

We’ll need extra hands setting up tables and chairs, decorating, organizing event areas, getting food and beverage stations ready, and taking care of all those finishing touches before our guests arrive.

Come early, crank up the music, and help us get the party started!

## 🍂 Event Volunteers | 4:00–8:00 PM

Want to be right in the middle of the fun? Join us during Arctoberfest!

We’ll have several ways to help throughout the evening, including:

* **Welcome Crew** – Greet guests and help everyone feel at home from the moment they arrive.
* **Seating Helpers** – Help guests find their way and keep things running smoothly.
* **Food & Hospitality Crew** – Help with food service, keeping things stocked, and making sure our guests are well taken care of.
* **Wherever-We-Need-You Crew!** – Events always have a few surprises. Be one of our flexible volunteers who can jump in wherever an extra set of hands is needed.

And yes — **you’ll still get to enjoy Arctoberfest while you’re helping!**

## 🧹 Cleanup Crew | 7:30–8:30 PM

Every great party eventually has to come to an end — and many hands make cleanup MUCH easier!

Help us pack up decorations, clear tables, straighten the space, gather supplies, and leave everything looking great. Give us one last hour and help us finish Arctoberfest strong.

## ❤️ We Really Cannot Do This Without You!

Arctoberfest is about community — and that includes the amazing people who help make it possible.

**Grab a friend. Pick a shift. Come have some fun.**

Whether you can volunteer for one shift or stay with us for the whole adventure, **YOUR help will make a difference.**

### Sign up today and be part of the team that makes Arctoberfest happen! 🎃🍻🍂

Born and raised in Omaha, Democrat Jess Goldoni was shaped by a strong Nebraska work ethic and the belief that opportunity is earned. Now a candidate for Nebraska's 18th Legislative District, Jess is running to lower costs, strengthen schools and families, and move Nebraska forward with discipline, optimism, and common sense.

Denise Powell is a mom, small business owner, former corporate executive, public school champion, and healthcare advocate who knows that a strong work ethic and a love of family and community are the Nebraska way of life. She also knows the Good Life is getting harder to come by. After Trump’s election in 2016, she founded an organization that has supported hundreds of Nebraskans running for local office, protected our public schools and the families they serve, and helped stop extremists from passing abortion bans in the state.

## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

When local lawmakers recently conducted a surprise visit to the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center here at Mesa Gateway, they were sickened by what they found. Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

events.description:
Join the Madison NorthEast Dems to Get Out the Early Vote for the Midterm Elections! This is our time to motivate our neighbors to cast their early in-person or mail-in votes for our Democratic candidates.

The NED Team Needs You!

Our candidate slate for the state is great!
•	Governor – David Crowley 
•	Lt. Governor – Sarah Godlewski
•	Attorney General – Josh Kaul
•	Secretary of State – JoCasta Zamarripa
•	Treasurer – Yee Leng Xiong

We will also be canvassing to GOTEV for our state assembly candidates, Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford and Andrew Hysell and our Congressman Mark Pocan.

Have you heard?! There are 3 constitutional amendments on our ballot this November. We're voting NO on every one of these.

- Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment

Ballot language: Prohibits state government from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any person based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, education, contracting, or administration. 

Context: Wisconsin already prohibits discrimination under state and federal law; the amendment also bars “preferential treatment” programs aimed at equity. 

- Prohibit Partial Veto to Increase Tax or Fee
Ballot language: Bars the governor from using the partial veto power to create or increase any tax or fee.

Context: When Republican State Legislatures have passed budgets eliminating the funding of programs that serve the people, a Democratic Governor has been able to use this power to ensure the program is funded. 

- Prohibit Government Closure of Places of Worship During Emergencies

Ballot language: Bars the government from closing gatherings at places of worship during declared emergencies, including public health emergencies.

 The NED team offers new canvasser training at the start of every shift. We will try to pair up new canvassers with more experienced ones as folks are available. We provide all the materials you need to canvass; literature, a list of voters, a script to follow, a bottle of water, and a snack. You just need to bring your smartphone. We'll be using the MiniVAN App to collect the voter responses and guide you through your turf. Please download the MiniVAN Touch or MiniVAN 9 App by NPG VAN and create and Action ID before coming to the canvass. Training on how to use MiniVAN is included in the new canvasser training. 

 Don't want to canvass, but you still want to help? Sign up and tell the NED team member who reaches out to confirm that you want to help in another way, such as making phone calls for volunteers, delivering yard signs, or assisting with canvass launches. There is a place for you on the NED team. 

 This year is our first opportunity in 16 years to win a trifecta of Democratic government in Wisconsin. We can win the State Assembly, Senate, and Governor's seat this November. With a Democratic trifecta, progressive priorities can become law. Lower taxes, higher wages, funded public schools, affordable health care, environmental protections, the overturning of Act 10, and more can be in our future by wining these November elections. You need to be a part of this effort. 
Join NED to Get Out the Early Vote!

events.title: Bridge Brigade — Monday Mornings
events.description:
Meet on the Tower Bridge Overpass over  WI-53 near Costco (off Black Avenue). Parking on Gooder & Tower, Eau Claire, WI 54703.

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We are NOT allowed to attach the signs to the fencing on the overpass. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

See you at 7:30am for setup and 8:00am to wave!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Potluck and White Elephant Get Together
events.description:
LET’S CELEBRATE! 
Let’s get together, share some food, swap some questionable gifts, and talk about how much fun we had along the way! 
POTLUCK
Bring your favorite dish to share for a late lunch. Homemade, store-bought, famous family recipe, mystery casserole.
WHITE ELEPHANT FUN
Bring a wrapped gift valued at $25 or less. Don’t put your name on it. Just add it anonymously to the gift pile.
Then the fun begins!

Everyone draws a number. In numerical order, each person gets to choose a wrapped gift OR steal a gift someone else has already opened.

 THE STEAL RULE
A gift can be stolen up to four times. After the fourth steal, that gift is officially LOCKED IN and cannot be stolen again.

Come hungry. Bring a gift. Prepare to defend your treasure.
And, most importantly, come ready to celebrate with friends!

At the gathering we are also collecting for the Children’s  Holiday Toy Drive, brought to you by The ZIPPER JUNCTION Project™, The goal is to ensure that children in need, residing in Wayne and Pike Counties, are served by this local community effort.

events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

This is a local Indivisible event! Join Indivisible, Middletown Outrage into Action and Shore Area NOW as we protest in Middletown!! We show up to voice a slew of concerns, including the Trump administration's disregard and disrespect for our Constitution, the illegal war in Iran, ICE’s illegal detention of immigrants without due process, ICE’s escalation of illegal and cruel behavior at Delaney Hall, around NJ, and throughout the country, the cuts to Medicaid, USAID, SNAP, and the Veterans' Administration and other essential federal programs, the tax cuts to billionaires, the slush fund for insurrectionists and Trump’s threats to other countries as well. Until Rep. Chris Smith and the rest of Congress begin to show genuine congressional oversight and push back against the unconstitutional actions of the Trump administration, we will protest. 

Join us Wednesday from 4:30 to sunset in front of Rep. Chris Smith's former Middletown office located at 1715 Route 35! While Chris Smith has abandoned this office, we have not. His office building is just north of the Middletown Post Office on 35. Look for us roadside on the grass in front of the office building's parking lot. We stay on the grassy area which is public property and do not enter the office building or its parking lot which are private property. Please do NOT park at the post office or at the 1715 office building. We are permitted to park at the enormous Staples/Mattress store parking lot where there is ample parking. Remember to bring your signs, your flags, and your friends!! Please note that we are welcome new protesters to join our peaceful group! If you want to stand up for democracy, then we would like you to come join us! Thank you!!

events.title: Canvass Tulare CD22 | October 23, 24, 25
events.description:
**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect Randy Villegas in 2026 and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our 2026 voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 stipend** a day available to offset the cost of gas and lodging.

 - Friday, October 23 | 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm

 - Saturday, October 24 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Sunday, October 25 | 9:30 am to 1:00 pm

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Read more about Randy Villegas here - https://www.villegasforcongress.com

Never canvassed before or need a refresher?  Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: Phone Bank for Angie Carraway in HD 89
events.description:
Talking to voters is one of the simplest ways to help Angie’s campaign
reach more people across House District 89.

Join us online every Friday from 6:00–8:00 p.m. Central for our
virtual phone bank. You can call from home, talk with voters about
what’s happening in their communities, introduce them to Angie, and
make sure they know there’s a teacher and neighbor running to
represent them in Austin.

Never phone-banked before? That’s completely fine. We’ll spend the
first 30 minutes walking new volunteers through everything: how the
calling system works, what to say, what to expect, and what to do when
you get a question you don’t know how to answer.

And yes, calling strangers can feel a little awkward at first. Most
people get the hang of it pretty quickly. You’re not there to give a
speech. You’re there to have a conversation.

Please join from a laptop or desktop computer with a reliable internet
connection. A quiet place to talk and a pair of headphones will make
things easier.

We’ll send the Zoom link after you RSVP.

Come once. Come every Friday. Bring a friend if you want. We’ll get
you trained, get you comfortable, and get you talking to your
neighbors!

events.description:
Join us every Monday at 6:30 PM CT for Team Lauren's weekly volunteer call on Zoom. This is the hub of our campaign's grassroots organizing operation and the space where we come together, share updates, celebrate wins, and show you how to get involved from across the district.

We are less than 2 months from Election Day on November 3, 2026, and early voting begins in just five weeks. With mail-in ballots going out soon, the work we do right now is what will determine the outcome of this race.

Lauren Jewett is a special education teacher running to unseat Steve Scalise and bring real representation to Louisiana's 1st Congressional District. She is running to lower costs, protect our coast, strengthen public schools, expand access to healthcare, and make Congress actually answer to the people it represents and not special interests in Washington.

Every volunteer who shows up to this call is part of what makes that possible. See you on Monday night!

**Join States Win MA-RI to knock doors and talk to voters in New Hampshire to help elect Ben Ming!** 

Every Saturday in October, join the campaign in Hollis, NH for canvasses starting at 10am, 12pm, and 2pm. Drive up on your own, recruit some friends to go along. 


ABOUT BEN MING

Ben Ming is an attorney, former NH State Representative, a member of the Hollis Planning Board, husband, and father of four. He served in the NH House from 2022 to 2024, and was the first Chinese-American elected to the NH General Court.
 
Professionally, Ben practices law with a focus on real estate and estate planning. His experience on the Hollis Planning Board has given him firsthand insight into housing, growth, and local government issues affecting NH families.

We’ll be calling fellow union members to talk about what’s at stake in this election, the candidates endorsed by our union movement, and making sure working people turn out to vote.

Never phone banked before? No problem. A quick training will be provided at the beginning of each Zoom before calls begin.

All you need is your cell phone plus a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet.

Pick a Tuesday or Thursday, sign up for a shift, and help get out the #UnionStrong vote.

These phone banks are hosted by the New York State AFL-CIO as part of labor’s statewide member-to-member GOTV program.

events.title: CO-08: Deep Canvassing with We The Fighters

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
We are canvassing in Greeley to hold Congressman Gabe Evans accountable!

This is one of the most competitive districts in this election, and we know that Gabe Evans only won by a few thousand votes. That is why We the Fighters, a grassroots team of volunteers, is holding weekly canvasses to talk to our neighbors in CO-08.

We are building a powerful movement to hold Rep. Evans and his allies in Congress accountable by organizing thousands of our neighbors across the district who are in danger of losing their healthcare or food assistance. Over the coming weeks, we'll be talking with people directly impacted by these cuts, helping them connect the dots between what has happened, who is responsible, and how they can hold Rep. Evans accountable.

Will you join us? Sign up to canvass with us! We'll provide training, scripts, and a partner, so no experience is needed.

events.title: Phonebank to Elect Justin J. Pearson for Congress!
events.description:
Join TIRRC Votes Action PAC as we call voters across the newly formed Congressional District 9 to inform them of their district and elect Justin J. Pearson as the new federal house district representative. Pearson has always worked to bring people together to solve real problems and his track record of standing up to the rich and powerful show he’s a champion for our communities who prioritizes lowering costs and delivering real change.

Pearson has been a candidate who has fought for clean air and water, gun reform, immigrant rights, and making life more affordable for all Tennesseans for years. Join us as we inform voters of their new districts and vote for a candidate who continues to fight for every single Tennessean, not just a select few.

Whether this is the first time you've phonebanked or you're an experienced caller, we NEED you. Let's stand for Justin J. Pearson the way he has stood up for our communities across the state.

Zoom link will be texted and emailed 48 hours before the event

Paid for by TIRRC Votes Action PAC P.O. Box 17149 Nashville, TN 37217 Not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Angie for Florida: Victory Leader Orientation
events.description:
A Victory Leader is ready to bump it up a notch!
You are willing to take on a larger area, commit more time, and help build the campaign's overall field operation. 
Commitment: Approximately 500 to 3,000 doors. Your area may extend beyond your immediate neighborhood. You will coordinate your work with the Regional Director assigned to your area. Victory Captains aren't expected to do all those doors alone. You're stepping into a larger leadership role by helping organize and support the people around you.

Victory Captains will be willing to:
- Help organize and run weekly canvasses with their Regional Director.
- Recruit friends, family, and additional volunteers to help cover their turf.
- Work directly with their Regional Director to plan and coordinate canvassing.
- Help motivate and support other volunteers.
- Assist with phone banks and help support phone-banking operations.
- Take on additional responsibilities as the campaign moves toward victory.

Your Support Team Gets Bigger
As a Victory Leader, you gain more support and more connection to the campaign's field operation.
You will work alongside your Regional Director, the campaign's field team, and other Victory Captains to make sure the larger areas are being covered.
You aren't just responsible for your own doors.
You're helping make sure the team gets the doors covered.

You only need to attend one of the trainings listed below at whichever date works best for you!

events.title: Knock doors with us in D8 (Duboce Triangle)
events.description:
We're knocking doors in Duboce Triangle seven days a week. Choose the time that works for you. We'll meet ya there! Just say when and where.

No experience needed - we train you on the spot and you will never knock alone your first time. Bring comfortable shoes and a charged phone.

events.title: Poll Greeter - Clemmons Library
events.description:
#### Poll Greeters are the last contact with voters before they enter the polling location. They offer our Democratic candidate information, remind voters to vote for _all_ the Democrats on their ballot & NO on the 3 Constitutional Amendments, and watch for issues that may occur outside the polling place. Greeters at the polls = more votes!####

**_Please read all the information below before signing up._**

**Training**: Due to changes in voting regulations, all Poll Greeters must be trained, whether you've been a greeter many times or this is your first time. You will receive a link to the training video and manual in the confirmation email.

**Notifications**: After you sign up for a shift you will receive a confirmation email from Forsyth County Dems via Mobilize. It will include information about _Greeter Bag Pickup_ and _Training Options_.  Please read it carefully. You will also be sent important information via email. You need to be sure that you receive and read them. If you don't find your confirmation email, check your spam folder. Still not found? Check your Mobilize Notification Settings and contact info@fcdpnc.org.

**Mobilize Notification Settings**: 
Be sure that your settings in Mobilize are set to receive emails and texts. Find your settings in the **Menu** at the top right of this page; scroll down to **Account and notification settings**; **For events you sign up for** – they should all be turned on (blue).

**To check your schedule**, go to **Menu** then **My schedule**. You can cancel your registration there if you need to.

**You must pick up your greeter supplies** from headquarters before your first shift (details in your confirmation email).

**Please Confirm**: The day before your shift you will receive a text and an email asking you to confirm that you are coming. Please do confirm either by text or email so that the HQ Team and Site Captain know that you will be at your shift.

**Consider volunteering for at least 3 shifts**. There are a lot of hours over 15 days of Early Voting at 14 locations. We need lots of volunteer-power! 💙

**_Thank you for your time and efforts supporting our candidates by being a Poll Greeter! Talk to your friends and invite them to sign up too!_**

## _This sign up is for volunteers who can be "on call" to fill in when a scheduled Poll Greeter cancels._

events.title: Poll Greeter - Paddison Memorial Library
events.description:
#### Poll Greeters are the last contact with voters before they enter the polling location. They offer our Democratic candidate information, remind voters to vote for _all_ the Democrats on their ballot & NO on the 3 Constitutional Amendments, and watch for issues that may occur outside the polling place. Greeters at the polls = more votes!####

**_Please read all the information below before signing up._**

**Training**: Due to changes in voting regulations, all Poll Greeters must be trained, whether you've been a greeter many times or this is your first time. You will receive a link to the training video and manual in the confirmation email.

**Notifications**: After you sign up for a shift you will receive a confirmation email from Forsyth County Dems via Mobilize. It will include information about _Greeter Bag Pickup_ and _Training Options_.  Please read it carefully. You will also be sent important information via email. You need to be sure that you receive and read them. If you don't find your confirmation email, check your spam folder. Still not found? Check your Mobilize Notification Settings and contact info@fcdpnc.org.

**Mobilize Notification Settings**: 
Be sure that your settings in Mobilize are set to receive emails and texts. Find your settings in the **Menu** at the top right of this page; scroll down to **Account and notification settings**; **For events you sign up for** – they should all be turned on (blue).

**To check your schedule**, go to **Menu** then **My schedule**. You can cancel your registration there if you need to.

**You must pick up your greeter supplies** from headquarters before your first shift (details in your confirmation email).

**Please Confirm**: The day before your shift you will receive a text and an email asking you to confirm that you are coming. Please do confirm either by text or email so that the HQ Team and Site Captain know that you will be at your shift.

**Consider volunteering for at least 3 shifts**. There are a lot of hours over 15 days of Early Voting at 14 locations. We need lots of volunteer-power! 💙

**_Thank you for your time and efforts supporting our candidates by being a Poll Greeter! Talk to your friends and invite them to sign up too!_**

events.title: Wednesday Texas Phone Bank
events.description:
### We are calling Black voters in Texas, encouraging them to vote in the upcoming November 3rd general election and providing resources that make it easier to check where they are registered and find the voting information they need.

Beginning phone banker? We start each call with a training for anyone who needs it. You can also train yourself beforehand by checking out [our training slides](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGstUCSwjE/oWn7cjYLXJDiksQn6VbPww/view?utm_content=DAGstUCSwjE&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h1f8f5f4824).

Experienced? You can start making these calls immediately and pop back into the zoom with any questions along the way.

You can also make these calls on your own time 9am-8pm within the target state's time zone - no need to wait for an event!

For more information about this phone bank, please visit the [CFCG Phonebank Page](http://centerforcommonground.org/phonebanks)

events.title: Knock Doors in Solon for Brian Poindexter and Annette Blackwell!

Brian Poindexter is running for Ohio's CD-7 because he's a union ironworker who knows what it costs to raise a family in this economy. He'll fight to bring those costs down, expand healthcare, and make sure working people have real power on the job.

Annette is running for Ohio State Auditor because she's got firsthand proof of turning a city from crisis to one of the best partners in the state. She'll fight to make cities safe and affordable, tackle state corruption that's raising costs, and safeguard our tax dollars from bad actors.

The Working Families Party stands with candidates who are done waiting for the working class of this country to get its fair share. We'll be knocking doors for them across Ohio every weekend through Election Day.

No experience is needed, and training will be provided. Bring a fully charged phone, your favorite shoes, and a friend!

events.title: Magnified Voices-South County Canvassing
events.description:
Join Magnified Voices for a community canvass in South Hillsborough County!

We’re hitting the doors to connect directly with voters, share important information about the November 3 election, and make sure our neighbors have the information they need to make their voices heard at the ballot box.

Whether you’re an experienced canvasser or this is your first time knocking doors, everyone is welcome! We’ll provide the information, materials, and support you need before heading out into the community.

Volunteers will:

Connect with voters in South County neighborhoods
Share nonpartisan voter information and resources
Help voters understand what will be on the November ballot
Encourage neighbors to make a plan to vote
Help build informed, engaged communities through one-on-one conversations

No canvassing experience is necessary. Come ready to walk, talk with your neighbors, and help make sure South County voters are informed and ready for Election Day.

📍 South Hillsborough County
🗳️ Election Day: November 3, 2026

Sign up to join us and bring a friend! Every conversation matters, and together we can help more voters make their voices heard.

Would love for you to join.

events.description:
Resistance work takes a significant mental and emotional toll. All freedom and liberation movements need community spaces to support the personal impact of the work. 

The core goals of this group are to:
(1) create dedicated time and space for giving and receiving emotional support
(2) learn practical strategies to deal with burnout, feelings of powerlessness, and the persistent exposure to instances of violence and oppression (just to name a few)

The group is co-facilitated by two licensed mental health professionals. 

The support group meeting will take place after the monthly Indivisible LT meeting, from 5:15 - 6:15 pm on the third Sunday of the month. Hosted at the Quaker meeting house at 110 Tulane Terrace, Lancaster, PA, 17603. You do NOT have to attend the Indivisible meeting to come to the support group​.

events.title: Signs of Democracy | Arlington
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

We have been meeting every week since February 2025, to stand up to growing authoritarianism and defend our rights, our democracy, and one another.  We show up with purpose, persistence, and plenty of joy.

We have fabulous music, creative signs, great community energy and the honking is epic!  Whether you’re a seasoned protester or it’s your first time joining us, you are welcome here and we can't wait to meet you!

The ground is mostly flat with no stairs. Please feel free to bring a chair.

We meet rain or shine, so be sure to check the forecast and dress for the weather. Bring your voice, a sign if you have one, and your good trouble spirit!  We will have music and extra signs to share. 


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.description:
Join the Madison NorthEast Dems to Get Out the Vote for the Midterm Elections! This will be our last big push to knock on every door to motivate our neighbors to cast their votes for our Democratic candidates.

The NED Team Needs You!

Our candidate slate for the state is great!
•	Governor – David Crowley 
•	Lt. Governor – Sarah Godlewski
•	Attorney General – Josh Kaul
•	Secretary of State – JoCasta Zamarripa
•	Treasurer – Yee Leng Xiong

We will also be canvassing to GOTV for our state assembly candidates, Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford and Andrew Hysell and our Congressman Mark Pocan.

Have you heard?! There are 3 constitutional amendments on our ballot this November. We're voting NO on every one of these.

- Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment
Ballot language: Prohibits state government from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any person based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, education, contracting, or administration. 

Context: Wisconsin already prohibits discrimination under state and federal law; the amendment also bars “preferential treatment” programs aimed at equity. 

- Prohibit Partial Veto to Increase Tax or Fee
Ballot language: Bars the governor from using the partial veto power to create or increase any tax or fee.

Context: When Republican State Legislatures have passed budgets eliminating the funding of programs that serve the people, a Democratic Governor has been able to use this power to ensure the program is funded. 

- Prohibit Government Closure of Places of Worship During Emergencies
Ballot language: Bars the government from closing gatherings at places of worship during declared emergencies, including public health emergencies.

Context: Covid was very serious before the vaccines were widely available.  Superspreader events led to illness and death outside the circle of the attendees.  

---
 The NED team offers new canvasser training at the start of every shift. We will try to pair up new canvassers with more experienced ones as folks are available. We provide all the materials you need to canvass; literature, a list of voters, a script to follow, a bottle of water, and a snack. You just need to bring your smartphone. We'll be using the MiniVAN App to collect the voter responses and guide you through your turf. Please download the MiniVAN Touch or MiniVAN 9 App by NPG VAN and create and Action ID before coming to the canvass. Training on how to use MiniVAN is included in the new canvasser training. 

 Don't want to canvass, but you still want to help? Sign up for a shift and tell the NED team member who reaches out to confirm that you want to help in another way, such as making phone calls for volunteers, delivering yard signs, or assisting with canvass launches. There is a place for you on the NED team. 

 This year is our first opportunity in 16 years to win a trifecta of Democratic government in Wisconsin. We can win the State Assembly, Senate, and Governor's seat this November. With a Democratic trifecta, progressive priorities can become law. Lower taxes, higher wages, funded public schools, affordable health care, environmental protections, the overturning of Act 10, and more can be in our future by wining these November elections. You need to be a part of this effort.

 Join NED to Get.Out.The.VOTE!!!

events.title: Riverdale Film Screening of "No Country for Mothers"
events.description:
You’re invited to join us for a screening of 'No Country for Mothers', a film sparking honest conversations about modern motherhood and building a movement demanding better support for families. It’s an investigation into the lies dividing American mothers and the movement to bring them back together.

This isn’t just about watching a film. It’s about coming together to talk openly about the realities of motherhood, family life, and the systems that shape them. Whether you’re a parent, an ally, or simply someone who cares about the future of families and communities, there’s a place for you in this conversation.

After the screening, we’ll have a moderated discussion where we can share experiences, ask hard questions, and explore what it means to build a movement for better support for families. We’ll then gather for a reception and continue the conversation together.

We’d love for you to join us and help spread the word to parents, non parents, and allies in Riverdale and beyond.

events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Resist to Exist: Voting Block Party
events.description:
Voting is more than a civic duty; it’s a celebration of our community’s power!

Voting should never feel confusing, inaccessible, or like something we have to do alone. So we’re bringing joy to the polls with a Community Block Party in East Oakland!

📍 When & Where
Saturday, October 24
12:00–3:00 PM

Allen Temple | East Oakland
Allen Temple is an early voting center and will be open during the event. That means you can pull up, cast your ballot, and then stick around to enjoy the all-ages, family-friendly block party!

If you need childcare, please fill out the form. You may need to copy and paste this into your browser: https://tinyurl.com/ResistToExistChildcare


Oakland is the Town of resistance.

We’ve resisted gentrification, displacement, housing crises, mass industry and job loss, eminent domain, and the other forces that continue to make it harder for our communities to stay, thrive, and call Oakland home. We resist every day simply by being here, loving our people, and fighting for a future where Black and Brown, working-class, immigrant, and formerly incarcerated communities have the opportunity to belong.

Our vote is no different. Our vote is one way we resist. One way we show up. One way we say: we are here, and we matter.

Our grandparents and great-grandparents organized and fought for the right to vote. We are not far removed from a time when Black and Brown people were systematically denied that right. Today, our voting rights continue to face challenges that threaten equal access to the ballot.

We refuse to take our history, or our power, for granted.

We Choose Joy. We Choose Community. We Choose to Show Up! 

Voting should be something we do together! So, pull up to Resist to Exist, the Oakland Rising Voter Block Party. 

Bring your people. Bring your ballot. Bring your joy.
See you at the Block Party!

events.title: New York's Youth Election Protection Training Series! (2026 General Election)
events.description:
You’ve seen the headlines: Threats of ICE at poll sites and in our neighborhoods, Supreme Court decisions greenlighting mid-decade gerrymandering to suppress Black voters, federal attacks on mail-in voting, and videos of long lines and broken machines at poll sites. With critical elections this year, New York voters are in the crosshairs of federal overreach in our streets and at the ballot box. 

It's going to be up to us to protect our democracy, defend free and fair elections, and make sure our friends, families, neighbors, and communities can vote with dignity, free from fear and intimidation, and that the will of the people prevails. Join Generation Vote and the Hands Off Our Vote NY Election Protection coalition to help protect our elections and become a trained volunteer for poll monitoring! 

At our 1.5 hour training you will understand your voting rights, challenges to youth voting rights, de-escalation techniques, and how to help voters at the polls. Come ready to join our movement of young people defending free and fair elections in New York and beyond. 

GenVote is sparking a movement of young people fighting for our right to vote and a just democracy for all. Since 2020, Generation Vote has been the leading (and one of the only) youth election protection training partners in the United States.  

Join GenVote and Hands Off NY Election Protection Coalition to become a trained volunteer for poll monitoring today!

events.title: 10/20/26 Open Volunteer Hours
events.description:
EIF currently offers open volunteering on Tuesdays from 9 AM to 12 PM. Each shift is an hour long, so sign up for as many as you like!

Our address is 2405 North Shore Drive, and we're operating out of our Volunteer Center. Please drive down North Shore Drive until you see the large Volunteer Center street sign on the left side; you'll park in the gravel lot and enter on the north side of the building through the door with the red awning.

Please keep in mind that while volunteering, the following are not allowed on the volunteer center floor:

•Dangling jewelry (earrings/necklaces)
•Open-toed shoes
•Tank tops
•Phones
•Food/beverage containers
•Gum

If you have any questions, please reach out to us at volunteer@eifoodbank.org. 

Thanks for volunteering with EIF!
