events.title: Hamburg Saturday Canvass (Weekly)
events.description:
Join fellow supporters for our weekly in-person canvass in Hamburg!

We’ll meet up, split into teams, and head out into the community to talk with voters about Aaron and his campaign to represent NY-23.

No canvassing experience necessary. Whether you’ve knocked hundreds of doors or have never done it before, we’ll show you everything you need to know.

What to expect:

(1) A quick run-down on canvassing if you've never done it before 

(2) Your canvassing turf and voter list (and a buddy to canvas with if you want)

(3) Time in the field talking with voters 

(4) Support from campaign staff and experienced volunteers 

(5) Good people working together to build this campaign

Door-to-door organizing is one of the most effective ways we can reach voters and it’s more fun when we do it together.

Come knock some doors, meet fellow supporters, and help us win NY-23 one conversation at a time.

NOTE: Each week we will meet at the Hamburg HQ and target a specific election district.

events.title: Operation: Talking to Our Neighbor

sponsor.name: Nancy Martiz for Huntington Park City Council (CA Working Families Party)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
We’re building a movement around ethical governance, safe streets, a greener city, and housing stability. We know our neighbors care about the same things, but we want to hear directly from our neighbors who call Huntington Park home.

The status quo has failed us. Look no further than our pool 👀 We’re here to bring big energy, new ideas, and a fresh voice to advocate for our city.

Join us for a canvass day! We’ll walk the neighborhood together, talk with our neighbors about what matters to them, listen to their concerns, and share why this campaign is fighting for progress.

No experience necessary, we will train you! Bring comfortable shoes, bring your energy, and bring a friend. We need your enthusiasm! 💪

Let’s get out there, meet our neighbors, listen, connect, and do this together.

🚪 Knock doors.
🫂 Meet neighbors.
👂 Listen to what matters.
🌱 Build a greener, safer, more stable city.
😈 Let’s get into some good trouble together!

Canvass with us and be part of the team to win!
____
Estamos construyendo un movimiento basado en una gestión pública ética, calles seguras, una ciudad más verde y estabilidad en la vivienda. Sabemos que a nuestros vecinos les importan las mismas cosas, pero queremos escuchar directamente a quienes consideran a HP su hogar.

Ya sabemos que el *statu quo* nos ha fallado. ¡Solo hay que ver el estado de nuestra piscina municipal! Estamos aquí para aportar mucha energía, nuevas ideas y una voz renovada para defender los intereses de nuestra ciudad.

¡Únete a nuestra jornada de contacto directo con los vecinos! Recorreremos el barrio juntos, hablaremos con los vecinos sobre lo que les importa, escucharemos sus inquietudes y compartiremos por qué esta campaña lucha por el progreso.

No se necesita experiencia; ¡nosotros te capacitamos! Trae calzado cómodo, tu energía y a un amigo. ¡Necesitamos tu entusiasmo! 💪

Salgamos, conozcamos a nuestros vecinos, escuchemos, conectemos y hagamos esto juntos.

🚪 Tocar puertas.
🫂 Conocer a los vecinos.
👂 Escuchar lo que importa.
🌱 Construir una ciudad más ecológica, segura y estable.
😈 ¡Metámonos juntos en «buenos líos»!

¡Participa con nosotros y forma parte del equipo ganador!

Come help us bring free trees to Nashvillians! We are looking for enthusiastic volunteers to help keep our giveaway running smoothly from start to finish.

No prior tree experience is required - our team will lead a brief orientation before the event starts!

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win (MV)
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 8 participants.**

We’ll also reflect on how simple, meaningful activities like this can contribute to the regenerative future we are building together in our region.

Come create, connect, and celebrate the possibilities of giving new life to materials that might otherwise be discarded.

events.title: Vote WFP Organizing Committee
events.description:
## YOU (yes you!) have the capability to be an organizer and take action to transform our state block by block, just like Mayor Zohran Mamdani did across NYC. 

To take the next (or first!) step in leveling up your organizing skills while building power for working class people this election, look no further than our **2026 VOTE WFP ORGANIZING COMMITTEE!** 

Every Tuesday evening until Election Day, the Vote WFP Organizing Committee will practice thinking, strategizing and taking action like an organizer. Each week we’ll learn and apply strategic thinking, organizing skills and field best practices. 

### Come ready to: 
- Learn and apply strategic thinking and best practices around field work (i.e. anything that involves talking to voters)
- Help lead events in your community to strengthen progressive power across the state 
- Deepen our collective political education around building a powerful, working class political party
- Connect and collaborate with equally passionate volunteers across NY state!

_NO PRIOR EXPERIENCE NECESSARY_

**What is Vote WFP?**
This November, we have the opportunity to send a clear message to Albany: New Yorkers want politicians that represent their interests, not those of corporations. 

Voting for Kathy Hochul & Adrienne Adams at the top of the ballot in the Working Families line this upcoming election shows the power working families have to deliver elections and where we want our governor’s priorities to be— with her constituents, not corporate donors. It also ensures we keep existing as a party. To maintain our ballot line, every two years we need to get 130,000 votes or 2% of votes, whichever is greatest, at the top of the ticket.

Let’s get Michelle Palmer elected to the State Board of Education!

events.title: Fall Fiesta to the Polls 🏵
events.description:
📅 Saturday, October 24, 2026/Sábado 24 de octubre de 2026
⏰ 2:00–4:00 PM
📍 Hustler’s Roost, 1111 N. G Avenue, Douglas, AZ

Celebrate early voting with RAZE and Hustler's Roost at this free, family-friendly fall festival!

Adults will learn how to correctly complete, package, and return a mail-in ballot. Children can enjoy face painting, coloring, seasonal art activities, and Halloween and Día de los Muertos-inspired fun.

We’ll end the afternoon with a short costume parade celebrating early voting and community power!

Come for the fun and leave prepared to vote early with confidence. Arizona voters should sign and date their ballot return envelope before submitting it.

✨✨✨✨✨

¡Celebra el voto anticipado con RAZE y Hustler’s Roost en este festival de otoño gratuito para toda la familia!

Las personas adultas aprenderán cómo llenar, preparar y devolver correctamente una boleta electoral por correo. Las niñas y los niños podrán disfrutar de pintacaritas, dibujos para colorear, actividades de arte de temporada y diversión inspirada en Halloween y el Día de los Muertos.

Cerraremos la tarde con un pequeño desfile de disfraces hasta el buzón oficial para boletas electorales anticipadas que se encuentra cerca del evento. Trae tu boleta completada y deposítala tú mismo, o simplemente acompaña a tus vecinos en esta caminata de tres cuadras, ida y vuelta, para celebrar el voto anticipado y el poder de nuestra comunidad.

¡Ven a divertirte y sal preparado para votar anticipadamente con seguridad y confianza! Antes de entregar su boleta, los votantes de Arizona deben firmar y escribir la fecha en el sobre de devolución.

events.title: Road to Black November "Boots on the Ground" Rally & Training
events.description:
Road to Black November is moving into the field—and we need all hands on deck!

The purpose of Road to Black November is simply to help increase voter participation in Jefferson County, Alabama.

Join Faith & Works for our virtual Boots on the Ground Rally and Canvass Training. This weekly gathering will prepare volunteers to go door to door across Jefferson County and help Black residents check their voter status, register or update their information, find accurate election information and make a plan to vote.

Faith & Works’ data identified more than 9,000 Black residents who are inactive or have been dropped from the voter file in the communities we are working to reach. Some residents may believe they are ready to vote, only to discover a problem when they arrive at the polls. We cannot wait until November 3 to reach them.

During the rally and training, you will:

Learn the Road to Black November canvassing strategy.
Practice how to introduce yourself and speak with residents.
Learn how to help residents check their voter status or register.
Review our canvassing tools, safety practices and volunteer expectations.
Get answers to your questions.
Choose upcoming canvassing shifts and invite others to join you.

No canvassing experience is required. Faith & Works will provide training, materials, scripts and support. Please bring your calendar so you can sign up for every shift you are available to serve.

Canvassing begins Saturday, September 26, and continues every day through Election Day, Tuesday, November 3—including Election Day. Our virtual Rally and Training will take place every Thursday at 7:00 p.m. Central Time.

We are not asking you to do everything. We are asking you to do your part. Invite a friend or family member to register, attend the training and canvass with you.

Road to Black November is strictly nonpartisan. We do not support or oppose candidates or political parties, and we will not tell residents who to vote for.

Learn more at www.RoadToBlackNovember.com.

events.title: Help Flip Colorado CD-8: Knock on doors with Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

Knock on every door in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, a canvassing partner, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

About the program

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

Why we’re starting early: We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

How we’ll go big: knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Fall Voter Mobilization and Training Series
events.description:
Dauphin County Democratic Committee: Fall Voter Mobilization & Training Series

This three-part virtual training series equips district leaders, committee persons, and volunteers with the necessary tools, state-level updates, and operational strategies to register and mobilize voters across Dauphin County. Will also have a hybrid in person option meeting at culture and commerce co working at 19 ½ N 4th st Harrisburg, PA

Program Overview & Strategy

Turnout Starts with Registration: Research indicates that for young voters (ages 18–24), the primary barrier to voting is navigating registration rather than lack of interest.

County-Wide Action Goal: District leaders will collaborate to coordinate at least four targeted voter registration drives across Dauphin County prior to the election.

Format: Three 60-minute virtual evening sessions featuring live operational training, state policy updates, actionable toolkits, and quick recaps of prior takeaways.

Official Portals: Direct all voters and volunteers to verify records using Dauphin County Registration & Elections or connect via the Dauphin County Democratic Committee

events.title: Finish Strong to Win BIG and flip MN-1! (Swing Left Twin Cities)
events.description:
This is it, folks! Our last chance to get out the vote for Jake Johnson and flip MN-1. 

This time we'll hit the streets in Zumbrota, MN – a town of 4,000 that went 60% for Trump in 2024. The Johnson campaign has not been active here, so we will use this last canvass to provide coverage there. 

Now... who's this guy we're canvassing for, anyway?

Johnson is a high school teacher seeking to follow in the steps of another teacher – Minnesota Governor Tim Walz – who flipped this district in the 2006 blue wave. Johnson has proven to be a strong candidate and is running competitively with Finstad, the Republican incumbent (and rubber-stamp for Trump's hare-brained schemes).

This race is absolutely within reach. But only if we get out there and do the work.

At this canvass, we’ll:
- Knock on **lots of doors**, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to. Our target turf will be curated, but we're still casting a wide net.
- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.
- **Gently persuade** on-the-fence voters to vote for Democrats.
- Encourage likely Democratic supporters to **make a plan** to vote.
- **Gather insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

This isn’t traditional canvassing – it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Join us and help turn the tide!

-- 
Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

**On location in Renton, Washington**

## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## What our babies need, our community builds.

What do Montgomery County children and families need to thrive from birth to age five?

Families need more than a childcare slot. They need affordable, accessible care. Strong families. Quality learning environments. And the resources parents need during a child's earliest years — before the systems that are supposed to serve them even show up.

This convening isn't a listening session for its own sake. It's where families and providers name the gaps, share what they're living through, and start building solutions together.

### What This Convening Does

- **Surfaces the real gaps** not assumptions about what families need, but what they're actually experiencing

- **Builds relationships across roles** by having parents, providers, educators, and community leaders in the same room, as equals

- **Plants the seed for a Montgomery County Early Childhood Coalition** family- and provider-led, built to set priorities, research solutions, and push for real local investment in kids from birth to five


## _The gaps are real. So is our power to close them._

events.title: YDNC Black Caucus Monthly General Meeting
events.description:
The Work Continues. The Table Is Set. 🖤🍂

Join the Young Democrats of North Carolina Black Caucus for our November General Meeting and FIRST Annual Friendsgiving as we come together to reflect on the work we’ve started, strengthen our connections, and build toward what’s next.

We’ll begin with our Black Caucus General Meeting, followed by an evening of food, fellowship, and Black joy at The Black Table: Friendsgiving.

During Our Meeting, We’ll:

- Share Black Caucus updates and reflect on our progress since the soft launch

- Discuss upcoming events, initiatives, and opportunities to get involved

- Hear from members and create space for ideas, feedback, and community priorities

- Discuss civic engagement and community outreach happening across our communities

- Hear updates from Black Caucus leadership and what's ahead. Then, We Feast!

Following the meeting, we’ll transition into The Black Table Friendsgiving, an opportunity to step away from the work for a moment, break bread, fellowship, and celebrate the community we’re building together.

We encourage everyone to bring a dish to share! Whether it’s a family favorite, a holiday classic, a side, dessert, or something you simply love to make, bring something to contribute to the table if you’re able.

This is more than a meeting. It’s a chance to connect, build relationships, celebrate Black joy, and strengthen our statewide network. Whether you’ve been with us since the beginning or this will be your first Black Caucus event, there’s a seat at the table for you.

📅 Friday, November 20, 2026
⏰ 6:00 PM — Black Caucus General Meeting
🍽️ 6:30 PM until 9 PM — Friendsgiving
📍 Raleigh, NC
📌 Location: TBD

The exact location is currently being finalized. A follow-up will be sent closer to the event with the confirmed location and additional details.

Come ready to share, connect, eat, laugh, and build.

For us. By us. Built together. 🖤

#YDNCBlackCaucus #TheBlackTable #BlackJoy #ForUsByUs

We hope to see you there! ✊🏾💙

events.title: UNITY Walk To The Polls
events.description:
On Sunday, October 25, more than twenty Guilford County organizations will walk together to the polls for early voting. We'll gather at the Episcopal Church of the Redeemer, 901 E. Friendly Ave., at 2:00 PM for speakers, gospel music, a drumline, and giant butterfly puppets, then walk nine-tenths of a mile to the early voting site at the old Guilford County Courthouse, 301 W. Market St. Information tables from our endorsing organizations will be waiting on the lawn. This is a nonpartisan, multicultural, interfaith gathering — immigrant justice and health care and workers' rights and voting rights, side by side, because right now voting is how we change things. Shuttles (as needed) can bring walkers back to Church of the Redeemer afterward. Let us know when you register if you need accessibility accommodations. 
All our neighbors. All our issues. One community.
events.accessibility_notes: The Unity Walk To The Polls is committed to full participation. If you need accommodations—such as mobility assistance, an alternate route, seating, or interpretation services—please contact gsointerfaithimmigrantjustice@gmail.com and describe your needs.

events.title: Weekly Text Banking
events.description:
**Text Bank for Hands Off Colorado — Weekly Shift**

Join us for a flexible, remote text banking shift in support of Hands Off Colorado! No experience necessary — everything you need is provided.

**How it works:**

*Every Monday, you'll receive an email with a link to that week's active campaign
*Commit to logging in for at least 1 hour sometime during the week — work whenever fits your schedule
*Scripts are pre-written, and responses to common questions are already prepared for you
*Just click the link, log in, and start sending texts to reach community members

**Why it matters:**
Hands Off Colorado is standing up for trans and immigrant communities across the state. Text banking is an effective ways to have real, personal conversations at scale — every text helps build support and mobilize people to act.

**What you need:**
*A computer or smartphone with internet access
*No prior experience required — the platform walks you through everything
*About 1 hour of your time, any time during the week

Need help? Join office hours every Monday from 12 - 1p on Zoom here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/85091758479

Sign up below and we'll send you the details each Monday to get started!

events.title: Post Election Potluck

The election’s wrapped — now we get to breathe a little. Join neighbors and friends for a laid back potluck in the park where we can unwind, catch up, and appreciate everyone who showed up, stayed engaged, and helped strengthen our community.

Bring a dish if you’d like, or just bring yourself. Wander in anytime between 1 and 5 and stay as long as you want. No agenda, no speeches — just good food, good people, and that easy post election sigh of relief.
Community matters long after Election Day. Let’s celebrate it together.

events.title: Knock on Doors in Novi/Northville!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!


This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.


Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.


Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.


Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Vote Ready Oklahoma: Voter Prep, Practice & State Question Info
events.description:
Vote Ready Oklahoma

Oklahoma's General Election is November 3. Early voting begins October 28. Vote Ready Oklahoma is your chance to walk in prepared.

Join Indivisible Edmond and Thanks For Voting OK for a nonpartisan community event built around one goal: getting every Oklahoman ready to vote.

Here's what's happening on-site:

🗳️ Mock election — walk through a real ballot start to finish. Great for first-time Oklahoma voters and anyone who wants to see what to expect before Election Day.

⭐ State Questions Info Session · 11:30 AM — a plain-language walkthrough of Oklahoma's 2026 state questions, hosted by Indivisible Edmond. Just what you need to know before you vote.

✍️ Notaries on-site — if you've already received your absentee ballot, bring it and we'll get it notarized so it's ready to hand-deliver or mail.

📋 Sample ballot walkthrough — bring yours or look it up on-site. We'll help you understand what you're seeing before you're standing in the booth.

❓ All-Things-Election Q&A — bring any question you have. Offices and what they do. How elections work. Where to find your precinct and polling place. When and where to vote early. If it's about voting, we've got someone who can answer it.

No party. No pressure. Just Oklahomans getting ready to show up.

Saturday, October 24 · 11:00 AM – 2:00 PM (SQ info session 11:30 AM)
Southern Hills Christian Church · 3207 S Blvd, Edmond, OK

Presented by Indivisible Edmond · In partnership with Thanks For Voting OK · Hosted by Southern Hills Christian Church

events.description:
**It's time to talk to Democratic voters in CA-22!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to win in 2026 and to defend democracy long term. Join Indivisible Yolo & fellow Yolo County activists, in partnership with the Bay Area Coalition, going door-to-door talking to Democratic voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our 2026 voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them. **$100 stipend** a day available to offset the cost of gas and lodging.

This canvass can be done as a one day event on Saturday, arriving in Fresno by 1pm and heading back in the evening. Or register for both Saturday and Sunday, canvass Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning with an overnight stay on Saturday night. Canvass stipends are available for 2 or more shifts.

Once you've signed up, a volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location, you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition Yes, You Can(vass)! workshop Tuesdays, 7 pm - https://www.mobilize.us/indivisibleyolo/event/987496/

events.title: Black Belt Crop Drop, Selma AL

address_lines: (Across the street from Westwood Baptist Church)  4085 US-80

events.description:
The Society of St. Andrew, the Southeast Produce Council, Tuskegee University, and many more community partners are teaming up for a community food distribution at the Black Belt Marketing & Innovation Center in historic Selma, Alabama! We will pack boxes inside the BBMIC on Friday, Nov. 13th, then distribute the boxes to community members Saturday, Nov. 14th.

This high-energy day is a vital extension of SoSA's and our partners' year-round mission to improve access to fresh, healthy food in the Black Belt. We’ll be sharing a massive bounty of fresh produce—but we truly couldn't do it without the Southeast’s finest farmers who grow it, and YOU who help us distribute it! Whether you’re a fresh face or a returning friend, join us for our best and most fun event yet.

There will be 3 shifts for volunteers:

Friday, 11/13
9:00 - 11:30 am CST -assembling boxes, packing food, & palletizing food boxes (indoors)

Friday, 11/13
11:30 am - 2:00 pm CST -assembling boxes, packing food, & palletizing food boxes, clean up (indoors)

Saturday, 11/14 
8:30-Noon am CST - set up, distribute boxes to families,  directing traffic in parking lot (indoor & outdoor jobs)

Please sign up for the shift that works best for you. You are welcome to sign up for as many as you like! Be prepared to jump in wherever help is needed.

--Please wear breathable clothing and closed-toe shoes both days, and a hat & sunscreen for Saturday.

events.title: Phonebank for No on 3 - Voter Rights MA
events.description:
Don't let billionaires buy our elections.

This November, Question 3 would replace our current primaries with a "jungle primary," where only the top two finishers advance to the general election, even if both are from the same party. The measure is funded by a small group of wealthy donors, mostly private equity executives. It would mean less choice for voters and more power for big money, and it would shut out minority and working class candidates from the November ballot.

Voters in other states rejected this same playbook in 2024. Help make sure Massachusetts does too.

What you'll do:

Join via zoom- link available upon sign up!

Call fellow Massachusetts voters, share why we're voting No, and ask for their pledge. Every conversation counts.

events.title: Vote Ready! Morning Commuter Outreach
events.description:

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Guided Hike: Nehalem River Segment
events.description:
The confluence of the Salmonberry and Nehalem Rivers is an incredibly special place--we are excited to show you the River Segment of the future Salmonberry Trail! We should be seeing some fall colors from the big leaf and vine maples, maybe even some wild mushrooms!

**What to Expect:**
We will hike along the Nehalem River to Snark Creek (1.5 miles in), ~3 miles total. 
The vegetation in this segment is dense along the path, please weary sturdy, closed toed shoes and long pants.
Bring a snack and plenty of water for yourself.

**There’s no formal address and no cell coverage in the area, so here’s the most reliable description:**

Meet at the North end of the Foss Road bridge over the Salmonberry River

**Landmarks:** 15.2 miles east of Mohler, 13 miles south of Elsie
Nearest known point: Morrison Eddy Campground (the hike parking area is 1.3 miles south on Foss Road)

**Coordinates:** 45°44’60.0”N, 123°39’08.9”W

**Map link:** https://maps.app.goo.gl/TrfHCtE91yVFGeQZA

We want everyone to get into the canyon—and out—smoothly.

## How to Get There (Read This Part)

Coming from the Portland area:  
- Head west toward Elsie  
- If you reach the restaurant in Elsie, you’ve gone too far  
- Turn onto Lower Nehalem Road and stay on it all the way to the destination

Coming from Wheeler / Coast side:  
- Take Highway 53 to Miami-Foley Road  
- Follow Miami-Foley to Foss Road  
- Stay on Foss Road to the bridge

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

events.title: Persuasion Canvassing for Talarico
events.description:
Join us to canvass for Talarico! 

This is a coordinated canvass event for volunteers who has attended a training (in-person or virtual!) to canvass for Talarico and are assigned to the Persuasion script for their next shift. In this canvass, we will be doing a quick refresher on the script, and then going out to do the Persuasion script. 

Here’s what to expect: 
- A quick refresher on the Persuasion script and deep canvassing best practices
- Lots of time at the doors having real conversations with voters
- Logging each conversation in the app
- A short debrief with an organizer as you wrap up your shift

What to bring: 
A charged phone with the People App installed, comfortable shoes, comfortable clothes, and water. 

Every conversation you have helps move voters towards Talarico, and helps us learn what works to persuade voters. People should only attend this canvass if they are assigned to do persuasion for their next shift. Sticking with your assigned script is what keeps our findings meaningful, so thanks for signing up for the right canvass! 

Questions, or not sure which script you/re assigned to? Reach out to Karyn or Blair. 

Assigned to GOTV instead? Sign up for the GOTV canvass (at the same time!) here: https://www.mobilize.us/swingleft/event/1039075/

Haven’t been trained yet, or want a more in-depth training? Sign up for a virtual training here: https://www.mobilize.us/swingleft/event/1036835/

events.description:
Do you care whether Social Security will continue to pay full benefits? Do you care that your prescription drug prices are increasing? Do you care that your local hospital may close, because of Republican cuts to Medicaid?

If you care about these issues, then join the Pennsylvania Alliance for Retired Americans (PARA) and the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO in helping to flip the US House of Representatives this fall. Join our phone banks calling senior voters in Pennsylvania districts where we can elect pro-senior, pro-worker, pro-retirement security candidates to Congress. The next Congress will decide whether Social Security is fully funded or whether every senior receives a benefit cut. The midterm elections are crucial for deciding whether seniors in this country can retire with dignity. Join PARA in the fight to protect and expand Social Security and Medicare by phone banking for pro-senior candidates with us.

Before making calls, PARA will provide all phone bank participants with a brief training on our phone banking system and a script to use when calling constituents. No phone banking experience is necessary to join us! All you need is a phone and a computer or tablet. Staff will be on hand to answer any questions and guide you through the process.

Speechifying, Shakespeare, & Sea Shanties! Every week, we stand on Burlington Mall Road with signs, costumes and flags. To fight against the terror visited on immigrants, we need to fight against our own internalized terror. We have nothing to fear. We are America, fighting back. events.description:
WELCOME to our once a month (third Wednesday) meeting of the Carrollton AREA Democrats Club.  Our focus is to get to know our Neighbors - to meet like-minded folks for fellowship, education, solidarity and purpose.  Learn how WE can shape our plans as we seek to SAVE OUR COUNTRY AND DEMOCRACY!  

Our November 18th meeting is a continuation of our mission to understand and get to know our neighbors better as we take a timely look at our "Mosaic of Carrollton" - people living in our community and how we can be Allies to Each Other. 

This month we have invited Madison Noelle McNair (she/her) to present "Disability & Democracy: Inclusion As A Core Value."  We will be discussing accessibility, inclusion, accommodations, activism, disability history, and how disability is intersectional with all causes.

Presenter's Bio:
Madison is 29, she was born & raised in the Dallas area, she has been disabled her entire life and is passionate about accessibility. She began her journey by volunteering starting at 5 years old, and started more dedicated advocacy at 18 years old. She has been honored to work with many non-profit and advocacy groups across Dallas including Sunrise Movement Dallas and Sunrise Movement Tarrant, Dallas For Change, La Colectiva NTX, El Movimiento, Viva Colectiva, Vecinos Unidos DFW, New Disabled South, Dallas Area Transit Alliance, and she feels extremely lucky to have worked for many more in addition to these. Madison is currently a part of the Class of 2026 and Cohort 7 of the LBJ Women’s Campaign School at UT Austin, on the Patient-Family Advisory Council (PFAC) at Parkland, and the Paratransit & Accessibility Advisory Group (PAAG) with DART.

Instagram: @monoqueenmadi 

We are looking forward to presenting additional educational topics at future meetings for all of us to learn about, understand, and appreciate our commonality. 

As always - we will give time to any candidates that are stopping by to introduce themselves and speak for a few minutes at the end of our meetings.

PLEASE NOTE - for those who can arrive early - about 5pm - you may participate in #CRAFTIVISM. If you arrive at 5PM or later - we will be creating "At Risk" packets to be distributed in our community for those who may be targeted by ICE. In addition - we have created "Whistle kits" for Allies.

THE MEETING WILL BEGIN A LITTLE BEFORE 7PM.

We are a Grass Roots Group dedicated to preserving our American way of Life that honors the Individual with Diversity, Equality and Dignity. Learn about ways you can participate in ACTIVISM.  Learn how you may participate in our HIVES (Precinct) project.  We are Creating FUN Caring Communities - and Winning Elections!  And we are building on our momentum from 2025 thanks to your growing enthusiasm! 

Let us help you find ways that you may use your skills, talents and strengths to participate in our fight to take back our country thru activism, demonstrations, precinct building, voter registration and much more.  

Our Goal is to be a source of Information to all Carrollton AREA Democrats so they may make informed and wise decisions at the voting booth. 

We now have a Web Site: https://www.carrolltondemocrats.com/. This will provide our Carrollton Democrats the resources they need whether they live in Denton or Dallas County.  

JOIN US every 3rd Wednesday of the Month:
Nico Nights with the Neighbors - Nico's Cocina (6:30 to 8:30). 

3065 N. Josey Lane, Carrollton, TX 75007

We meet in the EVENT ROOM to the right of the restaurant. 

Please sign up on Mobilize so we may prepare enough materials for everyone. 

If you wish to be placed on our email list, (only 3-4 a month) please SIGN UP on CarrolltonDemocrats.com.  And we'll be able to introduce you to your neighbors in your precinct.   

Again - we are happy you have found us - look forward to meeting you!

events.title: Missouri State University ALL IN Party at the Polls: Voting is Easy as Pie
events.description:
To encourage voting and democratic engagement in a positive and festive atmosphere, Paws to the Polls will be joining us yo greatly enhance our usual tabling for Election Day. 

We have a table and tent near the door of the polling location on campus, and our presence has always been greatly appreciated. Normally we supply sample ballots, voter guides, general nonpartisan information, pens, and stickers and the opportunity to take a picture with our “First Time Voter” sign for those starting out their civic engagement path. 

Our fall theme this year is “Voting is as Easy as Pie.” We will serve pizza pies but also regular pie, hot chocolate, and cider. Join us for a fair-like atmosphere (like we do at the Voting Fair), with our table-top wheel and the opportunity to answer questions and win prizes, and photos with our mascot (The Bill of Schoolhouse Rock fame).

events.title: Knock Doors in Athens

sponsor.name: Georgia Youth Justice Coalition for Action

events.description:
Nobody understands what our neighborhoods need better than the people living in them.

You already see what's happening right where you live. Some of these challenges are big, like the cost of housing, access to affordable healthcare,  and whether our public schools stay fully funded. Others are challenges only the people who live here know and see. What connects them all is that too many of the decisions shaping our neighborhoods are made without us, and our communities deserve the resources we need to thrive.

When we talk about these issues with our neighbors, we stop facing them alone and start showing up together to transform our community and our state for the better.

That's why we're going door to door to talk to our neighbors about what important issues we’re facing right now and figure out the next steps toward real solutions.
 
No experience needed — just a willingness to listen, share, and build a stronger community together. This is where change actually starts. Come be part of it!

events.title: Faith on the Frontlines for Our Communities Prayer Call
events.description:
Community leaders know this truth: when people gather with intention, something shifts. We would be honored to have you on our midterm elections prayer call.

Join fellow believers as we prepare for Election Day. This is a time to come together to hold space for our communities, our nation, and everyone showing up to participate in these elections. This is a time to ground ourselves in shared values—peace, wisdom, strength, and collective care—as we prepare to be heard.

Please invite other clergy, ministry leaders, and intercessors to join us. The circle grows stronger with every voice added. 

"For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them." — Matthew 18:20

We look forward to praying together with you.

events.title: Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm
events.description:
#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. 

#### Join by Zoom .. The Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday sessions: Burnout - ZOOM at 9:00 a.m. & This is the Plan @4pm CST, -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. - **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

    Listen deeply to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

    Persuade voters using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

About the program

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

    Why we started early: We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

    How we’ll go big: We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

    How we’ll go deep: Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

We will be joined by canvassers coming up from Philadelphia to help flip this Congressional seat.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and civic leaders, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. We partner with local organizations at every stop. 

In partnership with Interfaith Alliance of Southwest Florida, Americans United for Separation of Church and State-Greater Naples Chapter, League of Women Voters of Collier County, Misión Peniel, Families for Strong Public Schools, Naples Pride, Glisten, and Visuality, we're stopping in Naples, Florida for a Get Out the Vote event. 

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy depends upon people of all faiths and beliefs exercising their right to vote.

events.title: Duluth Indivisible Monthly Meeting and Potluck: Gender and Authoritarianism
events.description:
In November we'll welcome Megan Peterson and Erin Maye Quaid, the Executive Director and Senior Advisor, respectively, of [Gender Justice](https://www.genderjustice.us/) to present on "Gender and Authoritarianism" at our monthly meeting. 

Building off the enthusiasm for our "soup and cake" with the Debate Watch Party, November's meeting will kick off with a potluck STARTING AT 5:00 with the actual meeting beginning at 6:00.

Authoritarians regularly use gender as a wedge issue to create fear, divide people, and reinforce traditional hierarchies and patriarchy. The Trump regime is following this playbook on many fronts: trans youth participation in sports, Hegseth's attacks on diversity in the military, the SAVE Act to disenfranchise women voters, blocking health care for trans youth, and on and on. Gender Justice's presentation will outline these issues in a potent and coherent way and better equip us to protect the rights of ALL people to live fully and freely with respect to gender. 

Megan and Erin will present by Zoom, allowing us to share the event with Indivisible groups throughout CD8. This is something of an experiment. 

We will still meet in person in Duluth for the potluck at 5:00 PM, discussion and planning on how gender advocacy might fit into our 2027 planning.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early

address_lines: SE Corner of U.S. 41 and Ridge Road

events.description:
Join us on Saturday, Oct. 17, 12-1 to encourage attendees and passersby to vote early. 
Then join our rally on Oct. 24 as we encourage everyone to vote. At 1pm we'll put away our signs and join in a Walk to the Polls at Wicker Park where those who haven't yet voted can vote.
These rallies are nonpartisan events sponsored by Indivisible National with the goal of turning out as many voters as we can.
Our Vote Is Our Power!  We're urging everyone to vote early!


We’ll be in Highland on the SE corner of Ridge and 41 at the Highway of Flags Veterans Memorial. Limited parking, along with handicapped spots, is available behind the memorial. If the lot is full, park at Wicker Park and rally on the NW corner of Ridge and 41. Or park in the old Ultra parking lot and rally on the NE corner. Bring your signs and your passion! And please bring nonperishable food items. We donate to a different pantry each week.

There are no bathrooms at the Memorial. There are restrooms at Wicker Park on Ridge Rd. and at the Highland Public Library, 2841 Jewett Ave.

events.title: YOUR VOTE IS YOUR VOICE: NON-PARTISAN  GET OUT THE VOTE WORKSHOP

location.venue: Louise Roberts Room at Claremont United Church of Christ

events.description:

We'll open with a speaker who will briefly share about the importance of early voting in the November general election, followed by activity stations featuring hands-on strategies for getting out the vote — actions you can take on the spot, plus tools you can share with friends and neighbors who can't join us that day.

This event is non-partisan. Table attendants will not tell you what or who to vote for.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

RSVP to let us know if you plan to attend.

events.title: March to the Polls - Washington Township
events.description:
### March to the Polls - Washington Township

Millions of Americans have joined together to reject power grabs and voter suppression. Now, we are taking the next step: moving from protest to participation, making sure we are ready to vote early and choose our own leaders. No king, no politician, and no president gets to decide who wins an election.

The starting point for this march will be at Holliday/86th - southwest corner of the St. Lukes parking lot. This march will take place rain or shine, except in the case of thunderstorms.  **Come join us!**

You must be registered to vote in Marion County and provide a photo ID in order to cast your ballot. Voter registration closes on October 5. Please verify your voter registration at [IndianaVoters.com](https://www.IndianaVoters.com).

events.title: Knock on Doors with the Mitchell County Dems!
events.description:
Join Mitchell County Democrats for a neighborhood lit drop and voter outreach shift.

We’ll meet at MCDP Headquarters in Bakersville, get our routes and materials together, and then head out around Mitchell County.

Most stops will be simple: leave information from our candidates, remind neighbors that an election is coming up, and move on to the next house. If someone wants to talk, that’s great but you don't need to give a speech, debate anyone, or have an answer for every question.

We’ll partner up and go over the routes and materials. Bring a charged phone, water, and comfortable shoes. The plan is to be out for two hours, but teams are welcome to stay out longer if they’d like.

If talking to strangers at the door isn’t your strong suit, that’s okay. This is just a straightforward way to help get election information into people’s hands.

events.title: Vote Early Day: Benton County AR Election Commission HQ
events.description:
# Join us October 24

Thousands of communities are stepping up. Learning together. Empowering neighbors to vote early. You're part of that.

In 2026, over 40 states are restricting voting. Shorter windows. ID requirements. Fewer polling places. Mail ballot restrictions. That's exactly why we're here.

Learn your voting options. Check your registration. Make a plan to vote early on your terms.

It’s easy to check your registration, find a voting center, and even figure out what’s on your ballot before you go. The Arkansas Secretary of State has one site that will do it all: [Voter View](https://www.voterview.ar-nova.org/voterview)

**No lines. No waiting. You vote on your schedule.**

events.title: Poll Station Tabling – Early Voting - October 14–29
events.description:
About this event
Poll Station Table Volunteers are needed for Early Voting during the November election, October 14 - October 29. Volunteers will staff an information table at the Library poll station. It's our last opportunity to help voters hear about Democrats on the Ballot!
Note: You will receive Mobilize email about this event when you sign up.

Volunteers, a MUST READ, please!

Thank you for your commitment! However, if something happens and you cannot fulfill your shift, please give as much notice as possible by calling or texting 336-601-8183 or 865-469-1513.

Preparation

•	Wear comfortable clothing, such as a BCDP T-shirt, hat or similar top. We have BCDP buttons available to use for your shift if you don’t have BCDP logo items. Please leave the buttons for the next shift. 

•	You must cover up any political logos before entering the library, so bring an extra cover up shirt. 

•	Bring a beverage/water, snack, sunglasses or hat if you so desire.

Set Up

•	The table will be set up under the tree near the book drop-off. Please keep the sidewalk area clear so we aren’t impeding public access.

•	2 metal chairs are provided as well as 1 small table along with all the supplies. There is an umbrella, rain poncho and a plastic cover for the table.

•	In the case of rain, cover the table with the plastic cover and wait it out in your vehicle if you so desire. Either wait it out and reset when the rain has passed or call for table pickup 336-601-8183 or 865-469-1513. 

•	By Law, anything campaign related MUST BE 100 ft from the entrance of the polling location (in this case, the Library entrance)

Interaction with voters

•	Our mission is to interact with voters. To attract their attention, lots of friendly WAVING and SMILING as cars go by will help with getting them to stop by.

•	Use the buddy system, taking turns. Stay aware and alert. It’s great to get to know each other as you are at the table together, but please be sure you are paying attention to the visitors at the table.

•	Have visitors sign in on the sign in sheet. Ask them if they would like to volunteer with party and if so, circle the Yes in the last column and give them a Yellow Card to fill out with their preferences. Keep the card after reviewing to ensure their contact information has been provided.

•	Offer them the candidate information that is available. They may take it into the booth with them.

•	Ask the visitor if they are on our mailing list for our newsletter. If not let them know they can sign up for it on Blountdems.org

•	Ignore any haters. Do not interact with them in any way.

events.title: Weekday Canvassing in Troy
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: PA: Springdale Data Center Public Meeting
events.description:
A massive hyperscale data center slated for Springdale, PA, has been approved at the local level. But it still has to meet Allegheny County’s land development standards — and the developer's current application will not meet the requirements for the county’s subdivision and land development ordinance, or SALDO.

If they plan to follow their own laws, Allegheny County officials should reject the data center application before any public hearing process begins! 

**Make your voice heard!** Join Food & Water Watch, your fellow Allegheny County neighbors, and allied organizations on October 28th for the Springdale Data Center Land Development Public Meeting!

Once you sign up, we'll send you instructions on how to register for public comment during the meeting and talking points, as well as info on requesting accommodations. We'll also keep you in the loop with updates on this issue and future actions you can take.

Your presence makes a difference. **When we show up together, we send a strong message: our future shouldn’t be decided by corporations looking for profit at our expense!**

events.title: Vote Forward x Stand Up America Letter Writing Events
events.description:
Join Stand Up America, Vote Forward, and volunteers across the country to write letters to voters!

Vote Forward partners with volunteers to take evidence-driven, high-impact actions to strengthen our democracy by building trust in government and increasing voter participation. Everything we do is grounded in evidence: we rigorously test our tactics, learn from the results, and evolve. Our 2026 campaigns build directly on what we learned in 2025, and include some of our most novel and exciting work yet. We have ambitious goals, but we make it easy to get started.  

Join us to learn about the available campaigns, and the strategy behind them.

The most common question we receive at Vote Forward is: "what should I write?" This letter writing event is the personalized, in depth answer to that question. Vote Forward staff will help you craft an effective, personal message to voters. Whether you’re writing letters for the first time or you’re an experienced letter writer looking to refine your message, this event is for you!

RSVP today, and we’ll let you know how to join this event. Invite your friends and family, too and encourage them to join in with Vote Forward! 

Never written with Vote Forward before? No problem! Visit [votefwd.org/instructions](https://votefwd.org/instructions) for all the information you need, and sign up for an account at [votefwd.org/standupamerica](https://go.votefwd.org/standupamerica).

events.title: GOTV Oakland: BART & AC Transit Activations
events.description:
Resist to Exist! 

Volunteer with us at BART and AC Transit Centers in Oakland to Get Out The Vote! 

Oakland Rising is organizing activations at BART and AC Transit centers to get our community out to vote! 

Too many people miss important information about their voting rights, where to vote, and when to vote. That's why we’re meeting people where they are to bring them the information they need! 

We need your help! ⚠️
We need volunteers to take up space, cause a scene for democracy, and help us reach hundreds of Oakland Voters over four outreach days!

What to bring! ⚠️
Positive energy and willingness to talk to our neighbors 
Comfy shoes for long standing and walking 
Water to stay hydrated! 
Your favorite democracy or Town attire! Dress up in a dinosaur costume! Help us make a scene 

Sign up for one or two shifts! We will be at two BART stations on the 29th and two AC Transit stations on the 30th. 

The schedule is as follows:

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Get ready to Party at the Polls in Phoenix, Arizona on Saturday, October 24! Vote Early Day is a national day of action and we are inviting everyone — our neighbors, friends, family, even nuestras abuelitas — to come out and vote early together. 

Free food, transportation, entertainment, voting information, and more will be available — and at 10 AM MST, we will caravan to the nearest polling location. Join us in Tolleson/South Phoenix at a large outdoor venue (details available after registration) to gather in community and celebrate our power. Bring your ballots and come vote with us!
Early voting makes participating in our elections easier and more accessible for everyone. In elections as big as the one on November 3, it is important that we take the time to vote now rather than later.
Impress your abuela — join us to vote early and avoid the dreadful "que te dije"!

Disclaimer: Party at the Polls events are nonpartisan celebrations of voting. They must be free and open to the public, and any food, entertainment, or other goods must be available to all attendees, regardless of whether they have voted or plan to vote. Parties must comply with all relevant state and local rules and regulations. Parties must not advocate for or against any candidate, ballot initiative, or political party. Hosts are responsible for ensuring that their parties are accessible, well managed, and legally compliant.

events.title: WIN the Midterms, ENFORCE the results: A SURJ Direct Action Training Series
events.description:
**This is a 3-part training series, please sign up for all three!**
**Recordings will be sent after the training if you have to miss any, though please try to be there live!**

As white people organizing for racial justice, we know what's at stake in this moment. We know that the billionaires see multi-racial democracy as a threat to their power, so they use race and class to divide us so that we don't join together to build the world we deserve - a world with clean air and water, fully funded schools, healthcare for all, free accessible childcare; a world of racial and economic justice. Power holders are so threatened by our power that they are not only scapegoating our black, brown, immigrant, and trans neighbors to distract us from their corruption, they are also working in earnest to dismantle our democracy in order to cement their wealth and power.

We know that white people have an outsized influence in both the electoral and political spheres, which is why Showing up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is working hard to move white people to both WIN the midterm elections by big margins so that they are hard to contest and then ENFORCE the election results.

In order to enforce our wins after the midterms, we will have to engage in direct action noncooperation by disrupting business as usual and refusing to cooperate with MAGA's attempts to steal our votes.

In these direct action noncooperation trainings we will learn:

**Training one:**

* Our strategy from now until the election

* Why we need to engage in noncooperation

* Why noncooperation is white people’s work

* What is noncooperation and why is it strategic

* What will our potential targets and actions be?

* Tips to build your crew who will take action with you

**Training two:**

* How to design a powerful action

* What roles are needed at actions

* Protest safety

**Training three:**

* Setting the tone for your action

* Messaging and visuals

* Documenting your action

* Media

Please join us for this three part series and be a part of our historic movement to block MAGA and build a world where we all thrive.

events.title: PR Committee Meeting - Democratic Party of Outagamie Co.
events.description:
Join the Democratic Party of Outagamie County’s Public Relations Committee to help us use tech to build the messages, visuals, outreach, and community connections that move local Democrats forward. We are an all-local, all-volunteer team within our county party, working to elect dems and further progressive values right here at home.

Volunteers with specialized skills often lead projects in their areas of expertise, but there’s room for learning and collaboration, too. You don’t need to know every tool already, we’re looking for people who are comfortable using technology, willing to learn, and ready to take ownership of tasks.

Whether you are a web developer, designer, photographer, chronically online, spreadsheet organizer, metrics-minded planner, email design wizard or simply someone who wants to pitch in when you can, there is a place for you on the PRC. Most volunteer roles are designed for a manageable 2–3 hours per week, and monthly project-based assignments are available for people who cannot take on an ongoing role.

At this meeting, we’ll:

- Welcome new and returning volunteers and make space for quick introductions
- Share updates on social media, email, events, and current PR projects
- Review open assignments and volunteer needs
- Match people with roles based on their interests, skills, and availability
- Discuss ways to support DPOC events, candidates, Outagamie Action Teams, and local community partners
- Gather ideas for future content, campaigns, and projects

We are currently especially looking for volunteers interested in:

- Social media static & Carousel content design, videos, and engagement
- Copywriting, editing, proofreading
- Graphic design, Canva templates, print materials, and email design
- Photography, short-form video, and video editing
- Website updates and event information
- Project coordination, deadline tracking, and intake support
- Press releases, talking points, media relations, and rapid-response writing
- Event promotion, flyer distribution, and volunteer coordination

No prior committee experience is required, just be comfortable working between your phone and laptop, learning new software as needed, and communicating digitally to a modern audience. We can provide tools, templates, direction, and a supportive team, bring your skills, curiosity, and ideas. If you are not ready for a standing role, you can also join our Project Volunteer pool and opt into one-off assignments that fit your schedule.

The PR Committee is where we turn good work into clear, local, people-centered communication. Help us make sure Outagamie County voters know what Democrats are doing, where they can get involved, and why every election matters.

Please RSVP so we can welcome you, share meeting materials, and help connect you with the right opportunities.

Meeting link sent upon sign up!

events.title: No Kings Vote Early RALLY & Souls to the Polls March- Lynchburg, Virginia
events.description:
NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY RALLY AND SOULS TO THE POLLS MARCH 

Indivisible LYH, the Lynchburg Voters League, NAACP Lynchburg Chapter, and the League of Women Voters of Central Virginia invite you to join us on October 18 from 2 to 4 beginning at Miller Park for a GET OUT THE VOTE  rally and Souls to the Polls March to vote early and in person at the Kemper Street registrar‘s office! 

For over a year, millions of people have come together to send a clear message: in America, we have no kings. No Kings: Vote Early is the next step: this is not purely a protest, it is a day of nonpartisan voter participation

Because in America, leaders do not get to choose who votes, whose voices matter, or what future our communities deserve. The people choose their leaders.

For generations, everyday people have changed the course of this country by organizing, marching, and voting. Power does not belong to billionaires, strongmen, or politicians who believe they are above accountability. Power belongs to the people, but only if we use it. On October 17, we are making sure every eligible voter knows their options for how to vote, has a plan to vote early where local law allows, and is ready to make their voice count. Join us.

No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.

Check out indivisiblelyh.org for more information.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters. A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Protest MAGA Tiffany before the Debate
events.description:
Tom Tiffany is coming to Milwaukee for his televised debate for Governor — and Birds on a Wire is showing up before he walks through those doors.

The debate will be held without a live audience, but that doesn’t mean Wisconsin voters have to be silent.

We’ll be outside — peaceful, joyful, loud and impossible to ignore.

Tiffany’s record in Congress will be part of what protesters are calling attention to. He voted for the 2025 reconciliation law that made major changes and reductions in projected federal Medicaid spending, while Tiffany has defended his vote as protecting benefits for vulnerable people and targeting waste and eligibility requirements.

We want Wisconsin voters asking questions about healthcare costs, Medicaid, reproductive freedom, immigration, public education, the cost of living, data centers, taxes, and whose interests our next governor will serve.

Bring your signs. Bring your friends. Bring your voice.

SHOW UP. STAND UP. SPEAK UP.

We have the power to make better possible — but only when we use it.

Join Birds on a Wire from 5:00-6:00 PM, immediately before the debate begins.

Let’s give the cameras something to see — and Wisconsin something to hear.

PEOPLE OVER BILLIONAIRES.
HEALTHCARE IS A HUMAN RIGHT.
WISCONSIN BELONGS TO ALL OF US.

This will be a peaceful, nonviolent protest.

One detail I’d consider adding to the event page: “The debate begins at 7 PM and will be televised statewide.” That gives people another reason to come—the protest is immediately before a major statewide media event. WISN says the debate will air in southeastern Wisconsin and be distributed to partner stations around the state.

events.title: ICE Out For Good Jacksonville, Florida
events.description:
On July 27th, 2026, Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitian immigrants was rolled back. According to former Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem, Haiti no longer met the requirements for TPS.

Hardly a month later, a young man by the name of Pierre Damas Bel would pull his car onto the shoulder of Interstate 70 in Clark County, Ohio, and walk into oncoming traffic where he was hit by a truck and died at the scene.

It was 2024 when Bel and his family — along with many other Haitian immigrants — came to the U.S. seeking asylum due to the unstable conditions of the country. Even now, as of 2026, according to the official website of the U.S. Department of State "Travel.State.Gov", Haiti is deemed a level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory. This means a very high risk of physical, sexual, or financial assault for both locals and U.S. citizens.

Despite Haiti being dangerous, TPS was rolled back. So, Pierre Damas Bel, someone who was not only an asylum seeker but also came to the U.S. in a legal manner, was issued an ankle monitor by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) shortly after July 27th. Within a month, Bel had his protected status revoked, was criminalized, shamed, and harassed. As a result, he took his own life on the morning of August 31st 2026.

There have been at least 10 suicides linked to ICE detention centers in 2025 and at least 2 linked to bullying regarding ICE.

This rally is intended to protest the fearmongering perpetuated by the current administration against all immigrants and people of color. We protest to demand restrictions on and/or the abolition of ICE. We demand to reinstate and extend TPS for Haitian and Syrian people seeking safety and asylum.

A broad coalition will organize on Thursday October 22nd 2026 at Friendship Fountain 1015 Museum Cir, Jacksonville, FL 32207. Rain or shine, let’s protest for justice and the safety of our communities. Remember to bring food and water bottles, as well as first aid if needed. Please also remember to abide by road rules, do not impede traffic or block parking lots or any safety vehicles that need passage. Do not do anything that puts you or your fellow protestors at risk.

*A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.*

events.title: Yes4EDR Town Hall - Plymouth
events.description:
Join Common Cause Massachusetts for a Town Hall at the Plymouth Public Library to discuss what a YES on ballot question #4 (Election Day Registration, or EDR) would mean for Massachusetts! Bring yourself and a few friends to this discussion.

About the Campaign

Election Day Registration (EDR) is a straightforward, secure, and proven reform to increase voter turnout and strengthen our democracy by allowing eligible voters to register to vote and cast a ballot on Election Day.

​To ensure EDR becomes law in Massachusetts, a coalition of nonpartisan, nonprofit groups that advocate for voting rights have formed the Yes 4 Election Day Registration ballot question committee. Members include Common Cause Massachusetts, League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, MassVOTE, Mass Voter Table, and the ACLU of Massachusetts. These groups have been leading the campaign for Election Day Registration in Massachusetts since 2008.

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
One night. One film. The founder of Moms First, in the room, in Denver.

RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mft-moms-first-present-no-country-for-mothers-live-with-reshma-saujani-tickets-2002174965218

Only valid tickets purchased through Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

We need to talk about something bigger than the next dance floor. The culture wars have divided us — this is how we come back together.

MFT is proud to partner with Moms First to bring their film No Country for Mothers to Apollo Hall, Denver — with founder Reshma Saujani joining us live.

No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the "girl boss" and "trad wife" labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. Following activist Reshma Saujani, the film charts a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win the kind of historic support families actually need.

Since its June 2026 NYC premiere, the film has reached 1,000+ community screenings nationwide and holds the record for the most producers ever credited on one feature. On November 9, it's Denver's turn, with a live, intimate Q&A led by the film's Executive Producer and Moms First Founder & CEO, Reshma, in person.

Moms First is fighting for the policy change mothers deserve — paid leave, real childcare, structural support. We've spent years building the other half of that fight: the community, joy, and permission to come first that prove what happens when moms feel seen, resourced, and supported — we take on the world.

The night:

- Cocktail hour, charcuterie & cash bar
- Full screening of No Country for Mothers
- Live Q&A with Reshma Saujani
- Apollo Hall, Denver — Monday, November 9, doors 5pm
- $45 (+ fees) per ticket · 10% of proceeds go directly to Moms First
- Dress code: glam, elevated cocktail — wear something that makes you feel powerful. Can't swing it? No sweat, just bring the vibe.

Endless gratitude to Apollo Hall for donating their beautiful space and believing in this mission as much as we do — this night wouldn't be possible without them.

This isn't for a side. It's for every mother who's tired of being asked to pick one.

RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mft-moms-first-present-no-country-for-mothers-live-with-reshma-saujani-tickets-2002174965218

Only valid tickets purchased from Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

In the month of October, we have to reach out to hundreds of thousands of neighbors to get out the vote and win this election, and we cannot do it without you. 

There are so many reasons to get involved right now. Whether you are struggling to pay your bills and need Elon Musk and other billionaires to pay their fair share. Whether you are fighting against climate change, against ICE, against genocide and foreign wars, or for abortion rights and freedoms of all kinds. You are needed. 

It doesn't matter whether you've knocked doors or made calls before — we start every event with a training and cannot wait to meet you!

events.title: GOTV Towson
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**
