events.title: Knock Your Neighbors

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join the Get the Facts Community Coalition for a neighborhood literature drop to help Coloradans learn about Proposition 132 and get out the vote ahead of the November election.

We’ll start at the CCJRC office with a quick overview of Proposition 132, what it would change, and the key facts voters should know. We’ll also make sure you feel prepared to answer basic questions if someone wants to learn more.

Then we’ll load you up with Get the Facts materials to take back to your own neighborhood and distribute to your neighbors.

This is a lit drop, NOT a full canvass. You will not be knocking on doors or expected to initiate conversations with voters. The goal is simply to leave educational materials in your neighborhood so people have accurate information about Proposition 132 as they prepare to vote.

If you happen to encounter a neighbor who wants to talk or asks you a question, don’t worry! Before you leave, we’ll walk through what to say, how to share the facts, and where to direct people who want more information.

No campaign or canvassing experience is required. Just come to learn the facts, grab your materials and snacks, and help us get information about Proposition 132 and a reminder to vote into neighborhoods across the community.

Come learn. Grab some lit. Drop it in your neighborhood. Help your community get the facts and get out the vote.

events.title: Purple on Purpose: Improv for Civil Discourse

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Forget everything you thought you knew about Improv. It’s not frightening, scary or demanding. It’s a lesson in life and in these times, it will serve us well.

Improv for Civil Discourse isn't a debate. There's no topic, no "sides," and no one arguing politics in this room. Just an evening of discovering how "yes, and" might lead to a better tomorrow. We experience acceptance, not agreement. Curiosity, not division. 

Our facilitator for the evening is Will Dennis. Will leads the Unscripted Leadership wing of Unscripted Productions, Ltd. in Washington Crossing. He is highly skilled at changing rooms through deep listening, humor, practical skill building, and strategic facilitation. 

This incredibly fun and enlightening evening will explore innovative ways to increase communication, collaboration, problem solving, adaptability, and creativity.

No pointing fingers. No he said/she said. No accusation.
Just joy and fun, and connection!

The event is free however, donations are welcomed.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth and Bend the Arc Riverdale in Rockland County NY-17!

location.venue: 50 Blauvelt Road, Nanuet (Miller Elmentary School Parking Lot

events.description:
Join Bend the Arc Riverdale and the Unity Democratic Club for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Dunmore Community Canvass: Knock on doors with Action Together!
events.description:
Community canvassing with Action Together NEPA is about more than just knocking on doors — it’s about building real connections with our neighbors. By having one-on-one conversations, we listen to what matters most to people, share important election information, and make sure every voice in our community is heard. These conversations are proven to be the most effective way to strengthen democracy and inspire action.


When you volunteer, you’ll be part of a supportive team, get quick training, and head out together to engage with your community. It’s a fun, energizing way to make new friends, build skills, and create real change right here for NEPA families. Let’s make sure that local voices shape the future of our region!


One more reason to canvass: all of our canvass volunteers get a free t-shirt! Be sure to include your size when you sign up so you can complete your fit when you head out with the team to knock on doors.

events.title: Get Out The Vote at Kent State (Statewide OSA Action)
events.description:
Students could flip House District 72, Kent State University’s seat in the State House, but it’s up to YOU to make the difference. Join your classmates and students from around the state to canvass to GET OUT THE VOTE at Kent State on October 23rd, 11-4 PM, so we can elect someone who will ACTUALLY represent Kent State students and put pro-SB 1 anti-Kent incumbent Heidi Workman out of a job.

The choice is between Heidi Workman, the incumbent who voted FOR Senate Bill 1, the demolition order for everything that makes Kent State feel like home. It shut down the Multicultural Center, the Women’s Center, and the LGBTQ+ Center in a single day. Students lost scholarships they were already counting on. Professors can’t even strike anymore. Students report Africana students – a program that only exists because students organized for it – is being cut, and even the May 4th class at the May 4th school is under threat. She never met with students. She endorsed Vivek Ramaswamy, who’s talked about shutting Kent State down – her own alma mater – and wants data centers all over Portage County. Jeff Clapper is Kent City Council president; he’s anti-data center, his daughter graduated from Kent State; and he actually wants to make college and trades affordable so students like us can build a future here. Students are pledging to vote, and they’re voting Clapper.

Join students from around the state as we carpool and travel to Kent to knock doors so we can talk to students about the facts of this race and make plans to vote. If students win HD 72, along with other key districts statewide, we could end the supermajority of Republicans that makes it impossible to better our campuses. This is students’ chance to take back our power in Ohio, and it’s up to YOU. RSVP here to get more information so that YOU can make a difference this November. 

We will teach you how to canvass and provide lunch.

events.title: Beacon Shine the Light Thursdays: ICE OUT of Great Neck!
events.description:
Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. When local police or sheriffs collaborate with ICE, it undermines trust, separates families, and makes all of us less safe.

***Our goal is simple and clear:***
No local resources for ICE. No contracts. No data-sharing. No collaboration.

At this event, we will:

1. Bring together neighbors, workers, and allies
2. Prepare to meet with local elected officials (or attend a public meeting)
3. Call on our [city/county/state] leaders to move forward policies that disentangle ICE from local law enforcement

Take concrete steps toward passing local protections

This effort builds on years of organizing led by immigrant communities nationwide — from the fight against 287g contracts to the sanctuary victories that have proven local action works. Cities and states that say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights.

There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

events.title: GOTV Windsor Mill
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

## Fight on Two Fronts: Health Equity is Political Power! 

**Vote. Call. Text. Write. And we'll do it in PINK.**

October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. It's also election season. And here's the truth: **Black women have higher mortality rates from breast cancer AND less political power to demand the healthcare access we deserve.**

This October 24, we're connecting both fights.

The Equity Alliance is hosting **Paint the Ballot Pink** - a full-day GOTV (Get Out The Vote) mobilization combined with Breast Cancer Awareness programming. We're calling voters, texting voters, writing postcards, all while honoring the fight against breast cancer and the fight for our votes.

### What You'll Do:

- ☎️ Make voter contact calls (we provide scripts and training)

- 📱 Text banking to reach voters

- ✉️ Write postcards to voters to push them to the polls on Nov. 3

- 🎀 Connect with breast cancer support organizations and health partners

- 🗳️ Join the PINK PARADE to the election commission for early voting


## _We deserve healthy bodies AND political power_

At the Campbell County Democratic Party, our motto is "Here For Good." That means we are here to serve our community and make it just a little bit better through our hands-on acts of service, showing up for our neighbors when it matters most.

We invite all community members, volunteers, and local Democrats to join us as we volunteer our time and energy at The Soup Kitchen on the second Monday of each month. Whether you are helping prepare meals, serving food, or assisting with cleanup, your presence makes a direct, meaningful difference for families and individuals in our area.

Come put our values into action alongside fellow community members who care deeply about lifting one another up.

What to Expect & How to Prepare

Tasks: Volunteers may help with food prep, serving guests, kitchen organization, and clean-up duties.

What to Wear: Please wear comfortable, casual clothing and closed-toe shoes. Aprons and hair restraints will be provided on-site if needed.

All Are Welcome: You don't need any prior volunteering experience, just a compassionate heart and a willingness to lend a hand!

Note: Please RSVP in advance so we can coordinate our volunteer count with the soup kitchen coordinators. We look forward to serving alongside you!

events.title: March to the Polls to Vote 🗳️ Early-Wayne Township ❌👑Krannert Park

location.venue: Tawheed Islamic School Parking Lot (Marching to Krannert Park as a group)

events.description:
March to the Polls to Vote Early in Wayne Township ❌👑w/ Hoosier Voting Alliance and partners.  https://www.hoosiervotingalliance.org/event

Millions of Americans have joined together to reject power grabs and voter suppression. Now, we are taking the next step: moving from protest 🪧to participation, making sure we are ready to vote early and choose our own leaders. No king, no politician, and no president gets to decide who wins an election.  Let's celebrate Marion County voices 🗣️ at the polls. 🎉 

The starting point for this march will be a short walk 🚶🏽‍♀️‍➡️ from the voting center starting at Tawheed Islamic School Parking lot. This march will take place rain ☔or shine 🌤️, except in the case of thunderstorms. ⛈️Come join us! Bring a friend 🤝, offer a ride 🚌, make a plan📓.

You must be registered to vote in Marion County & provide a photo ID 🪪to cast your ballot 🗳️ Voter registration closes on October 5. Please verify ✅ your voter registration at IndianaVoters.com by the 5th. 📆

By submitting this form 📝, you consent to sharing your information with the event's sponsoring organizations.  See you on October 24th! 📢

events.description:
Join the KY State AFL-CIO for the Labor2026 program as we hit the pavement to build power for working families!

Elections are won at the doorstep. This election season, we are mobilizing union members across the Commonwealth to talk to our siblings and neighbors about the issues that matter most: protecting our right to organize, securing fair wages, and ensuring safe working conditions for every Kentuckian.

Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or a first-time volunteer, we need your voice. We will provide all the training, materials, and snacks you need to have meaningful, face-to-face conversations with voters in your community. By showing up for our endorsed candidates, we ensure that labor has a seat at the table in Frankfort and beyond.

Why Join a Labor Phone Bank?

Strength in Numbers: Show our collective power as a unified labor movement.

Direct Impact: Research shows that peer-to-peer union conversations are the most effective way to turn out the vote.

Solidarity: Connect with fellow union members from across various trades and sectors.

In Solidarity, The KY State AFL-CIO Labor 2026 Team

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Huntington (NY-01)!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Phonebank to Elect Justin J. Pearson for Congress!
events.description:
## Hey friend, got a phone? Great. We need your help real quick!.

### Don't worry, you can help us from anywhere in the United States.

**The Equity Alliance Fund** needs you to grab your phone and make some calls with us. Here's why:

Tennessee's 9th Congressional District was redrawn, splitting Memphis across three congressional districts and leaving thousands of Tennesseans navigating new district lines. In fact, many voters affected by the changes were not expected to receive notices in the mail telling them their district had even changed.

We know this was a deliberate attempt to dilute our vote and our voices. So, this is where we need YOU...

We’re calling our people. We’re making sure they know their district, and we’re making sure Black voters understand the power we still hold, no matter how they redraw the map.

We need to make sure our communities know what district they are in, where they vote, what's at stake, and **why we're supporting Justin J. Pearson for Congress.**

Justin has shown us what it looks like to fight for Black communities, not just when cameras are watching, but when our neighborhoods, our families and our futures are on the line. 

Never phone banked before? We’ll show you how. 
Been doing this for years? We need you, too. 

Grab your phone, share this with your people, give us a little of your time and help us make a BIG impact.


_Zoom link will be sent via text and email 48 hours before the event._

Fall Festival Volunteer Opportunity

Date: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
Time: 3:00–6:00 p.m.

Join us for an afternoon of fall fun as we bring together children and families for Thompson’s Child Development Center Fall Festival! We’re looking for enthusiastic volunteers to help create a welcoming and memorable experience filled with games, face painting, temporary tattoos, delicious food, and more.

Volunteer Responsibilities:

* Assist with event setup and breakdown.
* Help facilitate games and activity stations.
* Support face painting and temporary tattoo stations.
* Welcome families and assist with event activities.
* Help maintain a safe, organized, and engaging environment for all attendees.

Volunteers should be comfortable standing for extended periods, interacting with children and families, and assisting with light lifting and event materials as needed.

Come share your time, spread some joy, and help make this Fall Festival a wonderful experience for the families we serve!

events.title: Sweetwater Monthly Executive Committee Meeting!
events.description:
🌵 Sweetwater County Democrats Monthly Meeting

Third Thursday. 6 PM. Rotating towns, same crew. 💙

It’s our monthly Executive Committee meeting! Come hang out, catch up, and help keep the wheels turning for the Sweetwater County Democrats.

We’ll talk about what’s happening, what’s coming up, where we can lend a hand, and how we keep showing up for our community.

📍 Green River Library
🕕 6:00 PM
📅 October 15th, 3rd Thursday of the Month 


We’re keeping our monthly meetings moving around Sweetwater County so we can stay connected to folks across the county. That means we’ll see you in Green River in October, Rock Springs in November, Green River in December, and keep rotating from there.

📅 October 15 — Green River
📅 November 19 — Rock Springs
📅 December 17 — Green River

We’ll kick things off at 6 PM with a short meeting — usually just 10–20 minutes to cover the business we actually need to cover. Then? That’s when the good stuff happens.

Stick around to catch up with fellow Democrats, meet new folks, swap ideas, ask questions, or jump into a training or organizing project. Sometimes we’ll have a specific training planned; sometimes we’ll just figure out what our community needs that month.

No fancy credentials required. No secret handshake. Just show up, bring a friend, and help us build a county party that knows its neighbors and knows how to show up for them.

Come for the meeting. Stay for the friends. 💙

events.title: Monthly Executive Committee Meeting! (Sweetwater)
events.description:
🌵 Sweetwater County Democrats Monthly Meeting

Third Thursday. 6 PM. Rotating towns, same crew. 💙

It’s our monthly Executive Committee meeting! Come hang out, catch up, and help keep the wheels turning for the Sweetwater County Democrats.

We’ll talk about what’s happening, what’s coming up, where we can lend a hand, and how we keep showing up for our community.

📍 White Mountain Library
🕕 6:00 PM
📅 3rd Thursday of the Month 


We’re keeping our monthly meetings moving around Sweetwater County so we can stay connected to folks across the county. That means we’ll see you in Green River in October, Rock Springs in November, Green River in December, and keep rotating from there.

📅 October 15 — Green River
📅 November 19 — Rock Springs
📅 December 17 — Green River

We’ll kick things off at 6 PM with a short meeting — usually just 10–20 minutes to cover the business we actually need to cover. Then? That’s when the good stuff happens.

Stick around to catch up with fellow Democrats, meet new folks, swap ideas, ask questions, or jump into a training or organizing project. Sometimes we’ll have a specific training planned; sometimes we’ll just figure out what our community needs that month.

No fancy credentials required. No secret handshake. Just show up, bring a friend, and help us build a county party that knows its neighbors and knows how to show up for them.

Come for the meeting. Stay for the friends. 💙

events.title: Tacos & Treats: Your Vote, Your Voice, Your Fiesta
events.description:
**Join us for Tacos & Treats: Your Vote, Your Voice, Your Fiesta!**

Bring the whole family for a fun, welcoming, **nonpartisan civic fiesta** where community, food, and voting resources come together.

Enjoy **free tacos, Halloween activities, festive treats, music, local vendors, and a family-friendly Halloween contest**—all while getting helpful **voting resources** in one convenient place. Guests can check their voter registration, learn about voting options, find official ballot drop boxes, and get support creating a personalized plan to participate in the election.

After gathering together, we’ll offer a short community walk to a nearby official ballot drop box, with rides available for those who need them. Anyone who is ready to return their ballot can do so safely and securely on October 24!

Washington’s 2026 general-election voting period begins **October 16**, with ballots mailed to registered voters. Voters can use official ballot drop boxes, return ballots by mail, or access voting centers for in-person assistance. Official drop boxes are available throughout the state and accept ballots through **8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3**.

**Join your neighbors on October 24 for food, fun, music, conversation, and the information you need to make a voting plan that works for you.**

Come for the tacos. Stay for the treats. **Leave ready to participate!**

This event is in partnership with Poder Latinx, WCA, La Casa Hogar, NAACP and APIC.

events.title: Ready to Vote: Duplin County
events.description:
Are you concerned about what you’ll face when you go to vote in 2026? Want to connect what’s on the ballot to community concerns? Interested in getting trained to protect voters this fall? 

Common Cause North Carolina has got what you need to help your neighbors get ready to vote (and stay safe as they go). 

This 60-minute Ready to Vote training, co-hosted ShackleFree and Duplin County NAACP, will help you turn anxiety into action and a desire to volunteer into voter protection you can be proud of!  

Join us in Duplin: 

📅 October 18, 2026

🕕 2:00-3:00 PM

What are you waiting for? Whether you’re a seasoned organizer or new to helping your neighbors, we’re ready to help you get your community Ready to Vote!

events.title: CLAWS OUT FOR ANGIE NIXON! Livestream with Angie & Friends
events.description:
We’re going LIVE on CLAWS OUT FOR ANGIE NIXON with The Conscious Lee, Sara Wiles, USMC Angry Veteran (Matt Gordon), Abiola Agoro, and more good troublemakers on Sunday, October 25. And Angie herself is closing it out.

We’re spilling the tea on her opponent, Ashley Moody, laying out what the billionaires don’t want you to know, and having some laughs trying to figure out what the hell the deal is with JD Vance.

It’s FREE to join the live-streamed action. Get in the chat with claws OUT and bring your takes and questions to the comments.

We’re also raising grassroots dollars to fuel Angie’s people-powered fight. If you can chip in $5–$25, amazing. But first, get yourself registered!

events.title: Working People's Canvass for Chris VanDijk & Adrienne Benevidez | Denver
events.description:
Join union members, workers, neighbors, and supporters as we hit the doors to elect Chris VanDijk (HD32) & Adrienne Benevidez (SD21) in the November 3rd General Election!

Chris & Adriene are fighting for working families and standing up for good-paying union jobs, safe workplaces, affordable healthcare, and dignity on the job. Together, we can build the grassroots power needed to win this election.

We’ll meet for a brief training before heading out to talk with voters in the community. No experience necessary — new volunteers are welcome! Canvassing materials, scripts, and walk packets will be provided.

Event Details

Date: Sunday November 1st
Time: 10 AM
Location: 5660 Logan St Denver, CO 80216

What to Bring

Comfortable walking shoes

Water bottle

Weather-appropriate clothing

Union swag encouraged!

Together, we can elect leaders who will fight for workers and deliver for our communities. We hope to see you there!

events.title: CA: Stop Data Centers Texting Power Hour

**Join our texting power hour to support the latest data center moratorium push!**

- **What:** Stop CA Data Centers Texting Power Hour 
- **When:** Biweekly on Thursdays, 4-5 p.m.
- **Where:** On Zoom – Register for the link to join.

**We'll be texting constituents to connect them with key elected officials scheduled to vote on an upcoming moratorium to urge them to vote yes.**

From Oakland to LA, communities need our help to get moratoriums across the finish line.

Help communities pass data center moratoriums and bans in California!

We’re hitting the pavement and knocking on doors for Rob Sand and Iowa Democrats up and down the ticket. Talking to voters face to face is the best way to have an impact on this election. What better way to make a difference this election than talking to your friends and neighbors!

Rob is visiting every corner of the state to share his vision of an Iowa that isn’t Redder or Bluer, but Better and Truer with voters, and so are we! Whether you’re a long-time volunteer or stepping up to help for the first time, we’ve got you covered.

We can't wait to see you!

events.title: Can't Stop CA: Orange County Neighborhood Vote Protection Training

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Protect the vote in your neighborhood!

Become a neighborhood vote protector. Every vote is a decision about our healthcare, housing, wages, and who gets to make the rules – which is exactly why it needs to be protected. The Trump administration is trying rig the outcomes of the election by creating chaos, fear and new roadblocks to keep us from voting.

We are training dozens of Neighborhood Vote Protectors across Orange County to watch the polls in their communities, safely document and report incidents to legal experts, and make sure every voter knows their rights to cast a ballot without fear or intimidation.

See you soon!

~

¡Protege el voto en tu barrio!

Conviértete en defensor del voto en tu vecindario. Cada voto es una decisión sobre nuestra salud, vivienda, salarios y quién dicta las reglas; por eso mismo, es fundamental protegerlo. La administración Trump está intentando manipular los resultados de las elecciones creando caos, miedo y nuevos obstáculos para impedirnos votar.

Estamos capacitando a decenas de Protectores Vecinales del Voto en todo el Condado de Orange para que vigilen las urnas en sus comunidades, documenten e informen de manera segura los incidentes a expertos legales y se aseguren de que cada votante conozca su derecho a emitir su voto sin temor ni intimidación.

¡Nos vemos pronto!

events.title: Sippin’ Pints & Speakin’ Politics
events.description:
## *Galt x Neighbors RESIST are fostering a new, welcoming space in Galt to get involved, remain informed, and have a greater voice in the local area!*

### ** *We are founded in centrist and left-leaning ideals, but open to all perspectives!* **

> ### ***LET’S RESIST DIVISIVENESS, TOGETHER!*** ✌️🦋💕💪

#### Come drop by River Rock Brewery on a 2nd or 4th Tuesday, and join your local community in discussing local and current politics! We also have local event fliers, campaign/action information, signatures for Medicare For All, occasional post carding, and so so much more! Come get involved! 💕

##### 🦋 *It’s hard to admit, but there are so many of us long-time Galtonian residents that have scattered further north and south in our activism ventures; Meanwhile, our city needs us right here and now!! If you’re interested in getting organized more locally, ***please***, come join us!!* 🦋

#### Sit with us at the table to partake in conversations about local & federal government, current events, campaigns, causes, activism, volunteering, local happenings, and ways we hope to achieve positive impacts in our community together!!

### 💪 ***Connect With Neighbors*** 
### 👀 ***Discuss Local News*** 
### 💕 ***Share Concerns*** 
### 🦋 ***Get Involved and Active***

events.title: True North Boston Bi-Monthly Zoom
events.description:
You are invited to True North Boston's second meeting of the month – this time on Zoom.   

After meeting in person the 1st Tuesday of the month, as needed, we meet virtually on the 3rd Tuesday.   


### For Tuesday, October 20th: 

> Election Day is three weeks away, and the work of defending our communities and our democracy is only beginning. Join True North Action Alliance Boston's Zoom meeting to get on the same page about how we’ll respond when something happens, and how that response fits into the bigger picture.   
>     
> **What we’ll cover:**
>     
> - True North’s rapid response plan: how alerts go out, how to get plugged in, and what your role could be
> - How our plan connects to local, state, and national rapid response networks
> - Where election defense work fits in, and how you can help protect the vote in the weeks ahead
> - Time for questions and discussion
>
> **Before the meeting — a short homework assignment:**   
Please take an hour before we meet to catch last week’s episode of What’s the Plan?, the weekly show hosted by Indivisible co-founders Ezra Levin and Leah Greenberg. You can **[watch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I3dJVCV5_Ak&list=PLS73jRQ3qBiUf_C76Z1qoR4rAiGGoxTcT&index=1)** or **[listen](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/whats-the-plan-with-leah-greenberg-and-ezra-levin/id1869456664?i=1000794064034)** here. It’s a clear, practical look at where things stand and what we can do next, and it’ll give us a shared starting point for our conversation. If you only have a little time, start watching/listening around 30 minutes for the specific discussion about rapid response.

*Please sign up save your spot and receive the meeting link.*    

*We look forward to seeing you on Zoom!*

events.title: Write to Win
events.description:
Join People Powered Maine to meet your neighbors ready to do the work with you. Building grassroots power happens face-to-face with people who share your values. Come for 20 minutes or stay for the whole two hours. All materials, postcard lists, and writing supplies will be provided.

What we’ll do together:

Connect & Reflect: Share experiences with neighbors, process thoughts on upcoming elections, and discuss local strategy.

Write & Mobilize: Handwrite postcards to key voters who we have had conversations with at their doors to drive turnout.


People Powered Maine is an independent, volunteer-led 501(c)(4) building a permanent grassroots organizing group in Maine, county by county. We organize year-round around a seven-point economic and human-rights platform.

New people are always welcome.

events.title: The Vote Is Sacred Tour - Montgomery, Alabama

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. 

Interfaith Alliance of Alabama and Interfaith Alliance are partnering together for this stop. Featuring a press conference and rally at the Alabama State Capitol, you’ll hear from national and local faith leaders as we stand together in solidarity for democracy and civic participation. 

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

events.title: Train Your Neighbors - Ambassador Program
events.description:
Join and Grow the Hands Off NYC Ambassador Program!

If you are ready to prepare yourself and your neighbors to stand up as unified New Yorkers into the midterms and beyond, join our ambassador program.

In this training, we’ll prepare you to train more of our neighbors on the risks we’re facing, what we’re doing in response, and how they can join the fight.

You’ll leave the training with concrete steps to bring to your neighbors and grow our collective strength across NYC. And once you’re an Ambassador you’ll be part of a citywide web of trained, connected neighbors ready to move together when it matters. 

What to expect: 
📅 Monthly Training of Trainers — every last Thursday of the month
📍 Virtual gatherings
🎯 You'll leave with training materials and messaging to run your own neighbor sessions
🔁 Report back at the next Training of Trainers to share progress and get support
🤝 Ongoing support via monthly check-ins and a Signal thread 

New York City is big - it will take many of us to ensure every borough is equipped with the knowledge and connection to stand in their power and face what’s to come, together.

events.title: Currituck Canvass

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**Join us for the Currituck Canvass!** Connecting face-to-face with voters is one of the most effective ways we can build community and make our voices heard across Currituck County.

Whether you’re a seasoned canvasser or taking to the trail for the first time, we’ll provide all the training, talking points, and materials you need before we head out.

**We Need Everyone: Rookies and Vets**

If you are new to canvassing, don’t worry! You will never go out alone. Every newcomer is paired with an experienced veteran who will guide you every step of the way. We work in teams to ensure a supportive, collaborative entry into grassroots activism.

**Safe, Professional, and Guided**

Your safety and comfort are our top priorities.

-   Targeted Outreach: We use advanced data to ensure you are visiting voters who are ready for the No Kings message. Politeness First: A simple "Thank you for your time!" is all you need for any rare non-supporter; you are always in control of the conversation.
    
-   Full Training: We provide on-site training before every shift. You  
    will receive a professionally developed script and hands-on guidance on using the MiniVAN app.
    
-   Ongoing Support: For any difficult questions, you can immediately  
    contact your Canvass Organizer for assistance.
    

**An Inspiring and Energizing Experience**

Canvassing is more than just work—it is empowering, rewarding, and energizing. Our volunteers consistently return from their shifts fired up by the incredible stories and connections they’ve made with neighbors. Spending time with like-minded activists and standing up against tyranny to secure a win is an unmatched feeling.

## What to Bring

-   Comfortable walking shoes.
    
-   A fully charged smartphone with the MiniVAN app installed.
    
-   Sunscreen or rain gear, depending on the forecast.
    
-   Water and snacks.
    
-   Your passion for democracy and making a difference!
    

[Click here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fLkpSPnA_FJhqjpU1tHU_7na4djzYl7rFKeAEX9oBNc/edit?usp=sharing) for more canvassing tips.

## Ready to help lay the groundwork for victory?

Sign up today and help us build the unstoppable momentum we need for November!

events.title: Phone Bank Party with Iowa City SURJ

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!##

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:##

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?## 

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:## 

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:### 

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

Join Common Cause Massachusetts for a Town Hall at the Cambridge Public Library to discuss what a YES on ballot question #4 (Election Day Registration, or EDR) would mean for Massachusetts! Bring yourself and a few friends to this discussion.

About the Campaign

Election Day Registration (EDR) is a straightforward, secure, and proven reform to increase voter turnout and strengthen our democracy by allowing eligible voters to register to vote and cast a ballot on Election Day.

​To ensure EDR becomes law in Massachusetts, a coalition of nonpartisan, nonprofit groups that advocate for voting rights have formed the Yes 4 Election Day Registration ballot question committee. Members include Common Cause Massachusetts, League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, MassVOTE, Mass Voter Table, and the ACLU of Massachusetts. These groups have been leading the campaign for Election Day Registration in Massachusetts since 2008.

events.description:
Indivisible Alamance NC, in partnership with the Alamance NAACP and many, many others want you to vote EARLY!

This is open to everyone. Voters, supporters, candidates, families... you get the idea.

We know things are going to be a bit gonzo on election day. We know absentee and mail-in voting is under attack both nationally and right here in North Carolina.

Therefore, to encourage people to vote (and make it a little more fun and interesting) we are hosting early voting marches TO EVERY EARLY VOTING SITE!

## Getting Ready to vote

If you haven't registered to vote yet, you still can through October 9th. But wait, there's more! During early voting, you can register when you arrive at the early voting location and vote immediately.

If you're already registered, please [check your registration](https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) to be sure everything is accurate and you haven't been unexpectedly cancelled.

## The more the merrier!

You can sign up to join us for any or all of the events but you can only vote once.

## Elmira Community Center SOULS TO THE POLLS

This is the big one. If you haven't voted by now, please plan to vote here. We want to ensure the numbers support keeping this early voting location open for many years to come.

When: Sunday, October 15, Meet at 2:00 P.M. March at 2:30 P.M.

Where: Parking lot at the corner of Hatch St and Rauhut St, Burlington - [map link](https://maps.app.goo.gl/JkAR26inNgfJq5V47)

How: We'll start with a invocation, a short rally and a speaker At about 2:30, we'll begin marching as a group to the community center. We will provide flags. You are welcome to provide family-friendly signs with your voting message.

We'll provide a light meal, snacks and water for everyone (while supplies last) at the destination. Rides back to the start will be available for those who need them. We'll also have a follow vehicle in case anyone needs assistance getting to the polling site.

events.title: October 24 Volunteer Tree-Wrapping Event! 9am at Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens
events.description:
Join us for a morning of stewardship volunteering at Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens! 

Help us protect the trees of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens from the busy beavers. As beaver activity increases this fall, volunteers will cut lengths of welded-wire fencing to size for approximately 252 trees near the ponds, pools, and wetland boardwalk. Each piece will be wrapped around a tree trunk and secured to form a sturdy circular barrier, shielding the bark from gnawing and damage. This hands-on project directly safeguards the park's beloved tree canopy, cultural integrity, and public viewshed that makes Kenilworth so special. 

Free registration, open to groups and individuals.

Space is limited for this event and pre-registration is required. 

Participate in a morning of park stewardship by taking on litter collection around the park. All tools will be provided. This event will run rain or shine—please dress accordingly and plan to work outside!

The park is accessible by car and there is a large visitor parking lot available for use. By Metro, the park entrance is 1.0 mile from the Deanwood Metro Station and 1.3 miles from the Minnesota Ave Station, both on the Orange Line. By foot or bike, access the park via the Anacostia River Trail.

We'll provide all necessary tools and supplies. We recommend you bring a water bottle, snack, hat, bag/backpack, a change of clothes, and sun protection. Please wear clothes and shoes you aren't afraid to get wet or muddy and dress according to the weather. We recommend that you do not wear jewelry.

We encourage families and students to join us. Volunteers under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult chaperone, parent or guardian. This event is eligible for Student Service Learning hours (SSL). Bring your form or email it to info@fokag.org.

Contact: For all other questions or concerns reach out to info@fokag.org.

More about Friends of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens: Check out our website (www.kenaqgardens.org) and follow us on Instagram, Facebook and Twitter (@kenaqgardens).

PHOTO/MEDIA RELEASE- By registering for this event, you agree to the following: 

"I grant Friends of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens, its partners, and representatives permission to use, publish, and share photographs, video, audio recordings, and other media of me for educational, promotional, and mission-related purposes. This includes use in print, digital, and social media. I understand that no compensation will be provided for such use."

events.title: Early Voting March to the Polls Elon South Gym
events.description:
Indivisible Alamance NC, in partnership with many, many others want you to vote EARLY!

This is open to everyone. Voters, supporters, candidates, families... you get the idea.

We know things are going to be a bit gonzo on election day. We know absentee and mail-in voting is under attack both nationally and right here in North Carolina.

Therefore, to encourage people to vote (and make it a little more fun and interesting) we are hosting early voting marches TO EVERY EARLY VOTING SITE!

## Getting Ready to vote

If you haven't registered to vote yet, you still can through October 9th. But wait, there's more! During early voting, you can register when you arrive at the early voting location and vote immediately.

If you're already registered, please [check your registration](https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) to be sure everything is accurate and you haven't been unexpectedly cancelled.

## The more the merrier!

You can sign up to join us for any or all of the events but you can only vote once.

## Elon South Gym

When: Wednesday, October 21. Meet at 5:30 P.M. Start at 6:00 P.M.

Where: Elon Community Church, 271 N Williamson Ave, Elon 27244

How: We'll have a short speech and provide light snacks and water at 5:30. We will begin the march at 6:00. We'll provide flags. You are welcome to provide family-friendly signs with your voting message.

events.description:
Vote Early Day: Fall Fiesta 

Voting early is one way to make your voice heard, and making a plan can help you feel ready to cast your ballot. That’s why Poder Latinx and community partners are hosting Fall Fiesta on Saturday, October 24: to bring our Orlando community together, celebrate Vote Early Day, and help neighbors take the next step toward voting.

Bring your family and enjoy live music, DJs, cultural performances, local food vendors, art, and fall activities. You can also visit our nonpartisan voter information stations to learn about your voting options, find an early voting location, and make a plan that works for you. Free transportation to an early voting location will be available for eligible voters who need a ride.

Join us for a day of community, culture, and civic participation!

**Drive directly** to Milwaukee, Wisconsin and knock some doors for Wisconsin Democrats!

We’re just weeks away from the crucial 2026 Midterm elections where we have a once in a generation shot at electing for substantial Democratic leadership. Together, we’ll defeat Donald Trump’s extremist agenda once and for all, but we’ll only succeed with your help. 

We'll see you in Milwaukee!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

**FEATURING:**

This is all about building community, strengthening relationships, and simply enjoying time together. Bring your family, bring a friend, and come connect with us!

**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.title: Wisconsin Voter Registration Calls with Rust Belt Rising
events.description:
Join Rust Belt Rising to help make sure that everyone is able to vote in this year's General Election!

Rust Belt Rising's innovative voter registration programs helped thousands of Great Lakes state residents register the last three cycles and will do so again this year.

Here's how it works: RBR partners at Civitech find targets of people who would likely vote our way but are unregistered at their current address as they compare commercial mail lists and voter files. They will mail these targets a pre-filled voter registration form with a motivational flyer and postage to their clerk. That's where we come in. In addition to our texting them, we need volunteers to call these targets to encourage them to complete the easy process of registering.

We would love for you to be part of a team that makes these calls to Wisconsin voters as part of our virtual voter registration chase! 

We'll teach you everything you know over Zoom and get you calling to remind voters to register because there is an election coming up!

events.title: Bradstock and W&J Dems Town Hall
events.description:
Southwestern Pennsylvania deserves a representative who listens.

Join Alan Bradstock and the Washington & Jefferson College Democrats for a community Town Hall in Washington, PA.

This Town Hall, co-hosted by the W&J College Democrats, is an opportunity for students, community members, and voters from across the area to ask questions, discuss the issues that matter most to them, and hear Alan’s vision for the future of Pennsylvania’s 14th Congressional District.

Come be part of a real conversation about the challenges facing our communities—from jobs and economic development to healthcare, veterans’ issues, Social Security, Medicare, and the future of Southwestern Pennsylvania.

Whether you’re a student, a longtime supporter, still getting to know Alan, or simply interested in learning more about the issues affecting our region, we hope you’ll join us.

Event Details

📅 Wednesday, October 21, 2026
🕕 6:00–8:00 PM
📍 Elks Lodge #776
138 E. Maiden St.
Washington, PA 15301

Co-hosted by the W&J College Democrats and Bradstock for Congress.

Doors open at 5:30 PM.

Questions will be taken from attendees throughout the event.

We look forward to seeing you there!

About Alan Bradstock

Alan Bradstock is the Democratic candidate for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 14th Congressional District. A U.S. Army veteran and former FBI Special Agent, Alan has spent his career in public service and is running to bring integrity, accountability, and common-sense leadership to Washington.

events.title: Hop on the bus to knock doors in Allentown (PA-07) to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Bob Brooks. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The next bus bus will leave from the Hudson Yards Area (600 W 34th St.) on Saturday, October 3 at 8:30 am and return around 7:30 pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:30 am to 5:30 pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

events.title: Tax the Billionaires: Protest Tesla HQ for YES on Prop 40
events.description:

California is one of the wealthiest places in the world, but working people are being asked to pay the price for devastating healthcare cuts so billionaires like Tesla CEO Elon Musk can get more tax breaks.

Prop 40 is our chance to change that. It makes billionaires pay their fair share so California doesn't lose healthcare funding and essential services.

At this weekly peaceful protest, we will be raising visibility for the billionaire tax, voter registration, and all things local! ✊🏽

Together, we're building a grassroots movement to mobilize one million Californians and win YES on Prop 40.

Tax billionaires. Save lives. Vote YES on Prop 40.

events.title: Studio Connections Theatre Company Tucson Party At The Polls!

address_lines: The polling place is in the library.  The party is in the parking lot!

events.description:
# **LET’S HAVE A HALLOWEEN PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️  
CAUSE VOTING ISN'T SPOOKY!

Celebrate our community. Cast your vote together.

We’re turning the ballot box into a Halloween block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power as the people!  

Join Studio Connections Theatre Company for a celebration of civic power, music, theatre and community spirit.  

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.  Drop your vote off with your pals, if you're so inclined!  Then stay and put the party back into political party! Costumes, singing voices, and willingness to be silly are highly encouraged but not required.  But all performers need an audience, too!


📍 Eckstrom-Columbus Library Parking Lot
4350 E. 22nd St.

📅  October 30 from 2-5 pm

There will be food by Revolutionary Grounds, music, karaoke, prizes, and other wacky activities!  Spectacle, for sure!

***Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.  This is a party for all parties.  Even those who are of no party are welcome to party.
events.accessibility_notes: The event will take place in the library parking lot, not within the library itself (that's the polling space).  But, you can use it for all the calls of nature- and the lot for parking.

events.title: CCNM Virtual Phonebank Party
events.description:
Join Cerelle, Cesar, and Abraham for Common Cause New Mexico’s Virtual Phonebank Party!

We’ll gather on Zoom to reconnect with people who have previously connected with Common Cause New Mexico, listen to their interests, and share upcoming events and volunteer opportunities.

New to phonebanking? You’re welcome here! We’ll provide a conversation guide, a brief demonstration, time to practice, and support while you make calls.

**Schedule**

Sessions run from 6-7:00pm on the dates listed. 
Zoom opens at 5:45pm for setup assistance. First-time callers are strongly encouraged to join early.

**What to bring**

- A computer with internet access for Zoom and Action Builder.

- Access to your email.

- A phone or another working calling method.

We call manually, without an automated dialer. If you prefer not to display your personal phone number, please set up and test a separate calling number, such as Google Voice, before the session.

After signing up, please review the preparation instructions sent to attendees. We’ll help you get comfortable and ready to start calling!

Approximately 77% of our volunteers in 2024 came from these phone banks, but we can't do it without your help!

A great way that you can make a difference is by calling volunteers and Democrats in our community and inviting them to take action with us. Whether you're an experienced volunteer or a first-time phone banker, we'll make sure you have everything you need for a successful experience. And once you get started, you'll find that phone banking is fun and rewarding!

We need all hands on deck to fight back against Trump and the Republican agenda, so sign up here to join us, and we can't wait to see you there!

California is one of the wealthiest places in the world, but working people are being asked to pay the price for devastating healthcare cuts so billionaires can get more tax breaks.

Prop 40 is our chance to change that. It makes billionaires pay their fair share so California doesn't lose healthcare funding and essential services.

At this community canvass, we'll be passing out literature in support of Prop 40 while making our way down 4th Street. Costumes encouraged!

We will meet at at V room (918 E 4th St, Long Beach, CA 90802) and then make our way through the night east on 4th St, ending the night at O'Connell's (2746 E 4th St, Long Beach, CA 90814)!

Together, we're building a grassroots movement to mobilize one million Californians and win YES on Prop 40.

Tax billionaires. Save lives. Vote YES on Prop 40.

events.title: ICE Out For Good Great Neck: Beacon Shine the Light Thursdays
events.description:
Join The Beacon for Thursday Shine the Light, as we bring our voices to the street every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 PM.

Each week, we make our voices heard wherever we are. As beacons, we shine light by making a sign and bringing it outside. Don't have a sign? Don't worry! You can borrow one of ours.

Together, we are building visible resistance and organized compassion, meeting our neighbors, and joining together in acts of solidarity. We find joy in resistance through community, music, comedy and street theater.

Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. When local police or sheriffs collaborate with ICE, it undermines trust, separates families, and makes all of us less safe. Here in Nassau County, families continue to live in terror of separation, detainment, detention and deportation.

We stand weekly in opposition to this unprecedented assault on the rights, safety, and economic security of people in this country. For 30 minutes every Thursday, we say ICE OUT OF OUR COMMUNITIES!  ICE OUT FOR GOOD! and we stand in favor of compassionate democracy and against cruelty, fear and despair.

People that come together in solidarity and say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights. There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

There are Beacon groups all over the USA. Our local Great Neck group meets every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 pm. We are joined by the Singing Resistance Great Neck to sing songs of solidarity and resistance, old and new.

For more information on The Beacon, visit www.beaconfordemocracy.org

A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.

Nonviolent at all times and lawful activities only
Community-led and locally grounded
Respectful of those grieving
Focused on accountability, not spectacle
Daytime events only

events.description:

Local award winning chef Erin Edds will be serving her gourmet craft dirty sodas, available for purchase, to help keep you energized while you contact voters.

We will have three ways to get involved, and lots of experienced people ready to show you the ropes- please come ready to learn new skills and have fun!

1) Phone banking: bring your fully charged phone, headset with microphone, and optional laptop if you prefer a bigger screen. You will get a list of voters to call and an easy script to follow! These will all be likely supporters who just need a gentle reminder to go vote.

2) Relational organizing: this is just a fancy way of saying text your contacts to share helpful voting info.

3) Social media banking: follow and share local candidates to help them reach more voters.

events.description:
**Drive directly** to Dubuque and knock some doors for Lindsay James and other Democrats in Iowa's 2nd congressional District!

We all know that farmers are the beating heart of America, and yet Iowans are disproportionately affected by Trump's Tariffs. The good news is that we finally have the chance to fight back against Trump's MAGA agenda. How? By driving on out to Dubuque to talk to Iowans! Let's make a difference! We'll be waiting for you!

If you arrive early or want to stay longer, no sweat! The office is wide open and would love to have you for as long as you're available to help!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)

Volunteers will meet in Iowa at 123 Main St, Dubuque 52001 Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

events.title: Bridge North Texas Community Field Canvassing
events.description:
Join us every Saturday in October as we head out into DeSoto to knock doors, connect directly with voters, and build long-term power in our community!

Face-to-face conversations are the single most effective way to make sure our neighbors have a plan to vote. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or knocking doors for the very first time, we will make sure you have everything you need to feel comfortable, confident, and supported.

What to Expect:
Training & Briefing: We start every shift with a quick 20-minute training on our messaging and canvassing apps (Empower / Solidarity Tech).

Pairing Up: First-time canvassers will always be paired with an experienced buddy!

Knocking Doors: We’ll launch in pairs to talk to target voters across DeSoto.

Debrief: We’ll regroup at the end of the shift to celebrate wins, log our contacts, and turn in materials.

What to Bring / How to Prepare
1. A fully charged smartphone with the Empower and Solidarity Tech    apps downloaded.
2. Comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle.
3. A friend! (Canvassing is always more fun together.)

Meet up location details will be reshared to RSVP's closer to event dates.

events.title: 10/24 Volunteer Training and Door Knock with Kelabe!
events.description:
Join us for a joint canvass with WA Working Families Party, Seattle DSA, and UAW 4121. The Nov 3rd election is a couple weeks away- help us get the word out to our neighbors about these incredible working peoples' champions!

Location: Othello Playground (4351 S Othello St, Seattle, WA 98118)

Kelabe Tewolde (LD37 - House Seat 1) is a child of refugees who advocates to stop redlining and environmental racism on the Seattle Planning Commission and an educator who mentors and uplifts youth of color with Rainier Scholars, and is challenging a 27-year-incumbent who has voted to increase rents and lower taxes on corporations. Kelabe, in contrast, is by community and for community.

Jaelynn Scott (LD37 - House Seat 2) is a Black trans activist and proud socialist who serves as Executive Director of the Lavender Rights Project, a national black trans feminist advocacy organization advancing justice for gender diverse communities. She has spent years working in community, organizing, responding to crisis calls, helping people find sanctuary, and trying to help folks navigate the confusing, frustrating, broken system of social services.

If it’s your first time, no worries! Each session starts with a brief training & Q&A. Don't be afraid to reach out with questions!

Bring a fully charged phone, water, and comfy walking shoes and we'll have all the info you need!

events.title: Virtual Textbank & Postcard Party
events.description:
Join us online for a fast-paced, high-impact Virtual Text Banking & Postcard Writing Party!

Together, we’ll reach target voters across North Texas to ensure our community has the info and support they need to make their voices heard.

Whether you’re a seasoned volunteer or this is your first time texting voters or writing postcards, we’ve got you covered! We’ll start with a brief live training so you feel fully equipped before we kick off.

What We’ll Do Together:
1. Welcome & Training: Quick walkthrough on our texting platform (Empower / Solidarity Tech) and postcard guidelines.

2. Action Time: Text voters and write postcards in real time with live support from our team.

3. Community & Q&A: Connect with fellow volunteers, share updates, and track our progress together on screen.

What You’ll Need
1. A computer, tablet, or smartphone with internet access.
2. Your favorite pen (if you are writing postcards with us!).
3. Energy to build a bigger community across Texas!

Important Virtual Access Info
Virtual Event Link: To keep our virtual space secure, the official join link will be emailed and texted directly to all registered RSVPs the day before the event. Make sure to sign up with your primary email and mobile number!

events.title: Texas Together: Learn To Leverage Your Personal Network
events.description:
Want to engage your personal network to ensure we win in November? This training is for you! We'll be teaching you all about Echo, an exciting new tool that will help you share important election-related information within your personal networks. It will also help you share insights from your communities with Democratic campaigns, so that candidates can address the problems voters care about most. 

Research shows that the most effective way to drive turnout is through one-on-one interactions with people you know. People listen to you in a way they never listen to an ad. Echo works like this: communicating important information, and content, to groups only you can reach. 

Curious to learn more? Don't miss out on this opportunity to help turn Texas blue!

This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We are creating a yard display with placards of those killed by ICE, including their photos with a short description, marigolds and actions you can take to End the Ice Age. 

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.title: Voter Protection calls to Cure Ballots
events.description:
Join VoPro Pros to help ensure that likely Democratic voters in states such as Georgia, Iowa, North Carolina, Nevada, and Ohio, and maybe more are able to cast their ballots this fall and have their votes counted!  Please join us for important and impactful voter protection phone banks to help votes count! 

In each shift, we will do phone banking to support the most critical and current voter protection priorities in one of these key states. As the ballots are returned and we get the data on rejected ballots, we will help voters fix mistakes, known as curing, so their voted ballots count!  Our calls may also include recruiting volunteers to serve as poll observers, so that we can help solve voters’ issues at the polls in real time; helping voters who had issues with their ballots in previous elections know what to do so their vote counts this time.  
We will meet on zoom and provide training, a script, and contact information for targeted voters.  We’ll call using the OpenVPB system, where you’ll call on your own phone or Google Voice (or a web based calling app).  No experience or background knowledge required.

Come to our 2 hour phone banks and make a difference! We promise your calling will be the most critical of the moment.  We will try to update you here, if we know the project of the day.  If you have questions, write to us at voterprotectionVPP@gmail.com

Probable upcoming phone bank topics, subject to change as needs change:

October 20 - NV Pre-cure

events.title: Step Up for Democracy: New Haven GOTV Canvass
events.description:
Join the League of Women Voters of Connecticut and LWV New Haven for a nonpartisan door-to-door canvass to empower our community and ensure every eligible voter’s voice is heard!

With key elections approaching, we are knocking on doors across New Haven to make sure our neighbors are fully prepared to cast their ballots by November 3rd. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or taking to the doors for the first time, we will provide the training and materials you need to make an impact.

What We’ll Be Doing:

Voter Education: Sharing clear, trusted details on voting options, key dates, and election procedures in Connecticut.

Voter Empowerment: Helping community members make a concrete plan to participate on or before November 3rd.

Answering Questions: Helping voters check their voter status, locate their local polling information, and navigate general voter resources like VOTE411.org.

Schedule & Agenda:

1:00 PM: Welcome & Canvass Training: We will kick off with brief nonpartisan messaging training, review route assignments, pair experienced canvassers with new canvassers, and walk through our canvassing app.

1:30 PM | Door-to-Door Canvassing: Pairs will head out to assigned New Haven neighborhoods to engage local voters.

3:30 PM – 4:00 PM | Debrief & Material Return: Gather back at our starting hub to drop off materials and share stories.

How to Prepare:

What to Wear: Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing.

What to Bring: A fully charged smartphone, a water bottle, and a friend!

The League of Women Voters is a strictly nonpartisan organization that encourages informed and active participation in government. We do not support or oppose candidates or political parties.

events.description:
In America, most people believe that voters should pick our leaders, not the other way around. But right now, people in power are trying to keep us from voting so they can control our elections and seize more power for themselves.

Join us at the Chester H. Ferguson Law Center for the tenth stop of the tour!

This tour stop is being organized in collaboration with local and statewide partners, including *Common Cause Florida, ACLU of Florida, All Voting Is Local, Florida Youth Action Fund, Fair Elections Center, Engage Florida, Florida Rising Together*, and more!

- Election Protection 101

events.title: Roll to the Polls to Vote Early
events.description:
# ROLL TO THE POLLS

**Deck out your ride. Roll out the vote.**

Streamers on the handlebars. Balloons on the golf cart. Pom-poms on the pickup. Bring your car, bike, trike, skateboard, wagon, or your own two feet, and dress it up to celebrate **early voting**. We'll gather at Long Wharf and parade together, horns honking and bells ringing, to the Dorchester County Board of Elections to cast our ballots on the very first day of early voting.

We're also bringing fresh donuts and coffee for the election workers who make it all happen. Want to add something sweeter? Bring a handwritten thank-you note, and we'll deliver it with the donuts.

**Thursday, October 22 · 8 AM**

Line up at Long Wharf, Cambridge

**Best Decorated wins bragging rights, and a prize.**

*Decorations should celebrate early voting, not candidates.*

**Voting at the end of the parade?** You'll need to be a Dorchester County resident.

First, [check your voter registration](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/VoterSearch).

Not registered? [Register online](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/OnlineVoterRegistration) by October 13.

Nonpartisan. Joyful. Everyone welcome.

events.description:
Join Swing Left Inland Valley, Swing Left Orange County, and other Swing Left groups for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.
