Join Miami Gardens ROSE Inc., Crime Survivors Speak, and Guns Down Voices Up Demanding Justice Inc. as we come together to honor the lives of those affected by homicide and support individuals, families, and communities healing from the pain of loss.

This community event will focus on remembrance, healing, awareness, advocacy, and access to resources. Attendees will also learn about Florida Victim Compensation, including what assistance may be available, who may qualify, and how to begin the application process.

Too often, surviving families learn about these resources only after they have already faced overwhelming emotional and financial burdens. Our goal is to help families become informed, supported, and connected.

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ 10th St & I-10 Pedestrian Bridge in DTPHX
events.description:
**Join us for our Tuesday afternonn rally on the 10th St pedestrian bridge over the I-10 freeway downtown Phoenix**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

**📆 TUESDAY AFTERNOONS**

The rally starts at 4:30. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 6:00 PM.

Starting 29 Sep 2026, running thru 27 Oct 2026... or longer, if we love it!

**🧑‍🤝‍🧑 GATHERING POINT**

We gather on the bridge. Look for the signs. Can't miss us!

**🪧 MESSAGING & FOCUS**

One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)
This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

The primary goal of this event is to encourage voter participation, but participants are welcome to bring any sign they wish. We will provide and display the main voting-related signs facing both directions of traffic. 

Bringing your own sign? Two large bars span the bridge. To make sure your sign isn't blocked, make it horizontal and no more than about 24" tall.

Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are commonly shared on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

**🅿️ RECOMMENDED PARKING**

Street parking is available along East Moreland Street throughout the surrounding neighborhood. There's also a parking lot at 10th St & Culver on the north side, but it may not be as "public" as we'd like. Stay vigilant!

**🚌 PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION**

Route 12

**📣 SPECIAL NOTES**

Because the event takes place on a pedestrian bridge over an active freeway, safety is our highest priority. Clear safety guidelines will be provided to ensure everyone's well-being on the bridge and prevent items from falling onto the roadway below. Safety notices will be posted at both bridge entrances, and all participants will receive safety information in advance of the event. 

Five weeks can make a difference! 

🥵 During hot weather, shade is limited. Bring water, sun protection, and consider a portable chair.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.description:
HELP US RAISE AWARENESS!

Our group holds signs at places throughout Salem, where someone was abducted by ICE.

• Please register to RSVP and get address.

• Every Friday, rain or shine.

• Signs are handed out and locations are assigned at a meeting spot to be disclosed.

• Teams of two then set out for one hour of sign holding.

• Bring a friend or we’ll assign you a partner.

• After the hour is up, meet back at the original meeting spot to turn in signs and check in.

Our purpose is not only to raise awareness of our neighbors being taken from us, but to hold sacred space and honor those who have been abducted and for their families who are dealing with the trauma of their loss.

• We hold these signs for each and every person languishing in detention centers across the US.

• We hold these signs in defiance of the fascism and the hate.

• We hold these signs to use our white privilege, for those of us who have it, and be the best allies we can be.

More about why we do this:

ICE activity in Salem has resulted in many of our neighbors being abducted over the past 18 months. The exact number is difficult to obtain, as ICE does not share information, but the local Rapid Response Team and PIRC (Portland Immigration Rights Coalition) data supports the number as being over 100 since Trump took office.

• Across the state, ICE has abducted over 2,500 individuals, 700 in August of this year. • Across the nation, ICE is ramping up numbers; also in August, 51,000 people were taken. • Most of which have no criminal record.

• Abductees are being warehoused in over 200 privately owned detention centers in the US, where they are held for months, or years, in deplorable conditions.

• There are documented cases of rape, abuse, malnutrition, bad water and food, restricted access to medical care and lawyers.

• GEO Group and Core Civic; the corporations who own most of the detention centers, earn $150 - $175 per person per day.

• Both corporations earned over 2 billion dollars in total revenue in 2025, with net profits exceeding $200 million.

• Half of the total revenue comes from ICE contracts.

Want to help us raise awareness?

events.title: Hosted by ARC: “Voices of the Vote: An Open Mic on Voting Rights via Poetry & Storytelling”
events.description:
Sunday, October 25, 2026

Hosted by ARC: “Voices of the Vote: An Open Mic on Voting Rights--via Poetry & Storytelling”

What is your voting story? With the 2026 Midterm Elections just days away, our collective voice has never been more vital. Behind every policy debate is a deeply human experience—and we are bringing those experiences to a shared national stage.

Join us on Sunday, October 25, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 1:30 PM CT for a captivating, virtual open mic.

We are building a truly cross-country virtual community. Whether you are dialing in from the East Coast, the West Coast, the South, or the Midwest, your regional perspective matters.

We are stripping away the digital noise. There will be no slides, no background music, and the text chat will be completely disabled. 

This is a space dedicated entirely to the raw power of the human voice—featuring an opening performance followed by an open floor for community members across the United States to share stories, spoken word, and poetry on the right to vote.

How it works:
The Open Floor:  The mic is open to anyone in our nationwide room. 
Bring a 3-minute story, personal reflection, spoken word piece, or poem about the right to vote.

Claim Your Slot Live: Once the floor opens, simply raise your hand on camera, and our host will bring you to the virtual stage.

Pure Visual Energy: Because the text chat is off, we ask all attendees to keep their cameras on and fill the screen with physical support—using visual snaps and jazz hands to celebrate each storyteller.

Taking Action Together: At the close of our event, our host will deliver a direct verbal call to action outlining how we can continue our collective energy by phone banking, text banking, and mobilizing our local communities back home—make a plan and vote!

Come to listen, stay to be inspired, and leave ready to continue GOTV actions. 

RSVP now to secure your spot. The secure Zoom access link will be delivered automatically upon registration.


Log-in Time: We will open the Zoom room exactly at 12:00 PM CT. 
Please log in 5 minutes early to test your camera and microphone.

See you on Sunday, October 25th!

Host: The ARC Team..(Antiracist.Conversations)

events.title: Cafecito con Nancy: Meet & Greet con Vecinos

sponsor.name: Nancy Martiz for Huntington Park City Council (CA Working Families Party)

events.description:
Join your neighbors for a Saturday morning with Nancy Martiz, your appointed City Councilmember and candidate for Huntington Park City Council, District 2.

Since joining the Council in April 2025, Nancy has stood up against unconstitutional ICE raids, passed fair housing protections that keep families in their homes, invested in our aging infrastructure, and expanded access to public spaces. Before joining the Council, she served as a Civil Service Commissioner, and she has been an engaged member of the community since moving to HP in 2012.

Like many of her neighbors, Nancy works a 9-to-5. Her career in HR and employee benefits has spanned the arts, higher education, health care, and global entertainment. Endorsed by the California Working Families Party, she believes local representatives should answer to working families, not special interests.

Come ask questions, share what matters to your neighborhood, and hear Nancy's plans for the next term. No speeches, just conversation. Light refreshments will be served, and everyone is welcome.

📅 Saturdays, October 3 & 24 · 🕗 8:00–10:00 a.m.
📍 Cruzita's Café & Deli
RSVP on Mobilize

Nancy does not accept corporate PAC money. This campaign is powered by neighbors. Learn how you can support her campaign for the working families of Huntington Park at nancy4hp.com.

Not sure which district you're in? Visit maphp.org

[Paid for by Nancy Cindy Martiz for Huntington Park City Council 2026. FPPC ID# 1495160]

Desde que se unió al Concejo en abril 2025, Nancy se ha opuesto a las redadas inconstitucionales de ICE, ha aprobado protecciones de vivienda justa que permiten a las familias permanecer en sus hogares, ha invertido en nuestra infraestructura envejecida y ha ampliado el acceso a los espacios públicos. Antes de unirse al Concejo, fue Comisionada de Servicio Civil, y ha sido un miembro activo de la comunidad desde que llegó a HP en 2012.

Como muchos de sus vecinos, Nancy trabaja de 9 a 5. Su carrera en recursos humanos y beneficios para empleados ha abarcado las artes, la educación superior, la salud y el entretenimiento global. Con el respaldo del Partido de las Familias Trabajadoras de California (Working Families Party), Nancy cree que los representantes locales deben responder a las familias trabajadoras, no a intereses especiales.

Ven a hacer preguntas, compartir lo que le importa a tu vecindario y conocer los planes de Nancy para el próximo período. Sin discursos, solo conversación. Habrá refrigerios ligeros y todos son bienvenidos.

events.title: Wind Changers Women's Gathering
events.description:
Wind Changers Women’s Gathering 2026:  2 night camp out. 

The “Wind Changers” represents a shift—a movement toward healing, restoration, connection, and renewed purpose. The Wind Changers Women’s Gathering is an intentional and sacred space created to bring women together for collective prayer, healing, meaningful connection, and empowerment.

In a world that can often feel isolating and overwhelming, this gathering provides a sanctuary where women from all walks of life can come together to build one another up, lift each other’s spirits, support one another, find motivation, and inspire each other.

The gathering is intentionally structured to help women move from isolation to community, creating an environment where women feel seen, heard, supported, and valued. Through shared experiences and meaningful connection, women are reminded that they do not have to walk through life alone.

The Gathering Will Provide:
Collective Prayer & Reflection: Creating a grounded and spiritually supportive environment where women can pause, reflect, reconnect, and renew their spirits.

Talking Circles: Providing safe and welcoming spaces for women to share their stories, express their experiences, release burdens, and receive mutual support without judgment.
Empowerment & Motivation: Creating impactful moments that inspire women to recognize their strength, build one another up, pursue their purpose with confidence, and encourage one another beyond the gathering.

Community Connection: Creating opportunities for fellowship, relationship-building, and meaningful connection so that no woman leaves feeling alone. The goal is for every participant to leave knowing she has a community around her.

We believe that when women have safe spaces to heal, connect, and grow, the impact extends far beyond the gathering itself. Women return to their families, communities, and neighborhoods renewed, strengthened, and empowered to become pillars of strength, hope, and positive change. 

At its heart, Wind Changers is about creating a shift within women that creates a ripple of change throughout families and communities. When women are supported, restored, connected, and empowered, they are better equipped to carry that strength, hope, healing, and purpose into the communities they call home.

Together, we can create a space where women feel seen, heard, supported, valued, and empowered—and where healing and connection become the beginning of lasting change.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. We partner with local organizations at every stop.

We will be part of the weekly Vigil for Immigrant Justice and the Call to End Section 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, which authorizes U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to delegate federal immigration enforcement authority to state and local law enforcement agencies. This is a time to reflect on what it means to stand witness and hold vigil as an act of participatory democracy. Calling for systemic change and an end to immigrant detention without due process, this vigil has taken place 50 weeks in a row, organized by faith leaders and people of conscience, standing in solidarity with other vigils across the state and nation.

This vigil is held in partnership with Interfaith Alliance of Florida, Voter Action Pinellas, the League of Women Voters of St. Petersburg, and the League of Women Voters of North Pinellas.

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

events.title: Sexual and Domestic Violence Awareness Workshop
events.description:
Sexual Violence and Domestic Violence Workshops are designed to help you build resilience, develop skills to keep you and your loved ones safe, and create bonds with those who have been through the same experiences as well as educating and informing the public for prevention. Survivors deserve active, accessible and affordable advocacy, support and the right to heal on their own terms.

This group is ran by peers and volunteers with a few experts coming to speak to us at certain times also. We started this group because we know we have a serious lack of education surrounding this and even sex education itself and in rural areas, we lack these resources and education even more. In a world where there is so much violence put on our children and ourselves as women, we must find and create spaces where we feel safe, comfortable, heard and overall have the support we all need.

Every last Tuesday of the month 5-6pm. The majority of our workshops will be at the Peebles Library in their meeting room. Depending on weather, we may have locations outdoors, at a park or hiking location for the woods or even the private 3rd space we created where our community aid garden is. Our lead, Taryn, will be there to greet you and get us started at each of these groups and workshops.
We are allies and accomplices here.

5-6pm Sexual and Domestic Violence Educational Workshops
6-7pm Women's Support Group

There are no age restrictions only to make this accessible. We don't want to make younger children or your children who may need this group to feel like they can't be apart of it just because of their age. If they have experienced hardship or need a safe space just like we do, we will not be turning them away. We do understand that this could potentially keep conversations from being too deep but if enough girls or younger women would like to attend, we can start a support group for our youth.

Our sexual and domestic violence workshops are to bring awareness to ourselves and our youth to help prevent further violence against children and women. Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around sexual violence and assault.

What to Expect:
Bonding, Venting and Relating
Mutual Support
Trauma-Informing to Foster Healing
Education on Women’s Health
Sexual Violence Awareness + Education Workshops
Skill Building
Sharing Resources
Safety and Confidentiality

Specific Workshop Examples:
What is Sexual Violence, What is and Can be Considered Sexual Violence, Consent 101, What is Grooming, What are Warning Signs, Women’s Health and Anatomy, Self-Defense and more. In hopes we keep our children and community safe.

There are no age restrictions. Everyone is welcome. We all need to learn these things to help with prevention. We want these workshops and the support group to be as accessible as we possibly can, that includes rides and childcare. If you have children, you can bring them to the first group or workshop you attend if you need to. A kid’s club will begin once we find more volunteers to help us make this successful as well and we will have them during these times. Once we find enough volunteers and go through background checks, we will talk more about this at the our group meetings or workshops and spread the word more. We’re working towards bringing our villages back. We can't have a village without villagers.

We want to add to ensure it's known, when we say women, we are always including trans women as well as non-binary folks who may also need a support system. As soon as we find a better term to use for only women and non-binary folks, the name of this support group will change. We apologize to anyone who may feel left out or uncomfortable to the term Women's Support Group.

Coffee and snacks will be available. Possibly pizza or other foods for dinner. If you have allergies, please inform us. We hope to see you at one or the other or even both. It matters to our health to have support and we must create spaces that lead to prevention of violence against us.

### Join Food & Water Action this October to talk with our neighbors about Iowa's water crisis, and elect leaders willing to stand up to Big Ag.  

Iowa has _the fastest-rising cancer rates in the country._ We know this is linked to pollution from industrial agriculture that flows into our waterways. 

Join us to talk to our neighbors and share information about keeping our water safe, _starting with electing candidates like Chris Jones for Ag Secretary,_ who will hold polluters accountable and clean up Iowa's water! 

We will meet at _Chamberlain Park_ for a brief training session on how to have effective conversations.

Then, we will pair up and head out!

After everyone finishes their list/shift, we meet back up at Chamberlain Park and debrief over pizza!

We will be knocking on October 10th, and October 24th.  You can sign up for either or both dates. 

**No prior experience canvassing is needed!**

We use the website OpenField to track our conversations, so please bring a fully charged phone. We'll spend some time during the training familiarizing ourselves with OpenField.

**Join us in getting out the vote to elect water champions in Des Moines!**

events.title: Clayton Tucker: Virtual Data Crew Coworking Night
events.description:
Clayton’s Data Crew is the behind-the-scenes team turning petition signatures into clean, organized data that can be uploaded into our campaign databases. It may not involve knocking on doors or shaking hands, but this work is a critical part of building an organized and successful campaign.
Each week, we’ll enter petition signatures from paper sheets into spreadsheets, review and clean up data, collaborate, troubleshoot, and occasionally cut up and entertain ourselves through the madness of campaign season, together.
You don't have to be a data professional, but you do need to be:
•	Comfortable working on a computer
•	Detail-oriented and accurate
•	Familiar with spreadsheets or willing to learn
•	Able to follow data-entry guidelines
•	Reliable and ready to pitch in
•	VAN access and experience is a big plus!
We're looking to grow an already strong and capable team with volunteers who enjoy the kind of work where details matter and getting it right matters even more.
We'll meet every Monday and Wednesday on Zoom through Election Day, November 3, 2026.
Bring your laptop, your questions, your spreadsheet skills, and your willingness to get a little nerdy with us.
No cowboy boots required.
Come help us turn stacks of paper into organized data—and organized people into a powerful grassroots operation.
Join Clayton’s Data Crew. Let's get to work!

events.title: Wenonah's Book of the Year: Author Talk with Zephyr Teachout [Livable Future LIVE]
events.description:
**Join us for a virtual conversation between Food & Water Watch Founder & Executive Director Wenonah Hauter and Zephyr Teachout, author of _Anti-Monopoly: A Citizen’s Guide_.**

_Anti-Monopoly_ is being called a “movement-defining” book that dives deep into the battle between the forces of oligarchy and the rise of the anti-monopoly movement. Zephyr explains how anti-monopoly sentiment cuts across traditional political lines, gives real teeth to economic populism, and offers actionable ways to use people power to solve this problem together. 

Zephyr Teachout is an award-winning author, constitutional law professor, and nationally renowned democracy and anti-corruption activist. _The New York Times_ called her “the godmother of the current moment of dissatisfaction with establishment politics,” and she has inspired anti-monopoly legislation in states across the country. Her additional writings include the books _Corruption in America_ and _Break ’Em Up_ and articles featured in _The New York Times_, _The New York Review of Books_, _Foreign Affairs_, and _The Nation_. Zephyr serves as Board Chair for Food & Water Action and sits on the board of Food & Water Watch, helping guide strategies on clean water, safe food, and climate advocacy.

events.title: Volunteer Recruitment National Phonebank
events.description:
This October, **A4TE is partnering with incredible organizations—including the Ballot Initiative Strategy Center (BISC), the National LGBTQ Task Force, and more**—to host weekly virtual phonebanks supporting states facing anti-trans ballot measures and other attacks.

Join volunteers from all over the country to **phone bank and help recruit volunteers for states who are knocking on doors to fight anti-trans ballot measures.** This is one of the most effective ways to make an impact from the comfort of your home—no matter where you are!

### What to expect: 

- **You’ll get trained.** Staff and experienced volunteer leaders will walk you through everything you need to know before you start making calls—no prior experience required. 

- **We’ll make calls together.** You’ll be part of a supportive, welcoming group where we can encourage each other and build community along the way. 

- **We’ll provide the scripts.** You’ll have everything you need to feel prepared and confident when talking with voters. We’ll provide scripts and talking points. 

- **No personal phone number required.** All you need is a computer or tablet with an internet connection to make calls. 

- **Your privacy matters.** Our dialer is designed to help protect your personal information when reaching out to voters. 

- **We’ll make a difference together.** Every conversation is an opportunity to connect with voters and share important information!

- **You’ll get trained.** Staff and experienced volunteer leaders will walk you through everything you need to know before you start making calls or sending texts—no prior experience required. 

- **We’ll send texts and/or make calls together.** You’ll be part of a supportive, welcoming group where we can encourage each other and build community along the way. 

- **We’ll provide the scripts.** You’ll have everything you need to feel prepared and confident. We’ll provide scripts and any relevant information.

- **No personal phone number required.** All you need is a computer or tablet with an internet connection to make calls/texts.

- **Your privacy matters.** Our tools are designed to help protect your personal information when reaching out to people.

- **We’ll make a difference together.**

events.title: Running an Effective Campaign Debrief
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Tuesday, November 10th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **Running an Effective Campaign Debrief**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Discuss the essential data and performance metrics to review at the end of a campaign

2\. Review suggested practices for planning and facilitating a campaign debrief

  

**This training is right for you if you're concluding the planning/execution of a 2026 campaign.** 

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: So You Want to Run for Office?
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Thursday, November 12th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **So You Want to Run for Office**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Understand the steps necessary to run for office

2\. Explain best practices for choosing which office to run for

3\. Identify what kinds of support you'll need to run for office

4\. Prepare for sharing your decision to run with your support network

  

**This training is right for you if you're considering a run for elected office but haven't yet made the commitment to run or filed your candidacy.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [Getting Your Campaign Off the Ground](https://traindems.org/course-details/100/getting-your-campaign-off-the-ground).  
_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: Precinct Chair and Candidate Recruitment
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Monday, November 16th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on Precinct Chair and Candidate Recruitment. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Identify key responsibilities of Democratic precinct chairs

2\. Introduce tactics used by local leaders to grow and engage membership

3\. Review approaches for persuading first time candidates to run

  

**This training is right for you if you hold a leadership position in a Democratic club/committee or progressive organization that actively supports candidates seeking elected office.**

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: Recovering from a Lost Election
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Tuesday, November 17th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **Recovering from a Lost Election****.** We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1.  Discuss productive ways to reflect on and debrief your campaign experience
2.  Plan a timeline for post-Election Day supporter engagement and goals for continued organizing efforts
3.  Explore ways to have an ongoing positive impact on local Democratic organizing, including the decision to seek election again in the future 

  

**This training is right for you if you are a candidate with some degree of desire to stay involved in political organizing, even if your bid for election is unsuccessful.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [The Fundamentals of Field Tactics](https://traindems.org/course-details/67/the-fundamentals-of-field-tactics)  
_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: What is a Democratic Precinct Chair?
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Wednesday, November 18th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **What is a D****emocratic Precinct Chair**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1.  Describe the structure and purpose of local Democratic Parties
2.  Review common positions people hold in local Democratic Parties
3.  Identify key responsibilities of Democratic precinct chairs
4.  Introduce tactics used by local leaders to grow and engage Democratic Party membership

  

**This training is right for you if you aren't currently involved with your local Democratic party but are exploring ways to get involved in Democratic power-building in your community.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [Member Recruitment and Retention for Local Democratic Parties](https://learn.traindems.org/learn/courses/23/member-recruitment-and-retention-for-local-democratic-parties).

### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

events.title: GOTV Columbia
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.description:

events.title: Special Community Meeting, Anthem Indivisible - Oct. 20
events.description:
### It’s spooky season in Anthem!

As the Halloween moon rises and the wind begins to hiss secrets through the desert sage, we’ll gather around a bubbling cauldron of **witch’s brews**, nibbling on **enchanted ember tarts, moon‑dust cookies**, and other spellbound sweets to keep our courage strong as the spirits stir. 🕯️🧙‍♀️🦇

Then we’ll step into the shadowy realm of **Election Protection Rapid Response** and **Sustained Mobilization**, calling our volunteers together like a vigilant coven — ready to guard voting access, respond with supernatural speed, and remain ever‑watchful when democracy sends out its midnight call for protection.

#### Logistics:

 - **Date:** Tuesday, October 20, 2026

 - **Time:** 5:30 PM - 7:00 PM

 - **Location:** Anthem Civic Center

*Costumes optional, civic spirit required! *

events.title: Canvass for Climate Champions in Milwaukee
events.description:
DATE: Sunday, October 18, 2026
TIME: 11-3 PM

Join 350 Wisconsin Action for door-to-door canvassing in Milwaukee! We’ll be talking with voters about the November election and issues shaping Wisconsin’s future, including clean energy, rising utility costs, data center accountability, and Wisconsin’s constitutional ballot referendums.

No canvassing experience is needed. We’ll provide training, materials, and support throughout the shift. Join us to talk with neighbors, share information, and help Milwaukee voters get informed and ready for the November election.

Join the Pickens County Democratic Party for our Flip the Future Canvassing program Saturdays from 10:00am–noon.

events.title: Phone Banking (Longmont)
events.description:
Join us at UCC Longmont to help GET OUT THE VOTE by phone banking!

**What to expect:**

We'll be using an online dialer platform that connects you directly to voters — no need to dial numbers yourself. Once you're connected, you'll read from a simple, conversational script designed to help you have real conversations, not a robotic pitch. The script walks you through an introduction, a few key talking points about what's at stake, and a couple of questions to gauge where the person you're speaking with stands.

Before calls begin, a trained lead will walk everyone through: 
- How to log into the phone bank platform 
- How the dialer works (it does the dialing — you just talk!) 
- A walkthrough of the script and how to enter responses 
- Tips for handling common questions or pushback

**Why it matters:**
Every conversation helps us identify supporters, share accurate information, and build the coalition we need to protect trans and immigrant Coloradans. Phone banking is flexible, low-pressure, and a great option no matter your schedule or experience level.

**What you need:**

*Computer
*Headphones
*Enthusiasm for the cause!

events.title: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear friends,

I am one of the millions of Americans who believes that voting is a fundamental right—not a privilege reserved for those who happen to have the right paperwork. But right now, Congress is trying to pass the SAVE America Act, a bill that would make it harder for eligible citizens to register and vote.

Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here's what's happening:

•	The SAVE America Act passed the House 218–213 on February 11, 2026

•	It requires documentary proof of citizenship—in person—to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot

•	Over 21 million eligible American citizens do not have proof of their citizenship readily available

•	It is an unfunded mandate that would cost states hundreds of millions of dollars with zero federal funding

•	The Senate has repeatedly failed to pass it, and even Republican leaders admit the votes aren't there

•	President Trump is now demanding that the Senate abolish the filibuster to force it through

📢 "Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act" – That's Our Message

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find Your Members of Congress

•	Find your U.S. Representative:
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

•	Find your U.S. Senators:
https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use This Template (Copy and Paste)

Subject: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to vote NO on the SAVE America Act (H.R. 7296 / S. 1383).
The SAVE America Act is a solution in search of a problem. It is essentially a backdoor poll tax, forcing 140 million Americans without a passport to pay fees for documents they do not have.

I ask you to:

events.title: Protest Against Mesa City Council & NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center Campus!
events.description:
### 🚨Protest NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center! 🚨

On May 13, 2026, the Mesa Planning & Zoning Board quickly and quietly voted unanimously to recommend approval of the 2,257,581 sq ft [Mesa Data Center Campus known as the NTT Global PH10]( https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/no-mesa-ntt-global-ph10-data-center). 

Mesa Valley Indivisible officially teamed up with our sister group, [Indivisible Mesa](https://www.indivisiblemesa.org)—who has been leading the charge against Mesa’s 287(g) agreement and predatory data centers, like the planned 2.2 million sq ft [NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/no-mesa-ntt-global-ph10-data-center)—to make our voices heard at City Hall.

As public turnout surged, city officials escalated their efforts to quiet community opposition: 

- **On June 8th**, A local activist was physically removed from a council meeting simply for silently holding a small sign. 

- At the next Mesa City Council meeting **on July 17th**, after the indoor sign bans forced us outside, police arrested a peaceful protester for using a megaphone despite the fact that she complied with their demands. She was charged with bogus charges and forced to spend a night in jail...FOR USING A MEGAPHONE. The charges were dropped at her 9/28/2026 court date. k 

- **On August 7th** when Indivisible Mesa recently pressed the City Council coordinator for answers, the city shifted its story yet again! They claimed the councilmembers will not be voting on the data center at all and that NTT can proceed administratively, but only after grassroots pressure began mounting.

If they won't let us show our signs inside, we will make sure they are impossible to ignore on the steps of City Hall. Mesa Valley Indivisible is pivoting this event to an outdoor protest starting at 5:00pm (meeting starts at 5:45pm). We will make our voices heard loud and clear from the outside!

## 📢 Calls to Action:

**Whether or not you can attend, please do the following three things:**

1. [Submit a comment here](https://us.openforms.com/Form/44ff3314-58bb-418a-a122-46fe7725feef)! Feel free to choose one of the concerns listed below if you do not want to write your own comment. 

2. [Email the Mesa City Council members by](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1llwS0FcrAfxBdC1DwOL0hayMQ9SWK1WJkHFZlxXYdQ4/edit?usp=sharing).** Contact info, directions, and scripts/templates provided!

3. [Call the Mesa City Council members](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qedOvsbfPZ9mG1N6BKkc7QvL3XeamSdmvA_oVY7bu8w/edit?usp=sharing)** and use the script provided or your own! 


## 🚨 Important: 

- We do not care whether or not the data center is on the agenda. MVI and other local activists know it is VITAL we voice our disgust every single council meeting in order to make sure they actually listen to their constituents! 


## ## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- Massive Handouts, Tiny Returns: Similarly sized data centers receive over $100 million a year in tax subsidies. That is revenue stolen directly from our local community services and neighborhood improvements.

- Virtually No Job Creation: Despite taking up huge amounts of space, this massive facility will only create 40 to 60 permanent jobs paying $60,000 or less. Compared to advanced manufacturing or bioscience, data centers provide practically zero high-quality jobs per acre.

- We Pay Their Bills: The infrastructure improvements and utility upgrades required for this project will likely be passed on to everyday customers, not the multibillion-dollar company.

- Driving Up Local Costs: Developments like this artificially inflate land costs, making it harder for our local farmers, small businesses, and families looking for affordable housing to survive.

- A 2.2 million-square-foot facility requires an astronomical amount of energy and water to keep its servers cool. In our delicate desert environment, this level of resource consumption is completely unsustainable and directly threatens the capacity of our local utilities.

- This project threatens the safety and peace of our residential areas. The constant, 24/7 roar of massive cooling fans creates severe noise pollution, while the sprawling, windowless buildings will industrialize our local landscape and destroy our community's character.


## 🪧 Sign Ideas:

- We won't be silent!
- No more Mesa Data Centers!
- NO one wants Data Centers!
- Hate data centers = bipartisan 


## 📷 Pictures & Videos
- Make sure to always tag **Mesa Valley Indivisible** on our group [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1CFYV1DSaT/), [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/mesavalleyindivisible/), [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc), [BlueSky](https://bsky.app/profile/mesavalleyindivisi.bsky.social), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc)
- Please also include #MesaValleyIndivisible #AbolishICE #CloseAROCC #RecuseBiggs #ReleaseEpsteinFiles
- Add all photos & videos to our [Google drive!](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hkgqf8L4uPRGBpwwLClceOBp63iS48It)

Poll Watchers monitor the elections process at Early Voting Locations and Election Day Polling Sites in every corner of the state, serving as the campaign’s eyes and ears on the ground. By being present and helping identify any issues right away, Poll Watchers play a vital role in protecting the vote -- and are as important as ever this election.

**Take the first step by signing up now to attend a Virtual Poll Watcher Training, hosted by the Texas Together Democratic Coordinated Campaign!**

At the training you will learn everything you need to succeed as a Poll Watcher, including what the role entails, what to expect, what to bring, and best practices. After completing the training process, you’ll be prepared to serve as a Poll Watcher during both Early Voting (starting October 19) and on Election Day (November 3).

*Please note that to serve as a Poll Watcher inside a voting location, you must be a registered voter in the county you are serving in, and you must complete an additional, separate training required by the Secretary of State (available at https://pollworkertraining.sos.texas.gov/). We recommend completing this training as soon as possible.*

**You only need to attend one Texas Together Democratic Poll Watcher Training session.

Join a short training to learn how you can look out for your neighbors, your block, and your local polling place.

events.title: Dial In for Democracy: Virtual GOTV Phone Bank
events.description:
Every vote in our community deserves a reminder, a clear answer, and a little encouragement. Join Imagine Black from home to call voters across Multnomah County ahead of the November 3 election.

This is a nonpartisan phone bank. We won't be talking about candidates or ballot measures. Our job is simpler and just as powerful: making sure people have the facts they need to vote. We'll remind voters how Oregon's vote-by-mail works, walk through ranked-choice voting in Multnomah County, and encourage everyone to return their ballot by 8:00 PM on Election Day. Too many people sit out elections because no one reached out or they weren't sure how the process works. A single call can change that.

No experience needed. We'll welcome you on Zoom, give you a quick training, and get you calling with support close by if questions come up.

What you'll need:

Reliable internet
A laptop you can use for the full shift
A web browser other than Google Chrome (Firefox, Safari, or Edge work best)
Headphones, helpful but not required

When we organize, we win. Come call with us.

Español Abajo

Protect the vote in your neighborhood
Become a neighborhood vote protector. Every vote is a decision about our healthcare, housing, wages, and who gets to make the rules – which is exactly why it needs to be protected. The Trump administration is trying rig the outcomes of the election by creating chaos, fear and new roadblocks to keep us from voting.
We Are CA is training thousands of Neighborhood Vote Protectors across the state to watch the polls in their communities, safely safely document and report incidents to legal experts, and make sure every voter knows their rights to cast a ballot without fear or intimidation. Join a short training to learn how you can look out for your neighbors, your block, and your local polling place.

Wed Sep 23 6-7:30pm

Wed Oct 14 6-7:30pm

Wed Oct 21 6-7:30pm

La administración Trump está tratando de manipular los resultados de las elecciones creando caos, miedo y nuevos obstáculos para impedirnos votar.
We Are CA está capacitando a miles de Protectores del Voto en todo el estado para vigilar los centros de votación en sus comunidades, documentar incidentes de forma segura a través de líneas directas legales, y asegurarse de que cada votante conozca sus derechos para emitir su voto sin miedo ni intimidación.

A quick training and walk list when you arrive

Friendly conversations with people who already support our ticket

events.title: UT Austin Campus - Texas Together: Run to the Polls
events.description:
On Monday, October 19th at 8:30 A.M., we are planning on running a 1.5 mile route from the back of the Texas State Capitol to a polling site in the LBJ School of Public Affairs on UT’s campus. Once at the polling location, runners will be rewarded with drinks and small prizes like stickers. The goal of this event is to mobilize all voters to the polls and raise awareness that the elections are open. Although Texas Together endorses Democratic candidates down-ballot, the event itself invites runners of all ideologies to exercise their right to vote, too. The event is free and is essentially a show of support for civic engagement. Because this event is people-powered, we’re inviting many people and run clubs to participate, and we'd love for *you* to participate!

Runners can show up as early as 8:15, and we will depart at 8:45. We will be giving out drinks at the LBJ School until supplies last - we expect this to be around 10:00 a.m.
events.accessibility_notes: You are not required to run. Walkers are welcomed too!

events.title: Election Eve Canvass | Every Vote, Every Member
events.description:
Election Day is 24 hours away, and the races that matter most to working Nevadans will be decided by just a few thousand votes. This is your second to last change to join union brothers and sisters from far and wide for one last day of member-to-member canvassing.

We’re knocking on the doors of union households to make sure every member has a plan to vote, knows where their polling place is, and has returned their mail ballot – join us! 

You’ll get the chance to meet veteran union canvassers, first timers, and Nevada union leaders for a full day of celebrating our hard work and knocking out what we still need to accomplish together. We’ll make sure you feel fully prepared with a quick training, a walk list, and talking points before heading out. 

Wages, working conditions, and the right to organize are on the ballot. Let's finish strong.

Join us at the Operating Engineers Local 3 Union Hall.

events.title: Become a Great Canvasser: CA-22 / Villegas for Congress Edition
events.description:
You don’t have to be an expert—or have the perfect speech—to be a great canvasser. The key is knowing how to listen, connect, and make the most of each conversation.

In this interactive 75-minute workshop, experienced canvassers will share practical strategies for engaging with voters of all stripes—including strong Democrats, those who rarely or never vote, and Republicans and Independents who want to see new leadership in our country. This CA-22 edition includes Villegas-specific context, PDI, and working with the campaign’s canvassing script (without sounding scripted).

Through real-life stories, demos, and practice, you’ll learn how to ask great questions, listen with empathy, and build trust. You’ll learn when to keep a conversation short—and when to slow down and get curious about what matters to a voter. We’ll show you how to use what you hear to connect voters’ priorities with Randy Villegas’s vision and help them find their own reasons to vote for him.

A knock on a stranger’s door can become a conversation that earns their vote. And in a razor-thin election, conversations like these can add up to the votes we need to win.

Note: To get the most out of this training, we recommend that you download the latest version of the PDI app onto your phone before the workshop.

events.title: Get Out the Vote with Team KMR & the MI Dems in Bay City!
events.description:
This race is close, and it's going to come down to turnout. Join us for Get Out The Vote canvassing for Kristen McDonald Rivet and Michigan Democrats up and down the ballot in Bay City!

We'll be knocking on doors of confirmed Democratic supporters and occasional voters — people who are already on our side but need a reminder that Election Day is here. We'll help them lock in their plan to vote, whether that's their polling location, early voting, or mail-in ballot options, and make sure they know their whole Democratic ballot matters — from Kristen McDonald Rivet all the way down.

This kind of face-to-face contact works: GOTV canvassing boosts turnout by an average of 8.5%. In a race this tight, that's the margin of victory — not just for Kristen, but for Democrats across Michigan.

What to expect:

A quick training and walk list when you arrive
A partner or team lead if you're new to canvassing
Friendly conversations with people who already support our ticket

Bring: comfortable shoes, water, and your phone.

No experience necessary — just enthusiasm for getting Michigan Democrats to the polls. Sign up below and help us bring the whole ticket home!

**Event Title:** Canvass for Change: Persuasion Canvassing with Hands Off Colorado

**Description:**

Join Hands Off Colorado for a day of voter persuasion canvassing! We'll be knocking doors and having real conversations with voters to build support for our communities, including trans and immigrant neighbors who are directly impacted by the policies on the ballot this year.

This is persuasion canvassing, which means we're not just checking in with supporters. We're talking to voters who are undecided or leaning against us, listening to their concerns, and having genuine conversations that can change minds. No experience necessary. We'll train you on everything you need to know before we head out, including how to have effective, empathetic conversations at the door.

**What to expect:**
- Brief training and script walkthrough at check-in
- Canvassing in pairs or small groups (great for first-timers!)
- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing recommended
- Snacks and water provided
- Bring a charged phone with the MiniVAN App Downloaded

**Why this matters:**
Every conversation we have moves us closer to a Colorado that stands up for all of its communities. Persuasion canvassing is one of the most effective tools we have to shift public opinion and win elections and we need volunteers like you to make it happen.

Sign up below and help us knock doors, change minds, and build the Colorado we want to live in.

events.title: Hop on the Bus to Harrisburg, PA to flip the House!! - GW Dems & Swing Left GWU
events.description:
Join GW Dems and Swing Left GWU on a planned day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to PA-10—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Janelle Stelson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### Here is the plan:
- **Ready to roll:** Once confirmed, your bus captain will provide departure details, training, and the Ground Truth conversation guide.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave the Foggy Bottom Metro on October 24th at 9 a.m.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly [Canvassing hours].
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. Can we count on you to help us get this bus on the road? Sign up today!

—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

Go solo or team up with a friend, whichever you prefer

Water and weather-appropriate gear
A charged phone for navigating your route with MiniVAN App downloaded

--voter registration drives,

--get out the vote efforts,

--volunteering for issue or candidate campaigns,

--phone banking for state, local, or national candidates,

--forming coalitions with other organizations, and more.

events.title: Final Friday Film: Mr. Smith Goes to Washington

location.venue: North East Bexar County Democrats Campaign Office

events.description:
Mr. Smith Goes to Washington is a 1939 American political comedy-drama film directed by Frank Capra, starring Jean Arthur and James Stewart, and featuring Claude Rains and Edward Arnold. The film is about a naive, newly appointed United States senator who fights against government corruption, and was written by Sidney Buchman, based on Lewis R. Foster's unpublished story "The Gentleman from Montana".[4] It was loosely based on the life of Montana US Senator Burton K. Wheeler, who underwent a similar experience when he was investigating the Warren G. Harding administration's Teapot Dome scandal.[5][6]

The film was controversial in the US when it was first released, with attacks from many politicians claiming that it brought Washington into disrepute, but it was very successful at both the domestic and international box offices, and it made Stewart a major star.[7]

Mr. Smith Goes to Washington was nominated for eleven Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor, winning Best Original Story.[8] Considered to be one of the greatest films of all time, the film was selected by the Library of Congress as one of the first 25 films for preservation in the United States National Film Registry in 1989, for being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".[9][10]

events.title: Hands Off Our Vote - Election Protection Training
events.description:
We are only weeks away from seeing whether or not Democracy stands a chance against Trump's best efforts to undermine elections. It is more important than ever that everyone, everywhere understands what is happening and what we can do to save our democracy and protect our vote!

Popular Democracy is now offering MASS TRAININGS on Election Protection and opportunities for anyone, anywhere to become a Guardian of Democracy. 

Join us to: 

- Strategize on election defense challenges and learn how to safely take nonviolent action

- Create a local solidarity network to share information and be ready for activation if something happens 

- Be ready to mobilize and respond to protect the vote 

Join Us!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**Want to fight authoritarianism? The time to act is now.**

This year’s elections are an opportunity for us to stop the rise of authoritarianism so we can create the future we all deserve. The regime is trying to keep people from voting so they can control our elections and seize more power—but we can stop them by taking action together.

In this training, you'll learn what authoritarianism looks like, what movements have done around the world to win the fight against authoritarianism—and how you can take action with local groups in Massachusetts.

Whether you’re new or experienced with political activism, come join your neighbors, get in formation, and get the playbook to protect and perfect our democracy in 2026.

Lunch, drinks, and a sense of purpose and community will be provided.

events.title: Stop the Illegal War on Iran
events.description:
Join us on October 20 as we demand an end to the illegal war on Iran.
 
On October 20, 2026, two weeks before the midterm election, people across the country will rally at congressional district offices to demand an end to the illegal war on Iran—to block funding, uphold war powers, investigate war crimes, and support a peace deal.
 
In Atlanta, we will be rallying on the 17th Street Bridge at Atlantic Station to make our voices heard to Senators Ossoff and Warnock that we demand they do more to stop this war. Specifically we are calling on them to:
 
*Pledge to oppose any defense appropriation or authorization spending that fails to end the war against Iran. This unauthorized war has killed schoolchildren and American service members, destroyed civilian neighborhoods and water treatment centers, and caused energy prices to skyrocket, wreaking havoc both for everyday Americans struggling to pay for gas and basic goods, and for people living in poverty around the world. If the President won’t listen to Congress when it directs him to stop this war, then Congress needs to use its power of the purse to cut off the funds.
 
*Release a statement affirming the legally binding nature of the Iran War Powers Resolutions and support future war powers resolutions. The founders of our country assigned the constitutional power to launch war to Congress, not leaving it up to one person. The House and Senate have both passed resolutions directing President Trump to terminate unauthorized hostilities against Iran. Members of Congress should use their position to enforce.
 
*Publicly push for the full release of the Department of Defense’s investigation into the U.S. bombing of the Minab Elementary School. It has been months since this strike tragically killed 120 children and dozens more teachers and staff, yet the Department of Defense has still not publicly released its promised investigation into the incident despite it being complete for weeks.
 
*Publicly call for and support a peace agreement, which will require lifting sanctions and unfreezing assets. Economic relief is a necessary component of securing verifiable nuclear concessions and long-term de-escalation. Everyday civilians bear the brunt of U.S. sanctions and freezing of public assets, with significant impacts on access to food, medicine, and basic economic stability. Congress should avoid measures that deepen this humanitarian harm or undermine diplomatic progress.
 
We must act now to stop the war machine. Join us and make your voice heard.

events.description:
Come eat, connect, and talk about what comes next.

Civic Forum is coming to Columbia for an afternoon built around community and coming together. We'll start with small bites and conversation, then hear from Civic Forum founder Reed Galen and Mondale Robinson founder of the Black Male Voter Project, in a live conversation about the places too often left out of the political story: small towns, rural counties, and the communities holding them together.

What does it take to build real civic power outside the big cities? How do we show up for each other when institutions don't? And what can South Carolina teach the rest of the country about organizing where people actually live?

This isn't a lecture. It's a conversation, and the room is part of it. Bring your questions, your neighbors, and your appetite.

Free and open to all. Space is limited, so please RSVP!

Civic Forum is a live civic conversation series bringing people together in cities across the country. Learn more at civicforum.org.

events.title: Spark - Let's Discuss Mis(Dis)insformation!
events.description:
**Let's Discuss  Mis- (and Dis-) information and Solutions - A 
Spark Discussion**

Let’s get together and discuss the problem of misinformation and disinformation and share solutions. How can we battle the river of manipulative lies? Can we prevent or identify disinformation? Who should be accountable? How can instances be debunked without amplifying them? How can we avoid falling victim ourselves? How will this issue change as social media develops?

An expert on this topic will give a brief history, examples on how to spot material meant to deceive us and how (or not) to respond to it. Then we’ll discuss aspects of it - bring your discussion questions and topics.

**No prior reading needed – just interest in talking about this topic.**

Here are some recommendations if you want more information:

**Websites (with links)**

- [Barrington Indivisible Truth Brigade Resources- Resources for Effective Communication](https://www.indivisiblebarrington.org/resources/truth-brigade#h.i68tkhhn1245)

- [Disinfo-Busters Persuasion through Education](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1g7KnhlJQWwUVa8ihE69-GZcG07ulMgoM/edit#heading=h.nefp513xyh7k)

- [University of Michigan Resource Guide “’Fake News’ and Misinformation”
Articles](https://guides.lib.umich.edu/c.php?g=283063&p=4471741)

**Articles**

- ["Why Do People Believe in Conspiracy Theories?” by David Ludden in Psychology Today.](https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/talking-apes/201801/why-do-people-believe-in-conspiracy-theories)

- ["Why Do People Believe in Conspiracy Theories?” by Shweta Mishra in www.scienceabc.com](https://www.scienceabc.com/social-science/why-do-people-believe-in-conspiracy-theories)

- ["Contemporary trends in psychological research on conspiracy beliefs. A systematic review” by Irena Pilch et al. in the NIH database](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9945548/#S3)

- ["Have beliefs in conspiracy theories increased over time?” by Joseph Uscinski et al.](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0270429)

**Books**

- **The Death of Truth** by Steven Brill
- **How to Stand Up to a Dictator** by Maria Ressa (on how the Philippines fell victim to social media)
- **The Chaos Machine** by Max Fisher (on social media)
- **How Minds Change** by David McRaney

Join us on Wednesday, October 28, from 7-8:30. We’ll be at the Barrington Area Library in the Zimmerman Room.


*The Barrington Area Library provides Meeting Room space as a community service. The Barrington Area Library neither sponsors nor endorses this event nor the presenting individuals or organizations.*

We greet voters at the polls, offer them the Sample Democratic Ballot (which comes in two versions for 2026), encourage them to vote for ALL the candidates on BOTH SIDES of the ballot, and thank them for voting. Volunteers who can communicate in Spanish are particularly welcome at this site.
  
Sign up below and be a friendly face for voters. After you sign up, Mobilize will send you a confirmation email with a link to download CCDP's 2026 Poll Greeting Guidelines and a link to optional, but highly recommended, Poll Greeters online training video for both new and experienced poll greeters.

events.title: Riverdale-Kingsbridge Mini-Rallies for Early Voting (1)
events.description:
Northwest Bronx Indivisible is hosting four mini-rallies in October to promote early voting in our community in Riverdale and Kingsbridge. 

Early Voting begins on October 24. Voting early – on or soon after October 24 – amplifies the impact of each vote by avoiding government efforts to disrupt voting, ensuring that mail-in ballots are counted, and  motivating others to vote. These rallies will inform and encourage our neighbors to vote ASAP.

NWBI’s four Mini-Rallies will occur on:

-Wednesday, Oct. 21. at 4:30-5:30 pm,  at Broadway & W. 231st St. 
-Friday, Oct. 23 at 4:30-5:30 pm, at Monument
-Saturday, Oct. 24 at 2-3 pm, at Boo! On Mosholu 
-Tuesday, Oct. 27 at 5:00-6:00 pm, at W. 235th St. & Johnson Ave.

If  you would like to encourage your neighbors to vote early, please sign up for the rally or rallies you would like to participate in.  Each rally has a separate sign-up page on Mobilize. 

If you have any questions, please contact:  mguck517@gmail.com

events.title: PA Poll Guardian Training / Capacitación para guardianes de las urnas
events.description:
### Join We Are CASA and partners in our Election Protection Training to learn how to serve as a Poll Guardian, understand Pennsylvania’s voting rules, recognize and document potential problems at the polls, and know what to do when a voter’s rights may be threatened.

We’re building a movement of trained community members across Pennsylvania who are ready to show up, watch what happens, and help ensure that the will of the people prevails come Election Day and beyond. Let's be ready together to protect the vote.

Make sure to [fill out the form](https://forms.gle/LetSz2s9NJPr2sFu6) to join the We Are CASA campaign to Protect Our Votes!

### Únete a We Are CASA y a nuestros socios en nuestra capacitación sobre protección electoral para aprender a desempeñarte como guardián de las urnas, comprender las reglas de votación de Pensilvania, reconocer y documentar posibles problemas en las urnas, y saber qué hacer cuando los derechos de un votante puedan verse amenazados.

Estamos creando un movimiento de miembros de la comunidad capacitados en todo Pensilvania que estén listos para acudir a las urnas, observar lo que sucede y ayudar a garantizar que prevalezca la voluntad del pueblo el día de las elecciones y más allá. Preparémonos juntos para proteger el voto.

¡Asegúrate de [llenar el formulario](https://forms.gle/3S9m3gprhxw8gwu99) para unirte a la campaña de We Are CASA y proteger nuestros votos!

events.title: Team Massachusetts Canvass in Milton
events.description:
Team Massachusetts is launching a series of door-knocking canvasses across the Commonwealth to reelect Governor Healey, Lt. Governor Driscoll, Senator Markey, and Democrats up and down the ballot.

Join us in Milton on Saturday, October 24th at 11 a.m. We're building the grassroots organizing effort that will power Democratic victories across Massachusetts, and we want you to be a part of it. Together, we'll have conversations with voters, identify supporters for Democrats, and help to make sure voters have a plan to vote this November.

We'll begin with a brief training, where you'll receive your turf, materials, and everything you need to hit the doors with confidence. Whether it's your first time canvassing or your hundredth, we'll make sure you have the tools and support you need.

Electing Democrats up and down the ballot is how we continue delivering results for Massachusetts. We need all hands on deck.

We can't wait to see you there.

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
Lt. Governor Gay and Representative Berry are hosting a screening of a documentary about what motherhood really looks like in America today.

This isn’t just about watching a film; it’s about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly and realize we’re not alone.

Doors open at 5:30 p.m. with light refreshments, and the film begins at 6:00 p.m. Following the screening, join us for a fireside chat with Representative Berry and Lt. Governor Gay as we continue the conversation about motherhood, family, and the experiences of mothers in America today.

We would love for you to join us.

events.description:
Help us accomplish in Arizona in ‘26 what we did in Virginia in ‘25!

Join us to write postcards for Democratic candidate JoAnna Mendoza, running to flip AZ's Congressional District 6 from #redtoblue!    

Why Arizona? AZ has been one of the most important battlegrounds states since 2018 elections, both at the national level and in their statehouse—given this is ground zero for extremist, MAGA election deniers and insurrectionists:

In 2024, Ruben Gallego won the state to become its second Democratic Senator.

In 2020, President Biden won the state by 10,457 votes—which means every single vote in the Grand Canyon state counts.

In 2016, every statewide AZ office was Republican-controlled, as was the state legislature (35 - 25 in the House, 17 - 13 in the Senate).

Today, thanks in part to the efforts of States Win SF (formerly Sister District Project SF) volunteers, all but one statewide office is Democratic and the GOP has only a four seat margin in the state house and a three seat margin in the state senate.

2026 is the year we flip the AZ state legislature and the U.S. Congress blue!

events.description:
Join Mom Dog, Woven and Juniper Green at The Old School Farm for a screening of No Country For Mothers: a documentary that explores what motherhood really looks like in America today.

The film examines the culture wars surrounding motherhood and why labels like “girl boss” and “trad wife” ultimately distract from the bigger issue at play in our society: the lack of support for American families. The documentary traces a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win historic support. 

The screening will be followed by an open discussion, led by Maddie Adams (Matrescence Coach and founder of Mom Dog), Whitney Gorbett (owner of Woven Events), and Molly Martin (owner of Juniper Green and The Old School Farm).

DETAILS:

This al fresco film screening includes open conversation, food from Nashville food trucks, and drinks from The Old School Farm bar. BYO lawn chairs or picnic blankets to create a space where you and your friends can enjoy the evening together. 

Guests are welcome to bring their own picnic dinner, but please note that outside alcohol is prohibited.   

5:00PM - Food, drinks and mingling at The Old School Farm
6:30PM - Film screening, followed by conversation

This night isn’t just about watching a film. 

It’s about being in community with other mothers, linking arms with our sisters to form stronger connections, and saying the things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly — because maybe some of what we’ve been taught to carry privately was never meant to be carried alone.

Join us for this special evening:

Step 1) Sign up below to attend.

Step 2) Purchase your ticket here: https://www.mom-dog.com/all-events/ncfm

Step 3) Share this event with your friends and encourage them to attend, too!

events.title: Blue Wave Bookworms - "The Nerd Reich" by Gil Durán
events.description:
Blue Wave Bookworms – Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 1:30 pm.   
 
Selection – The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy • NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER
“This transfixing debut from journalist Durán investigates the antidemocratic ideologies espoused by tech billionaires linked to the second Trump administration...It’s an ominous look at an insular elite arrayed against American democracy.” —Publishers Weekly (starred review)

When Silicon Valley says it is ‘‘moving fast and breaking things,’’ the world interprets the chaos as a necessary cost of innovation. Gil Durán reveals something far more sinister: a decades-long campaign to replace elected governments with corporate rule.

Drawing on insider political experience and new investigations, Durán traces this ideology from its philosophical roots in The Sovereign Individual by James Dale Davidson and Lord William Rees-Mogg. He introduces its modern apostles—Peter Thiel, Marc Andreessen, Balaji Srinivasan, and Elon Musk—and shows how the promise of technological liberation has transformed into a global movement for digital feudalism, powered by cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence, and the algorithmic propaganda of social media.

The Nerd Reich explains the origins, strategies, and ambitions of Silicon Valley’s war on democracy for the first time. From San Francisco’s weaponized elections and secret billionaire projects to the White House, Durán exposes how the world’s richest men are building a new political order.

The Nerd Reich is more than a hidden history, it’s an urgent warning: democracy is being dismantled not by coups or tanks, but by code, capital, and the illusion of innovation. Durán insists there is still time to fight back—if we act now.

Interfaith Prayer Meeting for Peace is a collaboration of people of faith from various organizations. We grieve this administration’s assault on human dignity and life at home and abroad. As people of faith and conscience committed to peaceful, legal, prayerful presence, we agree to the following:

We agree to respect “that of God in every person” and refrain from hostile language and insults.

We agree to leave room for repentance in those with whom we disagree and to oppose violence, not people.

We agree to trust the Divine to bring about peace, shalom and wholeness in our world.

We agree to follow all legal instructions from law enforcement.

We agree to quickly cooperate with peacekeeper and Meeting facilitator directions that are for our safety.

As an interfaith gathering, we agree to exercise freedom of expression and respect the freedom of expression of others. If you have a prayer, reading, song, or other activity, it will represent your faith and conscience with integrity. If someone else’s sharing does not align with your faith and conscience, you are free to abstain from participating during that moment.

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: MEET YOUR NEIGHBORS!!! Port St. John

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Dan Cicirelli is running for State House in District 31. He grew up here, he's a handyman in Cocoa, and he spends part of every week doing free repairs for older folks who can't afford to pay for them. He's running because the people we keep sending to Tallahassee stopped paying attention to what it costs to live here, or whether you can find a doctor, or what's happening to the lagoon.

Team Cicirelli out in the neighborhoods every day, knocking on doors and having real conversations with people about who Dan is and why he's running. People remember when a neighbor shows up at their door. They don't remember a mailer.

Here's the honest part: Dan doesn't win this unless a lot of us do this, a lot. If we don't get out there and talk to people, we don't win.

You don't need any experience. We'll walk you through it in about ten minutes, pair you up with somebody, and send you out with a list on your phone. Walk a few blocks and talk to some neighbors.

WHAT TO BRING

A FULLY Charged phone with the MiniVAN Application installed
Water
Sunscreen
More water
WHAT TO WEAR: 
1. Wear plain clothes, or a Dan Cicirelli campaign shirt. 
2. Wear WORKOUT oriented clothing. Shorts, t-shirt/tank top. Something that says "I am walking up to 2 miles in the 90 degree Florida sun) 
3. Bring something to carry your water and literature with if possible. A small tote bag will do!

If walking isn't your thing, come anyway. We need people at the table checking folks in and people making calls.

Mail ballots start hitting mailboxes at the end of September, and every weekend between now and November 3 counts. Sign up, show up, and bring somebody with you.

RSVP TODAY and our organizers will be in touch with more details soon!
