events.description:
🧡 Kits of Care: Pack with Purpose!

You’ve been donating. Now let’s get packing! 🙌

Over the past two months, we’ve been collecting supplies for three types of kits to share with community members served by Partners for Our Communities (POC):

🍪 Christmas Cookie Jars filled with baking ingredients and a recipe for a homemade holiday treat.
💜 Period Kits with menstrual care essentials.
🎒 Unhoused Kits with personal care items for neighbors experiencing homelessness.

Donations are coming along beautifully, and now it’s time to bring everyone together for our first assembly event!

📅 Saturday, November 14 | 1–3 PM
📍 Countryside Church Unitarian Universalist (CCUU), Palatine

We’re looking for 50+ volunteers to help put together 150 Christmas Cookie Jars, 150 Period Kits, and 75 Unhoused Kits. That’s 375 kits packed with care in one afternoon!

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 This is a kid-friendly event! Bring your family or a friend. Kids and adults can decorate cards with cheerful messages, fill jars, and pack supplies. No experience needed. We’ll show you what to do! This is a great opportunity for teens to get volunteer hours!

🎁 There’s still time to donate! Check out the list of items we still need: [Kits of Care Flyers - 10/12/26](http://bit.ly/4hOfxzS)

Whether you’ve donated supplies or are joining us for the first time, we’d love to have you there. Come meet your neighbors, learn about Partners for Our Communities and the services they provide, and help care for others! 🧡

We will have a second packing day on Sat, Jan 23rd. Look for the Sign up in December.

Sponsored by Indivisible Barrington, Countryside Church Unitarian Universalist (CCUU), and Partners for Our Communities (POC).

events.title: Phone Banking with Common Cause NC in Mecklenburg County
events.description:
It's time to phone bank to make sure every voter's voice is heard, and we would love to have you join us! We can make a major difference for our democracy by working together!


Common Cause North Carolina will be phone banking this election cycle in Mecklenburg County!  Stand up by joining us in building a movement through phone banking and engaging with your community on voter education through distribution of non-partisan voting resources!
 
How does it work? Here are some highlights, but we will send you more details once you sign up.


You are never alone! For every phone banking shift, you will have a lead organizer who helps you navigate the shift. We will provide training for the first 15-20 mins. of every shift to go over the phone bank program and scripts, the list of areas and to answer any questions!  You will be able to join us from anywhere to phone bank with us! Phone banks will happen via zoom. You will receive zoom details for the phone banking shift once you sign up! 
 
Common Cause NC is a nonpartisan grassroots organization dedicated to upholding the core values of American democracy.  We work to create open, honest, and accountable government that serves the public interest; promote equal rights, opportunity, and representation for all; and empower all people to make their voices heard in the political process. 
 
All phone bank information and scripts will be non-partisan!

Together, we can build the momentum needed to win in November. Let’s flip this seat!

આપણે સાથે મળી નવેમ્બર માં આ ચુંટણી જીતવા જરૂરી ગતિ ઉત્પન્ન કરીશું. ચાલો આ બેઠક ને આપણી તરફ તબદીલ કર દઈએ!

events.description:
Happy Halloween! Start your Saturday by knocking doors for our Democratic candidates.

It's the last Saturday before Election Day, and every voter in Weber County has their ballot by now. We'll visit neighbors who haven't turned theirs in yet, remind them to fill it out, and help them find the closest drop box. This close to Election Day, a drop box is a safer bet than the mail.

Where to find us: the park pavilion, marked with candidate yard signs.

We'll have water, snacks, and a few Halloween treats for our volunteers.

events.title: Dialing Days - Southern NV Union Member Phonebank
events.description:
Join the Nevada Labor movement to call fellow union brothers and sisters across the state in support of Labor endorsed, pro-worker candidates. 

Our phone bank event is a part of our grassroots member-to-member program informing fellow union members and their families of the candidates who earned labor’s endorsement — and why they earned it. We rely on union members to talk to fellow union members about these candidates so we can elect leaders who will fight to defend our contracts, our wages, and our ability to come together. 

Don’t worry if phones make you nervous; this event is for first timers and seasoned phone bankers alike and training is available at the start of the event. Our power comes from learning and working together. We will be thrilled to have you participate and will be there to support you throughout the entire event. 

All you need to participate remotely is a computer and a phone (headphones are helpful, but not required).  For those participating in-person, phones and computers will be provided. 

Together, we can help elect leaders who will fight for working families and build a stronger Nevada.

Join us online via Zoom or in-person at the NV AFL-CIO office.

See you in the square!

The overpass light brigade is fashioned after other overpass light brigades popping up all over the country. It is part of our regular Saturday actions. 12noon-1pm.

events.title: 10/24 - Voter Mobilization & Get Out the VOTE - Sand Branch, TX
events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift in **Sand Branch, TX**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with voters during a _Get Out the Vote_ effort in the community
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone!

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[10:00am - 10:30am]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **[11:00am - 2:00pm] Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members and get folks set up on Reach. _After the event concludes, voters will team up in the community to caravan separately to early vote._

- **[2:00pm - 2:30pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.description:
Join Digital Ground Game and Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. 

There will be a morning shift, then lunch, followed by an afternoon shift. If you don't have a full day, feel free to participate in the shift you have time for.

We can flip PA-01 blue and replace Brian Fitzpatrick with **Bob Harvie**. Additionally, there's a real chance that PA Dems can win a trifecta for the first time since 1993. PA Republicans last had a trifecta 2011, which lasted until 2014 and caused a lot of problems that PA is now facing. If PA Dems win a trifecta this year they can raise minimum wage, secure stable funding sources for SEPTA and PRT, start much needed repairs and upgrades on rural highways and roads, and many more things. 

For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

What’s on your ballot? Come find out—and have some fun!

Join the League of Women Voters of the CSRA for a special Turnout Tuesday: Democracy Carnival at Allen Homes on Tuesday, October 20, from 5:00–7:30 PM!

* Spin-the-Wheel Trivia

events.title: AZ-01 GOTV Text Bank
events.description:
AZ-01 Weekly Text Bank, Every Monday

Join us as we text Arizona voters to help them return their mail ballots and make a final plan to vote before the November 3 general election.

Every week we reach voters across Arizona so they're ready to take part in one of the most competitive House races in the country. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide who wins. We're making sure no voter is left behind.

We'll text voters who usually skip midterm elections to remind them of key deadlines and help them make a clear, confident plan to vote: by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send voters who plan to vote early or on Election Day the information they need, including early voting sites, polling locations, and how to track their mail ballot.

Volunteers will have real one-on-one conversations with voters by text, answer their questions, and help turn intention into action so ballots get returned and votes get counted.

💬 Weekly text bank: Mondays at 6 p.m. PT (every week through Election Day)
🔥 No experience needed. All you need is a laptop. We provide training, scripts, and support.

Close races are won by making sure every vote counts. Your text could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Arizona!

Join People's Action Power and Team '26, a coalition of movement organizations across the country, to reach the working-class voters in must-win Congressional and Senate races that will decide who controls Congress -- and whether we save our democracy. 

## 📞Phonebank Schedule: 

###  🚒 Pennsylvania Tuesdays: Bob Brooks for Congress (PA-7)
A 20-year Bethlehem firefighter and former president of the firefighters' union, who fought a ten-year battle to win mental health coverage for his crew. He's taking on Ryan Mackenzie, who voted to cut healthcare for his own neighbors and constituents while cutting taxes for billionaires. 

### 🏥 Michigan Thursdays: Will Lawrence for Congress, MI-7, and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for US Senate 

- Will Lawrence is the Sunrise Movement co-founder who helped win the largest green jobs program in US history and delivered hundreds of millions to Mid-Michigan. He co-founded Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High to win statewide renter protections. 

- Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a medical doctor who realized broken politics was making people sick, and he went to work fixing government: rebuilt Detroit's Health Department after bankruptcy, got lead out of the schools, and canceled $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders. He wrote the book on Medicare for All, and now, he's going to the Senate to make government work for you, not billionaires. 
 
The message from the primary season was loud and clear: Working Families candidates are winning. Working people aren't settling for just any candidate. They're demanding Movement Champions who answer to them, not big corporations and big money. 

Are you fired up? Sign up for the shifts leading up to Election Day. Share this link widely with your friends and family. 

No prior experience is required to join this phone bank. A laptop or tablet is recommended.

Let's go! Let's take back the People's House.

events.title: Phonebank for Jerry Jones Jr. and NH4A - Training Included!
events.description:
Join us for a phonebank on Zoom to help elect Jerry Jones Jr. to the New Hanover County Board of Education!

We’ll start with a training led by Field Captain Ebony Savage on how to make calls using Scale to Win. Then we’ll stay together on Zoom while we phonebank, with support available throughout.

Whether you’re an experienced phonebanker or making your first calls, we welcome you to join in to build a better future for New Hanover's students. We’ll provide the script and everything you need to get started.

Time: 10:00 AM–1:30 PM
Location: Zoom — join from wherever you are!

What to bring: A computer, a phone, and a reliable internet connection.

events.title: Boulder: No On 134 + 135 Saturday Canvassing
events.description:
Join us every other Saturday at 12pm to knock doors and educate our neighbors on the dangers of these ballot initiatives! Stay for the social after!

LOCATION WILL BE EMAILED AND TEXTED WEEKLY. Training will take place before you are sent out with your materials and packets!

No On 134 + 135 is a local campaign with the goal of defeating Ballot Propositions 134 and 135 in the November 2026 election. Help keep CO Safe for our trans siblings!

events.title: Vote Early Rensselaer County Today!

location.venue: Intersection of Rts 43 and 150, near Hannaford's

events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

events.title: Boston ICE Tea Party 2.0
events.description:
Join the Boston ICE Tea Party 2.0!

We call upon all patriots to join us again on Dec 12th, 2026 for the second Boston ICE Tea Party on the ​​250th anniversary of our nation’s founding, to retrace the footsteps of this historic protest and declare once more - America has No Kings!

We will gather at 7:00pm at the Irish Famine Memorial Plaza, across the Old South Meeting House. We will march to Waterfront Plaza, by the Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum. And we will dump ice into Boston Harbor, to declare loud and clear: No Kings! No Tariffs! No ICE!

There will be clean ice provided for dumping. Please do not bring your own ice.

For over 250 years, Bostonians have refused to bow down to tyranny. When King George III forced soldiers into Boston’s streets, levied unjust taxes on imported tea, and refused to hear the people’s voices, the colonial patriots took a stand. On December 16, 1773, hundreds of colonists hurled tea into Boston Harbor in protest of King George’s tyranny, in what some call the single most important event leading up to the American Revolution.

Today, a President who behaves like a king occupies the White House. He has sent ICE to harass our city and kidnap our friends, families, and neighbors. He has levied unjust tariffs, and made our tea, our groceries, and our lives more expensive. Let us rise together once more to take down tyranny!

This a local Indivisible event!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: November 9 Meeting of Bellaire/Braeswood and West U Area Dems with Jeremy Wallace
events.description:
Come join the Bellaire/Braeswood Democrats and the West University Area Democrats at the November 9, 2026 meeting with Jeremy Wallace of the Houston Chronicle.  Jeremy will analyze what just happened on November 3rd and what to expect will happen going forward because of the results.

Jeremy Wallace has covered politics and campaigns for more than 20 years. Before joining the Hearst Texas newspapers in 2017, he covered government and politics for the Tampa Bay Times, The Miami Herald and the Sarasota Herald-Tribune. Previously he covered Congress for the Boston Globe and Detroit Free-Press. Originally from San Antonio, he attended the University of North Texas and earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Missouri.

Jeremy also authors the Texas Take with Jeremy Wallace newsletter, where he shares insights from inside the Capitol.  Work on the Texas Take has him frequently on CNN, PBS, BBC America, MSNBC and statewide NPR stations.

Social time: 6:30 - 7:00 pm. Business time: 7:00 - 8:00 pm
Location: West University Community Center at 6104 Auden St. 77005

events.description:
Great Scott Farms is graciously extending a field to harvest fresh produce for families in need. This is a great way to way to give back, enjoy the outdoors, and share in meaningful community service.

All are welcome! The more hands we have to help- the more produce we can recover! Produce is available for anyone in need. 

We are beginning many gleans at 11am due to private gleans that are scheduled on the same day. The private groups will only be gleaning for an hour so there should be plenty of produce left over to rescue. 

If you would like to be a receiving agency please reach out to the leading coordinator or Megan at (863) 224-0403. 

🌱 What to Bring:

✅ Closed-toe shoes (required)

✅ Comfortable clothing that can get messy

✅ Hat, sunscreen, and gloves (optional but helpful)

✅ A reusable water bottle to stay hydrated

📢 RSVP or Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen
📞 (863) 224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is gleaning?

- Gleaning is collecting leftover crops from farms that would otherwise go to waste. These fresh fruits and vegetables are then donated to food banks and hunger relief groups.

#### 2. Who can attend?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve. (Kids must be with an adult.)

#### 3. Are tools provided?
- Yes! We’ll supply any tools and bags you’ll need to glean.

#### 4. What if it rains?

- We’ll monitor the weather and let you know if anything changes. Safety first!

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need. If you are an organization in need - reach out to the event coordinator to become a recipient. 

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates, visit: https://www.mobilize.us/endhunger/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets

events.title: Step Up for Democracy: New Haven GOTV Canvass & Lit Drop
events.description:
This is our last day in New Haven neighborhoods! We will mostly be dropping off the doorhangers! 

Join the League of Women Voters of Connecticut and LWV New Haven for a nonpartisan door-to-door canvass to empower our community and ensure every eligible voter’s voice is heard!

With key elections approaching, we are knocking on doors across New Haven to make sure our neighbors are fully prepared to cast their ballots by November 3rd. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or taking to the doors for the first time, we will provide the training and materials you need to make an impact.

What We’ll Be Doing:

Voter Education: Sharing clear, trusted details on voting options, key dates, and election procedures in Connecticut.

Voter Empowerment: Helping community members make a concrete plan to participate on or before November 3rd.

Answering Questions: Helping voters check their voter status, locate their local polling information, and navigate general voter resources like VOTE411.org.

Schedule & Agenda:

1:00 PM: Welcome & Canvass Training: We will kick off with brief nonpartisan messaging training, review route assignments, pair experienced canvassers with new canvassers, and walk through our canvassing app.

1:30 PM | Door-to-Door Canvassing: Pairs will head out to assigned New Haven neighborhoods to engage local voters.

3:30 PM – 4:00 PM | Debrief & Material Return: Gather back at our starting hub to drop off materials and share stories.

How to Prepare:

What to Wear: Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing.

What to Bring: A fully charged smartphone, a water bottle, and a friend!

The League of Women Voters is a strictly nonpartisan organization that encourages informed and active participation in government. We do not support or oppose candidates or political parties.

events.title: Signature Verification and Early Ballot Tabulation Volunteers

Starting Wednesday, October 14, Navajo County begins verifying signatures and counting early ballots, and we need eyes in the room to make sure every ballot is handled correctly and counted.

We're filling two volunteer roles, both in Holbrook from 8:30 am until the day's ballots are finished, hours will vary. 

Signature Verification Observer
📍 Navajo County Recorder's Office
Observe staff as they match signatures on early ballot envelopes to the voter rolls.

Tabulation Observer

How scheduling works: Verification and tabulation only happen when there are enough ballots for a shift, so not every date will be needed and the final schedule isn't set yet. Sign up for every day you're available, and we'll call you the day before to confirm your shift.

Every ballot matters. Thank you for helping protect them! 🗳️

events.title: Share Mark Pinsley's videos (Easy!)
events.description:
Democrats have not controlled the Pennsylvania Senate for three decades. Their path to flipping it likely runs through the Lehigh Valley and Bucks County (SD-16), where Mark Pinsley is running against Republican incumbent Jarrett Coleman.  Mark is ahead by one point, according to the latest polls.  

Mark's videos are funny and interesting.  You don’t have to be a tech wizard or even a social media fan to increase the reach of the videos that can change voters’ minds.

### Click here to [Watch, Like, Comment, and Share Mark's Facebook videos](https://www.facebook.com/VoteMarkPinsley/reels/). 

You can also find Mark on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/markpinsley/)
 and [Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/@voteformarkpinsley).

Here are six simple steps that go a long way.

1. WATCH the video till the end. This tells the algorithm people are liking and engaging with it.

2. LIKE the post, with the “love” or “wow” emojis rather than a simple “like.”

3. COMMENT on the video. Explain why you like it, using first person and emotive terms. For example: “This is why I love candidate Mark Pinsley – he tells it like it is."

4. SHARE the video on your social media feeds if you have them. Sharing is worth 30x more than a Like on the latest Facebook algorithm.

5. REPLY TO POSITIVE COMMENTS
Be emotive and use the first person. Do NOT respond to negative
comments or get into online arguments as this wastes your time and rewards their trolling.

6. AMPLIFY other comments by liking them, pinning them to the top of the comment thread or replying to the comment with phrases like “Right on! We need more people who will go out and vote like you will.” Follow up questions encourage others to comment, creating a “comment thread” which tells the algorithm the post is getting attention and should be offered to others. “My friends are all stoked to vote for candidate Mark Pinsley. Are you seeing the same enthusiasm?”

These are steps you can take easily, on your own schedule, whenever a candidate or volunteer posts something watchable. Instant gratification for you and an instant boost for your cause.

Refreshments, snacks, Live music and games

events.title: Caring for Our Community Trees

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Tree Pittsburgh this Fall in the Mon Valley for a free tree education series!

Whether you're new to tree planting and care or want to build your skills, these sessions will give you practical, hands-on experience and useful knowledge you can apply to the trees in your neighborhood.

*Register now to stay up to date on session dates, locations, and other event details.* 

Throughout the series, you'll learn about tree planting, tree care, tree health, and common tree stressors through a mix of hands-on activities and classroom-style learning. We'll host most sessions in *Braddock, PA *, with additional sessions in *Rankin, PA*. Some sessions will use a hybrid format with an online portion.

You can attend the sessions that work for your schedule. We'll provide refreshments at most in-person sessions.

*Come prepared for the weather!* We plan to hold outdoor sessions rain or shine and will only cancel or reschedule when severe weather, such as thunderstorms, makes it unsafe to continue. 

*Need accessibility support?* Email the ReLeaf team at releaf@treepittsburgh.org or call 412-781-8733 (x213).  Please contact us at least *72 hours before the event you plan to attend* so we can best support your participation. 

Complete all sessions to earn your Tree Tender certification and receive a pair of hand pruners. Come learn with us, build your tree knowledge and tree care skills!

events.title: Brookline Rally for Democracy, December 2026
events.description:
Brookline Rally for Democracy

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.
events.accessibility_notes: All are welcome, including participants with walkers, wheelchairs, scooters, and other mobility devices.

events.title: Carson City Indigenous Voices of Nevada Disc-Go to the Polls!

location.venue: Stewart Indian School Cultural Center & Museum

events.description:
In 2016, the Pyramid Lake Paiutes and the Walker River Paiutes won a lawsuit against the state of Nevada to establish early in-person voting and Election Day polling sites in towns located within their respective reservations. 

On October 24, 2026, join Indigenous Voices of Nevada and friends to celebrate their successes with free food, disco, karaoke, and community spirit. Tribal members will be able to cast their vote using NV EASE and there will be additional resources for people interested in participating in their local communities.

events.title: Games People Play

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Breaking the ICE is a deliberate, breathless convergence—a strategic intervention that breathes life into the space between us. It unites women who move through entirely different worlds, weaving together the lives of Black, African Diaspora, Arab, Latina, White, and Asian women. We gather with intention, bridging the deep, silent divides of culture, faith, socioeconomic lineage, and raw lived experience.

This event is designed to be an intentional, transformative space where community organizing meets cultural celebration.

This time, we gather around the table.

Every game has its players. Every player has a strategy. There are rules spoken aloud and rules you only discover once you are already in play. There is power in knowing when to move, when to wait, when to protect your queen and when it is finally time to take the king.

The Games We Play is an intimate evening of strategy, pleasure, competition, and political discovery. Across scattered tables, women will gather over chessboards, cards, and games designed to make us think differently about power. We will laugh, challenge one another, break bread, and uncover the quiet calculations behind the political world we move through every day.

Because politics has always had its games.

Who gets invited to the table? Who knows the rules before the game begins? Who has spent years quietly learning the board? And what happens when women from entirely different worlds sit across from one another and begin sharing what they know?

Event Schedule

5:00 PM–8:00 PM | The Board, The Players, The Power and light dinner.

Take your seat.

Move between tables filled with games, conversation, food, and connection. Learn the seductive discipline of chess—patience, sacrifice, protection, anticipation. Enter Political Healing Monopoly, where those who have spent years doing the work help reveal how power, relationships, resources, and organizing actually move through our communities.

And somewhere between the laughter, competition, and the next move, we will enter a deeper conversation about the games of politics to the rules nobody writes down, the rooms where decisions are made, the relationships that shift the board, and the strategies communities have used to survive, organize, and build power.

Come curious. Come competitive. Come ready to teach something and ready to be taught.

The board is already set.
The question is: how will you play?

Because once you understand the game, you can begin to understand the board.

Host Committees & Partners

Brought to you in powerful solidarity with:

* Fems for Dems
* Arab Americans for Progress
* Reproductive Freedom for All
* ABISA

events.description:
Come knock doors in Iowa with us to knock doors for Democrats in competitive congressional, gubernatorial, and U.S. Senate races!

We'll be carpooling from Naperville to Iowa at 9:00 AM. You may also *drive directly* to our Iowa-based launch location, where we will meet at 12:00 PM. 

No matter what you choose, you'll be canvassing with the same people in the same place! We'll see you there!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)
### Staging Location

Volunteers will either meet in Naperville or drive directly to Iowa (Address to be shared prior to event). Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

events.description:
It's time to beat back fascism and elect pro-working people candidates. Deep canvassing is the best proven tactic to move voters!

Join us for two joint door-knocks with Austin Indivisible and TakeAction Minnesota.

Canvassers will receive a deep canvassing training on site prior to knocking doors. Our team will coordinate ride share informally for anyone that needs one. The exact meet up location will be shared in the days before the knock - we will be knocking in Austin, MN!

As working people struggle to make ends meet, billionaires and corporations are pulling the strings. We are pushing back and working to elect pro-worker candidates to Congress this fall!

For some extra prep, join us at our virtual deep canvass training on 10/13 --> https://www.mobilize.us/takeactionminnesota/event/1053163/

Join us for an afternoon honoring Dia de los Muertos and our lost loved ones whose memories live on through our families, traditions, and stories shared.

Together we will honor the lives taken by harmful policies and practices across many social justice issues: violent immigration enforcement, environmental injustice, labor injustice, reproductive injustice, and all other threats to human rights and our communities.

events.title: MI Dems Michigan Poll Challenger Training
events.description:
Learn to become a Poll Challenger! Our democracy is on the line and we need Poll Challengers across the state to stand as the first line of defense for voter's rights. Time is running out to join! These attacks on our elections won’t stop on their own, we need you to help us build this resistance.

First time? No problem. We'll provide all the training and support you need to protect the polls. Join us for this live virtual training session to get ready for service.

Join our frontline defense- if you haven't yet, sign up now by visiting www.michigandems.com/voterprotection!

As a Poll Challenger, you work with our Boiler Room Team to resolve voter and polling place issues in real time. Observe and report issues through Early Voting, Election Day, and absentee ballot counting on and before E-Day. Active Oct 24 - Nov 3.

events.title: Let's Talk about Data ... Centers!
events.description: Join Chispa TX for a conversation and learning opportunity to understand what is happening in local fights around encroaching data centers. Together we will understand more of the threats that data centers pose to water, energy, and local communities as well as what has been successful as local leaders push back. Come to learn, share, and ask questions.

events.title: Tent Setup/Takedown for Early Voting at Kville Paddison Memorial Library
events.description:
Please help create a strong presence for the Dems, and shelter your fellow Dem volunteers, by setting up and/or taking down the Dem table and tent at early voting. We've represented the Dems well for years at Kernersville's Paddison Memorial Library's polling location...and need to do it again this year! Tent and table will be provided--just need the setup help. 
If possible, when you sign up to pick up the tent and table at the end of the day, then also register for the next morning shift to set it up...so you won't have to hand off the materials. Thank you!

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

Early Voting is here, and Friends of Fonde Park is turning the trip to the ballot box into a neighborhood block party! events.title: Vote Early
events.description:
Join us for a special SOS at the corner on 10/20/2026 at 3:30PM as we encourage everyone to VOTE EARLY. VOTING EARLY IS HOW WE USE OUR POWER. Bring your "Vote Early" signs and your American flags.  

Voting is the core of our democracy. Voting early means your voice is locked in and safe, and it gives you room to fix anything that goes wrong, a signature mismatch, a missing form, waiting in a line that's too long, or not being able to make it if your shift runs late.

events.title: 🎨 Crafting Change: A Voting-Inspired Arts & Crafts Night 🗳️✂️
events.description:
# 🎨 Crafting Change: A Voting-Inspired Arts & Crafts Night 🗳️✂️

### **About this event**

Join us for a relaxing, creative evening of community and civic expression! 🌟 We are gathering at **The Dovetail** in Warren on **Thursday, October 30th, from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM** for an open arts and crafts collage night centered around civic power and voting. 🗳️✊

Whether voting means defending your community, fighting for bodily autonomy, honoring civil rights leaders, protecting public education, or speaking truth to power, art is one of the most powerful ways to make our voices visible! 🗣️💫

We want to explore the personal spark behind our ballots:
* 🗳️ **Why do you vote?**
* 💡 **What issues, people, or future visions inspire you to take action?**
* 🤝 **Why is community participation essential for our collective future?**

**All materials will be provided free of charge!** 🆓✂️ We’ll have cardstock, magazine clippings, prints, markers, glue, scissors, and decorative craft supplies ready for you. No prior art or collage experience is needed—just bring your ideas, your story, and your vision! 🖍️✨

---

### 🖼️ **What happens to your art?**
You are welcome to take your finished collage home that night, or you can lend it to us to be featured in an art installation display at our **November monthly meeting**! 🏛️🎉

---

### **Event Details:**
* 📅 **Date:** Thursday, October 30th
* ⏰ **Time:** 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM
* 📍 **Location:** The Dovetail (29200 Hoover Rd, Warren, MI 48093)
* 🎟️ **Cost:** Free & open to all!
* ✂️ **Supplies:** 100% provided

Space is limited, so please RSVP to help us ensure we have enough craft supplies and seating for everyone! 📝 Bring a friend, grab a beverage or treat ☕🍪, and let’s turn our passion into art! 🎨✨

events.title: Austin Dia De los Muertos

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join us for a late afternoon honoring Dia de los Muertos and our lost loved ones whose memories live on through our families, traditions, and stories shared.

Together we will honor the lives taken by harmful policies and practices across many social justice issues: violent immigration enforcement, environmental injustice, labor injustice, reproductive injustice, and all other threats to human rights and our communities.

We welcome you to bring your family, memories, stories, and a picture of a loved one to place on the altar. We will have pan dulce, champurrado, and more to celebrate this holiday.


Español Abajo

Acompáñanos a compartir una tarde en conmemoración del Día de los Muertos, honrando a nuestros seres queridos que ya no están con nosotros, pero cuyas memorias siguen vivas a través de nuestras familias, tradiciones y las historias que compartimos.

Juntos honraremos las vidas que hemos perdido a causa de políticas y prácticas dañinas relacionadas con distintas luchas por la justicia social, incluyendo la violencia de las políticas migratorias, la injusticia ambiental, la injusticia laboral, la injusticia reproductiva y todas aquellas amenazas contra los derechos humanos y nuestras comunidades.

Te invitamos a traer a tu familia, tus recuerdos, tus historias y una fotografía de un ser querido para colocarla en nuestro altar. Tendremos pan dulce, champurrado y más para compartir en comunidad y celebrar esta hermosa tradición.

events.description:
These workshops aim to dispel common voting misperceptions and provide the election and ballot information you need to simplify the voting process and make you a more confident voter. You are welcome to bring your ballot. Definitely bring your questions.

Voter turnout is paramount, especially this year. The more who vote, the better chance of having a more representative government.

Additional dates/time are offered at https://yakima-indivisible.org/events/ They are all the same workshop. More dates may be added.

If you would like to host a workshop for your employees, or club, or church, or any group, email us at contact@yakima-indivisible.org with the subject line Decoding Your Ballot. We will do our best to accommodate your request.

events.title: Election Protection: Virtual Poll Monitoring Training
events.description:
Join Bridge North Texas (Dallas County), the Election Protection Coalition, and 866-OUR-VOTE to protect the vote and ensure fair, accessible elections in our community! We are partnering to provide training, resources, and ongoing support for nonpartisan election work, canvassing, and poll monitoring.
Whether you're ready to dive right in or want hands-on assistance getting started, we have two simple pathways to help you get involved:

Choose How You Want to Join:
  Option A: Self-Paced / Direct Sign-Up
   Sign up via our link anytime to complete the online training with Common Cause Texas. Once finished, you will be connected directly with a local Bridge North Texas organizer to coordinate picking up your materials.

  Option B: Hands-On Setup & Walkthrough
   Sign up ahead of time with Bridge North Texas! Our team will walk you through the registration process step-by-step, assist with setting up your training, and prepare your materials for pickup.

What You'll Be Doing:
  Poll Monitoring: Help observe voting locations to protect voters' rights and ensure smooth election site operations.

  Canvassing & Community Outreach: Distribute voter education information, answer questions, and direct voters to key resources.

  Rapid Response Support: Work in tandem with the national 866-OUR-VOTE hotline network to address nonpartisan voting issues in real time.
Sign up today to protect democracy in North Texas!

events.description:
Join the HD-82 campaign’s **Van Wert County Anytime Canvass** from **October 4 through November 3**.

The Anytime Canvass is designed to make volunteering flexible. Instead of signing up for a specific scheduled shift, you can help when it works for you—whether you have an hour after work, a free afternoon, or several hours on a weekend.

Volunteers can choose how they would like to participate:

- **Direct voter contact:** Knock doors and speak with voters using an assigned canvassing list.
- **Literature delivery:** Help distribute campaign literature to assigned households without conducting voter conversations.

No previous canvassing experience is required. Instructions and the information you need to complete your assigned area will be provided.

After signing up, we’ll coordinate with you on an available area in **Van Wert County**, provide the necessary canvassing information and materials, and make sure you know how to report your completed area.

You can participate more than once throughout the month. If you finish an assignment and want another, we can provide an additional assignment.

**Sign up, choose the type of canvassing that works for you, and help cover Van Wert County on your own schedule between October 4 and November 3.**

The film, No Country for Mothers, explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the "girl boss" and "trad wife" labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families.

This isn’t a film meant to be watched or shared only by mothers; we’ve all had a mother and we all have friends, partners, colleagues, neighbors, and relatives who are mothers. Therefore, we all have a valid POV & contribution to make.

The event is being held at Fuegos LA, and their delicious empanadas, full menu and drinks will be available for purchase.

The film runs for 78 minutes, and we’ll have some group discussion pre- and post-film.

If you can’t make it, please share with anyone you know who would love to be there!

events.title: Volunteer to Phone Bank Canvass for Endorsed Candidates
events.description:
### **Saturday Weekend Action Days: Canvass & Phone Bank!**

**Join us every Saturday to make a real impact in our community!** Whether you prefer talking to neighbors face-to-face or reaching out over the phone, we need your help to power our grassroots movement. 

You can sign up for a single day or secure your spot for multiple Saturdays to keep our momentum going. 

#### **Shift Information**
* **Standard Shift:** 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM
* **Flexible Hours:** We want to work with your schedule! If you are available to help outside of our standard hours—such as an afternoon shift from **2:00 PM – 7:00 PM**—please sign up for a regular shift and reply to your Mobilize confirmation email to let the event contact know your preferred hours.

#### **What to Bring & Expect**
* **Time Commitment:** If you can't stay for the full shift, that is not a problem! If you can manage about **45 minutes for training** and then phone bank or canvass for **about an hour**, that is sufficient to make a big difference.
* **For Canvassing:** Comfortable walking shoes, a fully charged smartphone, and a water bottle.
* **For Phone Banking:** We have **5 phones and tablets available** for volunteer use. However, if you are comfortable doing so, we highly encourage you to **bring your own laptop and mobile phone**. 
* **Audio Gear:** A headset (microphone and headphones) with a **traditional headphone jack** is highly recommended to help you make calls easily, but it is **not required**.


*Training and materials will be provided at the start of every shift. No prior experience is necessary!*

**Choose your dates below and shift into action with us!**

Join Minnesotans to phonebank from home and get out the vote for our full DFL-endorsed ticket of candidates!

On November 3rd, we have the opportunity to elect leaders who will build a better future for all of us, but we can't do it without your help. Every call made and conversation had brings us closer to victory – so invitea friend and log on to talk to your neighbors about why you support our DFL ticket!

Whether it's your first time phonebanking or you're an experienced dialer, we'll provide a short training and all the materials you need! Just make sure you have access to a phone and a computer or tablet!

events.title: Madison Educator Days of Action! (Carpool to Dodgeville)
events.description:
Join WEAC Regions 5 & 6 and MTI members for four days of educator action. Sign up for one, or all four.

We’ll meet at the union headquarters and carpool together to knock doors in Dodgeville, an important area for the state races and also a school district facing a critical school referendum on November 3.
 

Schedule:

10am: Meet at WEAC building, 33 Nob Hill Road, Madison for training and carpool* assignments

10:30am: Depart in car caravan for Dodgeville

11-2:30pm: Door knocking in pairs or singles. Free lunch will be provided.

2:30pm: Cars head back to WEAC building.

events.description:
The Madison Democratic Town Committee invites you, your family, and your neighbors to an enchanting production of The Little Mermaid at one of our community’s greatest treasures: The Madison Arts Barn!

The Arts Barn is truly a pearl in our little neck of the Shoreline. For years, "The Barn" has provided a welcoming, safe, and inclusive space where Shoreline youth find their creative voices, gain confidence, and build lifelong friendships. Our town is vibrant and strong because of grassroots cultural spaces like this, and the Madison Democrats are proud to champion and support the performing arts right here at home.

Now, our talented local youth are bringing the beloved undersea kingdom to life on stage, and they deserve a packed house!

Performance Details:
Production: The Little Mermaid
Venue: The Madison Arts Barn, 8 Campus Drive, Madison, CT
Dates: NOV 6 & 7, 2027
Tickets & Info: madisonartsbarn.org to reserve your seats directly 

Why Join Us?
Celebrate Local Talent: Cheer on our amazing young performers, musicians, and stage crew who have poured their hearts into this production.

Support Shoreline Youth: Help ensure The Barn continues to thrive as an accessible, creative haven for all children across the Shoreline.

Connect with Community: Enjoy a wonderful family-friendly outing alongside neighbors, friends, and fellow Madison Democrats.

Bring your family, wear your ocean colors, and let’s show our local young performers just how proud Madison is of their hard work.

See you under the sea at The Barn! 🐚🎭🎶

events.title: Texas Together Block Walk: GOTV Southeast Arlington
events.description:
### Join Texas Together in Southeast Arlington as we ramp up the action to Get Out The Vote and knock doors to support **Texas Democratic** nominees up and down the ballot. 

It’s time to organize, unify, and build the movement that will carry us through the last 31 days until Election Day, November 3, 2026.

During the block walk, volunteers will:

- Identify Democratic supporters

- Share information about our Democratic ticket

- Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots efforts and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We’ll provide training, materials, and turf at the start of each shift. 

Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend.
**RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.**

events.title: Kanawha County IEP Circle
events.description:
IEP Circles WV is a parent-led community where families of exceptional learners come together to find support, build knowledge, and create change. If you're navigating an IEP, 504 Plan, evaluations, school communication, or accessing services, these gatherings are designed to help you feel informed, connected, and supported.

Each meeting brings caregivers together with experienced advocates, education attorneys, and community partners who provide practical guidance, answer questions, and facilitate meaningful discussions. You'll have opportunities to share experiences, learn from other families, discover helpful resources, and build lasting relationships with people who understand the challenges you face.

Beyond individual support, IEP Circles helps families understand the larger issues affecting special education. We'll explore how school funding, staffing shortages, IDEA funding, and state and federal policy decisions impact the services available to students. By connecting personal experiences to these broader challenges, families can better understand why obstacles exist and how they can work alongside educators and other parents to improve public education.

For those interested in taking the next step, IEP Circles also offers opportunities to develop advocacy skills through workshops on legislative advocacy, storytelling, public speaking, community organizing, and civic engagement. Whether you simply want support or hope to help shape the future of special education in West Virginia, you'll find a welcoming community where your experiences are valued and your voice matters.

Together, we can strengthen support for our children, build stronger communities, and advocate for a public education system that works for every student.

events.title: FOTV Canvass in Tioga County - Part One
events.description:
Dear Friends,

As we push our way into the final weeks of the general campaign, we are looking to join forces with the Coordinated Campaign to ensure every possible vote is contacted before election day. Join us and a team of volunteers from CC to knock on doors and encourage our voters to get out and vote!

Materials and training will be provided. We will get fresh GOTV walk lists generated by the Shapiro/Davis campaign as well as talking points. At this stage, we are no longer trying to persuade voters. We are simply reaching out to those who support our Democratic candidates and make sure they cast those votes!

You should be feeling excited as we enter this final phase. Enthusiasm for our Governor, for our State House and US Congressional candidates, and, indeed, for Democrats all across the country, is growing. The mood is shifting and the people are ready for, and demanding, change. Now.

Join us. This part is so important, and we need you! Thanks in advance!

Gabe Hakvaag
Chair
Tioga County Democrats

events.title: Angie for FL: Youth for Angie Weekly Winter Park Canvasses
events.description:
We are less than 35 days away from Election Day. Some voters will have already received their mail-in ballots. We need to get out into our communities and get out the vote for Felipe Sousa-Lazaballet for Florida House District 42 and Angie Nixon for US Senate!

Join Team Angie and Team Felipe as we canvass Winter Park and Rollins's College to let people know all about them!

We will hand out lists of doors to knock (of friendly, persuadable voters!) and pair people up with a buddy or in teams. The more the merrier!

You will need: 
Comfortable walking shoes and clothing for the weather (bring an umbrella or rain jacket in case of light rain) 
Sun protection (hat, sunscreen, etc.) 
Hydration (a bottle of water or two)

events.title: Rally Against The Regime - Election Season

location.venue: I-5 Overpass & NW Stewart Parkway (on the sidewalk)

events.description:
# Rally Against The Regime – Election Season

## 🗳️ Election Season Is Here, and We're Taking It to the Overpass

From now through the November election, our weekly **Rally Against The Regime** moves to the **I-5 Overpass at NW Stewart Parkway**. Thousands of drivers pass this spot every day, and we want every one of them to see our message:

**Vote the Trump administration and its Republican enablers out of power. End fascism. Take our country back to the democracy it was meant to be.**

Ballots are coming. This is our moment, and it starts at the mailbox.


## 📍 When & Where

- **When:** Saturdays, **12:00 pm – 2:00 pm**, through the election

- **Where:** **I-5 Overpass & NW Stewart Parkway** (on the sidewalk)
  3599 NW Stewart Pkwy, Roseburg, OR 97471


## 🧰 What To Bring

This isn't just a protest. **It's people power on display.**

### 📣 Make Your Voice Visible

**Go BIG.** Drivers are moving fast, so **large signs with short messages** in thick, high-contrast letters work best. Here are some ideas:

- **VOTE EARLY. VOTE THEM OUT!**

- **MY BALLOT IS MY VOICE!**

- **DOUGLAS COUNTY VOTES BLUE!**

- **FILL IT OUT. MAIL IT IN. VOTE EARLY!**

- **REPUBLICANS HAD THEIR CHANCE!**

- **HONK IF YOU'RE VOTING EARLY!**

- **BALLOTS ARE HERE. USE THEM!**

- **REAL CHANGE STARTS AT THE MAILBOX!**

👉 Or create your own. **Be bold. Be direct. Don't hold back.**

### 🎨 Get Creative

- 🪆 Giant puppets

- 🎭 Creative props

- 🧥 Costumes

- 🚩 Banners & flags

- 🎶 Street-theater vibes


### 🥤 Stay Comfortable

- 💧 Water

- 🍎 A snack

- 🕶️ Sunglasses & sunscreen

- 🧢 Hat or umbrella for sun or rain

- 👟 Comfortable shoes

- 💊 Any medications you need

⚠️ **No bathrooms on site. Plan accordingly.**


## 🕊️ Our Commitment to Nonviolence

This is a **peaceful, nonviolent demonstration**. Please:

- **Stay on the sidewalk** and keep it clear for people walking by. Never step into traffic.

- **Secure your signs and banners** so the wind can't carry them onto the roadway below.

- **Don't engage with counter-protesters**, and help calm things down and de-escalate if tensions rise.

- **This is a non-violent action. Leave all weapons at home.**

---

**See you on the overpass. Let's vote them out.** 🇺🇸

**Note on Parking:** To access the overpass facing the Northbound I-5 traffic, park in the empty lot all the way at the top of Boulder Drive on your left (go up the curved road behind Oregon Pacific Bank off of Edenbower Blvd and Boulder Drive) or along the roadway. Crossing to the other side of the overpass (facing Southbound I-5 traffic) is done at your own risk.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: BOONTON: Be an Early Voting Poll Watcher with the Morris County Dems
events.description:
Join the team in protecting our Democracy and ensuring the polls are open, functioning, and free of voter intimidation. We will be staffing polls across the county. 

What is a poll watcher? 

A Poll Watcher or "Challenger" is a person appointed to observe the conduct of an election on behalf of a candidate, political party and/or the proponents or opponents of a question.

The integrity of elections is a concern of all citizens and although poll watchers may represent particular candidates, political parties or specific questions, their main interest is in the conduct of a fair and honest election.

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Organize and Win Senate Phonebank

events.description:
From now until Election Day we are doing everything we can to elect progressives to the United States Senate. Abdul El-Sayed, Peggy Flanagan, and Angie Nixon are all Senate candidates in key states who Senator Sanders has endorsed.

Letter from Senator Sanders: 

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few. 

Right now, our movement is winning. Why? 

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges. 

We now have candidates all over the country who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement. 

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up. 

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us. 

Let’s get to work. 

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.title: Bernards Township: Be an Early Voting Poll Watcher with the Somerset County Dems
events.description:
Join the team in protecting our Democracy and ensuring the polls are open, functioning, and free of voter intimidation. We will be staffing polls across the county.

What is a poll watcher?

A Poll Watcher or "Challenger" is a person appointed to observe the conduct of an election on behalf of a candidate, political party and/or the proponents or opponents of a question.

The integrity of elections is a concern of all citizens and although poll watchers may represent particular candidates, political parties or specific questions, their main interest is in the conduct of a fair and honest election.

events.title: Weekly Meade Ave Bridge Bannering Over I-805 | Tuesdays
events.description:
Meet on the Meade Ave bridge over I-805.

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

events.title: A surgeon in Gaza
events.description:
On Monday, October 26, 2026, Indivisible East Bay's Gaza Action Squad will host a trauma and general surgeon from the Bay Area who recently returned from working at Al Shifa hospital in Gaza City.  Our guest will describe how his international team from a small NGO, Humanity Auxilium, worked with local doctors, in particular women, to provide care where medical supplies are subject to engineered shortages. Our guest will describe what it means to provide medical care under these conditions. All are welcome.

The IEB Gaza Action Squad opposes the ongoing destruction of the society and people of Gaza and the West Bank, and we do what we can to stop it. We lobby Senators and other legislators to stop military aid to Israel, promote divestment from companies that facilitate genocide, support initiatives such as the Oakland People's Arms Embargo, and meet with people with first-hand knowledge of events in Palestine. location.venue: Bark Haul Road (at the I91 overpass)

events.description:
Concerned about the mid-terms? Outraged about the state of our country? Join a massive multi-state overpass visibility campaign to promote voting for the upcoming midterm election on Saturdays October 10 and 31. Our messages will build impact as drivers see sign after sign the longer they drive. The Longmeadow overpass will be one of a host of sites on I-91 and across the northeast. The campaign spans from Boston, all the way west on the Mass Pike, across New York state to Erie, PA, as well as north-south from CT and RI to VT on high visibility routes including I-93, I-91, 495, Route 128 and more. Join us!!

How to Get There: The address Bark Haul Road will get you there if you're using Waze. (Bark Haul Road is off Route 5.) The event is on the I-91 overpass. There's plenty of parking at either end of Bark Haul Rd, and parking on the overpass is discouraged.

No signs can be attached to the overpass fencing so be prepared to hold your sign. Never drape anything over the fence, even with ropes, because it would be very dangerous if it accidentally fell onto the highway.

Please take everything you brought away with you and leave the site totally clean.


When: Saturdays October 10 and 31 Time: 11am to 12:30 pm ET. Come for any length of time that works for you.

Where: Bark Haul Road at the I91 Overpass, Longmeadow, MA

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We expect all participants to uphold this commitment. We recommend that all participants review our safety and security resource before the event: https://indivisi.org/safety.

events.title: Phone Banking (Fully Virtual)
events.description:
Join us online to GET OUT THE VOTE by phone banking!

**What to expect:**

We'll be using an online dialer platform that connects you directly to voters — no need to dial numbers yourself. Once you're connected, you'll read from a simple, conversational script designed to help you have real conversations, not a robotic pitch. The script walks you through an introduction, a few key talking points about what's at stake, and a couple of questions to gauge where the person you're speaking with stands.

Before calls begin, a trained lead will walk everyone through: 
- How to log into the phone bank platform 
- How the dialer works (it does the dialing — you just talk!) 
- A walkthrough of the script and how to enter responses 
- Tips for handling common questions or pushback

**Why it matters:**
Every conversation helps us identify supporters, share accurate information, and build the coalition we need to protect trans and immigrant Coloradans. Phone banking is flexible, low-pressure, and a great option no matter your schedule or experience level.

**What you need:**

*Computer
*Headphones
*Enthusiasm for the cause!

events.title: Hyper Local 101 Training
events.description:
Wisco, a friend and ally from MN is one of the people instrumental in creating the area’s Community Defense Network known as “Hyper Locals,” which were created in response to the ICE surge in the Twin Cities that began in December of 2025.

Hyper Locals are independently created and run community-based groups that covers any size community up to an entire town with the 
purpose to connect, organize and train community members to be ready to respond to whatever threat may surface in their area.

Hyper Locals serve not only as community 
defense, but as a means to strengthen and support communities through collective action and connection. Like most states combating the overreach of ICE, CT is dealing with a similar own set of challenges keeping our communities safe from ICE. Hyper Locals would connect and communicate with established Immigrant Defense orgs around the state doing amazing work & offer support however and whenever possible. 

Wisco will be conducting a Training on how to build a Hyper Local in your community. This training will include an explanation of what a Hyper Local is, how to form one, what it can look like to fit your communities needs, structure, setting up signal chats, vetting, patrols, dispatching, training & more. A Q&A will follow as well as hands on help for anyone who needs assistance setting up Signal. Attendees will also be able to join a state-wide Signal chat for Hyper Locals to keep everyone connected.

A newly formed Hyper Local in Milford & The Perseus Project will be on hand to speak to the work they are doing and how they created their groups based on this model. Information will also be provided for many of the areas Immigrant Defense organizations.

Following the training there will be time for a Potluck. We encourage attendees to bring something to share and spend this time getting to know one another, building our community and our connections.

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ Thomas & Central

address_lines: North Central Avenue & West Thomas Road

events.description:
**Join us for our Thursday morning rally on Thomas & Central in Midtown Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 The rally starts at 7:30. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 8:30 AM.  

✴️ We gather on the huge sidewalk on the NW corner, but some walk to the SE corner (to avoid the sun) or the NE corner. Lots of room! Look for the signs. You can't miss us.

🅿️ There's an abandoned parking lot on the NW corner, just south of the dispensary. Alternatively, the stores at the south end of the shopping center, on the SE corner, aren't open until later in the day.  

🪧 One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

😷 RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are common on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.title: Canvass with us in Indiana Congressional District 5!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
CD-5 is the most flippable red seat in Congress in Indiana - but we need YOUR help talking to voters to make that happen. 

In 2022, Indiana had the LOWEST midterm voter turnout in the country at 40%. There is a pervasive sense of "Indiana is red and always will be." But in truth: 

**Indiana is a purple state that DOESN'T VOTE.** 

We have the chance this month to use our votes to end the corruption. End the violence. End the lies. A House majority would give Democrats the ability to rein in Donald Trump.

And so...we are going on offense.

**Join one or more of our canvassing shifts to knock on doors in Congressional District 5 to help elect J.D. Ford.**

The voters we will canvass are just folks who need a little nudge to remind them to vote blue. You won't be talking to anyone MAGA or hard right. 

Democrat J.D. Ford is a well regarded and well liked sitting Indiana State Senator who is running against CD-5's current congressperson, Republican Victoria Spartz, for the congressional seat just north of Indianapolis. Rep Spartz has a reliable voting record in support of Donald Trump's agenda. 

So what can you do?

**You can join us.** 

If you haven't canvassed before, we will make it easy. You show up for your shift at a meeting spot with a shift leader and other canvassers to get your voter addresses and instructions. 

**Feeling shy, but you want to try it?** 

Simply sign up for a canvassing shift and a link to a general training about talking to voters will be sent to you. We can pair you with another canvasser, or you can bring a friend to walk with you while you knock on doors. 

Upon arrival at the meetup location, you will receive canvassing tips and JD Ford handouts to share at each door. You will be able to easily enter results as you canvass into the [MiniVAN app](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tv9-HHb1VQA) on your smartphone. 

A lot of canvassers like to make a fun day out of it: you can bring a friend and go out together for lunch or dinner after your shift. You can feel the satisfaction of doing your part for our democracy while getting in quality time with a friend. Win-win!

Registering for one or more shifts confirms that you agree to our [Code of Conduct and our Volunteer Waiver](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cpXG6qbL36S10EYFRqAVAIzfdSFiOG0utHdCFWdZ-9E/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.l1k2qhtuewim).

events.title: Spotlight on LexisNexis: The Hidden Data Pipeline From Your 911 Call to ICE
events.description:
What happens to your information when you call 911? Thousands of local law enforcement agencies are sharing their records — 911 caller data, victim information, witness information and more — with LexisNexis, a private data broker that sells access to federal agencies including ICE. This often happens without local officials and citizens realizing it, even in communities with sanctuary policies.

Join this De-ICE Action Network webinar to learn about this little-known data pipeline and what you can do to prevent local police departments from sharing sensitive private data with federal immigration enforcement and other agencies.

**Presenter:** Shawn Segal, Public Interest Researcher at [FinePrint](https://fineprint.report/), an investigative outlet covering mass surveillance, privacy and policing.

**Who should attend:** Organizers, advocates, local officials and staff, and anyone who wants to know how their community’s data may be helping fuel ICE’s cruel agenda.

**Registration required.** We hope to see you live, but please register even if you can’t make it! All registrants will receive a recording to watch later, along with a toolkit for taking action.

events.title: 10/18 - Voter Mobilization @ Hocus Pocus Drag Brunch
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift at **Hocus Pocus Drag Brunch**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
- Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. 

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.title: Knock doors for Randy Villegas, CD22 | October 16, 17, 18 in Delano!
events.description:
**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's get out the vote to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 daily stipend** is available to offset your out-of-district travel costs.

 - Friday, October 16 | 12:30 pm to 4:30 pm

 - Saturday, October 17 | 9:00 am to 12:30 noon and 1:00 pm to 4:30 pm 

 - Sunday, October 18 | 9:00 am to 1:00 pm

New to canvassing?  We will train you (and we are lots of fun).  Bring a friend.  Or two.  Be a part of the change we're all looking for.

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options ... and we have cooling cars if the weather is warm. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.  Alternate start times can be accommodated as needed.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/
