events.title: South Shore Bridge Brigade

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Meet on the 794 PEDESTRIAN overpass just North of Howard Avenue.

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters - to VOTE EARLY. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.
We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep clear to allow them to pass.
We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.
We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.
We are NOT allowed to attach the signs to the fencing on the overpass. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.
If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.
We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.
Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.
Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!
The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.
See you at 3:30 pm for setup and 4:00 pm to wave!

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: Texas: Social Media Monitoring Training
events.description:
We cannot afford to sit back as bad actors flood social media with misinformation. 

Join Common Cause Texas, the Election Protection Coalition and Voter Protection Corps to learn how to fight back. 

This training will focus on how election misinformation and disinformation show up online, how to identify and document concerning narratives, and how volunteers and community partners can help strengthen the broader response to misleading election information.

We’ll also spend time on the issues and narratives that are most relevant in Texas, with space to discuss what partners are already seeing and what may be helpful to monitor in the weeks ahead.

During the training, we’ll cover:
-How to recognize common forms of election misinformation and disinformation
-What to look for when being in online spaces
-How to document and report concerning content
-How monitoring can help identify emerging narratives and patterns
-How this work connects with broader election protection and response efforts

This session is open to anyone interested in learning more about election misinformation, social media monitoring, and ways to support voter protection work in Texas.

events.title: FMAD October Club Meeting -- Topic: Data Centers
events.description: Join us for our monthly club meeting. At this month's meeting we'll be talking about Data Centers. Simon Mathew, who is an IT Infrastructure & Systems Engineer at Virbac with 10+ years experience in solutions architecture, threat management & vulnerability remediation, will be presenting. North Texas is seeing a rapid wave of data-center development, from Dallas and Fort Worth to Garland, Mesquite, Westlake, Keller, and other suburbs. This presentation asks whether our cities are prepared to handle the real impacts: water use during drought, massive electric demand, noise, diesel generators, tax incentives, limited permanent jobs, and the long-term cost of building infrastructure for private companies. Data centers may bring investment and tax revenue, but cities need to ask harder questions about who benefits, who pays, and what protections residents receive. Before more projects are approved, North Texas needs transparency, enforceable safeguards, and regional coordination. The first half hour (6:30-7pm) is for socializing & snacking. Feel free to bring something snacky to share. The presentation will start promptly at 7pm. Sign up and let us know you're coming.

events.title: Hand Out Flyers Near the South Pearl Street Farmers Market — Vote NO on 83
events.description:
Here's the thing: most Denver voters have never heard of Amendment 83. It's buried deep on a very long ballot, and ballots are already sitting on kitchen tables.

So we're heading to South Pearl on Sunday mornings to talk to people. Grab a coffee, bring a friend, and spend a couple of hours handing out flyers to folks picking up their produce. No experience needed. If you can say hi to a stranger, you can do this.

What it looks like: You'll stand on the sidewalk near the market and offer flyers to people walking by. Most people just need one sentence: "Have you heard about Amendment 83? It could bring back steel-jaw traps Colorado voters banned back in 1996." That's usually enough to get them curious.

Before you come:

Print a stack of flyers at home ([flyer link]). 50 to 100 copies is plenty.
Wear comfy shoes and dress for the weather. Fall mornings on Pearl can be chilly.
Bring a friend if you can. It's way more fun in pairs.

A few ground rules, so everyone has a good time:

Stay on the public sidewalk, not inside the market. The vendors are there to sell, and we're there to talk.
Keep at least 100 feet away from any ballot drop box. It's the law while voting is happening.
Hand flyers to people directly. Never put them in mailboxes (that's a federal no-no).
If someone disagrees, smile, say thanks, and let them go. We're not here to argue, just to make sure people know what they're voting on.

Why it matters: Amendment 83 needs 55% of the vote to pass. We just need to keep it under that. Every person who reads the fine print before they vote gets us closer.

Questions? Reply to your confirmation email, and we'll get back to you.

See you on Pearl!

Learn more at VoteNo83.org

events.title: 🌻Colorado Stands with Ukraine: An Evening with Sunflower Seeds Ukraine
events.description:
🌻 Join us on Zoom for a conversation with guest speaker Chip Heldman of Sunflower Seeds Ukraine, a Boulder-based nonprofit run entirely by volunteers in both the US and Ukraine! Chip will explain why this work matters: Ukraine's military is so large that it can't efficiently supply every soldier with everything they need, so Sunflower Seeds Ukraine works to fill the gap. 🩹 That means medical supplies and equipment like Individual First Aid Kits (IFAKs), 🥽 protective gear such as eye and ear protection, rain gear, and gloves, and 🎒 tactical gear including backpacks, boots, drone detectors, and night vision devices. Beyond the front lines, the group converts ☀️ solar panels into USB chargers, sends 🏕️ kids to summer camp, supports a 🏫 school boiler project, and ships 🎣 fishing nets used to protect roads.

📦 You'll also get a behind-the-scenes look at how aid travels from Colorado to Ukraine. Donations are stored in donated warehouse space in Aurora, where volunteers gather every two months to repack items onto pallets that fill a 40-foot shipping container. 🚛🚢🚂 From there, the container is trucked to a US port, shipped by sea to Poland, sent by train to the Ukrainian border, and trucked to a warehouse in Ukraine. The US team handles fundraising, awareness, donor relations, newsletters, purchasing, and shipping, while the Ukraine team receives and distributes aid based on vetted online orders, sending it to the nearest frontline location. 💪 The impact is real: more than 6,000 solar panels delivered to schools, medical facilities, and frontline areas with little or no electricity, 10,000 IFAKs placed in soldiers' hands, and 10 shipping containers sent in 2026 alone, with over 1,000 requests arriving each month and roughly 500 processed monthly. 💛💙 Come learn how you can help by signing up for the newsletter, volunteering at events, sharing their story with friends and family, and donating!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Black Mountain Democrats Read Book Club
events.description:
Each month we discuss a book agreed upon at the previous meeting. The November pick is "The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State" by Jill Lepore. 

Inspired by Hannah Arendt's "The Origins of Totalitarianism," Lepore offers a critical examination of the modern technological revolution and how it has changed our social and political institutions. One review refers to the book as an inspiring wake-up call though a reviewer in The Guardian finds Lepore's recommendations limited or too facile. Read it and decide for yourself.

Who should attend:  Anyone who wants to read and discuss books of interest with fellow left-leaning readers.

events.description:
**Event Title:** Canvass for Change: Persuasion Canvassing with Hands Off Colorado

**Description:**

Join Hands Off Colorado for a day of voter persuasion canvassing! We'll be knocking doors and having real conversations with voters to build support for our communities, including trans and immigrant neighbors who are directly impacted by the policies on the ballot this year.

This is persuasion canvassing, which means we're not just checking in with supporters. We're talking to voters who are undecided or leaning against us, listening to their concerns, and having genuine conversations that can change minds. No experience necessary. We'll train you on everything you need to know before we head out, including how to have effective, empathetic conversations at the door.

**What to expect:**
- Brief training and script walkthrough at check-in
- Canvassing in pairs or small groups (great for first-timers!)
- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing recommended
- Snacks and water provided
- Bring a charged phone with the MiniVAN App Downloaded

**Why this matters:**
Every conversation we have moves us closer to a Colorado that stands up for all of its communities. Persuasion canvassing is one of the most effective tools we have to shift public opinion and win elections and we need volunteers like you to make it happen.

Sign up below and help us knock doors, change minds, and build the Colorado we want to live in.

events.title: GOTV Power Hour Phone Bank
events.description:
Join Team Hardin for our GOTV phone bank as we connect directly with voters across Columbus ahead of the Nov 3rd General Election.

This is one of the most important ways you can make an impact.
Volunteers will use our phone banking system, Scale to Win, to call voters, share key election information, and turn out the vote for Don Leonard, candidate for Congress (OH-15); Amy Acton, candidate for Governor; and Sherrod Brown, candidate for U.S. Senate. 

Whether you’re new to phone banking or have experience, we’ll make sure you’re fully prepared. Each session includes a brief training, a clear script, and support from our team so you feel confident every step of the way.

What you’ll do:
- Call voters in Columbus using our online dialer (Scale to Win)
- Share key details about the Nov. 3rd General Election and Early Voting - (October)
- Help voters make a plan to cast their ballot
- Identify supporters and strengthen our outreach efforts

What you’ll need:
A phone (cell or computer audio)
A laptop or tablet
A willingness to connect with your community

Why it matters: Elections are decided by the voters we reach. Every call you make helps ensure more people have the information they need to participate—and helps build the path to victory.

Join us, bring a friend, and be part of the team working to deliver leadership that shows up and gets results for Columbus. 
Let’s get to work.

The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. events.title: Yes4EDR Town Hall - Concord
events.description:
Join Common Cause Massachusetts for a Town Hall at the First Parish Church in Concord to discuss what a YES on ballot question #4 (Election Day Registration, or EDR) would mean for Massachusetts! Bring yourself and a few friends to this discussion.

About the Campaign

Election Day Registration (EDR) is a straightforward, secure, and proven reform to increase voter turnout and strengthen our democracy by allowing eligible voters to register to vote and cast a ballot on Election Day.

​To ensure EDR becomes law in Massachusetts, a coalition of nonpartisan, nonprofit groups that advocate for voting rights have formed the Yes 4 Election Day Registration ballot question committee. Members include Common Cause Massachusetts, League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, MassVOTE, Mass Voter Table, and the ACLU of Massachusetts. These groups have been leading the campaign for Election Day Registration in Massachusetts since 2008.

events.description:
What we're doing:
Eye-to-eye conversations are crucial. This weekend marks 30 days before in-person early voting begins in North Carolina: 10/15-31. We're heading out into NC-01 in force to knock on doors, visit Democratic + unaffiliated voters to listen + learn what's really on their minds this year, + to earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again: what was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, + it will come down to one thing: who shows up and has the best conversations at the door.

Thirty days out is a turning point. It's the moment voters start paying closer attention, making their plans, + deciding whether this election is worth their time. We want NC-01 to hear from us first.

We're not just asking for votes. We're listening first to what voters and their families care about, what they're worried about, + what they need from their next Representative. Then we're asking for their support, + reminding every single one of them: early voting runs October 15–31, + Election Day is November 3rd.

Why your help is essential:
Every conversation you have could be the one that moves a voter, a family, a whole household. Campaigns aren't won by ads alone, they're won door by door, by real people willing to show up and talk to voters. That's YOU. A big turnout this weekend sends a message: to voters, and to our whole team, that we're ready for the final stretch.

The ask:
Come knock doors with us this weekend. Use the script as your guide (not your script to recite), share literature, + invite folks to vote early or on Election Day.

No experience necessary: we'll train you, + our team will be right there with you every step of the way.

And a bonus: a walk is good for the spirit, and a real conversation with another human being is good for the soul. Come get both.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Are you ready to elect Emily Gregory? Do you want to show off your cool costume?

Well, come join us as we canvass in our costumes for Emily Gregory in House District 87!

You walk with a buddy, get fully trained, hand out a flyer, use a wonderful app to track your progress, and have fun doing it! It's not about going into deep policy discussions, just being a friendly neighbor to encourage awareness of Emily's platform for the November Midterm General Election.

More about Emily...

Emily Gregory is a mother of three, a military spouse, and a small business owner with a professional background in public health and mental health services. She has dedicated her career to assisting new mothers and families facing economic hardship. After a career in public health, she built her company, FIT4MOM Palm Beach, to create a healthy and supportive community for new and expecting mothers.

Emily and her family chose to make Jupiter their home for its great schools, affordability, and sense of community. However, over the past seven years, she has witnessed the rising cost of living, increasing insurance rates, and threats to the public school system. Motivated by the concerns she hears from other parents and community members, Emily is running for State Representative to bring practical, results-driven leadership to Tallahassee.

Her campaign is focused on building a healthier, more hopeful future for all Floridians.

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
MI 4 the People is hitting the sidewalks to talk to thousands of our neighbors about just how important this election is. Our representative, Bill Huizenga, has consistently voted against our interests. He's supported taking healthcare and food assistance away from people who need it, including children. He hasn't shown up for an in-person town hall since 2018. We deserve someone who isn't going to phone it in.

We are at a critical time in our nation's history. Every day our rights and freedoms are eroded by the Trump administration; and lawmakers like Huizenga do nothing to fight back. We have an incredible opportunity right now to take a stand and fight to keep our democracy alive.

If you've ever talked to a stranger at the grocery store, at the park, or on the street, you can do this. We provide all training and tools, but we aren't doing anything complicated. We're just having real conversations, making real connections, and talking about the kind of country we want for ourselves and generations to come.

We can't do this without you. Can you join us?

events.title: Knock on Doors in Delano | October 16, 17, 18 in CA-22 for Randy Villegas
events.description:
**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 daily stipend** is available to offset your out-of-district travel costs.

 - Friday, October 16 | 12:30 to 4:30 pm

 - Saturday, October 17 | 9:0 am to 12:30 pm or 1:00 to 4:30 pm

 - Sunday, October 18 | 9:0 am to 1:00 pm

New to canvassing? We will train you (and we are lots of fun). Bring a friend. Or two. Be a part of the change we're all looking for. 

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options ... and we have cooling cars if the weather is warm. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

events.title: Battle Creek Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Phone Bank for Talarico: Comparing Approaches
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth GOTV phone bank. Every conversation we have between now and Election Day is aimed at one thing: turning out voters for Talarico. In this phone bank, you will be reaching out to voters to either mobilize them to get out the vote, or to persuade them to support Talarico through our innovative deep listening program that is changing how phone banking works and delivering insights into voters' concerns and needs to vote.

Our goal: to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the Senate. We're building necessary qualitative understanding one phone call at a time, having real conversations with real people. During Ground Truth phone banks, we will talk to as many people as possible.

At this phone bank, we’ll:

- Call persuadable voters -- oftentimes voters who don't always vote like us.

- Have real conversations that LISTEN deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Connect voters to information about James Talarico's platform to answer voters' concerns and energize them to vote.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just come prepared with your phone and laptop or computer!

We recommend using earbuds or speakerphone to free up your hands as well! 

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: FLIP the SENATE: Phone Bank with Ground Truth & TMNYC
events.description:
Join Target Majority NYC for a Ground Truth GOTV phone bank into crucial, must-win Senate races run by Swing Left—and then listen deeply to understand how you can share candidate information that will resonate with each voter to help Democrats win this year. 

This innovative program is changing how phone banking works and delivering insights into voters' concerns and needs to vote. In fact, at this  unique phone bank, we'll be following up with folks who already spoke to a Ground Truth canvasser on their doorstep! We can see the specific notes from that conversation, and pick up right where they left off. 

All the training and materials you need are provided at the start of every shift, so there's no need to be an expert or even know much about Ground Truth yet! Just come prepared with your phone and laptop or computer! We recommend using earbuds or speakerphone to free up your hands as well.

You'll quickly get the hang of it. Then TMNYCers will all join our own breakout room, where we can dial together and share our experiences in the chat.

Our goal: to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We're building necessary qualitative understanding one phone call at a time, having real conversations with real people. During Ground Truth phone banks, we will talk to as many people as possible and focus on listening, making the case for Democratic candidates, and making a plan to vote.

At this phone bank, we’ll:

 - Call persuadable voters -- oftentimes voters who don't always vote like us.

 - Have real conversations that LISTEN deeply to voters’ concerns.

 - Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

 - Connect voters to the Democratic Candidate and their platform to answer voters' concerns and energize them to vote.

Phone bank paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Youth Canvass for Adam Cleveland
events.description:
Join the Young Democrats of Fulton County, the Young Democrats of Georgia Stonewall Caucus, the Young Democrats of Georgia AANHPI Caucus, and Adam Cleveland, candidate for House District 48, on Saturday, October 31 to canvass for our future! We'll kick off at 10:00 AM in the Democratic Party Field Office in Roswell (861 Holcomb Bridge Rd, Suite 207).

This is a youth canvass, but everyone is welcome! It's a great way for young people to meet others and get involved, especially if it's your first time. No experience needed. We'll provide training and supplies and pair first-timers with experienced canvassers. Just bring a charged phone, comfy shoes, and a friend!

Georgia elections are won on the margins, and young people are the margin. The blue wave that flips the House starts at the door. So please join us to let our voices be heard!

events.title: Blue Turn Indivisible Monthly Meeting, feat. Akemi Flynn (IPEN: Immigrant Protection & Empowerment)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
October meeting's guest speaker is **Akemi Flynn, Managing Director of the Immigrant Protection & Empowerment Network (IPEN) at Amigos de Guadalupe**. Akemi has decades of experience in community organizing and coalition-building in Silicon Valley, and is currently working across Santa Clara County to protect and support immigrant communities. You may have already come across Akemi as we've mobilized to support efforts against mass surveillance and ICE Out of Gilroy.

New people are welcome! Let's discuss plans and ideas for action, report on anything new we've learned, and chat with fellow defenders of democracy. Let's deepen our bonds and organize ourselves for strategic action.

With the election almost here, we'll also start talking about **what comes next**. We'll be returning our focus to immigrant protection, including opposing mass detention, and thinking more broadly about how we can support and uplift marginalized communities locally. Akemi will help us think about what's happening right now, what communities need, and where we can make a difference.

**Bring a friend and some food to share — it's potluck!**

If you can't make it to this or any of our monthly meetings, but would like to sign up to stay in touch:  
https://blueturnindivisible.org

events.title: Democracy Hub Canvass with Friendship Baptist

sponsor.name: Milwaukee Innercity Congregations Allied for Hope

events.description:
This isn’t just any election year. Our ability to make decisions for ourselves, our democracy is at risk. In the leadup to the November 2026 election, MICAH’s We All Belong Committee is calling on people of faith to rally neighbors, friends and family to vote – and to vote their values! We All Belong was created to protect democracy, reject white Christian nationalism, and build the Beloved Community. As part of that mission, We All Belong is inviting congregations to join the Democracy Collective.

The Democracy Collective is designed to strengthen congregations’ ability to educate and activate voters while creating deeper relationships, inside and out of the congregation. Central to the Collective are Democracy Hubs: neighborhood canvasses anchored by a MICAH congregation, organized in collaboration with other congregations. Canvassers receive training and food. 

Maybe your congregation is ready to get involved and looking for a good entry point. Maybe you are looking to get more engaged as a person of faith. We're excited to have you.

events.title: Hop on the bus from Corona to knock doors in CA-48 to flip the House!!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to CA-48—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Marni von Wilpert. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Corona around 9:00am and return around 5:00pm. 
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 10:00-4:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Salinas Hwy 101 Bridge Overpass Protest, this Friday, from 4:30 -5:30 pm

location.venue: Hwy 101 overpass behind Mt. Toro High School

events.description:
Join us for our Hwy 101 Bridge Protest on Friday.
We meet on top of the Hwy 101 Overpass Bridge located behind Mount Toro High High School from 4:30 - 5:30 pm
We will already have huge easy-to-read messages to set up facing the highway which will be seen by thousands of cars on highway 101 as well as the cars going over the overpass. Those who attend can wave their hands and cheer on support from cars below and on the street behind us

The Visibility Brigade (VB) is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability*. You participate with this understanding. See VB guidelines below:

VB guidelines and protocal are in this doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/12vigayVE4sCN922zsWbsq4wcKgDKEmNFMFlNWb1F6Yk/edit?usp=sharing

*Minors are required to have a waiver signed by a confirmed (parent or guardian) prior to participation. Copies of form are available at the event or at link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o4xNJUnh6abwHFhNnAzI4C7JUn0H_Ypbpxqj3tgNSlc/edit?usp=sharing

Bring: Yourself (and friends), a windbreaker, and a clear mind as the bridge is narrow and you'll need to be able to have enough balance to stay out from cars rushing past. The wind is generally forceful at this location so be mindful of the fact that larger signs can act like a wind sail and try to blow you into traffic (so smaller signs are safer generally).

Parking: The gravel parking entryway is below the bridge. It is only accessible from the right side from the north flowing traffic on 330 Sherwood Drive, Salinas CA 93906. Just before you enter the parking area you will see the sign that says, "Home of the Toros" and "Be More". Please park on the right-hand shoulder.

Bathrooms: Ensen Community Park 600 Sherwood Drive for bathrooms about 2000 feet away from the event.
events.accessibility_notes: The ramp up to the bridge might be steep for a person with mobility issues

events.title: 10/18/26 WFP LD 37 Canvass for Kelabe & Jaelynn
events.description:
Join us for a canvass with WA Working Families Party. We're knocking doors with our endorsed candidates in Washington's 37th legislative district! The Nov 3rd election is a month away- help us get the word out to our neighbors about these incredible working peoples' champions!

Location: We will be meeting at Columbia Park ( right outside of the Columbia City PCC) at 11am!

Kelabe Tewolde (LD37 - House Seat 1) is a child of refugees who advocates to stop redlining and environmental racism on the Seattle Planning Commission and an educator who mentors and uplifts youth of color with Rainier Scholars, and is challenging a 27-year-incumbent who has voted to increase rents and lower taxes on corporations. Kelabe, in contrast, is by community and for community.

Jaelynn Scott (LD37 - House Seat 2) is a Black trans activist and proud socialist who serves as Executive Director of the Lavender Rights Project, a national black trans feminist advocacy organization advancing justice for gender diverse communities. She has spent years working in community, organizing, responding to crisis calls, helping people find sanctuary, and trying to help folks navigate the confusing, frustrating, broken system of social services.

If it’s your first time, no worries! Each session starts with a brief training & Q&A. Don't be afraid to reach out with questions!

events.title: Banned Book Club - To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee
events.description:
For the remainder of October and throughout November we will be exploring How To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee. I feel it is important to advise that this book may have triggers for some people. If you feel you might not be in an emotional space to handle the topics mentioned, or that this title just isn't for you, please feel free to skip parts or the book in full and stay tuned for December's title.

Content Trigger Warnings for To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee include the following subjects:

• Abuse
• Murder
• N-word
• Racism
• Rape (mentioned)

Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

This month we will finish To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

events.title: Pro-Democracy Task Force
events.description:
Our democracy is in trouble. Our voting rights are under attack. This administration is trying to take us backwards and undermine our civil liberties. 

But we are not powerless. Their agenda can only succeed if we comply or idly stand by. 

With upcoming congressional and state house elections, we have a unique opportunity to stop the coalition of regression from growing their power. 

Elections are one of the main levers of our democracy. We must take action now to keep it that way.

Join us to learn how you can build community power to protect elections in your neck of the woods. 

We will provide a series of trainings to help you understand what we are up against, discuss election protection and what role everyday people can play, develop a county-based strategy and build community with individuals participating in this effort in different parts of the country.

“The arc of the moral universe bends towards justice - but only if we pull it.”
-MLK Jr.

events.title: Camp Verde ALPR Community Discussion & Next Steps
events.description:
The conversation continues — and we need you there.

Join your Camp Verde neighbors for a community discussion about Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology currently being used in our community.

📅 Saturday, November 7
⏰ 9:00 AM
📍 Camp Verde Community Library
130 N. Black Bridge Loop, Camp Verde, AZ

This meeting is an opportunity to come together, share what we’ve learned, ask questions, and talk about what comes next.

We’ll discuss:

🔹 What we know about the ALPR technology being used in Camp Verde
🔹 Questions and concerns from our community
🔹 What we’ve learned so far
🔹 How we can continue educating our neighbors
🔹 What steps we can take to encourage the Town to reconsider this technology
🔹 How YOU can get involved

You don't need to be an expert or have followed this issue from the beginning. If you care about privacy, transparency, and having a voice in decisions that affect our community, you are welcome.

📚 Want to get caught up before the meeting?

Visit: CampVerdePrivacy.org.

There you can learn more about the ALPR technology being used in Camp Verde, read background information and previous meeting materials, find educational resources and literature, and sign our community petition.

Whether you're just learning about this issue or have been involved from the beginning, there's a place for you in this conversation.

Come bring your questions, your ideas, and your voice.

❤️ Together, let's figure out what comes next.

events.title: Conestoga Valley: Election Day Volunteer Crew
events.description:
Conestoga Valley Democrats is looking for volunteers for Election Day poll observers and greeters. 

The poll observer’s role is to watch and report any irregularities, without directly interfering with election workers or voters.

The greeters inform people who come to vote, answer any questions, and hand out the “Voted” stickers. 

Shifts could be: 
 
- all day
- half day (morning)
- half day (afternoon / evening) - peak hours 7-9am;
- peak hours 9am-12pm;
- peak hours 12-2pm; 
- peak hours 2pm-5pm; 
- peak hours 5pm-8pm 

Training will be provided. 

Sign up and we will send additional training information. 

Plan to join for in person training on Wednesday October 24 or Sunday November 1.

events.title: Phone Bank with Scotland Dems
events.description:
Did you know nearly half of eligible voters sit out midterm elections, even though these races decide who controls Congress, state legislatures, school boards, and more? We're changing that, one call at a time!

Join us for a friendly, low-pressure phone bank where we reach out to voters who've skipped past midterms and help them commit to voting this year. No experience needed! We'll provide a simple script, talking points, and a quick training before every shift.

What we're asking callers to do:

*Make warm, respectful calls to identified midterm-skippers in our target area
*Invite people to make a personal pledge to vote
*Help callers find their polling place or request a mail ballot if needed

Why it matters:
Research consistently shows that a friendly personal contact, especially one that invites someone to make a concrete pledge is one of the most effective ways to boost turnout. You don't need to be a political expert. You just need to be willing to have a conversation.

Details:

events.title: Protect the Vote: Inside Poll Observer On-Demand Training
events.description:
### This is the _On-Demand_ training, you can find the _Live on Zoom_ training here: https://mobilize.us/s/lADmOM

# Protect the Vote as a Poll Observer

Every voter deserves the chance to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Inside Poll observers help ensure election laws are followed, identify potential issues, and report concerns so they can be addressed quickly. Most shifts are calm and routine, and you will never be expected to handle situations on your own. We'll provide the training, resources, and support you need to be successful.

### What You'll Learn

- Poll observer basics
- What to expect at the polling place
- Updated guidance for situations observers may encounter this fall
- What to look for and how to document issues
- How to report concerns and get support
- The role poll observers play in protecting voters

### Why It Matters

With critical elections ahead, we need trained volunteers in every corner of North Carolina.

Poll observers serve as our eyes and ears inside polling places, helping ensure election laws are followed and that voters can cast their ballots without unnecessary barriers.

Whether you've done this work before or are brand new, we'll help you get ready.

#### No Prior Experience Required

We'll provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel confident serving as a poll observer.

### After signing up, you'll be directed to the recorded training video and next steps.

#### Important: If you are an **attorney, law graduate, or law student** looking to serve as an **At-Large Legal Poll Observer through the NC Voter Protection Alliance (NCVPA),** please sign up here: https://tinyurl.com/NC26LegalPollObserver

events.title: Reach Your Friends. Help Pat Win.
events.description:
The most powerful political conversation isn’t always with a campaign volunteer or an advertisement, it’s with someone you already know and trust.

That’s why Team Halpin is launching Reach, a simple tool that lets you connect with friends, family, neighbors and coworkers who live in the district and personally encourage them to vote.

With Election Day just weeks away, we need supporters like you helping us have thousands of real, personal conversations about what’s at stake in this election.

Here’s how it works:
1. Sign up here on Mobilize.
2. You’ll receive a link that takes you directly into the Reach App
3. Reach will help you identify people you know who may live in the district.
4. You can then send them information about the campaign, use content and videos for social posts. 
5. Follow up and make sure they have a plan to vote.

You don’t need a script. You don’t need campaign experience. And you can do it from anywhere.

Even reaching out to 5 or 10 people you know can make a difference.

This is one of the most important midterm elections of our lifetimes. The decisions Washington makes over the next two years will affect the cost of living, healthcare, housing, Social Security and Medicare, public safety, our environment, and the future of our democracy.

The best messenger to someone you know is YOU.

Sign up, open Reach, and start a conversation today.

Let’s win this one conversation at a time.

events.description:
Daily from 12:15-12:30pm 
US Capitol East Front Plaza

RAIN OR SHINE, GRAB AN UMBRELLA AND BE SEEN.

When you arrive at the East Front Plaza of the U.S. Capitol, simply walk around and take in the scene. Do not gather in a static group, sit down, or set your umbrella on the ground; keep moving naturally along the wide public plaza perimeter maintaining a respectful physical buffer from other participants.

You are free to carry any umbrella, whether plain or bearing a message. Remain silent and avoid speeches, chanting, or loud noise. 

Circulate the Front East Plaza perimeter at your own pace until about 12:30pm, then simply turn and disperse as an individual, leaving the grounds just as quietly and seamlessly as you arrived.

Don't worry if only a few people show up, after all you are just out for a stroll. Keep coming back!

Umbrella Walk 4 Change

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Hop on the bus from NYC to knock doors in NY-17 to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to NY-17—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Cait Conley. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Hudson Yards at 9:30am and return around 6:30pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

events.description:
Are you ready to elect Emily Gregory? Do you want to show off your cool costume? 

Well, come join us as we canvass in our costumes for Emily Gregory in House District 87!

You walk with a buddy, get fully trained, hand out a flyer, use a wonderful app to track your progress, and have fun doing it! It's not about going into deep policy discussions, just being a friendly neighbor to encourage awareness of Emily's platform for the November Midterm General Election.

More about Emily...

Emily Gregory is a mother of three, a military spouse, and a small business owner with a professional background in public health and mental health services. She has dedicated her career to assisting new mothers and families facing economic hardship. After a career in public health, she built her company, FIT4MOM Palm Beach, to create a healthy and supportive community for new and expecting mothers.

Emily and her family chose to make Jupiter their home for its great schools, affordability, and sense of community. However, over the past seven years, she has witnessed the rising cost of living, increasing insurance rates, and threats to the public school system. Motivated by the concerns she hears from other parents and community members, Emily is running for State Representative to bring practical, results-driven leadership to Tallahassee.

Her campaign is focused on building a healthier, more hopeful future for all Floridians.

events.description:
Join Team Bernie and canvass for Abdul El-Sayed at the Birmingham Farmers Market from 10 AM- 11 AM. 

Organize and Win Michigan is our program to elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state.

Senator Sanders says it best:

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few.

Right now, our movement is winning. Why?

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges.

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement.

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up.

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us.

Let’s get to work.

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

Early Vote Walk + Rally

Your voice matters. Your vote matters. And your vote is your superpower.

Join The Resistance Alliance — Hawthorne, NJ as we kick off early voting with a joyful, nonpartisan Early Vote Walk + Rally celebrating one of our most fundamental rights as citizens: the right to make our voices heard at the ballot box.

This event has two parts — and everyone is welcome to participate.

PART ONE: WALK TO VOTE

We’ll gather at 11:00 AM in Hawthorne and make our way together toward the early-voting location.

If you are a registered Passaic County voter, come vote early with us! We’ll walk together in a celebratory show of civic participation before transitioning from rally participants to voters as we approach the voting location.

CHOOSE YOUR ROUTE

We’ll have two walking options so people can participate at the level that feels right for them:

💎 Diamond Trail — the longer walk for those who want the full route.

🐰 Bunny Trail — a shorter, easier option for anyone who prefers less walking or needs a more accessible route.

Both groups will come together as we make our way toward early voting.

IMPORTANT FOR VOTERS

Our walk and rally are pro-democracy and nonpartisan. Signs should focus on voting, democracy, civic participation, and using your voice — not candidates or political parties.

Before we reach the voting location, we will have a designated person collecting rally signs so anyone entering to vote can do so without signs or political materials. Signs can be retrieved afterward.

PART TWO: STAY AND RALLY

Not a Passaic County voter? Come anyway!

This event is open to supporters from throughout New Jersey. Those who cannot vote at the Hawthorne early-voting location are welcome to join the walk and/or stay for the rally as we encourage others to exercise their rights, participate in our democracy, and make their voices heard.

Some ideas:

USE YOUR SUPERPOWER — VOTE!

events.description:
November 9th 2026 we will be conducting our Virtual Monthly Education Justice and Childcare Meeting, set aside from our Roc Chapter meeting, and will be presenting New Updates from our Partner Organization "The Alliance for Quality Education(AQE)." 

We will be discussing the Wins Citizen Action and AQE have secured for 2026, what our projections moving forward will be, and our upcoming Advocacy Days at the State Capitol 2027.

We’re calling on parents, students, educators, and all who care about our young people to come together for an important conversation. Rochester is in a real crisis when it comes to education — and it’s going to take all of us to turn things around.

This meeting is about awareness, but also about healing. We’ll be sharing real tools to support mental well-being and build healthier environments for our youth, for parents, and for the folks working in our schools every day.

We know the impact poverty has had on our community — but we also know the strength we carry. Together, we can rise above the challenges and help our children thrive.

events.title: Florida NOW Film Screening: Reimagining Safety
events.description:
Join us as we close out the series with a screening of Reimagining Safety, a documentary filmed in the aftermath of the 2020 murder of George Floyd and the worldwide protests that followed. The film brings together 10 experts, including abolitionists, social workers, scholars, a former LAPD detective, and a former district attorney, to examine how policing and incarceration shape our ideas about safety.

The film revisits the 2020 protests and the growing calls to defund and abolish the police, while exploring the history and ongoing impact of police violence, racism, mass incarceration, mental health crises, housing insecurity, and the criminalization of poverty. It also highlights restorative justice, violence prevention, community responders, and other approaches that seek to build safety through care, accountability, and community rather than punishment and isolation.

Stay after the screening for our final community reflection and conversation in this series.

events.title: Michigan Voter Registration Calls with Rust Belt Rising
events.description:
Join Rust Belt Rising to help make sure that everyone is able to vote in this year's General Election!

Rust Belt Rising's innovative voter registration programs helped thousands of Great Lakes state residents register the last three cycles and will do so again this year.

Here's how it works: RBR partners at Civitech find targets of people who would likely vote our way but are unregistered at their current address as they compare commercial mail lists and voter files. They will mail these targets a pre-filled voter registration form with a motivational flyer and postage to their clerk. That's where we come in. In addition to our texting them, we need volunteers to call these targets to encourage them to complete the easy process of registering.

We would love for you to be part of a team that makes these calls to Michigan voters as part of our virtual voter registration chase! 

We'll teach you everything you know over Zoom and get you calling to remind voters to register because there is an election coming up!

events.title: Pinellas County - Día de los Muertos Day of Action

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

Join us as we mark one year of gathering every Sunday outside the Pinellas Justice Center as part of the broader national call to action through Disappeared in America. 

For a full year, people of faith and community members have gathered weekly to bear witness and call for an end to detention without due process, justice for immigrants, an end to 287(g) agreements, and more. 

This anniversary vigil will include an ofrenda, music, and a welcome back to the faith leaders who have led vigils throughout the past year. We’ll take time to look back at what we have built together — reflecting on the goals we set, the work we have done, and the successes and lessons of this past year — and to look ahead to the work still to come.

As we join this national call to action, we’ll come together in movement and community, renewing our commitment to the work ahead. Co-sponsored by the LWV of the St. Petersburg area, Interfaith Alliance of Florida, and Indivisible chapters across Pinellas County, Florida.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: 24th Annual ReLeafing Day at Glen Leven Farm!
events.description:
Join the Nashville Tree Foundation for the 24th Annual ReLeafing Day!

Held each year on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, ReLeafing Day is our signature community tree-planting event. Following the devastating 1998 tornadoes, our founders launched this initiative as a major restoration effort - raising $1,000,000 in six months and planting over 6,000 trees across the city. Today, that legacy continues as we focus on planting new trees in Nashville every November.

This year, we invite you to dig deep and plant trees at the beautiful Glen Leven Farm on Saturday, November 21st. We are proud to be supported by Root Nashville, helping drive the citywide goal of planting 500,000 trees by 2050, and funded by the Cumberland River Compact.

Whether you are an experienced tree planter or a first-time volunteer, this is the perfect way to connect with nature, meet fellow tree lovers, and actively grow our urban forest!

What to Expect: 
We will start the morning with a brief introduction and an overview of the day's goals. Our team will provide a step-by-step tree planting demonstration and review essential safety guidelines so you feel completely confident. Then, we'll plant our trees!

events.title: Youth Action for Trans Rights
events.description:
Join Amnesty International USA and New Era Action Fund in a day of youth action to turn out the vote this election. 

We will educate voters about two ballot measures that sound simple but aren't. Propositions 134 and 135 are being sold as measures about fairness and safety — but the fine print tells a different story, and voters deserve to know it before they vote.

Propositions 134 is so vague that it could subject any kid, in any sport, from kindergarten through college, to invasive verification just to prove they belong on the field. Propositions 135 hands medical decisions that belong to families and doctors over to politicians — and could block care for kids who aren't even transgender, including teens fighting cancer.

That's where you come in. Join Families Not Politics Coalition for a community canvass and help us have real conversations with Colorado voters about what these measures actually do. Our research is clear: when voters hear the full picture, they move — but it takes volunteers like you, at the doors, making the case.

No experience needed. We'll kick things off with training and a team briefing before heading out together. You'll leave with everything you need to have a confident, meaningful conversation. Wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and come ready to talk with your neighbors. Our hosts will have breakfast and lunch for all volunteers to ensure everyone is well fed before and after their shift.

Every conversation moves a voter. Every voter we move gets us closer to defeating these measures in November. We hope you'll join us.

events.title: A District That Works for Children, Youth, and Families
events.description:
**What would it take to build a District that truly works for all children, youth, and families?**

That’s what we will be asking at our end-of-year summit on **Thursday, December 3, from 6:30-8:00 pm.** At DC Action, we’re bringing together the DC Out-of-School Time Coalition, Under 3 DC, and the Youth Economic Justice Coalition to lead a bold conversation with the mayor-elect and elected leaders from across the District, and we want you to join us. 

This is a critical moment for the District, with a new mayor for the first time in a dozen years, major turnover on the council, and continued uncertainty about the economy. The budget and policy decisions made over the coming months, and the plans carried out in the next few years, will impact the District for generations to come. 

It’s vital that the needs of Black and brown children, youth, and families be at the center of these discussions. That’s why this event will be led by young people, parents, and direct service providers from the three coalitions, who will share their experiences and what they want to see from our elected leaders, from making child care more affordable, to expanding out-of-school time programs, and committing to ending youth homelessness.


**Doors open at 5:30pm.**

events.title: Mondays @ McCormick's - - 2000 Market St. Every Monday @ noon - Demand Dave McCormick meet with us!
events.description:
We call on Dave McCormick to say no to Trump and to say yes to reason & compassion.

We rally each week at NOON
Outside Dave’s Office, 
2000 Market St. Phila PA 19103

Resistance is NOT futile - it is essential. 

We launched "Monday's at McCormick's" after his election when he refused to meet with us.

We gather each Monday at noon - rain or shine - to assemble peaceably - as is our constitutional right - outside Senator McCormick's Philadelphia office until Senator McCormick agrees to meet with us and support our demands: (These will change as conditions develop)

 1 - Stop voting for legislation inspired by Trump's project 2025 agenda - a plan to slash Medicaid, gut school lunch programs, push back on environmental protections in service of big oil and the extration industries, and shut down nursing homes while handing more power to billionaires like Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and others. 

2- Roll back Trump's mean spirited and Unconstitutional funding pauses. Shutting down USAID is already killing people in need all over the World. Cuts to programs here in the US could do the same. Funding for these programs are up to the Congress and the US people to decide, not Trump! 

3 - Stop the Administration's wars of choice around the world.

4 - Re-engage with nuclear arms treaty regimes to reduce and eventually eliminate Nuclear weapons and ALL weapons of mass destruction

That's just for starters. Overall we want Senator McCormick to represent us all, not just his rich friends. We want Senator McCormick to DO HIS JOB!

The stakes could not be higher. The administration is pushing an authoritarian agenda that threatens our democracy, our rights, and the well-being of millions here at home and around the planet. 

We have the power to resist—and we must use every tool at our disposal to stop them.

events.title: Listening at the Door - Reflective Listening Earns Trust and Votes
events.description:
Join John Sabin and Ken Stanley for a hands-on Zoom session on reflective listening, the skill behind the best conversations at the door. As canvassing shifts from talking to listening, this is one of the most useful skills a canvasser can build, and you can make real progress in about an hour.

We'll start with quick introductions, then practice in a supportive, low-pressure setting, taking turns sharing and reflecting back what we hear. We'll close with a conversation about how we can all keep growing as canvassers. This workshop is designed for experienced canvassers. 

John Sabin is an expert in motivational interviewing, the listening-centered approach Elizabeth Chur draws on in The Joy of Talking Politics to Strangers, and he brings years of experience from his work with Citizens' Climate Lobby. Ken Stanley has been knocking doors since his first campaign at 16 in 1974, trained with Marshall Ganz, and has had well over a thousand conversations at the door, many recorded and reviewed with Swing Left's Script Iteration Team.

If you haven't heard of it, Swing Left is a national network that helps people find high-impact ways to support Democratic candidates. We focus on the most flippable races as an important step toward the progressive change needed to create a more inclusive and equitable government and society.

events.title: Adopt A District Office Hours
events.description:
Join our upcoming office hours to learn more about MoveOn's innovative Adopt A District Program, which allows you to contact the voters who are most critical to winning in our priority districts and flipping the House blue this year. 

You'll be able to contact MoveOn members who skipped the 2024 election, sharing details about our endorsed candidates and how to vote, and motivating them to turn out via postcard, call, text, or even a door knock if you live in the district. 

The best part? You can do it all on your own time when it's most convenient for you!

Already signed up for Adopt A District, but hit a road block? Office Hours are a space where you can come to troubleshoot MiniVAN, workshop your spiel on early voting, or even roleplay knocking on your first door! Our experienced team of organizers are on hand to make sure you feel prepared and have everything you need to get started.

Can't make an upcoming office hour? Email us at MemberSupport@MoveOn.org, and we'll make sure we find a time to connect with you!

events.title: Team Wiener GOTV Volunteer Training

sponsor.name: Team Wiener: Supporting Scott Wiener for Congress

events.description:
Join Team Wiener for our GOTV Volunteer Training and get prepared to help us reach voters during the final weeks before Election Day!

Whether you’re a brand-new volunteer or have been with us throughout the campaign, this training will give you the tools and confidence you need to have effective conversations with voters and take action during GOTV.

We’ll cover Team Wiener messaging, canvassing and door knocking, talking with voters at community events and farmers markets, identifying and accurately recording Scott supporters, making a strong voting-plan ask, and how you can host or help spread the word about a Ballot Party.

Our goal is simple: have real conversations, identify support, accurately record what we learn, and help supporters make a plan to vote. Team_Wiener_Volunteer_Canvassin…

You’ll also learn about Ballot Parties—small gatherings with friends, family, neighbors, or coworkers designed to make completing your ballot and making a return plan social and easy. Team Wiener. GOTV.Ballot Partie…

No prior campaign experience is required. We’ll walk through everything you need to know and leave time for questions.

Training offered weekly:
Tuesdays — Virtual
Wednesdays — In Person

Come ready to learn, ask questions, and get prepared to help Team Wiener GOTV through Election Day!

events.title: Team Krueger/Aronson Volunteer Orientation
events.description:
Join us online for a 45-minute Volunteer Orientation to get out the vote with Team Krueger & Aronson!

Find out how you can make a difference on Manhattan's East Side. We'll walk you through volunteer roles and what to expect: talking with neighbors, helping at community events and candidate meet-and-greets, and building visibility at polling sites during early voting and on Election Day.

Why team up? State Senator Liz Krueger (Senate District 28) and Vanessa Aronson, candidate for State Assembly District 73, represent overlapping East Side communities and share a commitment to tackling the affordability crisis, expanding health care access, combating hate crimes, strengthening climate protections, and defending our democracy.

Whether you're new to volunteering or have helped before, we'd be glad to have you. Bring your energy, and we'll help you put it into action!

We’re meeting up on the west side of 7th Ave between Lynnwood and Willetta.  

Please bring your short, apolitical posters that persuade people to vote early (rather than talk of candidates or parties).  Simple messages to vote early is powerful too!

Bring a chair if it’s best for you.
Grab your water bottle and meet us here.  The energy will be really high just days from Election Day!

There’s plenty of street parking in the neighborhood.


A core principle behind all Desert Democracy events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.description:
## Si se puede! Yes we can!

### Door Knocking in Waukegan and North Chicago

Support Get Out the Vote efforts through our partner **Mano a Mano** with their important **residential canvassing work.** Mano a Mano is working tirelessly over the next few weeks to **"Get Out The Vote"** to our **disenfranchised neighbors in Waukegan and North Chicago.** We encourage folks to sign up directly with Mano a Mano for phone banking and door knocking any time between now and Midterms here at their Sign-Up Site: www.bit.ly/LakeCountyVotes 

*These "Democracy in Action" efforts are sponsored by Mano a Mano, ICIRR, and Hispanic Federation.*

We will be collecting a group of our own **NE Lake County Indivisible volunteers** for **Saturday October 24**. Sign up for the morning or the afternoon or BOTH! :)

**Training and supplies will be provided.** Participants are encouraged to **dress for the weather and wear comfortable shoes.** 

We will be targeting households where individuals are registered to vote but rarely show up at the polls, reaching our most disenfranchised neighbors. Canvassers will ask the simple question, "How do you think things are going right now?" in sharing the nonpartisan encouragement to "Get Out the Vote!"

*Registration can be done here with our Mobilize to receive reminders and updates, or you may register directly with Mano a Mano at their site www.bit.ly/LakeCountyVotes .*

events.title: Indivisible Greater Grand Rapids Community Meeting with "Ask a Muslim" Discussion
events.description:
We are all seeing a lot of misinformation and disinformation about Islam on social media and in election campaign materials. In a time when we should be coming together as a community, we are seeing efforts to further divide us. At our October 26 community meeting, we are honored to have a panel discussion and Q&A with several Muslim women who will provide a brief Islam 101 presentation followed by a frank discussion of myths about Islam. We will also have an "Ask a Muslim" Q&A for community members to become further educated about Islam and how Muslims practice their faith. This session will prepare us all to be allies to the Muslim community by providing us with tips and tricks for answering questions about Islam in an appropriate way.
Social from 6:30 pm to 7:00pm. Discussion will start at 7:00pm. Please bring a snack to share!

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. We partner with local organizations at every stop.

Sikh American Legal Defense and Education Fund (SALDEF), in partnership with Interfaith Alliance, is hosting an interfaith community gathering and get out the vote rally at Sikh Dharamsal of San Antonio. Come hear from national and local faith leaders as we stand together in solidarity for democracy and civic participation. 

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

All The Vote is Sacred events are free, nonpartisan, and open to everyone. People of all faiths and no faith are welcome.

events.title: Rally: Keep Data Centers Out of New York!
events.description:
**Join us for a massive rally outside Governor Hochul's most important speech of the year to send her a clear, powerful message: Keep Data Centers Out of New York!**

Together, we won a moratorium on massive AI data centers in New York. Now, it's on all of us to keep them out for good. We've crisscrossed the state over the last few months and it's clear that New Yorkers everywhere oppose building these massive, polluting facilities in their communities. 

That's why we must bring the movement straight to Hochul's doorstep now. Together, we'll rally at the capitol to kick off the new year and show Governor Hochul and the Legislature that New Yorkers won't accept data centers in our state.

We can win this fight, but it's going to take a massive show of people power given the almost limitless budget on the other side.

*Sign up today to reserve your spot — transportation options from all corners of the state coming shortly.*

events.title: New York, NY: GasFreeNYC Training
events.description:
**We're in a climate crisis and our bills are too damn high! We need a GasFreeNYC!**

Buildings are New York City's largest source of greenhouse gas, in large part due to fossil fuel use. While Local Law 97 is successfully reducing pollution from large buildings, it does not cover the City's thousands of 1- and 2-family homes. 

The GasFreeNYC campaign is the next essential phase to moving off fossil fuels: expanding public funding and passing requirements to help homeowners get rid of their dirty old boilers and move on to clean-energy heat pumps. 

At the meeting, we'll discuss what we've won so far, what's next, and how you can be involved in winning a GasFreeNYC!

events.title: Carpool Canvass from Boston to Maine!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with Ground Truth—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Maine—a must-win Swing State—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Troy Jackson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

Knock More Doors: We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.

Deep Listening: We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built.

Capture Insights: You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

What to expect:

The Trip: For this weekend (10/11), Boston-based organizer Isabelle will pick up volunteers from the Medford/Somerville/Cambridge area between 9:00-10:00 am. Pickup and carpool captain details TBD following this weekend; option to carpool with friends from your own town to meet Isabelle there is always there!

Canvassing: We'll be knocking on doors in from roughly 12:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.

Preparation: You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your carpool captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus!

—

Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read Swing Left's waiver and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will.

Paid for by Swing Left, swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

events.description:
