We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.title: Lee County School Board Meeting
events.description:
Join FSPS-Lee at the Lee County School Board Meeting

Join the Families for Strong Public Schools – Lee Chapter as we show up, stay informed, and engage with the decisions impacting Lee County students, educators, families, and public schools.

The School Board of Lee County sets the policies and rules that govern the administration of the District. The Board operates according to Florida law and Florida Department of Education regulations, and it sets policy when members meet in official session.

That makes School Board meetings an important place for our community to be present and engaged.

Whether you are a parent, educator, student, or community member, we invite you to join FSPS-Lee to:

📚 Stay informed about decisions affecting Lee County public schools
📣 Make your voice heard on issues that matter to students and families
🤝 Connect with other public education advocates in Lee County
🏫 Support strong public schools and help build a stronger local network of advocates

You do not need to be an expert or have experience speaking at School Board meetings to participate. Showing up matters.

Together, we can make sure families and community members have a voice in the decisions shaping our public schools.

Our schools. Our community. Our voice.

💙 Join FSPS-Lee and show up for Lee County public schools!

events.title: Lee County School Board Workshop
events.description:
Join FSPS-Lee at the Lee County School Board Workshop

Join Families for Strong Public Schools – Lee Chapter as we attend the Lee County School Board Workshop to stay informed and engaged in the conversations shaping our public schools.

What is a School Board Workshop?

A workshop is different from a regular School Board meeting. Regular meetings are where the Board takes formal action and votes on agenda items. Workshops are primarily working sessions where Board members receive information, ask questions, discuss issues in greater detail, and explore potential policies or decisions before they may come back for formal action.

That makes workshops an important part of the public decision-making process.

By the time an issue reaches a final vote, Board members may have already spent significant time discussing it during workshops. Attending or tuning in gives families and community members an opportunity to understand what is being considered earlier in the process—not just when it is time for a vote.

Why Tune In or Attend?

📚 Get informed early about issues and proposals that could affect Lee County public schools.

👀 See the process in action and hear the questions, concerns, and priorities Board members raise as they consider an issue.

📝 Be better prepared to advocate when an issue moves forward for future discussion or action.

🤝 Stay connected with FSPS-Lee and other community members working to support strong public schools.

You don't need to be an education policy expert to participate. You can simply attend, listen, learn, and become more familiar with how decisions affecting our schools are made.

Strong community engagement doesn't begin when the Board takes a vote. It begins by paying attention throughout the process.

Our schools. Our community. Our voice. 💙

This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

Join us on October 24 as we call out the inhumanity, immorality and illegality of ICE actions and detention centers.

Meet at the Hertford County Courthouse, which is directly across from the Rivers/Winton ICE detention center. We will gather there and spread out along the road by the detention center. Bring your signs! We will also livestream the event; please register for information on how to connect.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Co-sponsors include: The Cultivator, Stop Detention Centers North Carolina, Democracy Out Loud, The Workers Circle, NC Council of Churches, Durham Congregations in Action, Fuerza Triad NC, NC Stop Torture Now.

events.title: Hop on the bus from NYC to knock doors in PA-01 to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to PA-01 —a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Bob Harvie. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Hudson Yards at 9:30am and return around 6:30pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

events.title: [Oldenburg, IN] Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: John Lewis: Good Trouble, Film Screening & Conversation
events.description:
John Lewis: Congressman, Activist and Civil Rights Icon. 
Sometimes change calls for a little trouble.

Indivisible Fremont CA and the League of Women Voters, presents a Free Screening of -

John Lewis: Good Trouble, as part of the film and community conversation series "Our Empowered Community Empowers Our Democracy." 

The film will be shown in the Niles Discovery Church's Sanctuary Theater. Afterward, guests are invited to the Fellowship Hall for refreshments and a community conversation about the film and what it means for protecting democracy at home.

"Protecting and securing our elections starts in the heart of every voter," said Lauren Teixeira, Co-Lead, Indivisible Fremont CA. Please join us on Saturday, October 24th, at 1 pm.

Our Empowered Community project will utilize documentary films to spark shared understanding and inspire dialogue as civic education—educating viewers while building connected, engaged communities. Focused post-screening conversations deepen this impact further, turning passive viewing into active reflection—transforming individual awareness into collective commitment and sustained democratic participation. 

IFCA is dedicated to promoting a welcoming and inclusive community, advocating for democracy and justice, empowering individuals to create positive change. To join our mailing list:  please visit, indivisible-fremont.org/join

events.title: Last Chance phone bank to help FLIP the House BLUE
events.description:
Join us in the FINAL DAYS of the election season as we call target voters in priority California Congressional districts to Take Back the House!

We are EXHAUSTING our lists of Democratic voters in districts 13, 45, and 48 to make sure we get everyone to follow through on their plan to vote in this very important midterm.  Winning in these California districts is critical to the plan to gain the House majority and turn Trump into a lame duck!

On Sunday evening (5:30-7:30 p.m.), we're calling voters in districts 45 and 48 for, respectively, Congressman Derek Tran and candidate Marni von Wilpert.

On Monday evening (5:30-7:30 p.m.), we're calling voters in districts 13 and 45 for, respectively, Congressmen Adam Gray and Derek Tran. 

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient so you'll need a computer, laptop or tablet and internet access to make the calls.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

This event is hosted by the Westside Democratic Headquarters. Partners include the campaigns for Marni von Wilpert, Derek Tran, Randy Villegas, and Adam Gray.  Additional partners include the California Democratic Party, the Los Angeles County Democratic Party, and Making Waves for Democracy.

events.title: Knock doors for Randy Villegas, CD22 | October 16, 17, 18 in Delano!
events.description:
**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's get out the vote to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 daily stipend** is available to offset your out-of-district travel costs.

 - Friday, October 16 | 12:30 pm to 4:30 pm

 - Saturday, October 17 | 9:00 am to 12:30 noon and 1:00 pm to 4:30 pm 

 - Sunday, October 18 | 9:00 am to 1:00 pm

New to canvassing?  We will train you (and we are lots of fun).  Bring a friend.  Or two.  Be a part of the change we're all looking for.

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options ... and we have cooling cars if the weather is warm. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.  Alternate start times can be accommodated as needed.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: Vote Forward x LCV Letter Writing Event with Executive Director Yasmin Radjy
events.description:
Join Vote Forward and League of Conservation Voters for our final letter writing party before the mail deadline, with special guest Yasmin Radjy, Vote Forward's Executive Director!

October 24 is the final day to send letters, and this is our last chance to write together before letters go out. It's a time to celebrate everything this community has accomplished this cycle, and to rally for one final push to the finish line.

Vote Forward partners with volunteers to take evidence-driven, high-impact actions to strengthen our democracy by building trust in government and increasing voter participation. Everything we do is grounded in evidence: we rigorously test our tactics, learn from the results, and evolve. Yasmin will share insights about the work we've done together this year, how we'll measure our impact, and the road to the finish line.

The most common question we receive at Vote Forward is: "what should I write?" Vote Forward staff will be on hand to help you craft an effective, personal message to voters. Whether you're writing your very first letter or your hundredth, there's still time to make a difference, and this event is for you!

RSVP today, and we'll let you know how to join. Bring your friends and family, too. The more letters we get in the mail before the 24th, the bigger our impact!

Never written with Vote Forward before? No problem! Visit [votefwd.org/instructions](https://votefwd.org/instructions) for all the information you need, and sign up for an account at [votefwd.org](https://go.votefwd.org).

events.title: Knock Doors: Halifax County
events.description:
What we're doing:
Eye-to-eye conversations are crucial. We're working hard before in-person early voting begins on 10/15 and heading out into NC-01 in force to knock on doors, listen to what's really on voters minds this year, and to earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again: what was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, and it will come down to one thing: who shows up and has the best conversations at the door.

This moment is a turning point. It's the moment voters start paying closer attention, making their plans, and deciding whether this election is worth their time. We want NC-01 to hear from us first.

events.description:
**On location in North Bend, Washington, hosted by Snoqualmie Valley Indivisible**

Bonus activity: After the training, SVI members will walk over to North Bend Way and Bendigo to do some get out the vote sign-waving!

## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour* basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

The course runs 1 hour. Please allow yourself a total of 90 minutes for the class + Q&A

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

events.title: YCAT Riders & Supporters: Make Your Voice Heard

location.venue: Yuma County Department of Development Services

events.description:
Your Story Matters. Now Let’s Take Action.

At the last YCAT board meeting, community members and students came out to share their experiences and speak about why public transportation matters in Yuma County. Board members heard those stories, and they want to continue hearing directly from the people who use and depend on YCAT.

Now, we need more community members to show up and testify.

YCAT connects people to work, school, medical appointments, groceries, and other essential destinations. Whether you ride YCAT regularly, have experienced challenges with public transportation, or have seen how these services impact your family or community, your story matters.

These monthly board meetings are an opportunity to make our voices heard, share what is working, identify what needs to improve, and help decision-makers understand the real impact of their decisions on our community.

You don’t need to be an experienced public speaker. We’ll provide information and support to help you prepare your testimony and feel confident speaking up.

📅 Join the next meeting: October 26 at 1:30 PM 📍 Yuma County Department of Development Services

Come share your story. Come listen to your neighbors. Come help shape the future of YCAT.

The board is listening. Let’s make sure they keep hearing from us.

events.title: Meet the Candidates for Multnomah County Commissioner, District 2
events.description:
Candidate Forum for the Multnomah County District 2 position (serving N/NE Portland) hosted by Portland District 2 Neighbors Indivisible and the Multnomah County Democrats. 

Albina Library, October 18, 1-2:30 pm. Doors open at 12:30pm.

The 5-member Multnomah County Commission controls a $4 Billion budget that funds a sprawling system of essential services, including Public Health, Housing & Homeless Services, libraries, Preschool for All, and Public Safety (Sheriff's Office, District Attorney, County jails, and County courts). 

Hear directly from all seven candidates and leave ready to rank your choices with confidence.

Getting there: TriMet bus lines 4, 6, and 44 all serve the library. The Rose Quarter and Oregon Convention Center MAX stations are each just under a mile's walk away. Sunday schedules can differ from weekdays, so plan your route with the TriMet Trip Planner (enter 205 NE Russell St as your destination). Limited parking on site.

events.title: Day of Service: Winter Warmth in Yuma ❄️
events.description:
Join us for a special Day of Service as we come together to help our neighbors stay a little warmer this winter! ❄️❤️

📅 Thursday, November 19
⏰ 5:00 PM
📍 Location: TBD

This November, we’re collecting donations to create winter care bags for people experiencing homelessness and others in our community who may need a little extra warmth and comfort during the colder months.

You can help by donating items such as:
🧦 New socks
🧣 Scarves
🧢 Hats/beanies
💧 Bottled water
🥨 Individually packaged snacks
🧤 Gloves
🧼 Small personal care items
💌 Notes of encouragement
…and anything else you think would be helpful to include in a winter care bag!

Donations will be used to fill drawstring bags with practical items and a little reminder that our community cares.

You don’t have to bring a lot to make a difference. Whether you donate one pair of socks, a few snacks, a warm hat, or several items, every contribution can help someone feel seen, supported, and cared for this winter.

Come join us, bring what you can, and help us spread a little warmth throughout our community! ❤️

Together, we can turn small acts of kindness into something that makes a big difference.

events.description:
Knowledge is Power is an inclusive and accessible group of progressive learners who are working to educate ourselves about the issues facing us today. From Central Ohio politics to climate change, we are arming ourselves with knowledge to actively work to better our world. More importantly, we are building community and supporting each other in these challenging times!

YOU ARE INVITED TO JOIN US! We meet monthly in Central Ohio to discuss a topic chosen by the group members. We offer multiple ways to access materials for each topic, from books and articles to podcasts and documentaries– because everyone learns best in different ways!

This topic came straight from suggestions by several group members, and it’s a hot one! For years, Gil Duran has been doing the heavy lifting of decoding and sifting through the flood of Silicon Valley weirdness. In his new book, The Nerd Reich, he pulls it all together and shines a bright light on it. Trust me, it’s even stranger than you think!  We will be reading excerpts from his recently published book, The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, as well as listening to an interview with him on the "Why Is This Happening?" podcast. The links are below.

P.S. - I am building the plane while flying it, so please bear with me.  If you have issues/suggestions/feedback, feel free to drop me an email at anaunderman@gmail.com

BOOK: The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, by Gil Duran (August 18, 2026).

events.title: White Christian Nationalism: How did we get here? What can we do about it?
events.description:
Pastor Jonathan D. Riedel will lead a discussion on the origins and goals of Christian Nationalism on Saturday, October 24 at Newaygo Congregational United Church of Christ, 432 Quarterline St, Newaygo, 4937. 

The doors open at 10am for refreshments and networking, with the program from 10:30 – 11:30am. This is part 2 of Pastor Jon’s research and discussion. All religious faiths and the public at large are welcome.

The Baptist Joint Committee for Religious Liberty state that Christian Nationalism “is a political ideology that is inherently incompatible with religious freedom because it seeks to merge Christian and American identities, distorting both the Christian faith and America’s constitutional democracy. Christian nationalism is not simply about belief. It is a political project. And that distinction matters.” (https://bjconline.org/christiannationalism/).

According to Copilot Search, White Christian nationalism is a specific ideology that combines Christian beliefs with a sense of racial identity, asserting that the United States was founded as a Christian nation and should remain so, often at the expense of non-white and non-Christian populations.

“Many Christian Churches in America have been struggling with an often silent but powerful force that has affected how they govern themselves and how they interact with the world around them,” states Pastor Jon. “Many churches have been complicit in spreading white Christian nationalism out of fear and out of the hope of sparking a sort of spiritual revival. This reinforces the impact that this pernicious philosophy has had on our politics.”

National and regional faith based organizations are taking collaborative efforts to assess the effects of Christian Nationalism on their own congregations, and on the politics of our country. One such local group is Michigan Christians Against Christian Nationalism, who state “We believe that Christian Nationalism threatens our faith and country. We are an independent local group affiliated with the national organization, Christians Against Christian Nationalism, and work on awareness, advocacy and local organizing.” They have a following on Facebook under their group’s name. The National organization can be found at https://www.christiansagainstchristiannationalism.org/.

A Michigan native, the Reverend Jonathan D. Riedel is known as a “weaver of stories”, and contributes to the Fremont Times Indicator Religious Column on a regular basis. He has served Newaygo Congregational United Church of Christ since 2010. 

Pastor Jon will bring information about white Christian Nationalism from the perspective of a Christian Pastor to the program, and will discuss the counter actions needed to deal with “this distortion of the Christian Faith.”

For questions, please contact: IndivisibleNewaygoCo@gmail.com.

We'll hold the text banks in Zoom. Each text bank shift is 2 hours long, and we stay in the Zoom together the whole time to answer questions and provide support.

We'll be using a user-friendly, web-based platform called Scale to Win to send the messages, so text bankers will need a laptop, computer, or tablet (and your personal phone number will not be used for texting).

Each text bank will begin with a brief training on how to use the platform and how to respond to questions from voters. All volunteers must attend the full training during their first shift before beginning text banking, so please arrive on time! 

Additional information about the text bank, including the Zoom link, will be shared via email prior to your shift(s).

On Saturday, Oct. 17, we will text county-level early voting information to voters in eleven Down Home counties.

On Saturday, Oct. 24, we will text lower-propensity voters who have not yet voted with their closest early voting site if they live in a county with four or more sites (six Down Home counties).

On Monday, Nov. 2, we will text voters who have not yet voted with their election day polling location and hours.

Thank you for joining us!

events.description:
Studies show that writing postcards to voters can increase turnout by 1.5% — and with our elections being so close, that could make a real difference.

Join your local Precinct Chair with the Windsor Park Area Democrats for a community postcard-writing party with our neighbors! We’ll write postcards to local voters and do our part to help secure victories up and down the ballot.

📍 Picnic tables outside Springdale General
🍕 Pizza provided by yours truly 
🍻 Additional food and drinks available for purchase at Front Page

Come write a few postcards, enjoy some pizza, and help make sure our neighbors turn out to vote! If you only attend an hour, that's fine! Just drop by and help us for a bit.

events.title: Canvass with Team Massachusetts in Mattapan
events.description:
Team Massachusetts is launching a series of coordinated door-knocking canvasses across the Commonwealth to reelect Governor Healey, Lt. Governor Driscoll, Senator Ed Markey, Attorney General Andrea Campbell, and support Democrats up and down the ballot.

The Mattapan Canvass is on Sunday, October 18th at 11:00 a.m. We are building the grassroots organizing effort to drive Democratic victories across Massachusetts, and we want you to be a part of it! Together, we'll have conversations with voters, identify supporters, and help make sure they have a plan to vote this November.

We'll begin with a brief training, where you'll receive your turf, materials, and everything you need to hit the doors with confidence. Whether it's your first time canvassing or your hundredth, we'll make sure you have the tools and support you need.

Electing Democrats up and down the ballot is how we continue delivering results for Massachusetts. We need all hands on deck.

We can't wait to see you there.

events.title: Democracy Defenders Training
events.description:
# Democracy Defenders Election Protection Training with Common Cause Arizona

## What Are Democracy Defenders?

Our Voice Our Vote Arizona's Democracy Defenders program is preparing community volunteers to help protect access to the ballot throughout the 2026 election.

This virtual training, provided with Common Cause Arizona, will prepare Democracy Defenders for election protection activities during early voting and on Election Day.

Participants will learn about:

- The role of election protection volunteers
- What volunteers can and cannot do at voting locations
- The 75-foot boundary at Arizona voting locations
- How to assist voters without interfering with the voting process
- How to recognize and document potential voting problems
- When and how to use the 866-OUR-VOTE Election Protection Hotline
- How incidents should be reported and escalated
- What to expect while serving at a voting location
- How Democracy Defenders will be assigned to shifts and locations

Our Voice Our Vote Democracy Defenders primarily serve outside the 75-foot limit as voter helpers and line monitors. Volunteers may help answer basic voting questions, provide Know Your Rights information, monitor conditions such as long lines or unexpected closures, document problems, and connect voters with the Election Protection Hotline when appropriate.

No previous election-protection experience is required.

Training must be completed before serving a Democracy Defenders Poll Defender shift.

After training, Our Voice Our Vote will follow up with participants about available volunteer opportunities and deployment information.

## Who Should Attend

Anyone interested in volunteering with the Our Voice Our Vote Democracy Defenders program, including:

- New Democracy Defenders
- Level 2 Defenders interested in election protection shifts
- Level 3 Captains and Captain candidates
- Community members interested in helping voters during early voting or on Election Day

## Format

Virtual training via Zoom.

Registration is required.

## What Happens Next

After completing the training, Democracy Defenders will receive information from Our Voice Our Vote about upcoming volunteer opportunities, available shifts, site assignments, and additional program-specific orientation or Q&A sessions.

Questions about Democracy Defenders can be directed to the Our Voice Our Vote Democracy Defenders Program Director.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Want to knock doors for Chris Backemeyer but need to do it on your own time?

This one’s for you. Stop by and grab your own walk list, then canvass whenever it works for you: an evening after work, a Saturday morning, or a walk with your dog.

How it works:
Drop by during pickup hours.  We'll have all of the materials ready for you and connect you with a turf (just let us know if there’s a neighborhood you’d like).

We’ll walk you through the script and get MiniVAN loaded on your phone. It takes about 10 minutes.

Knock your doors on your own time, ideally within 5 days. Most lists take 1–2 hours.

Your results sync automatically through MiniVAN. Bring back any leftover lit when you've made it through your list.

What to bring when you canvass: A charged phone, comfortable shoes, and weather-appropriate layers. We’ll provide the lit and everything else.

New to canvassing? Perfect. Our short script makes it easy, and most conversations are friendly and quick. You’re welcome to bring a friend and split a list together.

With Election Day on November 3, every conversation counts. Mike Flood is counting on voters in NE-01 staying home. Let’s make sure our neighbors know there’s a choice who will show up for them.

events.title: Canvass for Chris Backemeyer - Pick Up Your Walk List
events.description:
Want to knock doors for Chris Backemeyer but need to do it on your own time?

This one’s for you. Stop by and grab your own walk list, then canvass whenever it works for you: an evening after work, a Saturday morning, or a walk with your dog.

How it works:
Drop by during pickup hours.  We'll have all of the materials ready for you and connect you with a turf (just let us know if there’s a neighborhood you’d like).

We’ll walk you through the script and get MiniVAN loaded on your phone. It takes about 10 minutes.

Knock your doors on your own time, ideally within 5 days. Most lists take 1–2 hours.

Your results sync automatically through MiniVAN. Bring back any leftover lit when you've made it through your list.

What to bring when you canvass: A charged phone, comfortable shoes, and weather-appropriate layers. We’ll provide the lit and everything else.

New to canvassing? Perfect. Our short script makes it easy, and most conversations are friendly and quick. You’re welcome to bring a friend and split a list together.

With Election Day on November 3, every conversation counts. Mike Flood is counting on voters in NE-01 staying home. Let’s make sure our neighbors know there’s a choice who will show up for them.

location.venue: Somewhere in PA close to the DE border

events.description:
Join Indivisible Newark DE to canvass in Pennsylvania's 13th House District (HD13), in southeastern PA right by the PA/DE/MD border.

## Why HD13?

The PA House is critical for election protection efforts and voter security. The area is shifting from red to blue, as seen in other local races (e.g., school board). This is a flippable seat!

Every door knocked means another opportunity to reach a voter. The stakes extend beyond this district: PA election protection and voter security are critical for the 2028 presidential election. 

## Canvassing Logistics

- Addresses and script provided by campaign
- No experience necessary; training provided as needed
- You will canvass in pairs
- RSVP on mobilize required

## Canvassing Location

- The campaign has agreed to give us areas of the district that are close to the DE border
- Exact location will be provided once you are signed up and closer to the actual canvassing date

## We know that canvassing works! Join us!

We deserve a say, a stake, and basic safety, and we need to determine the future of this dangerous, powerful technology – not leave it to a handful of Big Tech CEOs.

**Bring your signs and your friends!**

events.description:
Join the Democratic Socialists of America, Los Angeles to knock on doors to elect Angela Gonzales-Torres for Congress and win YES on Prop 40 for a billionaire tax this November!

California is one of the wealthiest places in the world, but working people are being asked to pay the price for devastating healthcare cuts so billionaires can get more tax breaks.

Prop 40 is our chance to change that. It makes billionaires pay their fair share so California doesn't lose healthcare funding and essential services.

At this community canvass, we'll talk to voters about why California needs to tax billionaires to keep hospitals and ERs open, protect healthcare for California families, and fund food assistance and K-14 education.

No previous campaign experience is necessary. There will be a brief training at the start of the event and new canvassers can be paired with more experienced members.

Be sure to bring a fully charged smartphone, sun protection, and appropriate footwear for walking!

Together, we're building a grassroots movement to mobilize one million Californians and win YES on Prop 40.

Tax billionaires. Save lives. Vote YES on Prop 40.

events.title: Documentary Screening: Lightworkers

location.venue: Unitarian Universalist Church of the Monterey Peninsula

events.description:
Please join us for this special screening of the documentary, "Lightworkers". 
Lightworkers is a powerful documentary featuring 35 diverse voices -activists, celebrities, politicians, historians-confronting what they see as a defining crisis of our time: the dismantling of American democracy. Lightworkers presents a mosaic of voices reflecting on a shared question:
What can we do? The film highlights the power of individual choices and collective responsibility, inviting viewers to consider their own role in shaping a more just and compassionate world.

“People who live with purpose, guided by compassion and a sense of responsibility to others, are who I call Lightworkers.” ~ Bobby Roth, filmmaker

Come Watch. Come Listen. Come Be Inspired.

Every conversation counts. When we show up in person and listen, we build stronger communities. Your participation helps ensure that the Hispanic community's voices are heard and their needs are prioritized.

events.title: Vote Ready Oklahoma: Voter Prep, Practice & State Question Info
events.description:
Vote Ready Oklahoma

Oklahoma's General Election is November 3. Early voting begins October 28. Vote Ready Oklahoma is your chance to walk in prepared.

Join Indivisible Edmond and Thanks For Voting OK and Yes, It Affects You for a nonpartisan community event built around one goal: getting every Oklahoman ready to vote.

Here's what's happening on-site:

🗳️ Mock election — walk through a real ballot start to finish. Great for first-time Oklahoma voters and anyone who wants to see what to expect before Election Day.

⭐ State Questions Info Session · 7:00 PM — a plain-language walkthrough of Oklahoma's 2026 state questions, hosted by Indivisible Edmond. Just what you need to know before you vote.

✍️ Notaries on-site — Still holding your absentee ballot? We'll get it notarized so you can hand-deliver it.

📋 Sample ballot walkthrough — bring yours or look it up on-site. We'll help you understand what you're seeing before you're standing in the booth.

❓ All-Things-Election Q&A — bring any question you have. Offices and what they do. How elections work. Where to find your precinct and polling place. When and where to vote early. If it's about voting, we've got someone who can answer it.

No party. No pressure. Just Oklahomans getting ready to show up.

Tuesday, October 27 · 6:30 PM - 8:30 PM (SQ info session 7:00 PM) 
NE OKC Community and Cultural Center 

Presented by Indivisible Edmond and Yes, It Affects You · In partnership with Thanks For Voting OK

events.title: Reach out to friends to help flip the House & Senate with Stand Up America!
events.description:
Stand Up America and Vote Save America are teaming up for a relational organizing training to give you the tools to talk to your friends and family about the midterm elections! 

Talking to the people you know is one of the most impactful things you can do this election. People are far more likely to trust information when it comes from someone they know, but conversations about politics with people you care about can be challenging. This training will give you the tools and practice to have those conversations with confidence.

Your network reaches further than you think. We'll help you find the friends and family you have in battleground states and districts, talk with them about what's at stake this November, and help them make a plan to vote. 

**What to expect:**

- Why relational organizing is so effective, and what the data shows
- What's at stake in the midterms, including control of the House and Senate
- How to map your network and find the people you know in key races
- Best practices and talking points for conversations with friends and family
- Resources to help the people in your life make a plan to vote and follow through

No experience needed–just a desire to elect a Congress that will put a check on Trump’s corruption and abuses of power!

events.title: MICHIGAN Winning Working Families Majority
events.description:
# Phonebank to Take Back the People's House for Working People in November! 

Join People's Action Power and Team '26, a coalition of movement organizations across the country, to reach the working-class voters in must-win Congressional and Senate races that will decide who controls Congress -- and whether we save our democracy. 


### 🏥 Michigan Thursdays: Will Lawrence for Congress, MI-7, and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for US Senate 

- Will Lawrence is the Sunrise Movement co-founder who helped win the largest green jobs program in US history and delivered hundreds of millions to Mid-Michigan. He co-founded Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High to win statewide renter protections. 

- Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a medical doctor who realized broken politics was making people sick, and he went to work fixing government: rebuilt Detroit's Health Department after bankruptcy, got lead out of the schools, and canceled $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders. He wrote the book on Medicare for All, and now, he's going to the Senate to make government work for you, not billionaires. 
 
The message from the primary season was loud and clear: Working Families candidates are winning. Working people aren't settling for just any candidate. They're demanding Movement Champions who answer to them, not big corporations and big money. 

Are you fired up? Sign up for the shifts leading up to Election Day. Share this link widely with your friends and family. 

No prior experience is required to join this phone bank. A laptop or tablet is recommended.

Let's go! Let's take back the People's House.

events.title: Angie for FL: Brevard Dems Turf Pickup at Rockledge HS
events.description:
We are asking you to visit Democrats (or other party affiliations that have indicated they would vote for a Democrat) in your community. We'll provide you with a list of names and addresses (aka Turfs). Most answer the door and are glad to see you. We're reminding our neighbors to make a voting plan for the midterms. Plus, many people do not realize that all Vote-By-Mail (VBM) requests are deleted every two years. Voters must proactively request a VBM every election cycle. 

Remind voters that requesting a mail ballot doesn't mean they have to use it. They can still vote in person if they prefer. It's just good to have that additional voting method in case something unexpected happens that prevents them from voting in person (hurricane, health issues, etc.). That's where we can help.

No experience needed. We'll train you. We'll pair an experienced canvasser with you until you're comfortable with your skills and knowledge. Volunteers needed to knock on doors and/or drive for a canvasser. 

Turfs are handed out, and training is scheduled during this Turf pickup event. Then, the volunteer canvasser canvasses at their own pace during the coming week. If no trainer is available to partner with you at your Turf pickup event, then call trainer Sherri Hudson (321-960-4609) to schedule a canvass training date/time.

If this is your first canvass, please download the 'Mini Van' app (and create your account; it's free) to your smartphone as this is the tool we use to canvass.

Thank you for volunteering! This is what Democracy looks like.

events.description:
We are all Jane Doe!

Join us as we gather to raise awareness as we prepare for the mid-term elections. We will stand in solidarity for survivors of sexual violence, including Jane Doe at Cornell University, Kendall Francis at Louisiana State University, Epstein survivors, and every person whose experience has been dismissed. 

You don’t have to be a woman to experience sexual violence. We can all fight for changes. 

THIS FIGHT IS FOR EVERYONE!

Too often, survivors are asked to carry the burden of proving what happened to them while institutions, universities, systems, and people in positions of power fail to protect them or hold perpetrators accountable.

We're calling for systemic change and calling on institutions — from the frat house to the White House and beyond — to stop protecting abusers and their reputations at the expense of our safety.

This is a peaceful public demonstration. Participants will stay on the public sidewalk and keep pedestrian access clear.

Bring a sign, bring water, bring a friend, or simply show up. 

This a local Indivisible event!



*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Make Your Voice Heard
events.description:
Join your community of like minded folks and make your voice heard!!!

To be heard is not just to have your words acknowledged. It’s to feel seen, valued, and understood. It’s to know that your presence matters.

Our voice is more than what we say. It’s our identity. Our power. For some, that voice shows up with bold resistance. For others, it’s the quiet courage to speak up after years of silence, to challenge injustice, and to stand in solidarity.

When we speak with clarity, we create space for connection and growth. It’s a practice that deepens how we show up in life and for others.

So let’s make our voices heard and fight for positive change!

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The award-winning Declaration of Independence Banner Brigade will be participating in Vienna's Halloween Parade this year, and we'd welcome additional folks to join our group of "regulars" as we display the text of the Declaration on our artistic, home-made banners.  Based on experience (at other parades), it'll be fun, uplifting, and unifying. Note that we entered as a NON-PARTISAN group, so this is not a protest. 

This will be our first time at the Vienna parade (our 7th parade total); and their 2026 theme is "Haunted History: 250 years of America." So: We'll be carrying our Declaration Banners while wearing colonial-era COSTUMES (don't worry if you don't have one in your closet--we'll help a lot!--more details after you register.) The parade is rain or shine.

About the Banner Brigade: We're an informal group of friends/neighbors and other volunteers who have come together numerous times in the past year--with the goal of raising awareness of the Declaration's words, including our founders’ rejection of the abuse of executive powers. 

Please bear in mind that an accurate headcount is essential for the Brigade to work smoothly, so if you register—which we hope you will!—we’ll be expecting you to definitely show up, unless you notify us ahead of time that your plans have changed (we understand that last-minute things arise). events.title: 10/22 Poll Observer Training with the Maine Dems Voter Access Team
events.description:
Join the Maine Dems Voter Access Team for Poll Observer Training on Thursday, October 22, at 2:00pm.

Poll Observers are the eyes and ears of the Voter Access Team on Election Day. When a machine goes down, a line runs long, or a voter is turned away, we only know about it because someone in the room told us. That is how we respond in time to fix it.

Training is required to be a Democratic Poll Observer, and it takes one hour. Every session covers the same material, so you only need to attend one.

## What you'll learn

- What you can and cannot do inside a polling place, and what your standing as a Poll Observer actually is
- How Election Day unfolds hour by hour, what to check on arrival, and how to observe the absentee canvass
- Where poll workers most often get registration and identification wrong, including why a student ID answers identity but not residence
- The issues that come up most often, from students and New Mainers to how a challenge actually works
- How to use LBJ, our reporting tool, and why it matters to log the problem you solved yourself
- What to do in rare situations, including evacuations and federal law enforcement near or in the polls

## Can't make this session?

Poll Observer Training runs online through October 30. See all sessions at https://www.mobilize.us/mainecoordinated/event/1021719/

## What happens next

The week before Election Day, we will assign you to a polling place and give you the contact numbers you need for the day.

## Who can attend

Anyone interested, 18 or older. You do not need to be a Maine resident.

Questions? Email the Maine Democratic Party Voter Access Team at votersupport@mainedems.org.

events.title: Lancaster Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Here in Lancaster we have been hosting a series of sustained events to continue the pressure and educate the wider Lancaster County community. We gather along Fruitville Pike with our signs and our presence demonstrating our support for our immigrant neighbors. We urge our community to condemn the cruel and illegal actions of ICE throughout this country. We come together to be an example to our local community to ACT, to SPEAK UP, and to take a STAND!

events.title: PORTLAND: HCAO Community Building - Light Exercise, Tea Tasting and Body Doubling on HCAO Work
events.description:
HCAO Portland!!! We are fully in our wind up to get our universal health plan turned into a universal health care bill this session. In the meantime, let's remember what separates us from the opposition. We are grounded in community and we fight together because we truly believe the work we are doing is needed. We are not paid to do this work, but take meaning in the work we do, which is elevated by the fact that we get to do this as a community. 

Your Portland chapter chair will be organizing community building days. I know this is during the work week and not everyone will be able to join.

But I really want those of us who can attend to be able to be building some community together. Expect a light exercise activity followed by tea tasting. Feel free to bring snacks to share. 

**The first two hours are dedicated towards exercise and community building.

The following three hours are meant to lightly do some HCAO work together in an effort to body double and win universal health care. Please bring your laptop if you have one.  There will still be quite a bit of just hanging out**

events.description:
# **SOULS TO THE POLLS! ** #

*Good music. Good food. Great community. Let's celebrate the power of our vote! Sunday voting is open to all voters from 1:00 pm to 5:00 p.m.*

Join the Hampton Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., Hampton Branch of the NAACP, and First Baptist Church of Hampton for Souls to the Polls! We're bringing our community together for an afternoon filled with music, food, fellowship, and celebration!

** MARCH! ** Meet us at First Baptist Church of Hampton at 12:30 PM for a short, spirited walk to the Hampton Registrar's Office, 101 Kings Way, Hampton, VA

**Come for the fellowship. Stay for the celebration. Let's make it a day to remember!**

**This is a nonpartisan event.  All food, entertainment, and free items are available to voters and non-voters alike. #DeltaDecide**

events.title: Common Cause Hawai`i Annual Gala- Volunteer Signup
events.description:
Join us as a volunteer for Common Cause Hawaiʻi's Annual Gala, honoring Senator Karl Rhoads and his years of public service to Hawaiʻi!

This special evening will bring together approximately 150 guests to celebrate civic engagement, community leadership, and our shared commitment to strengthening democracy in Hawaiʻi. Proceeds from the gala will support Common Cause Hawaiʻi's work in election protection, voter education, advocacy, and community outreach.

We need enthusiastic volunteers to help make this event a success! Volunteer opportunities include event setup and decorating, guest check-in and welcoming, buffet assistance, event support, and cleanup.

Event Details

Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026

Event Time: 6:00–9:00 PM

Location: Inspiration Hawaiʻi Museum

Address: 900 Richards Street, Honolulu, HI 96813

Volunteer Shifts

Shift 1 – Setup & Decorations: 3:00–5:30 PM

Shift 2 – Guest Arrival & Event Support: 5:30–9:00 PM

Shift 3 – Cleanup & Breakdown: 9:00–10:00 PM

Volunteers may sign up for one or multiple shifts based on their availability. No prior experience is necessary—just a willingness to help!

Your time and support will help us host a memorable evening while advancing our mission of building a more accessible, accountable, and inclusive democracy in Hawaiʻi.

Mahalo for being part of our team!

events.title: LD3 Dems Adopt-a-Road Fall 2026 Clean-Up Event

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join us for our Fall clean-up! LD3 Dems has adopted a road, and our commitment includes having a clean-up event on our stretch of the road at least twice a year.

Our next event will be on the morning of Saturday, November 14 at 8:00 a.m.. We will be meeting at 24th St and Carefree Highway. All supplies are provided including including safety vests, garbage pickers, gloves and bags, as well as water and snacks. Comfortable closed-toed shoes and sunscreen are recommended. You will need to sign a waiver at sign-in.

No children under the age of 12 are allowed to participate. A parent/ guardian of a person participating under the age of 18 must complete a minor participation form, which will be available at the cleanup.

You may bring friends, family, and neighbors, and no, they do not have to be registered Democrats! If you have limited mobility or can only participate for a short time, you are welcome! Do what you can, or help hand out supplies and hold down the fort at the base camp.

We'll also be collecting non-perishable food donations for Foothills Food Bank. Bring non-expired food items with you! Thank you in advance.

Please register if you plan on participating. This allows us to get an approximate count for supplies.

events.title: Legal Observer Training
events.description:
Know Your Role. Help Your Community.

📅 Wednesday, October 21, 2026
⏰ 5:00 PM
📍 Camp Verde Community Library
130 N. Black Bridge Loop, Camp Verde, AZ

🍕 Pizza will be provided!

It's time to step up and be there for members of our community.

The more we can raise awareness, accurately document what is happening, and report it, the better we can support our neighbors and help ensure situations are handled appropriately.

Join us for a community legal observer training focused on learning how to safely observe and document events and interactions involving local, state, and federal law enforcement or government agencies.

What a legal observer does — and doesn't do

We'll cover:

How to safely observe and document events

What information is important to record

How to respond if someone is detained or arrested

How to stay neutral, safe, and out of the way

What to do if something goes wrong

How we can support and protect our neighbors — the right way

Legal observers are trained witnesses. You don't need to be a legal expert or have previous experience. This training is about knowing your role, being prepared, and learning how to be there for your community when it matters.

Know Your Role. Help Your Community.

Co-sponsored by Indivisible Rimrock & Indivisible Cottonwood, Cornville & Clarkdale (Indivisible CCC).

This training is presented using ACLU legal observer training materials.

events.title: Día de los Muertos Vigil at Greene County Sheriffs Office/Jail: End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos (Sunday Nov 1st), join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We will gather at the Greene County Sheriffs Office & Jail for a Vigil where we mourn the loss of the 6,000 people who have been taken from our community with a display honoring those who have been taken.

Various churches around Springfield will be making illuminated bags with the names of each of the 6,000 detainees who have been detained/deported through our jail to honor each person who has been detained in the Greene County Jail. Bag making will take place during or following service at various churches and will be displayed outside the churches. And for those who do not want to participate in any church services but would still like to make the memorials:

We will be gathering at National Avenue Christian Church at 2:30pm to assemble bags and other parts of the memorials. 

We will then gather the displays and bring them to the Greene County Jail for a sunset vigil.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones. We will also grieve for those who have not died, but whose lives here have ended because of the work of ICE and the Greene County Sheriff.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

events.description:
A March & Press Conference for Accountability
Tired of higher bills haunting you? WE’RE NOT SCARED ANYMORE!

Another electricity bill. Another grocery trip that costs more than the last. Another month of watching your paycheck disappear before you can even catch up.
For too many Pennsylvania families, the scariest thing isn't a haunted house. It's the cost of everyday life.
And we're done being scared into silence.
On Friday, October 30, from 3:00–5:00 PM, join GoodPower Action in Harrisburg as we take our frustration to the streets and march to the Pennsylvania State Capitol for Scary Perry's House of Bills & Chills!
We're bringing the nightmare of rising household costs to life with a larger-than-life haunted-house installation featuring the bills that keep Pennsylvania families up at night: electricity, groceries, and healthcare.
But this isn't just about scary bills. It's about accountability.
We'll spotlight Congressman Scott Perry's voting record, question the decisions affecting Pennsylvania families, and demand answers from the people elected to represent us.

Here's what to expect:
A community march to the Pennsylvania State Capitol, bringing neighbors together around the rising cost of living.
Our House of Bills & Chills installation, a creative, powerful visual showing the everyday expenses haunting Pennsylvania households.
Stories featuring community voices and a call for accountability.
A chance to take action, connect with other Pennsylvanians, and show that our communities refuse to be ignored.
Bring yourself, family and friends to voice your frustration with bills that keep climbing.

With the November 3 election just days away, the stakes couldn't be clearer. Our elected officials' decisions have real consequences for our families and communities.

This election, votes have consequences. And accountability matters.

We're not scared anymore. We're getting organized.

RSVP TODAY and march with us!

We'll share additional information about the meeting location and event logistics with registered participants.

Paid for by GoodPower. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. GoodPower.org

events.title: Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
events.description:
Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
Saturday, November 14, 2026
1:30 PM – 4:00 PM
Fort Myers Regional Library — Meeting Rooms (Separate Building)
Fort Myers, Florida

Families for Strong Public Schools Lee invites local organizations, community leaders, parent groups, educators, advocacy organizations, and other partners to join us for a collaborative gathering focused on one shared goal:
Strengthening public schools in Lee County.

This will be an opportunity for groups from across our community to come together, build relationships, share priorities, and strategize about how we can more effectively support students, educators, families, and strong public education.

We know there are many organizations throughout Lee County already doing important work. Rather than working in separate silos, we want to create opportunities to connect our efforts, share information, identify common goals, and build a stronger coalition for our public schools.

What to Expect

Join us for light refreshments and an informal but productive conversation about:
The biggest challenges currently facing Lee County public schools
Opportunities for collaboration between community organizations
Supporting and amplifying educators, parents, students, and school
communities
Improving public awareness and engagement around education issues
Coordinating advocacy and community outreach
Identifying shared priorities and opportunities for collective action
Creating stronger communication between organizations working to support public education

This is not about every organization agreeing on every issue. It is about finding the areas where we do agree and determining how we can work together to make a greater impact.

Who Should Attend?

We welcome representatives from parent and family organizations, education advocacy groups, teacher and employee organizations, civic and community organizations, neighborhood and grassroots groups, student organizations, nonprofits, faith and community partners, and other organizations whose work intersects with our children.

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. 

Interfaith Alliance is partnering with Georgia FWD, Georgia Interfaith Public Policy Center, and First Missionary Baptist Church for this stop. Featuring a press conference at First Missionary Baptist, a caravan to an early voting location and block party, then an election protection training, you’ll hear from national and local faith leaders as we stand together in solidarity for democracy and civic participation.

The training will focus on preparing community members to support voters outside polling locations, including situational awareness, de-escalation, voter care, documentation and reporting, and Georgia-specific election safety rules

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

events.description:
Want to engage your personal network to ensure we win in November? This training is for you! We'll be teaching you all about Echo, an exciting new tool that will help you share important election-related information within your personal networks. It will also help you share insights from your communities with Democratic campaigns, so that candidates can address the problems voters care about most.

Research shows that the most effective way to drive turnout is through one-on-one interactions with people you know. People listen to you in a way they never listen to an ad. Echo works like this: communicating important information, and content, to groups only you can reach.

Curious to learn more? Don't miss out on this opportunity to help turn Texas blue!

events.title: Vote for Kids: Rob Sand Textbank

events.title: Textbank for No on 3 - Voter Rights MA
events.description:
Don’t let billionaires buy our elections.

This November, Question 3 would replace our current primaries with a “jungle primary,” where only the top two finishers advance to the general election, even if both are from the same party. The measure is funded by a small group of wealthy donors, mostly private equity executives. It would mean less choice for voters and more power for big money, and it would shut out minority and working class candidates from the November ballot.

Voters in other states rejected this same playbook in 2024. Help make sure Massachusetts does too.

What you’ll do:

Join us on Zoom (link available upon sign up!) for a quick training, then respond to texts from fellow Massachusetts voters who’ve replied to our outreach. You’ll answer their questions, share why we’re voting No on 3, and ask for their pledge. No experience needed: we’ll provide suggested responses and support the whole time. Every conversation counts.

events.title: DAY OF ACTION
events.description:
THIS IS THE DAY BEFORE EARLY VOTING STARTS!!!
You would be surprised how many people know absolutely nothing about this election going on. They've literally never heard of Talarico or any statewide office, let alone county judge or district clerk. True story!

We need Democrats, Independents, and folks who might sit this out to show up at the polls. We need folks who know about the election and know the stakes. That's where we come in.  

Starting at our Democratic HQ at 17301 El Camino Real
2-4pm we'll be block walking in Heritage park and Autumn Lakes. this involves the MiniVAN app to help you know which house to knock and which house to skip.

4-5pm at HQ we'll be making phone calls to older voters to help them make a voting plan (vote by mail, curbside voting, where's the best polling location and more)

5-6pm we'll serve some pizza at HQ and chat about the day

6-7pm we'll go to to some very democratic leaning apartment complexes and hang our doorhanger on every door. This requires no talking to voters and no app, but may involve walking up stairs.

You can join us for any or all of the events that day.

This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

On September 20th of this year, ICE killed Mario David Coronado Juárez when they pursued his vehicle in Grand Rapids. Just days after that, they kidnapped more members of Mario's family.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We will be reaching out to local voters to ensure they know when, where, and how to cast their ballot early and share information regarding endorsed candidates Paul Nolley and Julianna Stratton.

Whether you’re a seasoned caller or phone banking for the first time, we’ll start with a brief training, walk through the script together, and support each other live on Zoom while we make calls.

## Before You Join: Required Tech & Setup
To ensure a smooth experience, please complete these two steps before the event begins:

Create an ActionID Account:

Our calling platform uses ActionID to secure your account and save your progress. If you don't already have one, please create an account ahead of time at VAN ActionID Login. - Directions will be sent upon sign up.

Prepare Two Devices:

For the best phone banking experience, you will need two separate devices:

Device 1 (Laptop, Tablet, or Computer): To log into Zoom for our team check-in, live support, and to view the call script/voter list.

Device 2 (Cell Phone): To make the phone calls.


## What to Expect
First 15–20 Mins: Welcome, ActionID check-in, and quick training on the script.

45–60 Mins: Live phone banking with the group (on mute in Zoom, but with chat/support available if you have questions).

Final 10 Mins: Quick wrap-up, debrief, and celebrating our impact!

events.title: Vote Tripling at Early Voting sites in DeKalb: Oct 13-Oct 30
events.description: One of the most impactful campaign activities can only be accomplished during Early Voting.  Vote Tripling (aka "Remind 3 Friends") is an proven way to both capture a voter's focus on voting AND convince them to triple their voting impact by reminding 3 friends (contacts in their phone) by texting them right away to VOTE.  Research shows that people are much more likely to vote if encouraged by a friend or family member than by a stranger.  In an election that is expected to be very close YOUR efforts could be the difference!  Sign up here and we'll connect with you to find a time and Early Voting location that suits your schedule!

events.title: Poverty 2 Prosperity Party At The Polls!
events.description:
Description
Poverty 2 Prosperity PS Inc. — Party at the Polls

When- Wednesday, Oct 21 5:30pm- 7:00pm
Where- C & J Velvet Hall
              1036 Gray Hwy Macon, GA 31211

Come out and celebrate community, connection, and civic participation at Poverty 2 Prosperity PS Inc.’s Party at the Polls! This exciting community event brings neighbors, families, and friends together for a day filled with music, delicious food, games, dancing, laughter, and fun while providing helpful information about the voting process.

Party at the Polls is designed to create a welcoming and positive environment where community members can gather, enjoy themselves, connect with local resources, and participate in the election process. events.title: Texas Together Block Walk w/ Team Wu & Southwest Dems
events.description:
Join Texas Together as we knock doors to get out the vote for James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, Vikki Goodwin, and Democratic candidates down the ballot, like Rep. Gene Wu!

Together, we will defeat Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott, and build a better future for Texas.

Wear comfortable shoes, bring a water bottle and a fully charged cell phone. We’ll start with a quick training and then head out to knock doors. No experience needed!

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
The Southwest Women's Law Center (SWLC), Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML) Coalition, and Los Alamos Early Childhood Collaboration (LAECC) are hosting a screening of a documentary about what motherhood really looks like in America today.

This isn’t just about watching a film; it’s about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly, and realize we’re not alone.

There will be a discussion following the screening about how a Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML) policy in New Mexico would provide much-needed support for our community.

Would love for you to join us!

events.title: TELL REP. JIMMY GOMEZ: FREEZE BIG AI NOW
events.description:
Join us on **October 20 at 4pm at Rep. Jimmy Gomez' local Congressional office to demand an immediate freeze on AI, now! 

Right now, Big Tech CEOS are using unregulated AI to steal our work, wreck job prospects, pollute our air and water, and endanger our communities with surveillance - and, as their own employees admit, creating threats to all of humanity. 

That's why we need an immediate freeze on AI, now - until we can ensure that we all have a say, and stake, and strong safety guardrails  over this powerful technology. 

And that's why we're walking out on October 20th - students, workers, neighbors, community members - coming together to share how unregulated AI is hurting our communities, and demanding Rep Jimmy Gomez take a stand. Because Angelenos deserve leaders who will prioritize us, our communities, and our futures, not just billionaire Silicon Valley execs. 

Rep. Gomez needs to make it clear: Will he side with the working class or the AI oligarchs? Everyday Americans or Trump and his tech billionaire buddies? Humans or robots?

Bring your friends and your signs! Speakers, chants, and more info to come!



Bring your signs and your friends!

events.description:
Hey Fort Worth!
MOVE Texas Fort Worth is hosting Coloring Outside the Ballot Box: Artivism Lab, and we want YOU to be part of it! 
Artivism is the practice of blending art and activism and is essential to truly connect with communities and culture. In this lab we will explore the concepts that help us join the two. We will also be sharing information on election protection and giving out free literature!
Join us to:
 - Connect with your community!
- Learn more about mixing Art & Activism!
- Get election protection information!
- Free literature!
- Free food!

- What: Artivism Lab

- Where: BLANC Cowork+studios
2212 W Peter Smith St. , Fort Worth TX 76102

- Meet MOVE Texas organizers, chapter members, and other people in your community.

- **Talk & Listen:** Take part in conversations about what’s happening in our community, what people are experiencing, and the issues people care about.

- **Get Involved:** Learn more about MOVE Texas, our local work, and ways to stay connected, volunteer, or take action with our chapter.

We hope to see you there!

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
HD75 is one of Tennessee's best pickup opportunities this cycle, and Sierra Club Tennessee is all in. Join us in Clarksville to knock doors for Allie Phillips in one of the most competitive State House races of 2026.

Allie is a working mom of two and a former small business owner who ran an in-home daycare. She knows what Montgomery County families deal with every day, and she's earned Sierra Club's endorsement because she'll stand up for the things that keep those families healthy: clean water, clean air and the right of local communities to decide what gets built in their backyard.

Paid for by Sierra Club TN Chapter PAC.

events.title: Second Line to the Polls with Claws Out NOLA, Ole & Nu Style Fellas, and Les Fous du Carnaval!
events.description:
*Party to the Polls*

Music, neighbors, and a second line to the polls to GEAUX VOTE! Let’s make an afternoon of it.

Join Claws Out NOLA, the New Orleans chapter of Cat Ladies for America, on Saturday, October 24, as we join Ole & Nu Style Fellas Social Aid & Pleasure Club, Les Fous du Carnaval, and Sportsmen’s Kids for a second line from Tremé to City Hall, early voting, and community speakers.

We’re joining **Put the Party Back in Politics** and other community partners to bring people together in a way New Orleans knows well: out in the streets, with music and good company!

Wear a costume, bring a parasol, put on your cat ears, or come as you are. Bring a friend. Bring 3! Bring ya mom’n’em! You’re welcome whether you’re voting that afternoon, have already voted, or are coming to support your neighbors.

**THE PLAN**

*This signup is for the downtown route.* [See companion second lines happening that day.](https://www.mobilize.us/mobilize/event/1039437/)

• Saturday, October 24: Gather at **12:30 pm**.

• Meeting point: **Tremé Center**, 900 N. Villere St., New Orleans, LA 70116.

• **1 pm**: Second line departs for City Hall.

• 2 pm: Parade disbands at 1300 Perdido St. Make time for early voting and speakers at the City Hall gathering.

THE ROUTE

Tremé Center → N. Villere Street → left on Basin Street → Loyola Avenue → right on Perdido Street → City Hall.

Can’t join us for the whole route? Join the second line at any point along the way, or meet us directly at City Hall, 1300 Perdido St., around 2 pm for the gathering and early voting. You don’t have to walk the parade route to participate!

GOOD TO KNOW

Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Costumes, parasols, and cat ears are encouraged, but absolutely optional.

This is a nonpartisan community event, with no candidate or political party campaigning as part of the programming. Everyone is welcome!

RSVP for gathering details and event updates.

Part of Put the Party Back in Politics’ series of community voting events. Find more at NOLA.vote.
events.accessibility_notes:
This is an outdoor second line from the Tremé Center to City Hall, with gathering at 12:30 pm and the parade scheduled for 1–2 pm. Expect amplified music, crowds, and periods of walking or standing.

Can’t join us for the whole route? Join the second line at any point along the way, or meet us directly at City Hall, 1300 Perdido St., around 2 pm for the gathering and early voting. You don’t have to walk the parade route to participate!

We are still confirming route accessibility and the availability of accessible restrooms and seating. If you have access questions or need an accommodation, please contact Laurie / 504.410.7556 so we can discuss arrangements before the event.

events.title: Tunkhannock Community Canvass: Knock on doors with Action Together!
events.description:
Community canvassing with Action Together NEPA is about more than just knocking on doors — it’s about building real connections with our neighbors. By having one-on-one conversations, we listen to what matters most to people, share important election information, and make sure every voice in our community is heard. These conversations are proven to be the most effective way to strengthen democracy and inspire action.

When you volunteer, you’ll be part of a supportive team, get quick training, and head out together to engage with your community. It’s a fun, energizing way to make new friends, build skills, and create real change right here for NEPA families. Let’s make sure that local voices shape the future of our region!

One more reason to canvass: all of our canvass volunteers get a free t-shirt! Be sure to include your size when you sign up so you can complete your fit when you head out with the team to knock on doors.

events.title: Atlanta  Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.
