events.title: Elevate District 8 and Knock Doors for Sharonda Huffman
events.description:
Sharonda Huffman is a longtime Essex resident, community advocate, Democrat, and public‑service professional with experience in government, housing, and disability rights. A wife, mother, and champion for accessibility and inclusion, she has spent her career helping residents navigate public systems and secure essential services.

Let's show our support for her run for County Council and knock some doors with Sharonda!

We will meet at Kestrel Cafe to launch each knock.

First time volunteering? No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out.

Are you a pro canvasser? GREAT! Join us in the parking lot to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors!

What you’ll need: Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things. 1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on iPhone or android. 2. A full water bottle 3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

events.title: Knock Doors with Team Manny and Mo Dower for HD 64
events.description:
Come knock doors with Manny Rutinel for Congress and Mo Dower for HD 64!

Manny is a longtime advocate and attorney who grew up working class. And now he’s working to ensure our communities have an honest shot at success. As a State Representative, attorney, and former economist for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, he’s learned that making progress requires working with others and working hard to get things done. He plans to use facts and evidence to fight for working families and deliver results that make your life better.

Mo Dower grew up the daughter of frugal, Depression-era parents in a suburb surrounded by farm fields—running the neighborhood until nightfall while also milking cows on Christmas Eve—an upbringing that instilled a strong work ethic, a practical mindset, and a passion for caring for humans and animals. As a large animal veterinarian, she spent her career working alongside horse owners, farmers, and ranchers, later becoming a nationwide subject matter expert for complex medical cases—demanding work built on quick thinking and showing up to get the job done. She's carried that same mindset into raising her family in Northern Colorado and into her service as a Berthoud Trustee and Mayor Pro Tem, which reinforced her belief that leadership should be grounded and community-focused, not driven by personal gain, and that public servants should represent their constituents as fellow citizens.

# ⚖️ Keep Experience on the Bench: An Evening with Judge John Stevens

**Hosted by Friends of Judge John Stevens**

📅 **Tuesday, October 20, 2026**
⏰ **5:00 PM – 9:00 PM**
📍 **The Neches Room, 246 Crockett Street, Beaumont, TX**

Early voting is underway, and it's time to rally! Join the Friends of Judge John Stevens on historic Crockett Street for a big night of celebration, community, and support for a judge who has served Jefferson County with fairness and integrity for nearly two decades.

### The record speaks for itself
- ⚖️ **20 years** as a federal prosecutor
- 🏛️ **19 years** as Criminal District Judge
- 👩🏾‍⚖️ Presided over **620+ felony jury trials**
- 📂 Disposed of **50,000+ criminal cases**

When it comes to the court that handles our community's most serious cases, experience isn't optional. It's essential.

### Why you won't want to miss it
- 🎉 Come early, stay late, or swing by after work
- 🤝 Shake hands and talk one-on-one with Judge Stevens
- 💬 Catch up with friends, neighbors, and community leaders
- 🗳️ Get fired up for the final stretch before Election Day

**Every contribution helps keep a proven, experienced judge on the bench.** Can't make it? [👉 Contribute to Judge Stevens here](https://checkout.square.site/merchant/MLCP2126SNMDS/checkout/XKUABIV3ZNKHH3FNRDR3OCEY)

Bring your spouse, your coworkers, and your friends. Let's pack the Neches Room! 🙌🏾

👉 **RSVP below and help us show Judge Stevens that Jefferson County has his back!**

events.title: ICUC - Become a Neighborhood Vote Protector
events.description:
**Protect the vote in your neighborhood**

*Become a neighborhood vote protector. Every vote is a decision about our healthcare, housing, wages, and who gets to make the rules – which is exactly why it needs to be protected. The Trump administration is trying rig the outcomes of the election by creating chaos, fear and new roadblocks to keep us from voting.*

We Are CA is training thousands of Neighborhood Vote Protectors across the state to watch the polls in their communities, safely safely document and report incidents to legal experts, and make sure every voter knows their rights to cast a ballot without fear or intimidation. Join a short training to learn how you can look out for your neighbors, your block, and your local polling place.

Wed Oct 21 6-7:30pm


**Español
Protege el voto en tu vecindario**
*Conviértete en un Protector del Voto en tu Vecindario. Cada voto es una decisión sobre nuestra salud, nuestra vivienda, nuestros salarios y sobre quién decide las reglas — y es precisamente por eso que necesita ser protegido. La administración Trump está tratando de manipular los resultados de las elecciones creando caos, miedo y nuevos obstáculos para impedirnos votar.*
We Are CA está capacitando a miles de Protectores del Voto en todo el estado para vigilar los centros de votación en sus comunidades, documentar incidentes de forma segura a través de líneas directas legales, y asegurarse de que cada votante conozca sus derechos para emitir su voto sin miedo ni intimidación.

Únete a una capacitación breve para aprender cómo puedes cuidar a tus vecinos, tu cuadra y tu centro de votación local.

Miércoles 21 de oct | 6–7:30 pm

events.title: Party at the Polls
events.description:
## 🎉 It's a Party at the Polls! 🎉

Voting isn't a chore. It's a celebration, and we're throwing the party!

Grab your friends, your family, your church crew, and your neighbors, and join the **Southeast Texas Minority Alliance** for an afternoon of food, fellowship, and community spirit during Early Voting. We'll be outside **two Beaumont early voting locations** with good food, good music, and good people. Then we'll walk in and vote **together**.

### 📅 When
**Saturday, October 24, 2026**
**Noon – 3:00 PM**

### 📍 Where (pick the one closest to you!)
**Johns Library**
4255 Fannett Rd, Beaumont, TX 77705

**Willard Library**
3590 E Lucas Dr, Beaumont, TX 77708

### 🍔 What to Expect
- **Free food** for everyone, while supplies last
- **Music and good vibes** all afternoon
- **Fellowship** with neighbors, friends, and folks who love this community as much as you do
- **Voting together.** Walk in with your community and make your voice heard!
- Friendly volunteers to answer questions about your ballot, your polling place, and what to bring

### 🪪 Bring Your Photo ID!
Texas requires an approved photo ID to vote in person. Acceptable forms include:
- Texas Driver's License or Texas Personal ID Card
- Texas Election Identification Certificate
- Texas Handgun License
- U.S. Military ID with photo
- U.S. Citizenship Certificate with photo
- U.S. Passport (book or card)

Don't have one? You can still vote by signing a *Reasonable Impediment Declaration* and showing a supporting document, such as a utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or voter registration certificate.

### 💙 Why We Party
When we show up together, we're stronger. This is our community, our county, and our future. Let's celebrate it, protect it, and vote for it, side by side.

**Everyone is welcome.** Bring the kids, bring your neighbors, and bring your best energy. See you at the party! 🎊

*Free food and fun are open to all attendees.

events.title: Urgent Opposition to Livestreaming Nidal Hasan’s Execution – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear Representative [Last Name],

I am writing as your constituent to express my profound objection to the Pentagon’s announced plan to livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, scheduled for December 3, 2026. This would be the first military execution in more than 60 years and the first public execution in the United States in nearly a century. I strongly urge you to publicly oppose this decision and to exercise congressional oversight to prevent the Department of Defense from turning a solemn act of military justice into a public spectacle.

I want to be clear: my objection is not rooted in sympathy for Hasan or in any doubt about the gravity of his crimes. He murdered 13 unarmed soldiers and wounded more than 30 others at Fort Hood in 2009, and he has never claimed innocence. The families of the victims and the survivors deserve justice and closure. But justice and spectacle are not the same thing, and the decision to livestream this execution is a profound mistake that will harm our nation’s moral standing, endanger our security, and undermine the very principles we claim to uphold.

The livestream would violate fundamental human rights standards.

The United Nations human rights office has warned that livestreaming an execution would amount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition on torture under international law. A UN spokesperson described the prospect of a government executing someone “in front of live cameras” as “abhorrent”. Amnesty International has condemned the plan as “reprehensible,” noting that international human rights bodies have long found public executions incompatible with the prohibition on cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. The United States should not join the ranks of nations that carry out public executions; according to Amnesty International, only Iran and Afghanistan are known to have done so in 2025. This is not who we are—or who we should aspire to be.

The livestream would make us less safe, not more.

Senator Jack Reed, Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, has warned that livestreaming the execution “only gives the shooter what he wants: more attention and more control” and that it is “a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters”. Congressman Jason Crow, a former Army Ranger, has similarly stated that a public execution “only gives our adversaries fodder for anti-American propaganda that makes us less safe”. Hasan has said he acted to stop soldiers from deploying to Afghanistan; broadcasting his death to a global audience would hand extremists a powerful recruitment tool and validate their narrative that America is at war with Islam. The last thing our national security needs is a propaganda victory for those who wish us harm.

The livestream would degrade our military and our legal system.

Army Regulation 190-55 governs who may witness military executions and does not provide for unrestricted public attendance. There is no regulation or precedent for a military execution to be livestreamed, and experts have noted that public executions are typically held in authoritarian countries to instill fear and demonstrate government power. Republican Senator Thom Tillis has said that public executions are what “oppressive dictatorships do” and called the plan “beyond disgusting”. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy accused the Secretary of Defense of “mimicking ISIS”. When lawmakers from both parties use the same language to describe an American policy that they use for our enemies, something has gone deeply wrong.

The livestream would traumatize victims and survivors.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former Army sergeant who was shot seven times during the attack and who plans to attend the execution in person, has said he does not agree with making the event publicly available without censorship. The families of the fallen and the survivors deserve to mourn and to seek closure in a manner that respects their dignity, not to have their trauma broadcast to the world as entertainment. As Senator John Curtis has warned, a civilization “erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment”.

What I am asking of you. I respectfully urge you to take the following actions:

1.	Publicly denounce the Pentagon’s plan to livestream Hasan’s execution and call on Secretary Hegseth to reverse the decision. Bipartisan voices—including Senators Reed, Tillis, Murkowski, and Curtis, and Representatives Crow and Smith—have already spoken out. Your voice would add needed weight.
2.	Exercise congressional oversight. The House and Senate Armed Services Committees should demand transparency regarding the legal authority for this livestream, the financial arrangements (including any potential monetization), and the consultation process that led to this decision. A letter from former national security officials has already raised serious questions about whether the execution could be used for “commercial gain or partisan political propaganda”. Congress must investigate.
3.	Support legislative or regulatory action to ensure that no future military execution is livestreamed or otherwise made available to the public for entertainment or political purposes. The default should be the solemn, limited-witness procedure prescribed by Army Regulation 190-55.

The death penalty itself is a matter of serious moral and legal debate, and I respect that Americans of good faith disagree on it. But whatever one’s position on capital punishment, livestreaming an execution is beyond the pale. It is cruel, it is dangerous, and it is beneath the dignity of the United States. Hasan’s crimes were horrific, but responding with a public spectacle does not honor his victims—it exploits them. It does not strengthen the rule of law—it makes a mockery of it. And it does not make us safer—it makes us a recruiting poster for our enemies.

I urge you to act swiftly and forcefully. Please let me know what steps you plan to take.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Email Address]
[Phone Number]

The signs will be available at meetings for a suggested donation of $20. Or contact Judy Clay @ 972 742-7910.

3065 N. Josey Lane, Carrollton, TX 75007

events.title: Indivisible Boca Raton presents “Immigration at a Crossroads”
events.description:
Immigration detentions by ICE and local law enforcement is surging in the country, South Florida, and in Palm Beach County. Family separation is rampant, detention centers are overcrowded and ripe with serious human rights abuses. People are dying from ICE shootings and in ICE custody.

The data shows that the overwhelming majority of the immigrants being detained are hard-working, family oriented, and net contributors to our community. They are our neighbors, not criminals.

This immigration enforcement regime can only exist by taking away people’s constitutional rights and by covering up their immigration operations from public view. On Monday, November 16, 6:00- 7:30 PM, at the Dr. Andre Fladell Civic Center, 16700 Jog Rd., Delray Beach, FL 33446 come hear the experts.
Moderator: Barbara Eriv, Indivisible Immigration Coalition (PBCIIC).
The current immigration policy landscape and possible policy change opportunities from the 2026 midterms and into the 2027 municipal election-Renata Bozzetto, Deputy Director at the Florida Immigrant Coalition
A profile of the immigrants in our community and the effects from family separation: Ruth Rosa MACP, Post-Release Services Clinician at Urban Strategies.
The legal and constitutional rules of the current administration and impacts on detainees and families-Jennifer Smith, Senior Litigation Attorney at Americans for Immigration Justice.
The longer term consequences to our community and economy-Philip Lewin, Associate Professor of Sociology, Director of Graduate Studies at the Florida Atlantic University (FAU)

events.title: Protect the Vote: Volunteer & Poll Observer Info Session (On-Demand)
events.description:
# Get Involved in Voter Protection: On-Demand Info Session

Whether you're brand new to voter protection or have volunteered with us before, this on-demand information session is your entry point into the North Carolina Democrats' Voter Protection Team.

**Watch anytime, at your own pace, and learn how you can help protect the vote in 2026.**

### Learn How You Can Protect the Vote

We'll introduce you to our Voter Protection program and the different ways you can get involved, then take a closer look at one of our biggest volunteer programs this fall: **Poll Observing**.

You'll learn what Poll Observers do, what to expect at the polls, how training and scheduling work, and how you can help protect the vote in your community.

### More Ways to Get Involved

Poll observing isn't the only way to help! We also have opportunities to support voter outreach and education, volunteer recruitment, voter assistance, and behind-the-scenes program operations.

Whether you're ready to sign up or just want to learn more, this session will help you find the role that's right for you.

### How It Works


### How It Works

This is a **recorded, on-demand information session**, not a live Zoom meeting.

After registering, you'll be directed to the recording so you can watch whenever it's convenient for you.

**Please note:** This is an introductory information session, not Poll Observer Training. To serve as a Poll Observer, you'll need to complete the separate required training.

### Ready to Take the Next Step?

- **Become an Inside Poll Observer:** Register for a [live or on-demand Poll Observer training](https://tinyurl.com/NC26PollObserver).
- **Explore other volunteer opportunities:** Find [upcoming Voter Protection trainings, phonebanks, and events](https://tinyurl.com/NC26VoProEvents).

Questions? Contact **pollobservers@ncdp.org**.

events.title: Texas Together Block Walk: GOTV Forrest Hill
events.description:
### Join Texas Together in Forrest Hill as we ramp up the action to Get Out The Vote and knock doors to support **Texas Democratic** nominees up and down the ballot. 

It’s time to organize, unify, and build the movement that will carry us through the last 31 days until Election Day, November 3, 2026.

During the block walk, volunteers will:

- Identify Democratic supporters

- Share information about our Democratic ticket

- Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots efforts and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We’ll provide training, materials, and turf at the start of each shift. 

Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend.
**RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.**

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
Comunidad Materna en Utah is hosting a screening of a documentary about what motherhood really looks like in America today.

This isn’t just about watching a film; it’s about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly, and realize we’re not alone.

Here at Comunidad Materna we are dedicated to connecting mothers with the resources and support they need to thrive. Our mission is to strengthen and empower expectant mothers through maternal health education, access to resources and continuous support throughout pregnancy, birth and postpartum. 

We invite all who share our passion and would to connect with us in this work. Together we can make the world a better place for mothers, and in-turn make a better world for everyone. 

Would love for you to join.

Comunidad Materna en Utah organiza la proyección de un documental sobre cómo es realmente la maternidad en Estados Unidos hoy en día.

No se trata solo de ver una película; se trata de compartir un espacio donde podamos expresar en voz alta aquello que hemos llevado en silencio y darnos cuenta de que no estamos solas.

En Comunidad Materna, nos dedicamos a conectar a las madres con los recursos y el apoyo que necesitan para prosperar. Nuestra misión es fortalecer y empoderar a las futuras madres mediante la educación en salud materna, el acceso a recursos y un acompañamiento continuo durante el embarazo, el parto y el posparto.

Invitamos a todas las personas que compartan nuestra pasión a unirse a esta labor. Juntos podemos hacer del mundo un lugar mejor para las madres y, a su vez, un mundo mejor para todos.

Nos encantaría que nos acompañaras.

Whether you've knocked hundreds of doors or have never volunteered before, there's a seat for you. Come meet the volunteers already organizing, hear what's on the ballot, and learn how James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, and Democrats down the ballot are fighting for Texas families.                                                                         

At each Community Night you'll:
• Meet other volunteers who live near you
• Learn about the races and candidates on your ballot
• Ask questions and share what you're hearing in your community
• Plan a block walk or other event with others.
• Get trained and leave ready to do your part before election day.

From time to time, special guests - including candidates and campaign leaders - may stop by to meet volunteers. Watch your confirmation emails for updates.

No experience needed. Bring a friend, bring your questions, and bring your neighbors. Light refreshments provided.

We win this election one conversation, one door, and one neighbor at a time. Let's do it together.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in East Greenbush/NY 19
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

**Winning this district, NY 19, is critical in order for us to retake the House.**

__PLEASE DON'T GHOST US!__ 
+ PLEASE WATCH FOR EMAILS WITH IMPORTANT PREPARATIONS TO DO BEFORE CANVASS DAY 
+ IF YOU HAVE TO CANCEL, PLEASE LET US KNOW ASAP. 
+ RESPOND IF WE TEXT YOU/Email or Call you.

__IMPORTANT INFORMATION:__ 
+CHECK FOR EMAILS OFTEN FROM GAIL OR MOBILIZE
+ YOU MUST HAVE A PHONE WITH THE MIC ENABLED.  
+ DOWNLOAD THE APP AND PRACTICE BEFORE YOU ARRIVE.

__Your confirmation email from Mobilize will include important training materials that will need to be reviewed and acted on before the canvass!__

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

If you would like to host a workshop for your employees, or club, or church, or any group, email us at contact@yakima-indivisible.org with the subject line Decoding Your Ballot. We will do our best to accommodate your request.

**Let’s Knock Doors for Tina Kotek—with Special Guest Shasti Conrad!**

Join us for a canvass kickoff with Shasti Conrad, Chair of the Washington State Democrats and Vice Chair of the Democratic National Committee! We’ll hear from Shasti, get fired up, and head out to talk with our neighbors about reelecting Tina Kotek.

Adopted from Calcutta and raised in rural Oregon by a single mom, Shasti’s commitment to building a stronger, more inclusive democracy has taken her from organizing campaigns to serving in the Obama White House. She’s worked on four presidential campaigns and made history as the first woman of color and youngest person to lead the Washington State Democrats—and the first South Asian woman to chair a state Democratic Party anywhere in the country.

Under her leadership, Washington Democrats won every statewide office, reelected every Democratic congressional incumbent, and expanded their legislative majorities in 2024. Now she’s bringing that organizing energy back to Oregon to help us turn enthusiasm into votes for Tina Kotek.

The conversations we have at the doors can make the difference in this race. Whether you’re a seasoned canvasser or joining us for the first time, we’ll make sure you have what you need to get started.

**RSVP, bring a friend, and help us send Tina Kotek back to work for Oregon!**

events.title: GOTV Canvass for Virginia Democrats in Culpeper County!
events.description:
This is it: the final stretch before Election Day! 🗳️

Months of work come down to these final days. From Saturday, October 31 through Election Day on Tuesday, November 3, the VA26 Coordinated Campaign will be knocking every door we can across Madison, Culpeper, Greene, and Orange counties to re-elect Senator Mark Warner and Congressman Eugene Vindman.

These last few days are all about turnout. We’ll talk with supporters to make sure they have a plan: where their polling place is, what time they’re going, and how they’re getting there. On Saturday, we’ll get folks to early voting before it closes. On Election Day, we’ll knock until the polls close at 7pm.

What to expect:

Quick welcome and canvass training (first-timers welcome!)
Walk lists and materials provided
Team up with fellow volunteers, so nobody knocks alone

What to bring:

A fully charged phone with the MiniVAN app downloaded
Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothes
A friend or two. Every extra pair of hands means more doors!

events.title: Indivisible ADK/Saratoga Chapter meeting:  Hands Off Our Vote!
events.description:
In addition to the usual benefits of attending a chapter meeting (joining together in community, staying in the loop about the ways in which we're organizing, and learning the ways you can get more involved), we will be offering an informational meeting about **Hands Off Our Vote!**  

Join us for this very special event with **We Get Out the Resistance**, one of our local organizing partners!

We know that Trump and his Big Lie cronies are plotting to do everything they can to undermine our elections in 2026. Whether it’s trying to end mail-in voting, targeting registration programs, blocking vote-counting, even trying to ban states from encouraging people to vote – it’s going to be no-holds-barred from them this year as they try desperately to block the free and fair elections.

But we’re going to cut through the noise, and we’re going to be ready for whatever dirty tricks they try. And we’re going to do it with community power and preparation, not panic.

There is only one force powerful enough to topple a dictator: **WE THE PEOPLE!!**

*Hands Off Our Vote is Indivisible’s national program to ensure all eligible voters get to cast their ballot, and that those ballots get counted. With our new PowerPoint we’ll help you be ready to respond to any attacks.*

Please note that this is a HYBRID MEETING! **You will receive a zoom link after you complete your registration**, in case you'd prefer to join us virtually.

*Indivisible ADK/Saratoga is a local chapter of [Indivisible](http://Indivisible.org), active in NY's Warren, Washington, and Saratoga counties, that welcomes people with our shared values and goals. We organize and mobilize for actions that safeguard and advocate for vulnerable communities, protect human rights, guard our planet, elect progressive candidates, and protect democracy. We are committed to non-violence as a guiding principle in everything we do.*

events.title: Our Voices Will Be Heard - Stand Up for Our Democracy!
events.description:
This is a local Indivisible event, happening in Johnstown on Sunday October 18th!

With the outrages perpetrated by the Trump Administration mounting by the day, we are coming to raise our voices in protest and to encourage action. 

We recognize that the most meaningful way to be heard is by our full participation in the voting process. So we will show up with our flags, our banners, and our signs in order to peacefully and respectfully express our views. 

But MOST IMPORTANTLY, we commit to the steps below. (Use of the Vote411 website, developed by the League of Women Voters is encouraged. )
* Checking our registration NOW to make sure we are able to participate in the fall election.
* Helping others to check their registration status/ getting registered to vote. Deadline to register is Oct 24th.
* Making a plan to VOTE EARLY and including family and loved ones in our plans!
* First day of early voting in NYS is Oct 24th and the last day of early voting is Nov 1st. We'll vote on day one if possible!
* If voting by mail, submit your ballot ASAP, preferably by delivering it to your local Board of Elections or at a Ballot Drop Box.
* We will share about our voting plans and actions on Social Media to encourage others to participate.
* We may even write a Letter to the Editor of our local newspaper, encouraging others to exercise their precious right to vote!

***A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.***

events.title: Installation of Democratic Yard Signs at Polling Stations in Washington County
events.description:
Join the quick action team to set up Democratic yard signs at polling stations for this election! 

This action will support:
- Jerri Green for Governor
- Marquita Bradshaw for US Senate
- Kristi Burke for US House
- Brad Batt for TN State House District 6
- Sarah Jayne Della Vecchia for TN State House District 7
- Dave Adams for JC Commission
- Sylvain Bruni for JC Commission
- Ryan Berkley for JC School Board

## For early voting
We will deploy on **Monday, October 12**. We'll meet at WCDP HQ starting at 5 pm and load up signs, then caravan to the three early voting sites (Freedom Hall, Gray Fire Station, and JBO School).

On **Thursday, October 29**, we will pick up the signs that need to be removed from the JBO School and Freedom Hall (partial pick-up) and from the Gray Fire Station (all signs) starting at 5 pm.

## For election day
We will deploy on **Monday, November 2**. We'll meet up at WCDP HQ starting at 5 pm and load up signs. Then, teams will go to the 20 polling locations with the relevant set of signs. 

Election day signs will be removed on **Tuesday, November 3** starting at 8 pm after voting ends. All signs will be returned to WCDP HQ.

events.title: Understanding HR 1: What the New Federal Budget Law Means for Lake County
events.description:
Join the Lake County Democratic Central Committee for a nonpartisan Community Forum on Medi-Cal, CalFresh, and the Local Impact of Federal Budget Changes.

Pre registration is required! To get the Zoom Link Register Here: https://us06web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_VVyeq-r2QZ2aKm9-XrCvkw

This is an informational Zoom webinar examining how HR 1, the recently enacted federal budget law, may affect residents of Lake County. This non-campaign educational forum will focus on the two programs that touch the greatest number of local households: Medi-Cal and CalFresh. 

Panelists will discuss what the changes could mean for healthcare access, food assistance, local government, and community services. Featured speakers include Mike McGuire, State Senator; Brad Rasmussen, County Supervisor; Allison Goodwin ,Redwood Empire Food Bank, CEO; Ben Anderson, Interim CEO, Mendocino Community Health Clinic.

Whether you receive these benefits, work with affected populations, or simply want to better understand how federal policy impacts Lake County, this webinar will provide practical information and an opportunity to hear from local and regional leaders.

events.title: What's on Your Ballot? NYC's 5 Charter Amendment Proposals
events.description:
Join us for an information session on the five NYC Charter Amendment Proposals on the November 2026 ballot!

We'll start with a brief overview of the ballot*, including the major federal, state, and judicial races. Then we'll explore how the five charter proposals came about, the role of the Charter Revision Commission, and the broader political context, including the balance of power between the mayor, City Council, and other stakeholders.

For each of the five proposals, we'll review the facts, share our personal perspectives, and address questions.

**Have questions already?** We want to hear them! Please send questions in advance to [jacksonheightsindivisible@gmail.com](jacksonheightsindivisible@gmail.com). We'll do our best to address as many as possible during the session. If we run out of time, we'll follow up by email.

### Read up before the session
Here are some resources to help you learn more about the proposals:

- [League of Women Voters of NYC: 2026 Ballot Proposals](https://lwvnyc.org/proposals-2026/)
- [NYC Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE)](https://www.nyc.gov/coge)
- [NYC FAST](https://www.nyc.gov/fast)
- [NYC Votes: 2026 Ballot Proposals](https://www.nycvotes.org/whats-on-the-ballot/2026-ballot-proposals/)
- [The City Reporter: 2026 Ballot Questions](https://thecityreporter.nyc/2026/09/23/ballot-questions-voting-november-election)
- [Citizens Union: Recommendations on the Five 2026 Charter Proposals](https://citizensunion.org/document/2026-10-01/citizens-union-recommends-a-yes-vote-on-all-five-2026-charter-proposals/)

Our goal is to help everyone understand what these proposals would change, ask questions, hear different perspectives, and make informed decisions. The session will be recorded and shared afterward.

We look forward to seeing you!

*We can't cover every ballot variation across the city, so we'll be basing this on the sample ballot of a Jackson Heights resident.

Alongside each candle, we will share concrete calls to action that anyone can take to demand that Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good. events.title: It's Up to Us: Early Vote Phone Bank - Wednesdays
events.description:
It’s up to us to make sure every voter in our community has a plan to make their voice heard! Join Indivisible Ogle County for our virtual Get Out the Early Vote  phone bank. We will be reaching out to local voters to ensure they know when, where, and how to cast their ballot early and share information regarding endorsed candidates Paul Nolley and Julianna Stratton.

Whether you’re a seasoned caller or phone banking for the first time, we’ll start with a brief training, walk through the script together, and support each other live on Zoom while we make calls.

## Before You Join: Required Tech & Setup
To ensure a smooth experience, please complete these two steps before the event begins:

Create an ActionID Account:

Our calling platform uses ActionID to secure your account and save your progress. If you don't already have one, please create an account ahead of time at VAN ActionID Login. - Directions will be sent upon sign up.

Prepare Two Devices:

For the best phone banking experience, you will need two separate devices:

Device 1 (Laptop, Tablet, or Computer): To log into Zoom for our team check-in, live support, and to view the call script/voter list.

Device 2 (Cell Phone): To make the phone calls.


## What to Expect
First 15–20 Mins: Welcome, ActionID check-in, and quick training on the script.

45–60 Mins: Live phone banking with the group (on mute in Zoom, but with chat/support available if you have questions).

Final 10 Mins: Quick wrap-up, debrief, and celebrating our impact!

# Every call counts. Sign up today and help us lock in the early vote!

events.title: Our Voice, Our Vote, Our Country

location.venue: U.S. Highway 8 Bridge at St. Croix River

events.description:
Join Polk Burnett Indivisible on Sunday, October 18, from 1 - 3 p.m. on the Interstate Bridge to show our love of country and our devotion to the Constitution. Our signs will celebrate the right of all citizens to choose their leaders in free and fair elections. We will encourage everyone driving by to exercise that precious right on November 3 ... or before!

A few ideas to stoke your creativity:
-Slogans that convince someone to vote for the first time.
-Share why you vote.
-Motivational slogans like “Rural Votes Matter” or "Find 3 new people to vote"
-Information-only signs: "Voting early in Wisconsin begins Oct 20" "Mail your absentee ballot by Oct 20"
No time to make a sign? We'll have extras there for you to use.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to these events.

# "Bring Your Own Book" Club with NELC-Indivisible

## The freedom to read is under attack - so let’s do something about it!

**NE Lake County Indivisible** is hosting a **"Bring Your Own Book" Club.** For the month of November, we will explore the theme of **Indigenous peoples.** 

Participants are encouraged to read ANY book relevant to Indigenous peoples' histories, characters, and lives. Books may be fiction or nonfiction. 

📅Date: Saturday November 21

🕝Time: 2:00-4:00pm

📍Location: Warren Newport Public Library

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

More about this "Let Freedom READ" initiative:

This event is following interest from our October 10 "Let Freedom Read" meeting which argues that now more than ever, we need to encourage literacy, inclusivity, and freedom of choice. These events are built upon the importance of defending books from censorship, standing up for libraries, and taking action in support of literacy and education. 

Let Freedom READ is a national effort. More information can be found here: bit.ly/LetFreedomReadDay

Want to take action NOW? Sign a petition here: https://uniteagainstbookbans.org/take-action

Have more time to give in support of BANNED BOOKS? Check out ideas for action here: https://bannedbooksweek.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/ALA_DayofAction_OneSheet_Final.pdf 

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### Some quotes from past participants:
- "It was great working with like minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"
- "It was fun working with people who share your feelings about what's happening in our country and overseas. I find it inspiring and it gives me hope."
- "great turnout, super well organized. welcoming and fun."
- "Well organized. Liked the materials included in the kits. Good location. Nice people. Thank you very much!"
- "I took action for NE Lake County IL Indivisible because last time we put together whistle kits, I was impressed by how organized the work was, how professional, encouraging and friendly the leaders were. It was the same this time. The leaders told us about other opportunities with the organization. They sat and chatted with the groups at each of the tables. The volunteers were all friendly. I felt able to speak freely. We didn't speak of frustrations. We talked of opportunity for helping others." 

## *ABOUT NE LAKE COUNTY INDIVISIBLE:*

NE Lake County IL Indivisible is a nonpartisan grassroots organization founded in 2025 in defense of democracy. We are Lake County residents working together to protect elections and neighbors. We aim to support targeted populations and take action on a local and national level to push back against authoritarianism. We welcome everyone, whether you voted this way or that way, or didn't vote at all in 2024.

### More about us can be found here:

### https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org
### https://linktr.ee/nelakecountyindivisible

events.title: A Joint Letter to End Foreign Wars Together
events.description:
Dear Congressman Derek Tran,

The Pentagon now confirms 21 U.S. service members killed and at least 865 wounded in the war with Iran. As a veteran, you understand what that means for military families.

Besides, the Iran War is destroying our lives and our future. As you said, resources should be directed to help American families, improve our local infrastructure, protect and honor our veterans, strengthen our health care and education, and so much more. 

Congress must strengthen its oversight of the executive branch's power to initiate unnecessary wars. We recognize your leadership and strong voice on ending foreign wars. We cannot bear another unnecessary war — now or in the future. 

We hope you will clarify your stance and your plan, including:

•	Clearly and publicly articulating the necessity of ending the Iran War.

•	Explaining how you will work to end this war.

•	Committing to continue your oversight role at the congressional level, ensuring war powers return to the constitutional framework.

•	Entering constituents' appeals and stories into the Congressional Record, so the people's voices become part of the official archive.

We, the people, are tired of foreign wars. The time to end this is now.

Looking forward to your response.

Respectfully,

Co-Sponsors:

Women Forward

Davis Democratic Club

Field Team 6

50501Supporters

events.title: Meet Your Candidates — An Evening at the Red Rooster
events.description:
Tuesday, October 20 | 5:00–7:00 PM MST
📍 Red Rooster Cafe
901 Main St.
Cottonwood, AZ

Join us at the Red Rooster for an evening with Democratic candidates and local leaders.

This is a chance to meet the people asking for your vote, hear what they stand for, and ask questions directly.

🗳️ Meet the Candidates

Christine Dargon — Arizona State Senate
State Senators help write and vote on Arizona's laws and state budget. The Senate plays a major role in decisions affecting education, healthcare, water, public safety, infrastructure, and the economy.

Nick Mansour — Arizona State Treasurer
The State Treasurer serves as Arizona's chief banking and investment officer, managing state funds and overseeing the state's financial resources. The office plays an important role in protecting public funds and managing Arizona's finances responsibly.

Kris Mayes — Arizona Attorney General
The Attorney General is Arizona's chief legal officer and represents the state in legal matters. The office also plays an important role in consumer protection, public safety, civil rights, and enforcing Arizona law.

Sandy Zalecki — Arizona House of Representatives
Members of the Arizona House help create and vote on state laws and the state budget. Their decisions can directly affect education, water, healthcare, public safety, local government, and Arizona families.

🏛️ Plus: A Conversation About the “Jail Tax”
We'll also hear from County Supervisor Nikki Check about the “Jail Tax” and issues facing Yavapai County.

County government has a direct impact on many of the services we rely on every day, making this a great opportunity to learn more about an important local issue.

💗 Come Meet Your Candidates!

You don't have to be an expert on every race. Come listen, ask questions, and get informed before you vote.

Co-sponsored with Indivisible CCC.

Bring a friend, grab a seat, and join the conversation at the Red Rooster!

Join Texas Together as we knock doors to get out the vote for James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, Vikki Goodwin, and Democratic candidates down the ballot!

events.description:
Join Team Kirschner and Team Bellamy for a Joint Manatee County Canvass in District 5, Lakewood Ranch area.

events.title: Filipino Sign-Waving Celebration

address_lines: Seward Highway & East Northern Lights Boulevard

events.description:
Samahan kami sa pagsisimula ng maagang pagboto sa pamamagitan ng isang masiglang selebrasyon ng pagwawagayway ng mga karatula! 📣 Lunes, Oktubre 19 ⏰ 6–8 AM at 4–6 PM 📍 Sa kanto ng E. Northern Lights Blvd. at New Seward Highway, sa tapat ng Midtown Mall.
Dalhin ang inyong sigla, anyayahan ang inyong mga kaibigan, at tulungan kaming ipakita sa Alaska ang kapangyarihan ng pakikilahok ng komunidad! Depende sa dami ng dadalo, magdaragdag kami ng higit pang mga lokasyon para sa pagwawagayway ng mga karatula sa buong Anchorage at sa iba’t ibang bahagi ng estado.
Magpapatuloy ang pagwawagayway ng mga karatula tuwing Lunes at Biyernes, sa parehong mga oras at lokasyon, hanggang sa ating huling kaganapan: 🎉 Martes, Nobyembre 3 — 6–8 AM at 4–6 PM.
Masiyahan sa musika, pagkain, at napakaraming enerhiya habang tinutulungan kaming bumuo ng momentum. Sama-sama nating gawing bahagi ng buong Alaska ang pagwawagayway ng mga karatula!
Pakibahagi ang post na ito at anyayahan ang iba na sumali! 📣 Alaska, simulan natin ang maagang pagboto sa pamamagitan ng isang statewide wave of support! 🇺🇸

events.description:
¡Acompáñanos a dar inicio a la votación anticipada con una celebración llena de energía y carteles de apoyo! 📣 Lunes 19 de octubre ⏰ De 6 a 8 a. m. y de 4 a 6 p. m. 📍 En la esquina de E. Northern Lights Blvd. y New Seward Highway, frente a Midtown Mall.
¡Trae tu entusiasmo, invita a tus amistades y ayúdanos a mostrarle a Alaska el poder de la participación comunitaria! Dependiendo de la cantidad de personas que participen, añadiremos más lugares para ondear carteles en Anchorage y en todo el estado.
La actividad de ondear carteles continuará todos los lunes y viernes, en los mismos horarios y lugares, hasta nuestro evento final: 🎉 Martes 3 de noviembre — de 6 a 8 a. m. y de 4 a 6 p. m.
Disfruta de música, comida y mucha energía mientras nos ayudas a generar impulso. ¡Hagamos que ondear carteles sea una actividad presente en todo Alaska!
¡Comparte esta publicación e invita a otras personas a participar! 📣 ¡Alaska, iniciemos la votación anticipada con una ola estatal de apoyo! 🇺🇸

events.title: Community Outreach: Connect with Texans in Austin at the Viva la Vida Festival & Parade
events.description:
Skip the doorbell. We’re taking the conversation to where people already gather: at the market, on campus, outside the big event. We’re testing a new way to reach people there, and we want you to help us do it. Too often, outreach finds the same folks over and over while plenty of neighbors never hear from anyone. Community outreach is about changing that.

We’ll meet up, do a quick training, and then head to a busy spot nearby to chat with people passing through. You’ll invite them to learn more about RALLY TX, a paid community engagement program, and sign up right then on their phones with a quick QR code scan.

No experience is necessary. We’ll provide a training, a script, a clipboard, and everything else you need. Conversations are short, friendly, and easy to learn.

Come ready to meet some neighbors, try something new, and share what you saw and heard afterward so we can make the program better.

events.title: Fall Into Voting Season!  Donuts, cider, coffee...and getting out the vote! 🍂
events.description:
### FALL INTO VOTING SEASON! 🍂

Join the Columbia County Dems on Friday, October 23rd for a perfect fall day of good company, great donuts, delicious coffee & apple cider, and getting out the vote!

_Did you know ... you can go to the Columbia County Elections Office and vote ON DEMAND? Stop by Dem Headquarters to learn more, pick up an application, and maybe even meet some great new friends!_

🍩 **Do-Nut wait to vote!** 😉

Do your part to build the BLUE WAVE by getting your ballot turned in ASAP. Hang out with us for some fall goodies and hear what else we can do to get out the vote in the final days before Election Day!


**A few voting season reminders:** 

- The last day to register to vote or update your registration is Monday, October 19th
- The last day to request your mail-in ballot is Tuesday, October 27th (but don’t wait until then!)
- You can vote on-demand at the Columbia County Elections Office until Tuesday, October 27th
- Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd. The polls will be open from 7AM to 8PM

events.title: 10/18 - Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization @ Pasadena Indoor Flea Market (Houston)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Election Day, November 3rd is around the corner. Join us to make a huge difference! Create awareness in the Hispanic community about the consequential midterm election.  We’ll be doing GOTV and help the community make a voting plan.  Spanish Speaking Volunteers is a HUGE PLUS but everyone is need. All Hands on Deck before Early Voting!

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—like transit centers, shopping districts, community plazas, and busy neighborhoods—we meet Texans right where they are to build lasting progressive power.

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Team Talarico Volunteers and Powered by People for a high-impact **Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization** shift at **Pasadena Indoor Flea Market**! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico.  We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting? 
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico, and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and create excitement for Talarico and the entire blue slate.
- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Check voters’ status on the spot
- Register eligible voters when we have a VDR at the event. Or hand out the paper voter registration form.
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:

- **12:00-12:30am: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, start training on time, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals.

- **12:30am-2:30pm: Hotspotting & Voter Registration** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to community members, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **2:30-3:00pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, turn in completed registration forms, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

**We’ll table so meet us at the table with “Talarico for Texas “ banner inside the flea market.**

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**:  We’ll table so meet us at the table with Talarico sign in the flea market.  


- **Volunteer Parking**:  Parking available at flea market parking lot. 

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

- **If you are a VDR**: Your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, voter registration forms, and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

events.title: For The People: A Union Rally To Elect Union Members with the Dropkick Murphys and Brian Poindexter
events.description:
IT'S TIME THE WORKING CLASS TAKE CHARGE OF GOVERNMENT!

The labor movement has always been a rebellion — built by working people who refused to bow down, back off, or let the powerful call the shots.

Across Ohio, union members and their family have been standing up to the donor class and running for offce to unrig our economy. This year, it's time to turn up that volume and bring the fighting spirit of working-class solidarity to the polls. For centuries, music, rebellion, and people power have come together in the fight for a democracy that belongs to ALL of us. We continue that tradition with the FOR THE PEOPLE RALLY!

Come prepared for some good old-fashioned union solidarity. AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler American Federation of Teachers President Randi Weingarten plus other union leaders will be on hand to help motivate the labor movement to work the next week and a half to elect over a dozen union members, including Ironworker Brian Poindexter in CD 7. The night will cap off with an acoustic set by the Dropkick Murphys

SHOW UP. BRING YOUR PEOPLE. GET TO THE POLLS. CAST YOUR BALLOT. STAND UP FOR EVERYONE'S RIGHT TO VOTE — AND MAKE DAMN SURE EVERY VOTE GETS COUNTED!!!

Opportunities to sign up to volunteer will be available at the event. From canvassing fellow union families to volunteering to protect the vote on Election Day, we will need you to fight back against this regime in the White House.

*RSVP does not guarantee entry if event hits maximum capacity. Doors open at 4:00pm, with the Brute Squad, an all-union band, starting us off at 4:30pm. The Dropkick Murphys are planned to take the stage around 6:00pm.  Food trucks will be on site. *ALL AGES WELCOME

Not a union member? No worries. You can sign up in site to be a member of Working America, the community affiliate of the AFL-CIO, to join us for this FREE event.

events.title: Phone Bank + Pizza + Dance Party in Menlo Park

events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

After the phone bank we'll chow down on pizza and shake out all the feelings with a little dance party.

## Logistics:

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.description:
There are only three political positions in America today:

1) I like the fascism

2) I'll acquiesce to the fascism (reasons for this one vary: money, cowardice, access, denial, Fox News, etc)

3) I oppose the fascism

The rest is details.

If you are in group 3, join us every Saturday from 11 AM - 1:00 PM in front of Tesla Motors, Lyndhurst, OH.

Rules & Reminders: Gather in front of Tesla Motors, 5180 Mayfield Rd, Lyndhurst, OH. Do not park in their lot or engage with their employees and customers. Bring a sign, flag and friends, we have extras if you need them. Stay on the sidewalk & allow pedestrians to pass, Do not jaywalk across Mayfield Road (police will be watching), Use the crosswalk just west of Tesla, Don't block driveway entrances or exits, Don't harass Tesla customers or employees, Do not argue with counter protesters, PROTEST PEACEFULLY. Watch for peacekeepers in yellow vests and immediately report any disturbances to them. Follow any instructions from Lyndhurst Police.

Parking is available at Messiah Lutheran Church, 5200 Mayfield Road. Please be respectful and park on the EAST SIDE of the lot first (away from the Tesla Store). Additional parking is available at the Lyndhurst Community of Faith Church, 5312 Mayfield Road. Please enter the EAST DRIVEWAY as the west driveway is exit only. Local street parking is also just a short stroll away.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. No one is coming to save us. Not politicians, not the media, not the courts.

Indivisable is a peaceful protest movement. We oppose violence, vandalism and destruction of property. This protest is a lawful exercise of our First Amendment right to peaceful assembly.

A core principle behind all Indivisable events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: Your vote, your voice @ NVC with NVC Progressives
events.description:
In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join us, NVC Progressives Club and local candidates for the Every Campus Counts tour at NVC! We are showing up to talk to students, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will:

Engage directly with existing and potential student voters
Register eligible voters on the spot
Connect with voters using Reach, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day
Voter Registrar Requirements
All volunteers are welcome! There are plenty of vital roles for everyone, whether you are certified or not.
Important Note: If you want to physically register voters at this event, you MUST be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (VDR) in at least Bexar County.
Not certified yet? Don't worry! You can get certified ahead of time by signing up for our VDR Training.
Shift Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, we ask all volunteers to arrive 60 minutes before event starts for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[1:00-2:00pm]: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals before the crowd gathers.
[2:00pm-3:30pm] Voter Registration & Mobilization | The main event! We hit the campus ground running, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach with candidates providing encouragement.
[3:30-4:30pm]: Takedown & Post-Event Debrief | We will pack up our gear, tally our total registrations, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps
How to Prepare
Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our mandatory online volunteer training on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

Where to Meet & Park
Meeting Location: Outside of Cypress Campus Center.
Volunteer Parking: Lot 10 near Cypress Campus Center is recommended. All parking at Northwest Vista College is free for both students and visitors.
What to Bring

events.title: Poll Runner: Virtual Training
events.description:
Election Night Volunteer Training: Precinct Results Reporting!

The Oklahoma Democratic Party is recruiting Election Night volunteers to help collect and report precinct-level election results across the state. We especially need volunteers in Cleveland, Canadian, Pottawatomie, Oklahoma, and Tulsa Counties.

Join us for a virtual Zoom training to learn how to serve as an Election Night Precinct Results Volunteer. This is a simple but incredibly important role that helps our team independently track election results as they are reported.

What You'll Learn:

How to locate publicly posted election results at your assigned polling location after polls close at 7:00 PM.

How to identify the official precinct results tape and capture clear, readable photographs.

How to ensure your photographs include the precinct number and results for all required races.

How to submit your results directly to our Election Night reporting team via text message.

What to do if results are delayed or difficult to locate.

What to Expect on Election Night:

Volunteers will be assigned one or more polling locations to visit after polls close at 7:00 PM. Once poll workers publicly post the precinct results, volunteers will photograph the results and text them to our reporting team. Results may not be posted until 7:15 or 7:30 PM, so volunteers should be prepared to wait.

No prior experience is necessary! All you need is a smartphone with a camera, reliable transportation to your assigned polling location, and a willingness to help.

Whether you're a first-time volunteer or a seasoned election volunteer, your participation will help us gather timely, accurate results from communities across Oklahoma.

Sign up for this Zoom training and help us make every precinct count on Election Night!

events.description:
Join VoteVets & VetsForward (VetsFWD) for a special Veterans Happy Hour in Phoenix, AZ with two fellow veterans and Arizona leaders: U.S. Senator Mark Kelly, a Navy combat veteran, and Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes, a Marine Corps veteran!

For more than 20 years, VoteVets has worked to organize and empower veterans, military families, and supporters across the country. We're excited to partner with VetsForward, a veteran-led organization dedicated to defending democracy through grassroots advocacy and elevating veteran voices on issues including voting rights, VA care, and protecting individual freedoms.

Together, we believe that service doesn't stop when we take off the uniform and that veterans have an important role to play in shaping the future of our communities and our country.

Come connect with fellow veterans and military families, meet members of the VoteVets and VetsForward teams, and hear from two Arizona leaders who have continued their commitment to public service.

Meet Our Special Guests

U.S. Senator Mark Kelly — Navy Veteran

Senator Mark Kelly is a retired Navy combat pilot, engineer, and former NASA astronaut. During his military service, he flew 39 combat missions during Operation Desert Storm and deployed aboard the USS Midway. He later completed four space shuttle missions before continuing his public service in the U.S. Senate, where he has represented Arizona since 2020.

Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes — Marine Corps Veteran

Secretary Adrian Fontes served on active duty in the U.S. Marine Corps. Raised in Nogales, Arizona, he comes from a family with a strong tradition of military and public service. Following his military service, he became an attorney and prosecutor, later serving as Maricopa County Recorder before being elected Arizona Secretary of State.

Event Details

⏰ 6:30 PM

events.description:
Join the Westside Democratic HQ on Sunday, Oct. 18 for a morning canvassing event in CD-45 to support Congressman Derek Tran!

We'll be talking to voters in Norwalk, located in Los Angeles County.  We need voters in this newly redistricted area to show up in the Midterm elections and re-elect Congressman Tran.

Keeping this district BLUE is mission-critical to flipping the House in November!  Let's give Congressman Tran a Democratic majority, so he can advance his ideas to help working people, older adults, veterans, and ALL Americans.

We'll meet at the WDHQ to grab coffee and bagels at 8:00 a.m. on Saturday, Oct. 17, and then head out at 8:30 a.m. to Norwalk to meet the Tran campaign.  We'll knock on doors and talk with voters from 10:00 a.m. to about 1:00 p.m.

Join Common Cause Arizona and Civic Engagement Beyond Voting for a virtual Poll Monitor training webinar!

Common Cause Arizona is partnering with Civic Engagement Beyond Voting to equip Arizonans with the tools and knowledge to become nonpartisan poll monitors, stationed outside the 75-foot line at polling places to engage with voters and report any voting issues.

Poll monitors are the first line of defense against attempts to discourage voters and spread disinformation. Through our Non-Partisan Poll Monitor program, you have the opportunity to help ensure that the voices of Arizonans are heard. This is a part of a series of in-person & virtual Election Protection Poll Monitor trainings across Arizona. Sign up to help voters this November and help your community feel supported in the decision to cast their ballot. It’s easy, it’s fun, and it’s a great way to support democracy!

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
Douglas County Thrives is hosting a screening of a documentary about what motherhood really looks like in America today.

Douglas County Thrives is an economic mobility project in service of anti-poverty goals outlined in the 2024-2029 Douglas County Community Health Improvement Plan (CHIP). The goal of Douglas County Thrives is to increase the percentage of single female headed households in Douglas County living at or able the ALICE (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed) standard. 

Community members are invited to attend the documentary screening and discuss opportunities to improve the well-being of families through focused efforts to support single female headed households in Douglas County.

events.title: Who's Got the Power? WE DO!  Georgia WFP × Vote Save America Canvass Launch & Happy Hour
events.description:
Knock Doors. Build Power. Celebrate Together!
Georgia WFP Canvass Launch + Post-Canvass Happy Hour

Georgia, we're taking it to the doors — and then we're getting together to celebrate!

Join Georgia Working Families Party and Vote Save America on Sunday, October 18, for a day of community, connection, and organizing in Atlanta.

With Election Day just around the corner, we're bringing together candidates, organizers, volunteers, and neighbors for conversations about the issues affecting working families across Georgia.

Joining us for the day:

- Peter Hubbard — Candidate for Georgia Public Service Commission, District 3
- Rohit Malhotra — Candidate for Fulton County Commission, District 4
- Kenn Collier — Candidate for Georgia State House, District 62
- Ruwa Romman — Candidate for Georgia State Senate, District 7
- Shaniqua McClendon — President, Vote Save America
- Britney Whaley — Southeast Regional Director, Working Families Party

And when the canvassing is done? We're keeping the good energy going with a post-canvass happy hour!

Come unwind, meet fellow volunteers, connect with organizers, and enjoy a little well-earned fun. Food and drinks will be provided.

One Event. Two Shifts. Join Us for Either or Both!

SHIFT 1: Canvass Launch + Door Knocking

📅 Sunday, October 18, 2026

🕙 10 AM–1 PM

📍 Atlanta, GA — Meeting location shared with registrants

Never canvassed before? No problem! We'll provide training, materials, and everything you need to get started. Just bring comfortable shoes, water, and a willingness to connect with your neighbors.

SHIFT 2: Post-Canvass Happy Hour

📅 Sunday, October 18, 2026

🕒 Time: 1:00 PM - 4:00 PM

📍 Location: TBD

Bring a friend, meet some new people, and spend your Sunday connecting with fellow Georgians.

Because the future of Georgia isn't going to knock on doors by itself -- but we are!

events.title: After the Midterms -- Now What? with Professor Sam Wang
events.description:
We don't yet know the outcomes of the 2026 midterm elections, but there's no doubt we'll need to regroup, reset our priorities, and -- hopefully! -- celebrate. Happily, there's no one better to strategize with than Professor Sam Wang. Many of us were impressed with Dr. Wang when he ran for US Congress in NJ's 12th district, and we are thrilled to have the opportunity to hear from him again. He'll address the fallout from the election, how to think about the impacts both short- and long-term, and what this means for our local activism. Please join us for this lively and thought-provoking discussion!

**About Sam Wang**

Sam Wang is a professor of neuroscience at Princeton University and a pioneer in the fight for our democracy and against gerrymandering. He has authored books on how the brain functions, and he worked on science and education policy in the US Senate. In 2026, he ran for the US Congress in New Jersey's 12th Congressional District, and while he didn't win in the primary election, for many of us, he won our highest regard. 

Sam is now continuing the campaign in the form of Third Mountain Action, an organization to save and rebuild democracy and science.

events.title: Medway DTC Election Day Visibility Tent
events.description:
Join us on November 3rd to staff our visibility tent outside the polls at Medway Middle School. We are there when the polls open until the polls close. A few of us stay to hear the unofficial results read after we pack up. That's a lot of hours, so sign ups are important to make sure that every hour is covered. It's more fun with more people, so share this with friends and sign up for as many shifts throughout the day as you'd like. 

Responsibilities are minimal and this is typically an exciting and energizing event. We have signs you can hold. And we also have chairs in the shade if you just want to join us for a bit. There is always a collection of Halloween candy and other goodies to keep us going. 

Committee members, if you are able, please commit to at least an hour, or join us for set up or clean up. Do you lean blue, but you're not a member?  You are very welcome to join us. We would love your help!  

Set up will begin at 6:45 and should only take about 15 minutes.

Clean up begins near the end of the 7:00 pm shift. There is no separate shift for clean up. If you can't help with clean up, you can still sign up for that shift. Signing up for that shift does not require you to clean up.
