events.title: 10/18 - Hotspotting and Voter Mobilization @ Aldine - Sunny Flea Market(Houston)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Election Day, November 3rd is around the corner. Join us to make a huge difference! Create awareness in the Hispanic community about the consequential midterm election.  We’ll be doing GOTV and help the community make a voting plan.  Spanish Speaking Volunteers is a HUGE PLUS but everyone is need. All Hands on Deck before Early Voting! We will be NON-Partisan. 

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—like transit centers, shopping districts, community plazas, and busy neighborhoods—we meet Texans right where they are to build lasting progressive power.

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Team Talarico Volunteers and Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift at **Aldine Sunny Flea Market**! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement about upcoming midterm election.  We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting? 
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement about upcoming midterm election , and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and inform them about upcoming election. **Note, for this hotspot we will be non partisan, mainly focusing creating awareness, the important of this mid term election & voter mobilization.**
- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- We are NOT registering voters until after November 3rd
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:

- **[1:00-1:30am]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, start training on time, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals.

- **[1:30-3:30pm] Hotspotting & Voter Registration** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to community members, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **[3:30-4:00pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

**We’ll table in the flea market. Note, for this event, we’ll be non-partisan**

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**:  We’ll table so meet us at the table in the flea market.  Host will provide details on exactly where our table will be. 

- **Volunteer Parking**:  Parking available at flea market parking lot. 

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing. 

- **Wear VOTE or PxP t-shirts but NOT any candidate shirts.  The event is non partisan. Election awareness & Voter mobilization only.**

- **If you are a VDR**: Your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, voter registration forms, and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

events.title: James Malone PA SD36 Postcard Distribution

address_lines: Arlington Center Porch (address shared upon registration)

events.description:
Swing Blue Alliance is focusing our efforts in Pennsylvania to flip the State Senate and three key congressional districts, crucial for Democratic control of the US House. Join us for this final postcard campaign before the midterms!

After his HISTORIC special election victory in March 2025, State Senator James Malone became the FIRST Democrat to represent this district since 1890. He is also the first Latino State Senator in Pennsylvania.

We're working to support Sen. Malone in his campaign to keep his seat in a historically red district, one of the top priorities in PA this election cycle. Democrats have a chance to counter Republican redistricting and add up to 4 Democratic members of Congress by flipping the Pennsylvania state senate to Democratic control and winning a trifecta.

Our state legislative candidate cards have also been shown to have up-ballot impact and will help increase votes for Democratic congressional and state-wide candidates.

Malone's priorities are those of his constituents. From public school access to affordability to common-sense gun laws, he truly is a champion of the people. He was the candidate to be endorsed by Governor Josh Shapiro and Lt. Governor Austin Davis in the midterms. Additionally, Malone has been endorsed by labor unions across his district.

The postcards are easy to complete: they only require writing a few words and placing an address label and stamp on the card before mailing.

The Malone campaign is paying to print these postcards. Swing Blue Alliance is raising funds to offset that expense. Please consider donating $6.50 per packet (the campaign’s cost) at https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mailformalone

events.title: Final Weekend GOTV Volunteer Blitz
events.description:
Final Weekend GOTV Volunteer Blitz

Saturday, Oct. 31 through Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3 | 10 AM-6 PM | 75 Queensway Drive

This is it. Four days remain, and every conversation we have between now and 6 PM on Tuesday could be the one that gets a neighbor to the polls.

We’re opening HQ for a final weekend GOTV volunteer blitz, and we need you. Using updated voter data from the election board, we’ll be reaching out to voters who haven’t cast a ballot yet. They need a friendly reminder, a plan to vote, and a little encouragement, and that’s where you come in.

What you’ll do

Phone bank from HQ, calling voters who haven’t voted yet
Canvass by knocking on doors in your neighborhood or nearby areas
Help people find their polling place, confirm their hours, and make a plan to vote

How it works

Shifts are 2 hours long, running from 10 AM to 6 PM each day: 10-12, 12-2, 2-4, and 4-6
Sign up for one shift or several. The more the better!
No experience needed. We’ll train you when you arrive and give you everything you need: scripts, walk lists, and a team to work with.

Dates

Saturday, Oct. 31
Sunday, Nov. 1
Monday, Nov. 2
Tuesday, Nov. 3 (Election Day, until polls close at 6 PM)

Where
Campaign HQ, 75 Queensway Drive

Bring a phone charger, water, and comfortable shoes if you’re canvassing. We’ll have snacks on hand!

Elections are decided by the people who show up, and that includes you. Pick your shifts below and bring a friend.

Sign up now and help us finish strong!

He has facilitated tax breaks for his corporate cronies. He's siphoned our tax dollars into his insurance company's coffers. And he's behaved like a mafia boss towards anyone who has dared to push back.

events.title: Fighting Oligarchy Tour Volunteer Sign-up with Bernie Sanders- VOTER ENGAGEMENT - (El Paso, TX)
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: This is a volunteer signup page for Powered by People's voter mobilization team. Signing up here will register you as a volunteer to work the event, not as a general attendee for the rally itself. Because we are partnering with Senator Sanders, all schedule details and locations are subject to change until finalized by the parties. We will send out confirmed logistics closer to the event date._

#### Ready to do the work that actually works?
In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for the Fighting Oligarchy Tour at the Abraham Theatre in El Paso! We are showing up as volunteers to this event to fire up the rally attendees, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will:

- Engage directly with passionate rally attendees and community members
- Check voter registration statuses on the spot (ensuring no one has been purged)
- Connect with voters using Reach, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

#### Shift Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive 2 hours before doors open so that we can optimize working the line of attendees. They will be lining up way in advance, and our goal is to check voter registrations for everyone waiting to get in. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[2:30-3:30pm]**: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the site leads, and align on our goals

- **[3:30-6:00pm]** Working the Line (Part 1) | As the crowd grows ahead of doors opening, we will  start engaging the very first people in line and continue moving down the line to check registration statuses and get folks set up on Reach. Once doors open, we continue to work the line and shift to the venue to catch any remaining attendees and trickling community members before the main programming starts.

- **[6:00-7:00pm]**: Stay for the event! | Once the programming begins, volunteers are invited and encouraged to stay, enjoy the rally, and celebrate the energy with our neighbors!

- **[7:00pm-8:00pm]**: Working the Line (Part 2) | After the event, we'll sweep the line of attendees waiting to take a photo with Senator Sanders, Rep. Casar, and Beto O’rourke *** may not stay for photos

#### How to Prepare
Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our [mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/) on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

#### Where to Meet & Park
Meeting Location: Inside the Abraham Theatre at PxP table
Volunteer Parking: Street and garage parking nearby, no designated parking

#### What to Bring
To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A clear see through bag for your belongings

- Comfortable shoes (you will be on your feet talking to voters!)

Whether you knocked one door or a thousand, this night is yours. Bring a friend, bring your energy, and let’s celebrate the work, because organizing doesn’t stop on November 4th.

events.title: Kailua Kona Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age

location.venue: Queen Ka'ahumany Hwy, behind the Mormon Temple
address_lines: Queen Ka'ahumanu Hwy, south of Henry St

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Thank you for being part of this movement!

— Team Mai

events.title: Signs of Fascism: Silent Street Protest

location.venue: Town & Country, next to the sign

events.description:
The damage being done to our communities and our democracy shows up in specific patterns: attacks on the press, scapegoating whole groups of people, abuse of police power, elections being undermined. These are warning signs of authoritarianism.

The *Signs of Fascism Street Theater Protest* is a way to make those patterns visible in the most literal sense. We will stand in silence along a busy street, each person holding a stark, simple sign naming one warning sign of fascism. Without chanting or waving, we just present a visible list of dangers that people can’t easily ignore or explain away.

Please make sure to **RSVP**: the meeting place may change and we need to be able to notify you.

Here’s what to expect:

- Wear black (preferably) or very dark clothing so the focus stays on the words.  
- Hold provided “Signs of Fascism” posters.  
- We’ll stand spaced out so drivers and pedestrians have a moment to read and think about each sign. If it's hard for you to stand, feel free to bring a folding chair.
- Some of us will offer a small handout to those who pass by which explains what the signs mean and how people can get involved.

We'll be experimenting with different locations around the Peninsula and South Bay. If you can't make this one, [join the team](https://blueturnindivisible.org/register/join.cgi?team=sof) and we'll keep you updated.

Are you willing to stand up, literally, and say: **I see what is happening, and I won’t look away**? Then join us. When people see others taking that stance in public, it gives them permission to do the same.

**Organized by [Blue Turn Indivisible](https://itsblueturn.com/) and [Indivisible Palo Alto Plus](https://indivisiblepaloaltoplus.org/)**

P.S. Our team is also doing Signs of Fascism in Palo Alto on select [Fridays](https://mobilize.us/s/HYwOZo). Perhaps the time will work better for you?

events.title: Phone Bank Party in Brooklyn
events.description:
## Come phone bank with SURJNYC!

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: Access the Vote: Postcard Writing Event

location.venue: Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh - Squirrel Hill

events.description:
In partnership with Access Mob Pittsburgh and the Pittsburgh Center for Disability Justice, we are inviting you to join us for an afternoon of community and civic participation! Together, we will write postcards and letters to our disabled neighbors living in institutions, to encourage them to vote and remind them that their voices matter—we are all part of the same community.

Even if you do not personally know somebody living in an institution, your postcard or letter will be sent to a disabled voter who lives in an institutional setting, like a nursing facility.

Who: Anybody and everybody, regardless of disability status!

What: Spend an afternoon writing postcards and letters to our disabled neighbors who live in institutions, encouraging them to vote and reminding them that their voices matter!

When: Sunday, October 18, 2026, from 12:30-4:00 PM

Where: 
Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh - Squirrel Hill (Meeting Room A)
5801 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15217
events.accessibility_notes:
TRANSPORTATION + ACCESSIBILITY. 

Pittsburgh Regional Transit: The closest bus stop is located on the corner of Forbes and Murray Ave, and it is accessible via 61A, 61B, 61C, 61D, 64, and 74. 

ACCESS Paratransit & Drop-Off: The drop-off location for ACCESS and other ramped vans is on Marlborough Street, right at the Marlborough Street entrance to the Library. Please note that the path is not for parking. 

Parking: Metered parking, designated accessible parking spots, and bike racks are located in the Murray Avenue Parking Lot. Metered parking and bike racks are also available on nearby streets (Forbes Ave and Murray Ave) with designated accessible parking spots located on Marlborough Street. 

Entrances: There are three access points to CLP – Squirrel Hill. 

The first entrance is located at 5801 Forbes Avenue. This entrance is wheelchair-accessible through an automatic sliding glass door. The sidewalk is level with the entrance. The elevator to the Library is inside this vestibule. 

The second point is located inside the Murray Avenue parking garage, managed by the Parking Authority. The Murray Avenue entrance has a ramp that is located on the right side of the garage as you enter. This wheelchair-accessible ramp leads to the same elevator and vestibule as the Forbes Avenue entrance. 

The third point of access is via the sidewalk, path, and ramp on Marlborough Street. Ramped vans and/or ACCESS vans can use the path to drop users off right at the entrance to the Library. Please note that the path is not for parking. 

ASL Interpretation: ASL interpretation will be provided. 

Air Quality: Air filtration will be provided at the event, courtesy of Clean Air Tools Pittsburgh. 

Masking: High-quality N95 masks are required to attend this in-person event. 3M Aura N95 masks will be provided to all attendees. Food and drinks will not be provided at this event, so you are encouraged to eat beforehand! If you do need to eat or drink at some point during the event, you are welcome to leave the meeting room to eat/drink and return afterward. 

To ensure language accessibility, the ASL interpreter will not be masked. Instead, they will be required to test for COVID-19 (with a negative result) shortly before the event. 

Restrooms: Wheelchair-accessible restrooms are located in the library, near the Marlborough Street entrance, across from Meeting Room A. 

Remote Participation: If you are not able to attend in-person, please reach out to Mallory Hudson at Mallory@KeystoneProgress.org to request a stack of postcards. If hand-written postcards are not accessible to you, you are also welcome to email a typed letter to Mallory, who will print out your letter and mail it to a person living in a nursing facility.

events.title: Your vote, your voice @ NVC with NVC Progressives
events.description:
In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join us, NVC Progressives Club and local candidates for the Every Campus Counts tour at NVC! We are showing up to talk to students, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will:

Engage directly with existing and potential student voters Register eligible voters on the spot Connect with voters using Reach, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day Voter Registrar Requirements All volunteers are welcome! There are plenty of vital roles for everyone, whether you are certified or not. Important Note: If you want to physically register voters at this event, you MUST be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (VDR) in at least Bexar County. Not certified yet? Don't worry! You can get certified ahead of time by signing up for our VDR Training. Shift Schedule & Flow To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, we ask all volunteers to arrive 60 minutes before event starts for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[1:00-2:00pm]: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals before the crowd gathers. [2:00pm-3:30pm] Voter Registration & Mobilization | The main event! We hit the campus ground running, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach with candidates providing encouragement. [3:30-4:30pm]: Takedown & Post-Event Debrief | We will pack up our gear, tally our total registrations, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps How to Prepare Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our mandatory online volunteer training on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

Where to Meet & Park Meeting Location: Outside of Cypress Campus Center. Volunteer Parking: Lot 10 near Cypress Campus Center is recommended. All parking at Northwest Vista College is free for both students and visitors. What to Bring To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed A water bottle to stay hydrated Comfortable shoes If you are a VDR: Please bring your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity Note: Clipboards, pens, voter registration forms, and all other necessary materials will be provided at the check-in table, but feel free to bring your own backup supplies just in case!

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single campus counts. Sign up for a shift today!

events.title: WOFA Monthly Membership-MOVIE NIGHT "My Omaha"
events.description:
WOFA VA Monthly Meeting: Film Night — My Omaha, plus a Live Conversation with Director Nick Beaulieu

This month we’re doing something different. Instead of our usual meeting, we’ll watch the documentary My Omaha together and then join a live Zoom conversation with the film’s director, Nick Beaulieu.

About the film
After finishing journalism school, Nick Beaulieu went home to Omaha, Nebraska, to document the city’s growing racial justice movement. At the same time, he tried to reconnect with his father, Randy, a committed Trump supporter. That effort became more urgent when Randy was diagnosed with stage-4 cancer. Community activist Leo Louis II guides Nick through Omaha’s long history of activism. The film follows a son and a city as they work through family conflict, political and racial division, and the hard search for common ground.

At a time when so many of us are struggling to talk across political lines, including with people we love, this film is a powerful starting point for conversation.

🎬 Watch the trailer: https://www.pbs.org/video/my-omaha-trailer/

Schedule

6:30: Gather and welcome
6:45: Screening of My Omaha (85 minutes)
8:15: Live Zoom Q&A and discussion with director Nick Beaulieu



Come with your questions and reflections, and bring a friend! All are welcome.

events.title: Lets Get Free: Early Voting Kick-Off Rally
events.description:
The Human Rights Campaign (HRC) Texas invites you to join us as we come together to celebrate the power of our voices, the importance of civic engagement, and our collective commitment to equality for ALL!

With so much at stake for LGBTQ+ Texans and our communities, this rally is about more than casting a ballot. It's about showing up, standing together, and making sure our voices are heard at the ballot box.

Join HRC Texas, Dallas County Democrats, community advocates, equality voters, and allies as we kick off early voting season with energy, unity, and a shared commitment to building a Texas where everyone can live freely, authentically, and without discrimination.

What to Expect:
- An energizing gathering of LGBTQ+ advocates, allies, and equality voters.
- Opportunities to connect with community members committed to advancing equality.
- Important information about early voting and making your voice heard.

sponsor.name: End Citizens United// Let America Vote Action Fund

events.description:
Join End Citizens United for an Organizing Briefing on one of the most urgent priorities of this election cycle: Voter Protection.

In this briefing, we will discuss what is at stake for voters across the country and how you can plug in. We will be joined by a guest presenter from Deliver My Vote Education Fund, who will walk us through the Voter Protection Advocate Network (VPAN), a nationwide, nonpartisan online training program designed to equip canvassers, volunteers, and trusted community validators with the tools and confidence to protect every voter's right to participate in our democracy.

Whether you want to serve as a poll monitor, a voter protection worker, a relational organizer, or talk directly to voters as a phone banker, you'll learn how to provide voters with accurate information. This is the moment to show up!

Stick around to take action!

Directly after this briefing, End Citizens United will be hosting a phone bank. If you are interested and ready to talk to voters, in competitive congressional districts, you can jump right in and start making calls with us. 

Sign up today, and let's get to work.

*Note: The Deliver My Vote Education Fund is not a sponsor of or participant in the phone bank, and does not support or oppose any candidate or party.*

Tax billionaires. Save lives. Vote YES on Prop 40.

events.title: Election Protection Poll Observer Training with Mai
events.description:
This training is virtual but is limited to those who are available to participate in person as Poll Observers here in Kansas as part of our Election Protection Program for the General election (11/3/2026).

We’re living through a political moment that can often feel overwhelming and discouraging. By signing up for Election Protection, you are taking concrete action to protect voters in your community. We think of this work as a form of joyful resistance.

Election Protection is non-partisan. During this training, you'll learn what it means to be a poll observer, how the 866-OUR-VOTE supports voters, and how you can defend access to voting for fellow Kansans on Election Day.

Please Note: This virtual training prepares you for an in-person volunteer shift at a polling location with us here in Kansas on Election Day.

events.title: Paws To Get Early Voting Information While You Rock-The-Vote
events.description:
We are in the final stretch; no time for a CATnap. Democracy is not a spectator sport; it's a Red Dot.

Pick something and make it PAWsitive. 
Do something PAWsome. Bring someone with the right CATtitude.

Join us to paint VOTE rocks and take them with you to place in high-traffic areas around Gaston County. We will have information on early voting, how to register and vote on the same day, how to check your voter registration, and nonpartisan voter guides. You can even walk across the street and get a FREE ID and VOTE! 
If you want to see change, we need your help to convince your peers to participate in this year's midterm election.

Turnout in midterm elections is 20% lower than in presidential election years (40% vs 60%).

Just because you are motivated to vote does not mean your neighbors and friends are. Poll results are meaningless if the people polled do not show up to vote!

If you truly want to see change, we need your help to motivate our community members to vote!!!

To achieve change, we need to turn out voters who want:
* Funded Public Schools 
* Affordable Healthcare
* Affordable Housing
* Fair maps
* Voting Rights
* Fair Taxes

Time for the "Power of the People" to make sure the people in power are working for *us*!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

As we head into critical 2026 midterms, we have a real shot at taking back the houses of government and finally rolling back Donald Trump's extreme, authoritarian agenda. But we'll only succeed if we're working together. We'd love you to join us!

Ballots are in mailboxes now, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Join neighbors from across Menlo Park on Sunday, October 25 for the launch of our Get Out the Vote push.

For weeks, our volunteers have knocked on thousands of doors to find out where our neighbors stand. Now the work changes. Elections are decided by whose supporters actually vote. GOTV means making sure every neighbor who’s with us returns their ballot and votes No on P all the way down the ballot. In a race that may come down to a few hundred votes, that’s where it will be won or lost.

Let’s make sure every supporter’s vote gets counted. See you on the 25th!

events.description:
This is a special event to join canvassers in Mount Vernon for a fun evening of knocking doors! Details on location will be sent after you register to knock, most likely we will meet at the river walk or a nearby park in the neighborhoods!

What to expect

New to canvassing? That’s completely okay! No experience is required, and we’ll start every shift with a short training so everyone feels prepared before heading to the doors.

We’ll meet together at a local location, go over the basics of the conversation, show everyone how to record who they spoke with at the door, and get paired up before heading out to canvass in the community.

For your first shift, you can shadow an experienced canvasser so you can hear how they talk with folks at the door and get comfortable before jumping into conversations yourself.

Most of the shift will be spent walking through a neighborhood and having short conversations with voters. You do not need to memorize a script or be an expert. We’ll provide the information, materials, and support you need.

Please bring:

A fully charged smartphone Comfortable walking shoes Weather-appropriate clothing Water and anything else you may need while walking

Additional details, resources, talking points, MiniVAN instructions, and arrival information will be sent after signup so you have everything you need to feel prepared for your shift.

Why door knocking matters

Most of us have had an election where the ballot showed up and we realized we hadn’t researched everything on it yet, or where voting almost slipped our minds altogether. One of the most effective ways to help people participate is simply reaching them before their ballot arrives, having a one-on-one conversation, and making sure they know what is on the ballot and why it matters.

Those conversations can make a real difference. Here in Whatcom County, the 2026 primary for the 42nd Legislative District Senate race came down to just four votes between two candidates.

If knocking on doors sounds intimidating, know that canvassing is typically a really positive experience. We’ll be reaching out to voters who regularly participate in elections and having short, friendly conversations with people in our community. You’ll also be out there alongside other volunteers, not doing it alone.

events.title: 🚐Trip to Arizona from LA to canvass for Democrats
events.description:
Join the Westside Democratic HQ for a Friday evening trip to Phoenix for canvassing event on the weekend of October 24-25 for the Democratic slate of Maricopa County!

Please sign up by Sunday, October 18 in order to receive overnight accommodations in Arizona.

Our mission in Arizona is to get voters to re-elect Democratic Congresswoman Yass Ansari -- which is critical to our overall goal of taking back the House majority.

While we're talking to voters, we'll also gain their support for other Democratic candidates, such as the gubernatorial slate of Katie Hobbs / John Giles, state senate candidate Christine Marsh, and state representative candidates Sarah Liguori and Aaron Márquez.

Also on the Arizona ballot are some Trump-connected ballot measures that need to be SHUT DOWN.  One of them is Prop 144, which proposes to change the state's election laws to require photo IDs as well as restrict early voting and mail-in ballot procedures.  Sound familiar?  We need the voters in Maricopa County to vote NO on Prop 141, 142, 144, 316, 317, 318, 319, and 320.

This is your chance to help Democrats in our sister state of Arizona by fighting side-by-side to prevent the sun from setting on democracy in the Sunset State.

We'll meet at the WDHQ in Venice to board transportation at 6:00 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 23 and drive to a hotel to spend the night.  On Saturday morning, we'll meet organizers from the Maricopa County Coordinated Campaign for a training session and then spend the day knocking on doors and talking with voters.  We'll spend Saturday night at the hotel, and then canvass more on Sunday.  We'll return to the WDHQ in Venice on Sunday evening.

As a volunteer, you'll be participating in the WDHQ's ground team for Taking Back the House Majority. This is important work and we would love to have you join us.

Meetup location will be at the Westside Democratic HQ, located at 228 Main Street (near Rose).  There is no parking available at the HQ lot, so please plan your transportation to the HQ accordingly.

Partner organizations for this event are the Maricopa County Democratic Party and Copper State Victory (Arizona Democratic Coordinated Campaign).

events.title: LIGHTWORKERS
events.description:
Join us for a special community screening of **Lightworkers**, a moving documentary exploring compassion, 
resilience, and human connection in modern communities. 

The film frames its core focus around a simple, urgent question: "What can I actually do?"

Rather than following a traditional narrative line or focusing on party politics, **Lightworkers** operates as a mosaic of personal stories. Roth interviews a cross- section of over 30 everyday activists, public servants, and notable figures-including musician Tom Morello, actors Henry Winkler and Peter Coyote, artist Shepard Fairey, Wellfleet resident Maryland CD-8 US Rep Jamie Raskin, and former Congressman Adam Kinzinger. 

Directed by veteran filmmaker Bobby Roth (Lost, Prison Break, Grey's Anatomy), **Lightworkers (movie trailer: lightworkersdoc.com)** is a documentary about ordinary citizens and prominent figures who refuse to stand on the sidelines during times of political uncertainty and division.

**Doors Open at 6:00, the screening is 6:30-8:00 followed by a brief community conversation.  The concession stand will be open.**  This is a free event.

events.title: Get Corporate Money Out of Our Elections

location.venue: Unitarian Universalist Fellowship of Redwood City

events.description:
Since Citizens United in 2010, campaign finance laws allow corporations to significantly influence elections. California legislation (AB1984) introduced this year aims to reduce the impact of corporate dollars.

Join us in Redwood City for an engaging panel discussion and Q&A. We'll gather in-person to for a live webinar with political strategist Christopher Armitage, Tom Moore of the Center for American Progress, and Democratic California Assemblymember Chris Rogers. We'll explore how to use state power when the federal government is unreliable. 

After the webcast, stay for networking and more discussion with fellow activists about important actions we need to take post-midterm elections. If you are unable to attend in-person, a link will be provided for the webcast portion.

This event is co-sponsored by Indivisible Mid-Peninsula and Indivisible Portola Valley.

events.description:
Join the Van Buren County Democrats for Postcard Writing Thursdays in October. With Election Day just around the corner, we're coming together to write postcards reminding our neighbors to get out and vote on November 3.

It's a simple but meaningful way to help encourage voter participation, connect with fellow Democrats, and make a difference in our community. Whether you're a longtime volunteer or joining us for the first time, we'd love to have you. Bring a friend or two and spend a little time helping us get the word out.

Dates: Thursdays, October 15, 22, and 29
Time: 10:00 am to 1:00 pm
Location: Van Buren County Democratic Party Office
32849 E Red Arrow Hwy, Suite 300, Paw Paw
(Next to the Secretary of State office)

Postcard stamp donations are especially appreciated. We'll be writing lots of postcards, and postage is an important part of getting those reminders into voters' hands. If you're able, please bring postcard stamps with you.

Can't attend? You can still help. Donations of postcard stamps can be dropped off at our Paw Paw office. Every stamp helps us reach another voter and reminds someone that their vote matters.

With just weeks remaining before the November 3 election, every effort counts. Come for an hour or stay for the whole session. Enjoy some friendly company, help us reach more voters, and be part of the work we're doing together to make a difference in Van Buren County.

events.title: GOTV Halloween Part
events.description:
With the election less than 2 weeks away (when the party happens), it's time to get out and get to voting. Theres nothing scarier this time of year than letting someone else make decisions for you instead of using your voice. Early in person voting starts Friday October 16th, but not everyone knows who they are going to vote for. So, while we are having a party, we will also have information on candidates in our area to help you decide.
But before how about a party.
I'll be hosting a party at our friend's place to just have some fun and let off some stress from months of campaigning.
We have a lot to plan! But make sure you come dressed up and ready to have fun. Do you have a favorite Halloween activity you would like to do? I would love to hear it, and we will see if we can get that planned.
Ideas so far: (all ideas are subject to change)
-Best Dressed Costume
-Most Scary Costume
-Most unique Costume
-Best Couples Costume
-Bon fire
-Pumpkin Carving
-Show off your dance moves
-Karaoke
-Your ideas!
This party is for 18+ since that's the voter age but all ages are welcome. This will be a safe space for people of all ages. Get Out The Vote with us and make your voice heard.
prepared and paid for by Keenan Gentry for MN House SD30B
www.gentryformnhouse.org

events.description:
For our November monthly meeting, Duluth Indivisible has asked Megan Peterson and Erin Maye Quaid, the Executive Director and Senior Advisor, respectively, of [Gender Justice](https://www.genderjustice.us/) to present on "Gender and Authoritarianism". Because we are meeting in person and they are presenting on Zoom, we've decided to offer the Zoom version throughout MN08. Hence this Zoom version of the event. People who register will get the Zoom link a few hours before the event. 

Authoritarians regularly use gender as a wedge issue to create fear, divide people, and reinforce traditional hierarchies and patriarchy. The Trump regime is following this playbook on many fronts: trans youth participation in sports, Hegseth's attacks on diversity in the military, the SAVE Act to disenfranchise women voters, blocking health care for trans youth, and on and on. Gender Justice's presentation will outline these issues in a potent and coherent way and better equip us to protect the rights of ALL people to live fully and freely with respect to gender. 

We will still meet in person in Duluth for a potluck at 5:00 PM, with the presentation at 6:00, followed by discussion and planning on how gender advocacy might fit into our 2027 planning. To sign up for the **in-person session**, please do so through this Mobilize link: [Gender and Authoritarianism: In Person](https://www.mobilize.us/duluthindivisible/event/1040294/)

events.title: Texas Together Blockwalk: GOTV Bear Creek- Euless
events.description:
### Join Texas Together in Euless as we ramp up the action to Get Out The Vote and knock doors to support **Texas Democratic** nominees up and down the ballot. 

It’s time to organize, unify, and build the movement that will carry us through the last 31 days until Election Day, November 3, 2026.

During the block walk, volunteers will:

- Identify Democratic supporters

- Share information about our Democratic ticket

- Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots efforts and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We’ll provide training, materials, and turf at the start of each shift. 

Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend.
**RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.**

Refreshments 🏳️‍🌈 Community 🏳️‍🌈 Inspiration

events.title: Poll Greeting for Justin Early: Bell County Early Voting

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Team Early at the polls! Poll greeting is one of the most effective ways to support our campaign during voting hours. As voters arrive at the polling site, poll greeters offer a warm welcome, hand out campaign literature, and ensure Justin Early remains top of mind right before voters cast their votes. Once you sign up, our team will reach out to confirm your preferred polling location. What You'll Be Doing
Welcome Voters: Stand outside the electioneering marker (100-foot line) to offer a warm greeting to community members as they arrive.
Distribute Literature: Hand out palmcards, candidate slates, and voting guides.
Share Justin’s Message: Share why you are volunteering for Justin. What to Bring
Comfortable shoes, water, weather-appropriate clothing, and your enthusiasm!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
TAKE TO THE STREETS FOR DOUG!
We hope you will come to our Doug Jones Street Party as we host weekly Thursday evening sign-wavings in both Foley and Daphne from 5 pm to 6 pm. 

Here's the plan for Daphne: 
Location: Hwy 98 at the intersection with Scenic 98.
Parking: Park in front of Pet Supermarket, behind Take 5 Oil Change.
Time: Meet in the parking lot by 4:45 pm. Waving signs from 5-6. Even if you can only come for a few minutes, please stop by whenever you can. 
We can easily stay on the sidewalks and out of danger and off private property. There are crosswalks in every direction, so some of us could safely walk in front of stopped traffic to wave and gain some attention. 

Foley plan: 
We'll park and meet at Heritage Park in the parking area near the corner of US Highway 98 and Hwy. 59. We'll assemble along 59 with signs, music, and a table with buttons and bumper stickers. We will provide the Doug signs to wave and water. Come and bring friends to make a joyful noise for Doug!

events.description:
The Silver Cow teams up with Artists for Angie AND the Angie Nixon campaign! We are gonna bring the house down!

Silver Cow and Artists for Angie link up to create a GOTV event for early voting here in Duval. 

Together we will help you plan our early vote! We will be able to provide you with information on where to vote along with election protection and best practices at the polls.

Donations of postage stamps are also appreciated to help cover mailing costs. Stamps can be brought to the event or mailed to 1233 Cedar St. #81, Owasso, OK 74055.

events.title: Baldwin County Canvassing for Doug
events.description:
We lost two weeks of campaigning due to torrential rains and a hurricane. So now it's all hands on deck!!

We will have two canvassing events this weekend to make up for lost time. We'll be visiting homes in Spanish Fort, meeting at 9:30 am at Fort Kids Park, 30701 Ember Lane. 

Then, Sunday afternoon/evening, we'll be knocking doors in Daphne, meeting at the public gathering area outside the Daphne Civic Center, 2603 US Hwy 98, at 3 pm. 

We need drivers too! 

Please do your best to make the most of our last three weeks to defeat Tommy Tuberville and return Alabama leadership to a Governor who cares about everyday working families!

events.title: Standout - Get Out the Vote with IBB
events.description:
Indivisible Bellingham (MA) and Beyond's monthly standout is held on the 4th Saturday of each month from 9am-11am in front of Bellingham Town Hall. 

This month, our focus is on encouraging our neighbors to vote in the midterm elections!

Please note that the Town Hall will be open for early voting during this standout, so all signage, apparel, and other materials related to the candidates and questions on the ballot are not permitted within 150' of Town Hall.

Looking for sign ideas? 

"Vote by 11/3" 

"Voting is a Civic Duty"

"Your Vote is Your Voice"

events.title: #TeamAmy and #TeamJag Joint Canvass in Folsom
events.description:
The November 3rd general election is right around the corner, and we've got doors to knock!

Join Team Amy and Jag Nagendra for canvassing in Folsom on Sunday, October 25th, from 9:30 AM - 1:00 PM. Whether you're new to canvassing or a pro, all are welcome.

Run of show : Intro: brief training + practice runs 💬, Material distribution (literature to distribute as you walk) 📋 Get your turf aka where you and your buddy will canvass 📲 Group photo 📸 Knock those doors!! 🚪

What to bring: Comfortable walking shoes 👟 Water (it's getting hot, folks)☀️ Your phone (for PDI Mobile, the canvassing app), and a friend (optional, but encouraged!) We will also have food and snacks for all volunteers, along with a free yard sign post-shift! See you there 🫡

events.title: San Francisco SEIU Local 1021 Saturday Canvasses
events.description:
Join fellow SEIU Local 1021 members every Saturday through November 3 (Election Day) to support our labor champions and union priorities.

* Vote for Gary McCoy for District 8 Supervisor
* Vote for DJ Brookter for District 10 Supervisor
* Vote No on Prop D to keep elections fair and accessible in San Francisco
* Vote Yes on Prop H to keep Muni running
* Support other top priorities!

Locations vary weekly, but we gather each Saturday from 10 AM to 2 PM somewhere in San Francisco (District 8 OR District 10) to knock on doors and educate voters on what matters most to working families in our city.

events.title: Legvold for Minnesota - Farmington Door Knock!
events.description:
Ready to make a real impact? We are hitting the pavement to have those critical face to face conversations that win elections! Every door we knock brings us one step closer to our goal, and we need your energy to keep the momentum going.

Whether you are a seasoned canvassing pro or this is your very first time, we’ll make sure you’re fully prepared. We will start the event with a comprehensive training session, go over our talking points, and set you up with a partner if you’d like.

Event Details 
What to Bring: Please wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a fully charged cell phone. We will be using a mobile app to track our progress!

What We Provide: Training, literature, snacks, and plenty of team spirit.

Your voice is the most powerful tool we have. Let's get out there, meet our neighbors, and share our vision for the future!

Questions? Please contact Will Fehrman at willf@senatedflcaucus.org or 312-307-0710 for any questions or additional information.

Let’s get to work!

events.description:
We’re hitting the pavement and knocking on doors for Rob Sand and Iowa Democrats up and down the ticket. Talking to voters face to face is the best way to have an impact on this election. What better way to make a difference this election than talking to your friends and neighbors!

Rob is visiting every corner of the state to share his vision of an Iowa that isn’t Redder or Bluer, but Better and Truer with voters, and so are we! Whether you’re a long-time volunteer or stepping up to help for the first time, we’ve got you covered.

Before knocking doors, we will make sure everyone gets trained on how to talk to voters, how to record canvassing data, and canvassing best practices. Then, we’ll hit the pavement.

Can't join us this time? Interested in other ways to get involved? Check out our other events here: https://www.mobilize.us/iowaforward/

We can't wait to see you!

events.title: Democracy Defender Training — Election Protection on the East End
events.description:
Democracy Defender Training — Election Protection, Suffolk County 

Saturday, October 24 · 5:00-7:30PM · Virtual

This is people power — something real you can actually do, together, to stand up for our democracy and our communities.

A Democracy Defender shows up on Election Day, stands just outside the polling place, and watches, documents, and reports if something isn’t right. No confrontation, no danger, and never alone — we built this to be done together.

Here’s why it matters right now: the DOJ is sending roughly 1,000 election monitors to polling sites nationwide this November, and the administration has moved to put ICE near polling places — a fight still playing out in court. Long Island isn’t the top target, but trainers are calling it a real risk this cycle, not the highest, but not nothing. We’re not waiting around to see what happens.

We’ve partnered with NYCLU, Common Cause NY, and Battleground NY on a training built specifically for the eastern Suffolk County — the first of its kind in Suffolk County. Nothing like this has ever been done here before. Be part of history, on the right side of it. This training is required before you can sign up for a shift.

You’ll learn:
— Your rights, and voters’ rights, at the polls in New York
— How to document and report calmly, without confrontation
— How to help a confused or worried voter
— Who to call the moment something needs to be escalated

After training, claim 2.5-hour shifts, as many as you want, at locations across eastern Suffolk County — close to home when we can, with our most vulnerable communities prioritized first.

Bring a friend. This is people power — the more of us, the more ground we cover, and the more it proves none of this is inevitable. Be part of it.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

## Feeling Unsure?

No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: Tyranny Tuesday 10-20-2026:  Famous Americans Who Would Not Take No-Vote For an Answer

location.venue: Bruce R. Thompson Courthouse and Federal Building

events.description:
**📣 Tyranny Tuesday • October 20, 2026 • Indivisible Northern Nevada**

*✊ Famous Americans Who Would Not Take No-Vote For an Answer: They Fought for the Ballot. Now It’s Our Turn.

🤝Friends, in two weeks Americans go to the polls. Before we raise our signs, let’s remember the people who made that ballot possible. None of them were handed the vote. They were mocked, arrested, beaten, and jailed, and they kept going anyway.

💙Women’s Suffrage & the 19th Amendment

Susan B. Anthony co-founded the National Woman Suffrage Association in 1869 and spent decades crisscrossing the country for a suffrage amendment. She was arrested for voting in 1872 and refused to pay her fine. The “Anthony Amendment” became the 19th Amendment. Her final public words: “Failure is impossible.”

Elizabeth Cady Stanton co-organized the 1848 Seneca Falls Convention, America’s first women’s rights convention. She wrote its Declaration of Sentiments, which proclaimed that “all men and women are created equal.” Even her allies called her demand for the vote too radical, but it became the movement’s founding goal.

Alice Paul founded the National Woman’s Party and led the 1913 suffrage parade in Washington, where a mob attacked the marchers. Her “Silent Sentinels” picketed the White House and were jailed, beaten, and force-fed during hunger strikes. Public outrage over their treatment helped win the 19th Amendment in 1920.

Ida B. Wells-Barnett was born into slavery and became a fearless journalist. A mob destroyed her press over her reporting on lynching. In 1913 she refused to march at the back of the suffrage parade. That same year she founded Chicago’s Alpha Suffrage Club, which mobilized Black women voters to elect the city’s first Black alderman.

Mary Church Terrell was one of the first Black women to earn a college degree. She became the first president of the National Association of Colored Women, whose motto was “Lifting As We Climb,” and she was a charter member of the NAACP. She fought racism and sexism alike. In her late 80s, she led the fight that desegregated D.C. restaurants.

🤝The 15th Amendment

Frederick Douglass escaped slavery and became the nation’s most powerful abolitionist voice. At Seneca Falls he stood up for women’s suffrage, and after the Civil War he campaigned tirelessly for the 15th Amendment. It was ratified in 1870 and barred voting discrimination by race.

The Civil Rights Movement: The 1965 Voting Rights Act & the 24th Amendment

Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. co-founded the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC) and helped lead the 1965 Selma-to-Montgomery marches. He endured bombings, arrests, and surveillance. Selma forced the nation’s hand, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 was signed five months later.

🪧Fannie Lou Hamer was a Mississippi sharecropper who was fired and evicted for trying to register to vote, then brutally beaten in jail. She co-founded the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party. Her 1964 convention testimony, “sick and tired of being sick and tired,” stunned the nation.

Ella Baker was the master organizer behind the NAACP, SCLC, and the 1960 founding of SNCC. She taught that “strong people don’t need strong leaders” and built the grassroots, community-led model that groups like ours still use.

Diane Nash led the Nashville sit-ins that desegregated lunch counters. When others wanted to stop the Freedom Rides after they were firebombed, she insisted they continue. She was jailed while pregnant, and she helped draft the voting-rights plan that became the Selma campaign.

John Lewis was a Freedom Rider and SNCC chairman. His skull was fractured on the Edmund Pettus Bridge on Bloody Sunday in 1965, and that sacrifice helped pass the Voting Rights Act. He served Georgia in Congress for more than 33 years and urged us all to make “good trouble.”

🏠The 26th Amendment: “Old Enough to Fight, Old Enough to Vote”

Sen. Jennings Randolph first proposed lowering the voting age to 18 in 1942. He kept at it for nearly 30 years until the amendment passed in 1971. It was ratified in about 100 days, the fastest in U.S. history.
President Dwight D. Eisenhower had sent 18-year-olds into combat in World War II. In 1954 he became the first president to call for giving them the vote.

Sen. Edward M. Kennedy pushed a law lowering the voting age in 1970. When the Supreme Court upheld it only partly, the result was a chaotic two-tier system, and Congress passed the 26th Amendment within months to fix it.

📣Our Charge

Every person you just heard about assembled, marched, petitioned, published, and spoke out. These are the 1st Amendment tools we use today. They used them to widen the circle of “We the People,” one amendment at a time. None of it came from the generosity of the powerful. It came from ordinary citizens who refused to be silent.
That is the tradition you are standing in today. Every sign you hold links Seneca Falls to the Pettus Bridge to this corner in Reno. You are using your 1st Amendment rights to expand equality and political representation, just as they did.

🪧Failure is impossible 
🌟Make good trouble 
💙And vote on November 3rd
✅ Your 2026 Voting Checklist

- 📝 Oct. 6 is the last day to register by mail or in person.** You can still register online through Election Day, or in person during early voting and on Election Day.

- 📬 Watch your mailbox.** Return your mail ballot early, or use a drop box by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

- 🗓️ Early voting:** October 17–30  *Election Day:** Tuesday, November 3

- 🔍 Check your registration** at [nvsos.gov](https://www.nvsos.gov) or [washoecounty.gov/voters](https://www.washoecounty.gov/voters/)

We'll be using Ground Truth, Swing Left's innovative approach to voter contact: real, in-depth conversations at the door that actually move voters, instead of rushing through a checklist.

- A training on the Ground Truth script and deep canvassing best practices
- Plenty of time at the doors having real conversations with voters
- Logging each conversation in the app
- A short debrief with an organizer to wrap up your shift

Every conversation helps move voters toward voting for Talarico and allows us to connect with voters who are traditionally overlooked by campaigns.

## Join Swing Left to canvass for James Talarico!

We'll be using Ground Truth, Swing Left's innovative approach to voter contact: real, in-depth conversations at the door that actually move voters, instead of rushing through a checklist.

No experience needed. Every shift starts with a training, so whether it's your first time canvassing or your fiftieth, you'll be ready.

**Here’s what to expect:**
- A training on the Ground Truth script and deep canvassing best practices
- Plenty of time at the doors having real conversations with voters
- Logging each conversation in the app
- A short debrief with an organizer to wrap up your shift

**What to bring:** A charged phone, comfortable shoes and clothes, and water.

Every conversation helps move voters toward voting for Talarico and allows us to connect with voters who are traditionally overlooked by campaigns.

We need volunteers like you!

Whether you’ve knocked hundreds of doors or this is your first time, we’ll show you everything you need to know.

Stop by Olean HQ to start. We’ll provide a quick run-down on canvassing, plus distribute lists of your canvassing turf, campaign information, and voter list.  From there you’ll go out (we usually recommend with a buddy) and knock the doors on your list to have in-person conversations with potential voters.  You should be able to complete your list of doors in 60-90 minutes. So many people haven’t heard of Aaron yet.  Let’s get his name out there!

events.description:
## Join Swing Left to canvass for James Talarico! 

We'll be using Ground Truth, Swing Left's innovative approach to voter contact: real, in-depth conversations at the door that actually move voters, instead of rushing through a checklist.

No experience needed. Every shift starts with a training, so whether it's your first time canvassing or your fiftieth, you'll be ready.

**Here’s what to expect:**
- A training on the Ground Truth script and deep canvassing best practices
- Plenty of time at the doors having real conversations with voters
- Logging each conversation in the app
- A short debrief with an organizer to wrap up your shift

**What to bring:** A charged phone, comfortable shoes and clothes, and water.

Every conversation helps move voters toward voting for Talarico and allows us to connect with voters who are traditionally overlooked by campaigns.

events.title: Peekskill, NY: GOTV Stop Data Centers Rally + Canvass Launch in NY-17
events.description:
Join Food & Water Action for a rally and canvass launch to get people to the polls on the first day of Early Voting in NY-17. 

NY-17 is one of the most watched congressional districts in the country. The seat is currently held by MAGA Mike Lawler, who has voted with Trump 100% of the time – cutting healthcare, food assistance, and clean water funding, and enabling handouts to the fossil fuel industry. He has also voted to fast-track the financing, permitting, and construction of new hyper-scale AI data centers across the country.

Join us to rally against data centers in New York and call for a halt to new data center development! Then we'll head out to knock on doors to kick Lawler out of Congress and elect Cait Conley, the only candidate to call for restrictions on data centers. 

No prior canvassing experience is necessary. After the rally, we'll have lunch and then train you before we go canvass. 

If you're taking the train, we'll have shuttles from the train station to the the rally and canvassing locations.

--

_Paid for by Food & Water Action, Not Authorized by any Candidate or Committee._

events.title: Syracuse NY Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Hop on the bus from Queens to knock doors in NY-17 to flip the House w/ Rep. Grace Meng!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to New York's 17th Congressional District—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Cait Conley. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Forest Hills at 10:00am and return around 6:00pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

events.title: District 34 Senate Candidate Forum
events.description:
Voters in South Dakota Senate District 34 will have an opportunity to learn more about the candidates seeking to represent them at a public forum on Wednesday, October 21, from 6 to 7 p.m. at the Minneluzahan Senior Center. Doors will open at 5:30 p.m. The forum is one of a series, sponsored by WRAD.

Democratic candidate Michael Calabrese and Republican candidate Taffy Howard have both been invited to participate in the forum. The event will provide an opportunity for voters to hear directly from the candidates, learn about their priorities, and gain a better understanding of their perspectives on issues affecting District 34 and South Dakota.

Michael Fell, a political strategist, will serve as moderator, guiding the discussion and helping ensure a constructive and informative conversation for attendees.

The forum is intended to give community members an opportunity to become more informed about the candidates and the choices facing voters in the upcoming election. All interested members of the public are encouraged to attend.

events.title: CATTY CHATS LIVE!  ICE Keeps Lying About Its Warehouses (w/ Morris NJ & Hagerstown MD RR activists)
events.description:
Anit-ICE activists join Catty Chats Live on Sunday to give updates on ICE activity near Hagerstown, MD, and Roxbury, NJ

What do you do when government officials lie to their constituents?

You dig deep to the bottom of the box and expose them.

In New Jersey, ICE wasn’t supposed to be detaining people at a vacant warehouse in Roxbury – by court order. But when two activists with Morris ICE Rapid Response saw increased activity at the warehouse, they sprang into action, collecting photos and video. Thanks to the activists’ work, the New Jersey Attorney General’s office began looking into the report that a person detained by ICE on Sept. 4 was held at the Roxbury warehouse before being transferred elsewhere.

Hagerstown Rapid Response in Maryland has been reporting on the lies told by members of the Washington County Commissioners for months, first about a proposed 1,500-bed ICE detention center near Williamsport. Now, they’re exposing collusion (and a sketchy non-disclosure agreement) between the commission and a data center developer. What has the commission told the public about the detention center and data centers? Not much.

Activists from both organizations will join us this Sunday, Oct. 18, on Catty Chats Live to update us on the fight where they live and to inspire us to speak up and claw back in our own hometowns. Sign up on Mobilize for reminders & YouTube link.

events.title: Love as Action: San Francisco
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and San Francisco Friends Meeting to bear witness to the authoritarian actions of ICE in our country. 

On Monday November 2 from 4 to 9, we will gather at the Festival of Altars in Potrero del Sol Park to honor those we've lost due to ICE's harmful, callous tactics. The altar we are building is intended to help us know their names, remember them, honor them, and ensure they know their deaths were not in vain. Please contact the organizers to sign up for a one-hour slot with the altar during the 4 to 9 time window.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather in communities across the country, showing love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Springs Bird Watch: Following the Water and the Life It Supports
events.description:
Calling all birders in the Sky Islands! We’re launching a new bird-monitoring project, Springs Bird Watch, to document the region’s avian diversity and the water sources that birds and other wildlife depend on, from low desert to upper pines. 

Join our virtual Coffee Break on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 9:30 a.m. to learn how to get started, where to go, and how your observations at springs can help both resident and migratory species, from hermit thrushes and hummingbirds to yellow-billed cuckoos and elegant trogons. Eamon Harrity, SIA’s wildlife program manager and an enthusiastic birder, will lead the talk and explain how your data will help advance both bird and spring conservation. 

Springs Bird Watch is funded in part by the Santa Cruz Valley National Heritage Area.

*Photo of hermit thrush at a spring in Chiricahua National Monument courtesy National Park Service.*
