events.title: Our Voices Roll Deep- Community Ride and Party At The Polls

tags.name: American Indians in Texas at the Spanish Colonial

events.description:
SHOWING UP FOR COMMUNITY SHOULD FEEL LIKE COMMUNITY

There's something powerful about coming together as relatives and neighbors. See familiar faces, meet new ones, and celebrate the people and communities that are the heartbeat of Yanaguana, San Antonio. Our Voices Roll Deep is bringing that spirit to the streets!

We'll kick things off with a community ride through San Antonio, showing up together to take up space, be seen, and be heard. From there, we'll roll into a family-friendly, cookout-style celebration with good food, music, games, activities, and plenty of opportunities to connect.

And the polls are right across the street! During Early Voting, registered Bexar County voters can vote at any designated early voting location in the county, no matter where they live. With the polls just across from our gathering, we can come together, vote alongside our neighbors, and keep the celebration going with good company and community care beyond the ballot.

Voting can sometimes feel intimidating or disconnected from the communities it represents. We're coming together to make room for something different. A space where people can show up as themselves, move how they move, and feel the joy of being part of something bigger than any one election. 

Our voices matter beyond a ballot, and they show up in how we care for and encourage one another! This is the heart of Our Voices Roll Deep

Whether you're riding with us, meeting us at the party, or simply coming out to enjoy your neighbors, there's a place for you here!
events.accessibility_notes:
Hi there,

Thanks for signing up for our Party at the Polls on Saturday, October 24, 2026!  We are so excited to have you join us! Please note the following details and time to ensure an easy arrival. 

The Community Ride starts at American Indians in Texas at the Spanish Colonial Missions, located at 1616 E. Commerce St., San Antonio, Texas. 
8:30 AM - Arrival and Rider Registration | 9:00 AM - KSU, Ride Starts. 
Please ensure that riders register ahead of time here: https://bit.ly/4s2SyWF 

The Party by the Polls starts at 10:30 AM, after our community ride arrives. The party location is L&S Countryside Party Venue
18053 US-281, San Antonio, Texas 

The Southside ISD Administration Building is the polling location we will be near, located at 1460 Martinez Losoya Rd. San Antonio, Texas

Parking will be marked for attendees upon arrival

1460 Martinez Losoya Rd. San Antonio, Texas 

Sober & Family-Friendly Event Disclaimer: Our Voices Roll Deep is a sober, family-friendly event welcoming community members of all ages. Alcohol, recreational drugs, and intoxication are not permitted. We ask all attendees to help maintain a safe, respectful, and welcoming environment for everyone.

Nonpartisan Event Disclaimer: AITSCM does not endorse, support, or oppose any political candidate or party, and participation is not conditioned upon voting. Individuals are responsible for confirming their voter registration, eligibility, identification requirements, polling location, and ability to vote. Participation in this event does not guarantee eligibility or the ability to cast a ballot. Please refer to official state or county election resources for current voting information.

Have questions or need help? Reach out to Jordyn Galvan, our Civic Engagement Coordinator, at jordyng@aitscm.org

We look forward to seeing you!

events.title: Texas Together & HCDP Reach 254 Friend Bank
events.description:
**254 counties. 200,000 voters. It all starts with the people you already know.**

We're in the final stretch of one of the most exciting election seasons in Texas history, and winning up and down the ballot comes down to one thing: YOU, having conversations with every Texan you know.

A conversation with someone you know is more than twice as effective as one with a stranger. One real chat with a person in your network does the work of *ten* doors knocked. 

**That's why we're asking volunteers in every county in Texas to commit to talking with at least 20 friends, coworkers, and family members about this election.**

Join us for a quick training, and a fun in-person friend bank at the **Harris County Democratic Party Office** at 6:30 PM **5445 Almeda Rd. Ste. 200, Houston, TX 77004** . We'll get you set up on the Reach app and give you the tools to have these conversations with confidence. We'll chat for about 30 minutes, then spend the rest of our time together adding contacts and sending messages!

Zero experience required. All you need is a cell phone, a laptop if you have one, and a commitment to flip Texas blue. We'll teach you the rest. See you soon!

events.title: Sunrise Orlando @ Public Comment: Orange County Board of Commissioners Meeting
events.description:
### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ Orange County Board of County Commissioners Meeting! 🌅

Join us for the Orange County Board of County Commissioners' weekly Public Comment to learn and discuss the decisions being made in our county, connect with the community, and advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the period scheduled during the beginning of the morning session of the Board of County Commissioners’ meeting. It is time set aside at each BCC meeting for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern within the BCC’s authority.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.
- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

events.title: Sunrise Orlando @ Public Comment: Orlando City Council Meeting
events.description:
### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ the Orlando City Council Meeting! 🌅

Join us at the Orlando City Council Meeting to learn about and discuss decisions that will shape our city, communities, and future, and to advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the time scheduled at the beginning of a meeting for public input. At each City Council meeting, time is set aside for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern listed on the meeting agenda. Only live in-person comments or written comments submitted in advance may be presented.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.

- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

events.title: Hudson Valley says Votes Early Presser

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Even in a highly competitive election, our democracy is bigger than any one race or political party. This press conference will bring together nonpartisan organizations and community partners across the Hudson Valley to send a clear message: we are united in ensuring every eligible voter has the information, resources, and support they need to make their voice heard.

Our goal is to demonstrate community solidarity by educating voters about their rights and voting options, activating residents to participate in early voting, and ensuring voters know where to turn if they encounter problems at the polls. As Election Day approaches, we want the public to know that trained, nonpartisan volunteers and organizations will be on the ground, working together to promote safe, fair, and accessible elections.

We will also highlight the importance of voter assistance hotlines, including 866-OUR-VOTE, which voters can contact if they have questions, experience barriers to voting, or need help during early voting and Election Day.

The message is simple: no matter how competitive the race becomes, protecting the freedom to vote is a shared responsibility. The Hudson Valley is showing up—not to tell people who to vote for, but to ensure they can cast their ballots with confidence and have their voices heard.

events.title: Amendment 3 Digital Doorknocking & Messenger Training!
events.description:
“Meet people where they’re at” is Organizing 101. These days, that means online! So let’s shift the narrative online and build power for working families. 

We’re reaching out to Florida voters to talk to them about Amendment 3 and we’d love for you to join us. 

In order for us to build a Florida we can afford, we need every eligible voter to show up at the polls this November and vote NO on Amendment 3 to save our services.

Whether you connect with friends on Facebook, Instagram, Tiktok, or any other platform, we’re asking you to use your voice to help make Florida work for all of us. At this virtual event, we’ll help you do that by:

-Providing a brief training on Amendment 3 and how to talk about it with your family, friends, and neighbors

-Sharing a script you can use as you reach out to people in your online communities

-Creating a fun and inviting online space for you to ask questions and connect with other folks who want to see real relief for Florida families

This event will be hosted by Florida for All, Florida Rising, Central Florida Jobs with Justice, and other coalition partners.

events.title: Indivisible Glen Burnie Monthly Meeting November 2026
events.description:
Two days after election day we will look at the post-election landscape and plan next steps.  We'll have updates from Indivisible Maryland Coalition, Indivisible National, and our coalition partners, all of whom have been doing extensive scenario planning about what we might be facing.   

The voters are casting their ballots to right the course of this ship.  Critical work continues AFTER the election.

What's encouraging is that when we stay connected and engaged, the people have real power.  Consider the way the dictator Milosevic got booted out in Serbia, or Viktor Orban got tossed out in Hungary.  The regime wants us to believe we are powerless, but the facts are different- we can make a difference.

See you on the 5th!

events.title: Fulton Democrats Early Vote Phone Bank | Virtual
events.description:
Georgia started Early Voting with record-breaking turnout. Now we need your help keeping the momentum going in Fulton County.

Join Fulton County Democrats for our remote Early Vote phone bank. We'll be calling Fulton voters to make sure they know Early Voting is underway, have a plan to vote, and have the information they need to cast their ballot.

Where? 

Anywhere. This is a fully remote phone bank, so you can make calls from home or wherever works for you.

When?

Our primary calling window is 5:00-8:00 PM each day, but the phone bank is available outside those hours as well.

Once you RSVP, you'll receive the information you need to access the phone bank and start calling.

First time phone banking? No problem. Join one of our virtual phone banking trainings here: https://mobilize.us/s/OGTdTu

Every conversation helps us reach another Fulton voter. Let's get out the Early Vote!

events.title: 10/24 WFP Canvass with Kelabe Tewolde and Jaelynn Scott for LD 37 · WA WFP + Seattle DSA
events.description:
Join us for a joint canvass with WA Working Families Party & Seattle DSA. We're knocking doors with our endorsed candidates in Washington's 37th legislative district! Ballots are due Nov 3rd- help us get the word out to our neighbors about these incredible working peoples' champions!

Location: Othello Playground, a 7 min walk from the Othello light rail station.

Kelabe Tewolde (LD37 - House Seat 1) is a child of refugees who advocates to stop redlining and environmental racism on the Seattle Planning Commission and an educator who mentors and uplifts youth of color with Rainier Scholars, and is challenging a 27-year-incumbent who has voted to increase rents and lower taxes on corporations. Kelabe, in contrast, is by community and for community.

Jaelynn Scott (LD37 - House Seat 2) is a Black trans activist and proud socialist who serves as Executive Director of the Lavender Rights Project, a national black trans feminist advocacy organization advancing justice for gender diverse communities. She has spent years working in community, organizing, responding to crisis calls, helping people find sanctuary, and trying to help folks navigate the confusing, frustrating, broken system of social services.

If it’s your first time, no worries! Each session starts with a brief training & Q&A. Don't be afraid to reach out with questions!

Our message is simple: Every voter deserves to vote safely, freely, and without intimidation. Every vote matters!

Stand Up! Show Up! Speak Up!

Together, we can protect the freedom to vote and the democracy we all share.

events.title: Call Out Data Centers! Phone Bank with Team Vikki and Odus Evbagharu
events.description:
**Special Guest Phone Bank with Odus Evbagharu**

Tax breaks for the corporations building data centers are projected to cost Texas nearly $1.8 BILLION a year by 2030. They'll keep coming, and they'll keep gobbling up Texas land and water with no regard for the people and animals who live here.

Dan Patrick's answer? Stall. But we don't have time to wait on him.

**Vikki Goodwin [has a better plan](https://www.vikkigoodwin.com/datacenters): stop new data center construction now, until Texas passes real protections.** People and animals drink first. Data centers pay for their own water and electricity, so your bills don't go up. Counties get the power to protect their communities, and companies that hide their water use face real consequences.

But passing real protections takes more than one office. **That's why we're teaming up with Odus Evbagharu, candidate for State Representative in HD 135. Odus has a record of bringing people together to get things done, and he's running to fix the power grid, stand up to corporate polluters, and lower costs for Texas families.**

Voters across the state are worried about data centers moving in. They need to hear who has a plan to protect our water and our wallets.

Join Team Vikki and Odus as we hop on the FairShot Texas dialer and call voters in HD 135. You'll hear from Odus himself, then we'll all make calls together!

No experience needed. We'll train you, and you will not do it alone! Just bring your voice, a phone, and a laptop. Let's protect Texas water, keep our bills down, and send Vikki and Odus to their new seats.

events.title: Get out the (early) vote drive & party

location.venue: Glacier Bar (Vellidan Pilates/former Backyard of Northstar restaurant)

events.description:
Join the Tompkins County WFP club and our many friends (including Indivisible Tompkins and local Democrats) at the Glacier Bar in Fall Creek on Sunday, October 25th!

State Senator Lea Webb and Assembly Member Anna Kelles will welcome everyone, and will help motivate us all to make a final push toward our shared goal of turning out as many early voters as possible by the end of the day.

The event begins at 1 pm. Around 1:30, participants can choose to head out to knock on doors all around downtown Ithaca, to encourage everyone to head over to the early voting polling location on Albany and State. Alternatively, participants can head over to the poll site and stand outside the 100' marker with signs and handouts. Or, participants can remain at the Glacier Bar, and make calls or send texts to their own friends and contacts in Tompkins County, encouraging them to go vote before 5 pm.

At 4:30, we will begin to gather again at the Glacier Bar for smoothies, Indian food from New Delhi Diamond Restaurant, and assorted side dishes and desserts that people bring from home. 

After the polls close for the day at 5 pm, we'll get an update on the number of voters (so far) from the Board of Elections, and raise our smoothie glasses in celebration of a powerful first weekend! 

Then the party can begin... Travis Knapp will arrive around 5:30 to play music and sing for us and with us. Other special guests are being invited. Anyone you know who voted early (preferably on the WFP line) is also welcome to come join the party!

The Glacier Bar is the new occupant of the former Backyard Bar of NorthStar Restaurant, and the north end of N. Tioga Street. They hope to open officially in November, but in the meantime they are happy to host us and to let us sample their smoothies for free!

Please RSVP so we can keep you updated on our plans as they evolve!

events.title: The Next Stretch: a Block by Block Campaign Call
events.description:
Midterm polling is looking promising for pro-working class candidates, but the races aren't a given. **When democracy is on the line, the best defense is a good, strategic offense.** We have to hustle to win these elections by margins that are too big to question, then protect the results and make sure these new lawmakers are sworn in. 

Join SURJ for a special session where we'll discuss how we win for our movement and enforce the results.  

**What we do in the final weeks before the election will set the stage for the next stretch of our work.**

If we win big, it will make it harder to deny the results. If we are prepared, strategic, and coordinated within our larger movement, we can protect democracy against election tampering and make it known that the people have the power.

Then, there's the work that continues for years: leveraging our chosen candidates' campaign promises to usher in policy that works for all of us. Organizing to set the terrain on which we can continue our fights. **Protecting democracy from authoritarianism and those who profit off our suffering. Fighting for change in every arena we have a foothold in.**


**This call is for you - someone who is looking for an outlet to channel their uncertainty and fear into a strategic movement for a new, better world that takes the fight to the ballot box, the statehouse, and the streets.**

**Join us for this Block by Block campaign call: another in a series of monthly spaces for SURJers to take our fear, confusion, and weariness and turn it into grounded action.**

We're about to enter the next stretch of our organizing - let's work it out together. 

_Note: this is the same call as the monthly Block by Block campaign call series for Block by Block organizers, captains, and crew. If you're already signed up there, you're all set!_

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Canvass for Peggy Flanagan at Minneapolis Farmers Market

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
Join Team Bernie and canvass for Peggy Flanagan at the Minneapolis Farmers Market from 10 AM to 1 PM. Pick a time in this window and bring a smile! We'll bring the rest.

Organize and Win Minnesota is our program to elect Peggy Flanagan to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state.

Senator Sanders says it best:

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few.

Right now, our movement is winning. Why?

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges.

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement.

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up.

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us.

Let’s get to work.

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.title: Fight the (F)right: Phone Bank with SURJ to Haunt the House and Senate!
events.description:
## **Fight the (F)right and haunt the House (and Senate) with SURJ in the final days before the midterm election!**

We'll have exclusive SURJ merch giveaways, special guests, games, and more as you work with us to call white voters in strategic races across the country where we're working to flip the House and Senate left. 

Come as you are to any shifts - no experience needed! Each phone bank includes full training & lots of support as you go. _No tricks, only treats and wins here!_

## Full Fight the (F)right Schedule:

- **10/31 - Halloween Costume Contest:** come dressed as something that would scare MAGA (or just your best costume). Prizes await those whose costumes go above and beyond!
- **11/1 - Dial-a-thon:** Join us for special guests, Phone Bank Bingo, prizes galore, and more while we dial all day! Special SURJ merch pack given to those who join all shifts. 
- **11/2 - Michigan's a Winner:** We're calling in to Michigan to kick MAGA to the curb in the mitten state. MI movement candidates will join us as we move Michigan left!
- **11/3 - Election Day Finale:** Bingo! Punch Cards! Prizes! It's all happening on election day while we secure the final votes for our movement-aligned candidates and block MAGA from gaining any more ground. 



**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

**For a full list of the candidates we're supporting, visit https://surj.org/2026-election/**
      
***

## Logistics:

-   These phone banks are online on the Zoom platform. Log into the call on Zoom on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).

-   Returners can start early.
-   You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!

## About SURJ:

## Small acts of kindness make a big difference!

**Mat-Su United for Progress**, in collaboration with **Planned Parenthood Action Alliance Alaska**, invites you to join us for a Period Product Donation Drive and Packing Event to benefit the Planned Parenthood’s Period Packing Initiative that provides free period products to shelters and those in need. 

With the rising cost of everyday necessities, more people are struggling to afford basic hygiene products. Period products are essential, not a luxury, and no one should have to go without them because of financial hardship.

**📦 JOIN US TO PACK DONATIONS!**

- 📍 Location: Commons Cafe, 231 E. Swanson Ave., Suite 24, Wasilla
- 🕛 Time: Noon–3 PM

Bring your donations and join us as we organize and pack period products for community members who need them. Every contribution helps!

**🩷 WHAT TO DONATE**

We're collecting:

- Menstrual liners in various sizes
- Tampons
- Travel-size wet wipes

Every donation, large or small, helps make a difference!

**☕ CAN'T MAKE THE PACKING EVENT? YOU CAN STILL DONATE!**

Drop off your donations at either of these convenient locations:

**Commons Cafe**

- 📍 231 E. Swanson Ave., Suite 24, Wasilla
- 🕒 Open 10 AM–6 PM daily except Sunday

**Cold Snap Coffee**

- 📍 4931 E. Mayflower Ln., Suite 2, Wasilla
- 🕒 Hours:

    - Tuesday–Friday: 8:30 AM–2 PM
    - Saturday: 8:30 AM–1 PM
    - Sunday and Monday: Closed

#### 💪 LET'S TAKE CARE OF OUR COMMUNITY!

When we come together, we can help ensure that our neighbors have access to the essentials they need. Whether you donate products, help pack supplies, or spread the word, your participation matters!

### Join Mat-Su United for Progress and Planned Parenthood Action Alliance Alaska in making a difference for our community.

events.title: Know Your Ballot: NYC’s 2026 Charter Proposals (COGE)
events.description:
This November, every New York City voter will see five charter revision proposals on the back of their ballot. These are from the Mayor’s Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE). One of them, Proposal 3, could change how quickly the City can build street safety projects like protected bike lanes, bus lanes, and redesigned dangerous intersections.

Join Transportation Alternatives and the COGE special projects team for a live webinar on what all five proposals would do. We’ll take a closer look at Prop 3 and what it means for the fight for safer streets.

The proposals cover:

**Prop 1:** Faster approvals for using public space, such as outdoor dining, ramps, benches, and planters
**Prop 2:** City contracting reform for small businesses and nonprofits
**Prop 3:** Faster street safety projects, plus faster sale and leasing of City property
**Prop 4:** One central hub for building permits
**Prop 5:** A required contribution to the City’s rainy day fund

This is your chance to ask questions directly of the people who wrote the proposals. Bring your questions, and leave knowing what you’re voting on.

**When:** Tuesday, October 20, 3:30 PM ET

**Where:** Zoom. RSVP on this page and the Zoom link will be emailed to you.

Can’t make it live? RSVP anyway and we’ll send you the recording.

events.title: Lifeline DC 2027: Walk For Lives
events.description:
On Saturday, September 11, 2027, we walk together in Washington, D.C.

Walk for Lives D.C. is the closing day of Lifeline DC, three days in the nation’s capital following Hill Day and the Synthetic Drug Summit. It brings the families, survivors, and advocates who walked in their own cities and towns in May to the National Mall, side by side, in one place.

We walk for the sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, parents and friends we have lost to fentanyl. We walk for the families still in the fight, and for the young people we can still protect. Every step says the same thing to the country: these lives mattered, and this crisis demands a response.

We walk on a date this nation already holds for remembrance. We carry that spirit with us, honoring every life that should still be here.

What to expect

A morning program with family speakers and a moment of silence
A gentle, accessible walk of about one mile, open to all ages and abilities
A Community Resource Village with treatment, recovery, and public health organizations
Time to connect with families who understand

Bring a sign. Carry the name or photo of someone you love, or a message you want Washington to see.

Schedule [CONFIRM]

8:30 AM: Check-in opens
9:00 AM: Opening program
10:30 AM: Walk steps off
11:00 AM to 12:30 PM: Community Resource Village

Location [CONFIRM]
Floral Library Gardens, Tidal Basin, National Mall, Washington, D.C.
Nearest Metro: Smithsonian (Blue, Orange, Silver lines)

Walk for Lives D.C. is free and open to everyone. Please register so we can plan for you, and share this event with someone who should be walking beside you.

Can’t be in D.C.? Walk for Lives returns to cities and towns across America on Saturday, May 15, 2027.

About United Against Fentanyl
United Against Fentanyl is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization that interrupts the use of illicit fentanyl through innovative, bold, and effective initiatives.

Questions? info@unitedagainstfentanyl.org

events.title: 10/18 - Voter Mobilization @ Collin County Talarico Rally [OUTDOOR]

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: This is a volunteer signup page for Powered by People's voter mobilization team. Signing up here will register you as a volunteer to work the event, not as a general attendee for the rally itself. Because we are partnering with an active campaign, all schedule details and locations are subject to change until finalized by the campaign. We will send out confirmed logistics closer to the event date._

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for the **Talarico for Texas** rally at **the [Red Tail Pavillion] in [Plano]**! We are showing up as volunteers to this event to fire up the rally attendees, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with passionate rally attendees and community members
- Check voter registration statuses on the spot (ensuring no one has been purged)
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive **1 hour before doors open** so that we can optimize working the line of attendees. They will be lining up way in advance, and our goal is to check voter registrations for everyone waiting to get in. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[3:30-4:00pm]: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the site leads, and align on our goals

[4:00-5:00pm] Working the Line (Part 1) | As the crowd grows ahead of doors opening, we will start engaging the very first people in line and continue moving down the line to check registration statuses and get folks set up on Reach.

[5:00pm]: Venue Mobilization | Once doors open, we continue to work the line and shift to the venue to catch any remaining attendees and trickling community members before the main programming starts.

[5:00-7:00pm]: Stay for the event! | Once the programming begins, volunteers are invited and encouraged to stay, enjoy the rally, and celebrate the energy with our neighbors!

[7:00-8:00pm]: Working the Line (Part 2) | After the event, we'll sweep the line of attendees waiting to take a photo with James Talarico


### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: Red Tail Pavillion

2801 E Sping Creek Pkwy, Plano, TX 75074

- **Volunteer Parking**: Free parking is available directly surrounding the Pavillion

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes (you will be on your feet talking to voters!)

_Note: Necessary materials will be provided at the check-in table, but feel free to bring your own backup supplies just in case!_

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single Texan counts. Sign up for a shift today!

Join us for a a rally calling on the city to commit funds to save the Neighborhood Restorations Homes. 

Neighborhood Restorations/Prime Property is a company that owns 925 affordable rental units in West and Southwest Philadelphia. Last July they announced their intention to sell. The sale of these units to a private developer could not only displace thousands of residents but also cause increased housing costs across the neighborhood. The city has said they are working on it, but has yet to commit the funds. 

This rally will be held at in front of a group of Neighborhood Restorations Townhomes that are among the 225 homes whose affordability contract has already expired.  This rally is to call on the City to commit the funds immediately to protect their affordability. 

We are calling on the city and state to commit funds to keep all 925 properties permanently affordable and to sell them to interested tenants at affordable rates. Attend this rally to demand that the city and state take action. 

Sponsored by One PA West Southwest Rising.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Harrisburg, PA (PA-10)!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

- **Offer vote swapping** for voters who might be more willing to vote Democrat if they can "swap" with someone in a solid blue or red district who will lodge a protest vote on their behalf.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Capitol Heights Tenant meeting Orientation
events.description: There is an urgent need to convene a tenant meeting at Highland Ridge Apartments due to the ongoing unsafe and unhealthy living conditions, lack of accountability, and growing frustration among residents. Within the past year alone, the property has undergone three different management changes, creating instability, poor communication, and a serious loss of trust between tenants and the property owner. Residents have reported inadequate heating, raising serious concerns about whether their homes will be properly heated as the colder winter months approach. In addition, tenants continue to face severe mold problems, rodent and insect infestations, broken building entrance doors that compromise residents' safety, and completely destroyed mailboxes that leave personal mail and packages vulnerable to theft. These conditions are not simply maintenance concerns; they are serious threats to the health, safety, dignity, and overall quality of life of families who deserve safe and habitable housing. This meeting is essential to bring residents together, document ongoing violations, rebuild collective power, and establish clear demands for immediate repairs and accountability from property ownership and management. Tenants deserve more than empty promises and constant management changes. They deserve meaningful action, transparency, and lasting solutions. The goal of this meeting is to ensure residents have a unified voice and a concrete plan to hold those responsible accountable for providing the safe, secure, and healthy living conditions they are entitled to.

State voter suppression laws have targeted Black voters with administrative hurdles, new ID proofs, and poll closures. Your call can make the difference as you'll provide critical non-partisan information to help Black voters overcome obstacles and vote.

events.title: Election Day Volunteer Poll Greeters in South Suffolk
events.description:
The Suffolk Democratic Committee is working to fill Suffolk's 30 voting locations with Poll Greeters on Tuesday, Nov. 3. We need "all hands on deck" to ensure Dem candidates are elected in this important mid-term race.  Shifts (3 or 4 hours) are available throughout South Suffolk. Sign up and BOROUGH CAPTAIN ROBIN H. WILL CALL OR TEXT YOU FROM 252.619.6078 to discuss scheduling a shift at your preferred location.
WHAT'S A POLL GREETER?
Poll greeters are the volunteers outside voting locations, who offer the Dem Sample Ballot to voters. How does this effort make a difference?  Unlike the top of the ticket (U.S. Senator, U.S. Congress), where the party for each candidate is marked clearly on the ballot, local candidates for City Council and School Board are NOT labeled by party. The Dem Sample Ballot clearly indicates the candidates who are endorsed by the Democratic Party.  That is how Poll Greeters make a difference - they help get ALL Dem candidates elected! The Sample Ballot also supports voting YES on the 3 Virginia Constitutional Amendments.

events.title: Michigan Get Out the Vote Wednesdays
events.description:
Michigan Weekly Phone Bank

Every Wednesday at 3pm Eastern Time / 12pm Pacific Time

Join us as we call MI-07 voters to help them return their absentee ballots and make a final plan to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.

Every week, we’re reaching voters across Michigan’s 7th District, home to Lansing and one of the most competitive House races in the country. Michigan voters will also decide an open U.S. Senate seat and an open governor’s race. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide the outcome. We’re making sure no voter is left behind.

We’ll help voters who have already requested absentee ballots complete and return them on time, understand key deadlines, and make a clear, confident plan to vote, whether by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We’ll also send follow-up texts with early voting, polling location, and ballot drop box information to those planning to vote early or on Election Day.

Volunteers will have real conversations with voters and help turn intention into action, making sure ballots are returned and votes are counted.

📞 Weekly phone bank: Wednesdays at 12p.m. PT / 3p.m. ET (every week through Election Day)

🔥 No experience needed. Training, scripts, and support provided.

This is how we win close races: by making sure every vote counts. Your call could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Michigan!

Kristin Hook, Ph.D., biologist, and candidate for Congressional District 21.

Shelly Nickels, M.D., and candidate for Texas State House District 122.

Adelita G. Cantu, Ph.D, RN, CHWI, FAAN, Professor UT Health San Antonio School of Nursing; Chair, Texas Physicians for Social Responsibility; Board Member, Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments

events.title: Phone Bank Party in Montpelier/Central VT

address_lines: Downstairs in the community room / vestry

events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!

We're calling to send Susan Collins hauling and Troy Jackson to action! Join us. 

If you are brand new to phone banking, we will train you and give you what you need! If you have made calls before, you are able to get started earlier! Either way, we will be together throughout, taking collective action, while being part of a national campaign! Power in numbers!

What to bring : 
- A charge computer and cell phone (you can make calls just through the computer, but easier to have both if possible. 
- other people to make calls with us! 
- a snack to share (totally optional!)
- arrive a few minutes early so we can jump in @ 3pm
- please RSVP (it helps us plan!)

See you there! 

--------------- below is more information about SURJ National's strategy and campaign! ----------

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: A Doctor, A Nurse, A Biologist and Two Politicians Walk Into A Bar
events.description:
Ever wish you could have a real conversation with a politician? No stump speech. No canned answers.

Ever wish you could sit down with a health care professional or scientist and get more than a short answer to the things that worry you?

Here’s your chance. Join a doctor, a nurse, and a biologist for two hours in a casual setting. They talk. You talk. Two of them are running for office right now, and all three want to hear what you think about:

-The environment -Maternal health -The return of diseases we thought we’d defeated -Why health care costs so much and stays out of reach for so many -How government policy and regulation can manage these risks

And more. Bring your questions, your concerns, and your opinions.

Here's your chance. Three leaders in medicine and science want to have a conversation with you in a bar.

Kristin Hook, Ph.D., biologist, and candidate for Congressional District 21.

Shelly Nickels, M.D., and candidate for Texas State House District 122.

Adelita G. Cantu, Ph.D, RN, CHWI, FAAN, Professor UT Health San Antonio School of Nursing; Chair, Texas Physicians for Social Responsibility; Board Member, Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments

Professional are opinions free, but you will have to buy your own beer.

events.title: Tending Environmental Grief: Part Two
events.description:
We are living in an era of significant environmental change and loss. In recognizing that these times are challenging to live in, adapt to, and cope with, it’s essential that we come together as a community to process our experiences. Supporting ourselves and one another is just as important as stewarding the land and waters. 

Join Sky Island Alliance and [Maria Renée](https://www.maria-renee.com/) on Thursday, Dec. 10, at 9:30 a.m. for a dedicated time to understand the terrain of environmental grief, work through emotions, celebrate this beautiful region, and practice building resilience together. This free webinar is the second in a series of opportunities to contribute your creative responses to a changing region, whether they come from grief, hope, or anything in between. Participants will have a chance to share their reflections and experiences in response to a series of prompts this fall.

_See [Tending Environmental Grief: Part One](https://skyislandalliance.org/2026/10/tending-to-environmental-grief/) >>>_

_Photo of cottonwood at the border in Lochiel._

Building off of the historic October 8th student mobilization, students are building an intersectional, cross-campus movement to demand our institutions protect survivors, invest in sexual violence prevention, fund our student services, and dismantle rape culture. 

Join us for a Mass Call on Wednesday (10/21) @ 8 pm ET/5 pm PT to connect with students from across the country and learn how we are going to organize our campuses to #StopSexualViolence.
  
From the frat house to the White house, we say no more. From ICE detention to Palestine, sexual violence is never acceptable. 

Let’s get organized to build the future free of sexual and gender-based violence we deserve. 

Contact info@feministgeneration.org with questions.

events.title: 10/19 - Voter Mobilization @ Fort Worth Talarico Rally
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: This is a volunteer signup page for Powered by People's voter mobilization team. Signing up here will register you as a volunteer to work the event, not as a general attendee for the rally itself. Because we are partnering with an active campaign, all schedule details and locations are subject to change until finalized by the campaign. We will send out confirmed logistics closer to the event date._ 

_⚠️ Additionally,  Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for the **Talarico for Texas** rally **in Fort Worth**! We are showing up as volunteers to this event to fire up the rally attendees, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with passionate rally attendees and community members
- Check voter registration statuses on the spot (ensuring no one has been purged)
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day


- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone!


### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive **1 hour before doors open** so that we can optimize working the line of attendees. They will be lining up way in advance, and our goal is to check voter registrations for everyone waiting to get in. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[5:00-5:30pm]: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the site leads, and align on our goals

[5:30-6:30pm] Working the Line (Part 1) | As the crowd grows ahead of doors opening, we will start engaging the very first people in line and continue moving down the line to check registration statuses and get folks set up on Reach.

[6:30-7:00pm]: Venue Mobilization | Once doors open, we continue to work the line and shift to the venue to catch any remaining attendees and trickling community members before the main programming starts.

[7:00-9:00pm]: Stay for the event! | Once the programming begins, volunteers are invited and encouraged to stay, enjoy the rally, and celebrate the energy with our neighbors!

[9:00pm -9:30pm]: Working the Line (Part 2) | After the event, we'll sweep the line of attendees waiting to take a photo with James Talarico


### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: North Crowley High School

- **Volunteer Parking**: In the general parking lot, but please be mindful to avoid the front parking spots to allow for ADA/handicap and guests if possible.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed(battery pack is a plus)

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes (you will be on your feet talking to voters!)

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single Texan counts. Sign up for a shift today!

events.title: NO FLOCK- NO ALPR'S-NO MASS SURVEILLLANCE
events.description:
FUERA FLOCK: Rally at Santa Ana City Hall!

It’s time to let Santa Ana City Council know how our community feels about automated license plate reader (ALPR) cameras.

On Tuesday, October 20, Flock and ALPR surveillance are officially on the Santa Ana City Council agenda. Join Chispa and community members at City Hall to rally, make public comment, and demand an end to mass surveillance in Santa Ana.

Important: Item 28 does NOT cancel the Flock or Motorola contracts. Instead, the item asks City Council to consider directing staff to return within 30 days with information about:

- Options and costs to terminate, suspend, or not renew the contracts
- The cost effectiveness of Santa Ana’s ALPR system
- Outside agencies’ access to Santa Ana’s ALPR data
- Compliance with California law and SAPD policy

This is an important opportunity for our community to tell City Council what we want them to do next.

ALPR cameras capture license plates and vehicle information as people travel throughout the city, creating searchable records of where vehicles have been seen. That raises important questions about privacy, data sharing, accountability, and how surveillance affects immigrant communities and everyone who lives, works, organizes, or travels through Santa Ana.

Our demands are clear: Cancel the Flock and Motorola contract. Do not replace it with another ALPR vendor. Invest in community, not mass surveillance.

Tuesday, October 20
 Santa Ana City Hall: 22 Civic Center Plaza
 Rally: 5PM
 City Council Meeting: 5:30 PM

Come ready to rally, bring a sign, and make public comment to let Santa Ana City Council know how YOU feel about these cameras.

Whether this is your first City Council meeting or you’ve spoken before, your voice belongs in this conversation.

RSVP not required, but you will be emailed talking points! Bring someone with you!  FUERA FLOCK FUERA ALPR'S ! 📸🚫

The county tax rate is already set to drop in January 2027, amendment or not. What these amendments would do is let corporations like Duke Energy and the wealthiest property owners keep dodging what they owe, and move the final say on your property tax bill from the county commissioners you elect to politicians in Raleigh. Billions for CMS, CPCC, Atrium Health and CATS are on the line.

You'll work in pairs, outside the 50-foot buffer zone, with talking points and materials we provide. First time doing this? No problem. We'll walk you through what to say when you arrive. Bring water, comfortable shoes and a charged phone.

Stand up against racist campaign ads in Tustin!

You don’t have to live in Tustin. You just have to care about fairness and honesty. Mayor Austin Lumbard is running against Letitia Clark, a woman of color, and false and racist mailers are targeting her.

We’re not having it.

Join us at City Council to speak up during public comment and make two things clear:

﻿Meeting ID: 940 8640 1921
Passcode: 600222
 
The meeting starts at 6pm on Oct. 20. 
Join a few minutes early and enter your full name so the clerk can call on you.
 
Prefer your phone? Call 669-900-6833 and enter the same meeting ID and passcode when prompted.
 
Phone callers are identified by the last four digits of their number when it’s their turn. When the clerk asks, press *6 to unmute and again to mute.
 
On Zoom, you’ll be able to speak but your video won’t be on.
 
Tip: Keep it short and personal. Two or three sentences about why fair, honest elections matter to you is plenty.

events.title: End the Iran War -- Visit Rep. Smucker!
events.description:
**Trump's Iran War is Terrible**

Join us to advocate for an end to the Iran war. Rep. Smucker needs to hear from his constituents that we oppose a violent path to nuclear nonproliferation and that we would like him to vote against it at every opportunity. Don't let him say, "I didn't hear anyone was against this!"

### Why Congress Must Act to End the War

**This War Does Not Reflect Who Americans Want to Be**

This nation stands for opportunity, dignity, and the belief that every human life has worth. When we bomb elementary schools, reduce neighborhoods to rubble, and cut families like ours off from food and water, we betray these foundational values.

● The war against Iran is the least popular war on record. More broadly, seven in ten Americans agree that they would prefer the US be a reliable neighbor who prioritizes responsible partnership over erratic warmaking.
● Bombing a girls’ school and calling for an entire civilization's destruction goes against our values, and signals to other countries that the U.S. is an unstable, unserious actor.
● Americans care about what’s happening to innocent civilians, especially when it’s our money being used to bomb their homes. We have the power to stand up and demand our leaders make decisions that respect and protect human life.

**This War Was Forced Upon Us and is Not “America First”**

● We didn’t vote for this war. President Trump promised no forever wars. This war wasforced on us by those who profit from never-ending conflicts in the Middle East, and it will continue to bleed us dry the longer it goes on.
● This war does nothing to benefit everyday Americans and conflicts with President Trump’s pledges to bring back manufacturing. When the costs of gas, fertilizer and other goods go up, we are not putting “America first”
– we are slowing economic growth.
● The president of the United States should be prioritizing the needs of American families — not advancing the political agenda of military contractors or foreign governments.

**The War is Hurting America. We Need to Fix Roads, Bridges & Healthcare– Not Waste Taxpayer Dollars on More Endless Wars**

● We are being robbed. The administration is taking from taxpayers’ money that we need for our hospitals, roads, and bridges, and wasting it on a war that is destroying with children overseas. We are paying for this war twice: first with tax dollars diverted away from our communities, and again every time we are hit by the global economic fallout of this conflict.  Americans are still struggling to afford gas and put food on the table.
Meanwhile, the administration has burned more than $2 billion a week on this conflict — enough to build 4,000 new homes every seven days. According to the US Department of Housing and Urban Development It is enough to end homelessness in the US in 10 weeks. It is enough to fund about 1.5 million public school teachers for a year with a salary and benefits package of $70,000. It is enough to Subsidize high-quality childcare for over 7 million children for a full year. 

Office visit sponsored by:

Peace, Justice, Sustainability NOW, an Associate of National Peace Action
Lancaster Peace Action Network 
NIAC--National Iranian American Council
Indivisible Lancaster Together
Third Act

events.title: 10/20 - Voter Mobilization @ Tyler Talarico Rally [INDOOR]
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: This is a volunteer signup page for Powered by People's voter mobilization team. Signing up here will register you as a volunteer to work the event, not as a general attendee for the rally itself. Because we are partnering with an active campaign, all schedule details and locations are subject to change until finalized by the campaign. We will send out confirmed logistics closer to the event date._

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for the **Talarico for Texas** rally at **Eagles Event Center in Tyler**! We are showing up as volunteers to this event to fire up the rally attendees, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with passionate rally attendees and community members
- Check voter registration statuses on the spot (ensuring no one has been purged)
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone, however you must be Reach certified.

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive **1 hour before doors open** so that we can optimize working the line of attendees. They will be lining up way in advance, and our goal is to check voter registrations for everyone waiting to get in. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[5:00pm-5:30pm]: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the site leads, and align on our goals

[5:30-6:00pm] Working the Line (Part 1) | As the crowd grows ahead of doors opening, we will start engaging the very first people in line and continue moving down the line to check registration statuses and get folks set up on Reach.

[6:00-7:00pm]: Venue Mobilization | Once doors open, we continue to work the line and shift to the venue to catch any remaining attendees and trickling community members before the main programming starts.

[7:00-9:00pm]: Stay for the event! | Once the programming begins, volunteers are invited and encouraged to stay, enjoy the rally, and celebrate the energy with our neighbors!

[9:00pm -10:00pm]: Working the Line (Part 2) | After the event, we'll sweep the line of attendees waiting to take a photo with James Talarico.


### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: Meet under the canopy in front of the building

- **Volunteer Parking**: On site

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes (you will be on your feet talking to voters!)

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single Texan counts. Sign up for a shift today!

events.title: Election Day Volunteer Poll Greeters in North Suffolk
events.description:
The Suffolk Democratic Committee is working to fill Suffolk's 30 voting locations with Poll Greeters on Tuesday, Nov. 3. We need "all hands on deck" to ensure Dem candidates are elected in this important mid-term race.  Shifts (3 or 4 hours) are available throughout North Suffolk. Sign up and BOROUGH CAPTAIN ROBIN H. WILL CALL OR TEXT YOU FROM 252.619.6078 to discuss scheduling a shift at your preferred location.
WHAT'S A POLL GREETER?
Poll greeters are the volunteers outside voting locations, who offer the Dem Sample Ballot to voters. How does this effort make a difference?  Unlike the top of the ticket (U.S. Senator, U.S. Congress), where the party for each candidate is marked clearly on the ballot, local candidates for City Council and School Board are NOT labeled by party. The Dem Sample Ballot clearly indicates the candidates who are endorsed by the Democratic Party.  That is how Poll Greeters make a difference - they help get ALL Dem candidates elected! The Sample Ballot also supports voting YES on the 3 Virginia Constitutional Amendments.

events.title: Community Outreach: Connect with Texans in Dallas at Dia de Los Muertos Festival
events.description:
Skip the doorbell. We’re taking the conversation to where people already gather: at the market, on campus, outside the big event. We’re testing a new way to reach people there, and we want you to help us do it. Too often, outreach finds the same folks over and over while plenty of neighbors never hear from anyone. Community outreach is about changing that.

We’ll meet up, do a quick training, and then head to a busy spot nearby to chat with people passing through. You’ll invite them to learn more about RALLY TX, a paid community engagement program, and sign up right then on their phones with a quick QR code scan.

No experience is necessary. We’ll provide a training, a script, a clipboard, and everything else you need. Conversations are short, friendly, and easy to learn.

Come ready to meet some neighbors, try something new, and share what you saw and heard afterward so we can make the program better.

California is one of the wealthiest places in the world, but working people are being asked to pay the price for devastating healthcare cuts so billionaires can get more tax breaks.

events.title: Election Protection Training with MOVE Texas!
events.description:
## Election Protection Training with MOVE Texas

Our work doesn't end when someone gets registered or arrives at the polls. We're working to make sure voters have the information and support they need to actually cast their ballots.

Join us for an Election Protection training to learn how you can support voters during early voting and on Election Day.

### What We'll Cover
- **Election Protection 101:** What Election Protection is, why it matters, and how MOVE is getting involved.
- **Parties at the Polls:** How volunteers can organize events that celebrate voting and support voter participation.
- **Poll Monitoring:** How trained volunteers observe polling locations, assist voters, and report potential voting barriers.
- **Getting Involved:** Opportunities to put what you've learned into practice.

Whether you're interested in hosting a Party at the Polls, becoming a poll monitor, or learning more about Election Protection, this training will help you understand the work and how to get involved.

**No previous experience necessary!** We'll cover the basics, share resources, and walk through next steps.

This is a nonpartisan training focused on supporting voters, regardless of their political preferences.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Nothing's spookier than not voting, but 65,000 **known** Democrats skip the midterms! 

Help us remind those Democrats in Coeur d'Alene on Saturday, October 31 to cast their ballot. This is the **easiest** kind of face-to-face outreach: knocking the doors of known Democrats who simply haven't voted regularly in the midterms. 

Now's you're time to remind them to get out there and inform them of their polling place. If they're not home, you'll place an oversized sticky note reminder that includes a QR code they can use to find their polling place.

**NO HEAVY PERSUASION**

You'll meet your knock host at the Kootenai Dems office in downtown CDA (address provided upon registration). There you'll get a list of doors and handouts, snacks for the walk, help setting up the door knocking app on your phone or tablet, and a door knocking buddy if you don't want to walk alone. Bring a friend to make it fun!

**What to expect:**

- Arrive at 9:30am to the Kootenai Dems office in downtown CDA
- Check in with the door knocking host; receive any training or help you might need with the MiniVAN app, a list of doors, materials, snacks, and a partner upon availability
- Head out to your doors!
- Come back to the office when you're done turn in unused materials

**How to prepare:**

- Download the MiniVAN app to your phone or tablet
- Create an ActionID if you've not already
- Confirm your attendance the day before
- Check the weather and dress accordingly—including comfortable walking shoes!
- Bring a water bottle
- Make sure your phone or tablet is fully charged
- Bring a friend to make it fun!

**Questions? Email [volunteer@kootenaidemocrats.org](mailto:volunteer@kootenaidemocrats.org)**
events.accessibility_notes:
Volunteers will be traversing various neighborhoods in the Coeur d'Alene area. 
If one is not able to walk comfortably for an hour or more at a time or access various home entries that include stairs and gates, please reach out to the Volunteer Outreach Coordination team to find ways to support this effort in other ways.

events.title: Community Outreach: Connect with Texans in McAllen at Oktoberfest
events.description:
Skip the doorbell. We’re taking the conversation to where people already gather: at the market, on campus, outside the big event. We’re testing a new way to reach people there, and we want you to help us do it. Too often, outreach finds the same folks over and over while plenty of neighbors never hear from anyone. Community outreach is about changing that.

We’ll meet up, do a quick training, and then head to a busy spot nearby to chat with people passing through. You’ll invite them to learn more about RALLY TX, a paid community engagement program, and sign up right then on their phones with a quick QR code scan.

No experience is necessary. We’ll provide a training, a script, a clipboard, and everything else you need. Conversations are short, friendly, and easy to learn.

Come ready to meet some neighbors, try something new, and share what you saw and heard afterward so we can make the program better.

events.title: 10/18 - Voter Mobilization @ Royal Lane Baptist Church Pumpkin Patch [OUTDOOR]
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift at **The Pumpkin Patch at Royal Lane Baptist Church**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with attendees/passersby
- Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **11:45-12:00pm: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **12:00pm-2:00pm Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

- **2:00-2:15pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Southfield Public Library

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
Join us to canvass for Abdul in the Oakland area Monday 10/19 @ 5:30 PM.

Join Team Bernie and canvass for Abdul El-Sayed at the Birmingham Farmers Market from 10 AM- 11 AM.

Organize and Win Michigan is our program to elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state.

Senator Sanders says it best:

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few.

Right now, our movement is winning. Why?

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges.

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement.

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up.

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us.

Let’s get to work.

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

Sarasota, let's get out the vote! Early voting phone banking will be happening at New Bethel Missionary Baptist Church in Newtown for the Defending Democracy Campaign: Get Out the Vote Outreach. 

With Early Voting starting on the 19th, we need volunteers to make calls to voters across Sarasota and the state and give them the information (and possibly motivation) they need to cast their ballots in our midterm election. We will be a friendly voice on the phone offering assistance and information.

events.title: Banned Book Club - December's Title TBD
events.description:
Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau
• To Kill A Mocking Bird - Harper Lee

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.
