events.title: The Great WNY Flock/ALPR Scavenger Hunt!

sponsor.name: Good Neighbors Getting it Done in Western New York

events.description:
Flocks and Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) have been in the news a lot lately in WNY but many don't realize exactly what or where they are. 

Don't have time to sit down and learn more? No problem! We've got you! And we'll make it fun! 

Get some friends and register for your checklist by October 30. Teams welcome!

Once you get your checklist, use use publicly available resources to solve riddles and take pictures of Flock/ALPRs in and around the towns of Lancaster and Cheektowaga. The goal is find as many answers as you can. 

Answers are due by 6:30 on November 2. You can submit at any time. 

We'll gather together at the final location on the checklist at 6:30 on November 2 for a group photo, the final answer, and prizes including fastest team, most creative team, and more! They'll also be a special event for Lancaster residents. 

The fun won't end on November 2nd, though! On November 3 (or after October 24) you can vote for the candidates with a plan for dealing with over-surveillance in our communities! Ryan Taughrin for Assembly, Sara Marmion for Erie County Legislature, and Rachel Martinez for Cheektowaga Town Council

events.title: IDEM Public Hearing on Google Michigan City's Dirty Diesel Generator Permit
events.description:
The Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) has published a draft air permit modification for the Google, referred to in the permit as Lavender Fields Holdings LLC, data center’s Building 2 permit for its facility under construction at 402 Royal Road, Michigan City.

The permit would add 66 more large diesel backup generators, on top of the 66 already permitted for Building 1. If finalized, the campus could run 132 critical diesel engines, ~725,000 gallons of on-site diesel, and bigger engines on Building 2 than Building 1 — with ZERO add-on pollution controls in this draft. 

Krueger Middle School and Paladin - Head Start are each about a third of a mile from the site's property line, and residences are nearby. The site is a contaminated brownfield under active IDEM oversight. Michigan City residents have shown up to speak out against Building 1, packed Council chambers, and demanded accountability for the past year, while the city tabled a strong local moratorium and local permits for Building 2 may still be pending. This state permit will determine whether Indiana allows a second diesel power plant next to our schools and homes without basic safeguards.

Michigan City deserves clean air! Join the virtual public hearing on November 17th to tell IDEM to protect our communities and airways from Amazon’s dirty diesel generators permit.

*The hearing begins at 6:00 PM CT and will conclude as soon as public comments are done, or no later than 9:00 PM CT.

events.title: SCREENING: The Long Game
events.description:
Join the Justice Network of Tarrant County, F.O.R.T, and Indivisible-TX12 for a viewing of "The Long Game", an examination of the decades long movement to privatize education in Texas, tracing how policy changes, along with political and economic interests, have helped transform public education into a multibillion dollar industry. Through multiple perspectives, the film explores the forces shaping the future of Texas Public Schools and the stakes for the communities they serve. 

Doors open at 1:30PM, film screening 1:30-3:30PM, followed by a 30 min panel discussion
**Snacks will be served ;)

events.title: Knock Doors with Governor Moore & the Washington County Democrats!
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore, Comptroller Brooke Lierman, AG Anthony Brown and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

We will be doing a VDP Coordinated Campaign Training before heading out to canvass.

Materials: Bring a good pair of walking shoes, a charged cell phone, downloading the application "MiniVan", and a bottle of water. Everything else will be provided during the shift.

events.description:
Election Day is November 3, so we're moving our regular first-Tuesday meeting to Wednesday, November 4!

It's time to come together, reflect on our work, and ask the question that now guides our monthly meetings: Are We Meeting Our Mission?

Over the past several weeks, Camel City United Indivisible has been in action across Forsyth County—from our No Kings mobilization to voter education, early voting outreach, neighborhood organizing, and helping our neighbors get to the polls.

Now it's time to assess our progress, celebrate our volunteers, and determine what comes next.

Our November conversation will focus on:

Getting Out the Vote: Reviewing our early voting efforts, voter protection activities, rides to the polls, and Election Day mobilization.

No Kings Debrief: What did we accomplish, what did we learn, and how do we turn participation into sustained community action?

Are We Meeting Our Mission? Measuring our impact in neighborhoods and communities across Forsyth County.

Moving Forward Together: Identifying our next steps beyond Election Day and strengthening our neighborhood organizing.

This isn't just another monthly meeting. It's an opportunity to evaluate whether our actions are making a difference—and how we can do even better.

Whether you've been canvassing, greeting voters, organizing events, providing rides, or simply looking for a way to get involved, your voice matters.

Join us Wednesday, November 4, at 6:30 PM on Zoom.

Register through Mobilize to receive the meeting link.

Camel City United Indivisible (CCUI)

Organizing our communities. Building lasting power. Meeting our mission.

events.title: Join the Longest-Running U.S. Economic Discussion: 13 Yrs Strong! Tues, Sept Rev’w: Oct 20@7 Zoom
events.description:
#### Join the Longest-Running U.S. Economic Discussion: 13 Yrs Strong! Tues, Sept Review: Oct 20th @7 Zoom

_Tuesday, October 20 @ 7 PM CDT — Fiscal & Economic September Review — 13 Years Running! Jobs, Wars, Tariffs, ICE & Deportations, Health Care, Affordability, & Inflation_

#### Let us know you will be attending … RSVP Here -> https://mobilize.us/s/7BPNGh

Join us for a timely discussion of September’s employment report, the latest inflation numbers, and what they mean for working people in Illinois and across the country.

#### The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ September employment report, released October 2, shows:

•	U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs in September, compared with an average monthly gain of 45,000 over the prior 12 months. 

•	The unemployment rate was 4.2%, with approximately 7.1 million people unemployed.[bls]

•	Labor-force participation stood at 61.8%, and the employment-to-population ratio was 59.2%. 

•	Average hourly earnings for private-sector workers rose 5 cents to $37.81—an increase of 0.1% for the month and 3.0% over the past year.[bls]

•	July and August job growth was revised downward by a combined 60,000 jobs. July now shows a loss of 10,000 jobs, while August’s gain was revised from 162,000 to 133,000.[bls]

#### Where Jobs Grew—and Where Workers Face Strain
Employment changed little across all major industries. Health care continued to trend upward, adding 17,000 jobs, while construction added 11,000 and manufacturing added 9,000. Financial activities declined by 7,000 jobs.[bls]

Behind the headline numbers, many workers continue to face significant challenges:

•	Approximately 1.9 million people had been unemployed for 27 weeks or longer, accounting for 27.1% of all unemployed people.[bls]

•	Another 4.5 million people were working part time for economic reasons but wanted full-time work.[bls]

•	About 5.8 million people outside the labor force said they wanted a job. Of those, 1.5 million were marginally attached—available for work and having searched within the past year, but not during the most recent four weeks.[bls]

•	The unemployment rate for Black workers increased to 7.0% in September.[bls]

#### Affordability & Inflation: The Pressure on Household Budgets

The latest available Consumer Price Index report, covering August, showed overall prices rising 0.4% for the month and 3.4% over the year. Annual increases included:
•	Food: 2.7%
•	Shelter: 3.0%
•	Energy: 16.3%
•	Gasoline: 27.4%
Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, was 2.4% over the year.

The September CPI report is scheduled for release Wednesday, October 14, at 7:30 AM CDT. We’ll include those new September inflation numbers in our October 20 discussion.

Let’s Dig Into the Numbers—and the Policy Choices

We’ll unpack September’s jobs report, the downward revisions to earlier months, and the latest inflation data. We’ll also discuss the Trump administration’s policies on war, tariffs, immigration enforcement and deportations, health care, and federal spending—and examine how those choices intersect with jobs, household costs, affordability, and debt.

What do these developments mean for working families? What is happening here in Illinois? And what can we do together?

Join us on Zoom to dig into the numbers, cut through the spin, catch up on this year’s U.S. and Illinois economic news, and share your thoughts. Bring your questions and your perspective!

events.description:
### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ the LYNX Board of Directors Meeting! 🌅

Join us at the LYNX Board of Directors Meeting to learn about and discuss decisions that will shape our public transportation and to advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the time scheduled at the beginning of a meeting for public input. At each LYNX Board of Directors meeting, time is set aside for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern listed on the meeting agenda. Members can provide in-person, virtual (Zoom), or written comments before the board.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.

- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

events.title: Dialing for Democracy — the Final Senate Push
events.description:
Join us on the last weekend before Election Day for a special Get Out the Vote (GOTV) event! On the final Saturday before the election, Indivisible Palo Alto Plus (IPA+) and Blue Turn Indivisible will be hosting an in-person phone bank at the Democratic Volunteer Center (DVC) in Mountain View.  

As we head into the final push before Election Day, we need all hands on deck to reach out directly to voters in critical U.S. Senate races. Talking with voters increases the likelihood that they will not just vote but also vote for pro-democracy candidates. Help us keep the momentum going, and help turn the Senate blue!

Our GOTV efforts could make the difference in the handful of tight races that will determine which party controls the Senate. The stakes couldn’t be higher: Control of the Senate would give Democrats the power to confirm judges and Supreme Court justices, to control hearings and investigations, and to decide which bills reach the Senate floor for a vote.

**How It Works**
Our efforts directly plug into a coordinated national infrastructure designed to identify, target, and mobilize key voters in pivotal battleground races. By connecting to a nationwide data network, you can be sure that every call you place has the potential to make a difference. This system will allow you to use your time efficiently to target voters in the races that matter most during the crucial final days before November 3.

**What to Expect** 
Making calls together, as a community, creates a special kind of energy. Whether you’re a brand-new caller or a seasoned volunteer, you’ll leave with new skills, meaningful connections, and the satisfaction of working to defend democracy alongside fellow activists.

- **Snacks and refreshments:** We will provide light snacks and beverages to keep our energy up.

- **No tech required:** DVC will supply laptop computers and other needed equipment, all set up and ready to use. No need to bring your own phone or laptop. Just bring yourself!

- **On-site training and support:** First-time phone banker? Don’t worry! A trainer will introduce you to the tech setup, walk you through the call script, lead practice calls, and make sure you feel confident before you make your first call. Friendly, experienced organizers will be on hand throughout the session to answer questions and to cheer you on.

 - **Focused outreach:** Our efforts will focus on making GOTV calls to known supporters. You’ll help ensure that likely Democratic voters have everything they need to cast their ballots in essential Senate races.

Show up whenever you can. We’ll get you set up right away. Then stay for as long as you’d like.

**Please RSVP** so that we can arrange for enough calling stations—and also be sure to have enough snacks for everyone!

events.title: [10/24] - Voter Mobilization @ San Antonio Talarico Rally
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: This is a volunteer signup page for Powered by People's voter mobilization team. Signing up here will register you as a volunteer to work the event, not as a general attendee for the rally itself. Because we are partnering with an active campaign, all schedule details and locations are subject to change until finalized by the campaign. We will send out confirmed logistics closer to the event date._

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for the **Talarico for Texas** rally at **the [VENUE] in [CITY]**! We are showing up as volunteers to this event to fire up the rally attendees, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with passionate rally attendees and community members
- Check voter registration statuses on the spot (ensuring no one has been purged)
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Voter Registrar Requirements

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone, _whether you are certified or not_.

- **Important Note**: If you want to physically register voters or update registrations at this event, you **MUST** be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (VDR) in at least **[COUNTY] County**.

- _Not certified yet?_ Don't worry! You can get certified ahead of time by signing up for our [VDR Training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908495/).

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive **1 hour before doors open** so that we can optimize working the line of attendees. They will be lining up way in advance, and our goal is to check voter registrations for everyone waiting to get in. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[10:45-11:30am]: Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the site leads, and align on our goals

[11:30am-1pm] Working the Line (Part 1) | As the crowd grows ahead of doors opening, we will start engaging the very first people in line and continue moving down the line to check registration statuses and get folks set up on Reach.

[1:00- 3:00pm]: Venue Mobilization | Once doors open, we continue to work the line and shift to the venue to catch any remaining attendees and trickling community members before the main programming starts.

[7:00-8:30pm]: Stay for the event! | Once the programming begins, volunteers are invited and encouraged to stay, enjoy the rally, and celebrate the energy with our neighbors!

[8:30pm -10:00pm]: Working the Line (Part 2) | After the event, we'll sweep the line of attendees waiting to take a photo with James Talarico


### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: [LOCATION]

- **Volunteer Parking**: [PARKING DETAILS]

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes (you will be on your feet talking to voters!)

- **If you are a VDR**: Please bring your VDR certificate/number for the  counties where you have VDR reciprocity

_Note: Clipboards, pens, voter registration forms, and all other necessary materials will be provided at the check-in table, but feel free to bring your own backup supplies just in case!_

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single Texan counts. Sign up for a shift today!

events.title: Young Adult Indivisible: Storytelling for Computer Game Design and a Better United States
events.description:
Adventure games, open world games, and interactive visual novels are great ways to help people envision a better future and a better United States! 

Through game experiences it's possible to not only normalize a different world, but learn how to behave in that world and make meaningful choices. We learn that different is not neccessarily scary--sometimes it's cosy as well as exciting! 

Through games we want people to embrace a country that shares power, and supports the well-being of all its citizens.

Speaker Katherine Phelps has a PhD in storytelling for computer game design, which she lectured on for nearly a decade. She also taught how educators can bring gaming into their classes in order to inspire students to dig deeper into a variety of education topics. 

In this online class Katherine will help you to learn how to make effective interactive stories, and perhaps even make your own game!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: 10/22 - Voter Mobilization @ Beaumont Talarico Rally

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: This is a volunteer signup page for Powered by People's voter mobilization team. Signing up here will register you as a volunteer to work the event, not as a general attendee for the rally itself. Because we are partnering with an active campaign, all schedule details and locations are subject to change until finalized by the campaign. We will send out confirmed logistics closer to the event date._

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for the **Talarico for Texas** rally at **the Neches Room in Beaumont TX**! We are showing up as volunteers to this event to fire up the rally attendees, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with passionate rally attendees and community members
- Check voter registration statuses on the spot (ensuring no one has been purged)
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive **1 hour before doors open** so that we can optimize working the line of attendees. They will be lining up way in advance, and our goal is to check voter registrations for everyone waiting to get in. Here is what to expect during your shift:

[9:30-10:00am] Setup & Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the site leads, and align on our goals.

[10:00-11:00am] Working the Line (Part 1) | As the crowd grows ahead of doors opening, we will start engaging the very first people in line and continue moving down the line to check registration statuses and get folks set up on Reach.

[11:00-12:00pm]: Stay for the event! | Once the programming begins, volunteers are invited and encouraged to stay, enjoy the rally, and celebrate the energy with our neighbors!

[12:00-1:00pm]: Working the Line (Part 2) | After the event, we'll sweep the line of attendees waiting to take a photo with James Talarico


### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: The Neches Room
246 Crockett St 
Beaumont TX 77701

Park in the lot across from the venue. Free Parking

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes (you will be on your feet talking to voters!)

_Note: Necessary materials will be provided at the check-in table, but feel free to bring your own backup supplies just in case!_

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single Texan counts. Sign up for a shift today!

events.title: Kingston: WFP Poll Site Visibility
events.description:
### Early Voting kicks off on Saturday, October 24th and we need YOUR help in getting out the vote for the Working Families Party ballot line! 

Join us  to talk to voters on their way to the polls! Pick an area when you sign-up and we'll follow-up with the exact location.

The only way we protect our democracy from Trump and MAGA’s power grab is by organizing together to defend our votes. **Here’s the bottom line: There’s a lot at stake in this election.**

First, we must get hundreds of thousands of votes on the WFP line for Kathy Hochul to keep existing as a party and to block MAGA Republican Bruce Blakeman.

This election is not just about defeating Blakeman — it's also about sending a clear message to Kathy Hochul and all of our elected officials that we want a government that centers working families and the urgent need for a more affordable New York for everyone.

### Never done poll site visibility before? No worries!! We will get you trained up and ready to go.

_If you’re not able to participate in poll site visibility and want to help turnout voters, join our Vote WFP phone banks on Mondays @ 6-8pm → [SIGN UP!](https://mobilize.us/s/gB5FFs)_

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in Ridgecrest
events.description:
**The No Kings Alliance is mobilizing urgent, nationwide action in response to the Republican government shutdown. Join us this weekend as we provide mutual aid and care to our neighbors hurt by the Republican government shutdown.**

Right now Republicans are refusing to protect critical healthcare and nutrition programs which will result in 42 million Americans losing the benefits that keep their families fed. When those in power hoard resources and use our government to punish people, we answer with collective care and resistance, feeding our bodies and fueling our movement.

Join us at 132 N China Lake Blvd from 9-11am to donate food, household, and personal care products to support families in need. Donations will be delivered to Salvation Army.

Salvation Army has requested the following goods: Rice-a-roni, Cup of noodles, pasta, canned protein (tuna, chicken, beef, beef stew), cereal & granola bars, cans of nuts, boxed cookies & crackers, dried fruits, beef jerky, dry milk, bottled water, mac & cheese, single serving cups of fruit & pudding, cereal, oatmeal packets, and jelly/jam (no peanut butter, they have enough.)

Donation drop off by the shopping center sign.

Find more out about our group at ridgecrest50501.com

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events._

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in WHITTIER,CA!
events.description:
Join the Whittier Indivisible Chapter at Michigan Park in Whittier, CA on November 15th, from 11-12:30pm to gather together and DONATE non-perishable food to support families in need. 

Our Chapter will also host a fundraising campaign for the entire month of November to help those in need - ALL proceeds to the Chapter will be sent to a local food pantry. You can donate here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblewc1368840224

Let us support and love on our community! Thousands in our own cities will be affected by the ending of SNAP benefits, and we want to help them. Will you join us?

Additionally, if you cannot make this Mutual Aid Drive & Potluck event on November 15th, we will be hosting various “pop-up tables” throughout the La Habra/Fullerton/Whittier areas to gather donations throughout the month. Please view our Facebook and Instagram pages for information on locations of these tables. All donations will be delivered to the Santa Fe Springs Interfaith Food Center.

All attendees will be sent more details, including the specific list of necessary food items, upon registration! We hope to see you there.
**PLEASE NOTE: We will be hosting TWO FOOD DRIVES at Michigan Park: November 15th and November 22nd (which is why you will see 2 Mobilize events.)
Thanks for joining us!
